assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegates must safeguard the security of the Sky Protocol through the Executive Vote process. To deal with emergencies related to Executive Votes, ADs are required to sign up for the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5).

ADs must strictly adhere to all onboarding procedures and usage instructions associated with this emergency contact mechanism. ADs that fail to do so will be considered in misalignment and will be derecognized.

The high operational security requirements applicable to ADs extend to their use of the emergency contact mechanism.
assessments.description: Requires Aligned Delegates to enroll in the approved emergency contact mechanism and follow its procedures, with derecognition for non-compliance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The enrollment duty is concrete and checkable, but adherence to 'all onboarding procedures and usage instructions' is delegated to an external document with no values given. The 'high operational security requirements' sentence is purely qualitative.
metrics: ADs must sign up for the approved emergency contact mechanism
ADs must strictly adhere to all onboarding procedures and usage instructions
Failure to adhere results in misalignment and derecognition
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states an explicit consequence, derecognition, for failing onboarding or usage procedures, which is a concrete remedy. However, the path to it depends on a misalignment report via the Reports of Misalignment catch-all, so escalation requires someone to volunteer it and no quantified penalty applies.

assessments.title: Protocol Security Workstream Lead Requirements
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead role must be held by an individual with demonstrated expertise in protocol security, smart contract security, and operational security practices. The individual must not have involvement in any business, political, or governance-related activities that could create a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to have security expertise and no conflicting business, political, or governance involvement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real, but 'demonstrated expertise' has no criteria, evidence standard, or verification method, and 'could create a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly' is open to judgment. No thresholds, cadence, or deadlines are stated, so a defender could plausibly argue compliance on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph cites no enforcement path, and the catalog mechanisms (penalties, conservatorship, insurance pricing, artifact review) target Primes, agents, or vaults rather than this role. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls plausibly apply.

assessments.title: Emergency Response System
assessments.quote: This Article defines a general emergency response protocol for managing emergencies or urgent situations outside of the standard Weekly Governance Cycle and Monthly Governance Cycle.
assessments.description: Introduces a general emergency response protocol for urgent situations outside the regular governance cycles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph only announces that a protocol exists and gives no thresholds, triggers, deadlines, or actors. It is a posture statement with no operative obligation a party could be checked against.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph imposes no obligation that a mechanism could enforce; the escalation machinery lives in sub-articles, not in this introductory text.

assessments.title: Definition Of Emergency Situations
assessments.quote:
An emergency situation is any situation that would require immediate intervention to prevent initiation of Emergency Shutdown, severe peg divergence, or harm to members and users of the Ecosystem.

Pursuant to [A.0.1.2.1 - Core Council’s Broad Discretionary Capacity](f18229fe-fbc3-4dc8-ad84-4bca2915f6c4), the Core Facilitator has broad discretion to apply the emergency-situation processes defined in [A.1.9.1 - Emergency Response](20dcf582-8862-48b3-9ca9-c3703871bd14) to urgent situations. Urgent situations are defined as any situation that involves a time-sensitive matter that would need an expedited governance process, where following a standard governance cycle would be too slow, risk a larger problem, or constitute an important missed opportunity.
assessments.description: Defines what counts as an emergency or urgent situation, granting the Core Facilitator discretion to invoke expedited emergency processes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The definition relies on undefined judgment terms such as "immediate intervention", "severe peg divergence", "harm", "time-sensitive", and "important missed opportunity", with no thresholds or measurable criteria. Compliance with the discretionary trigger is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines the scope of emergency processes rather than imposing a duty on an actor. Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is the process this definition gates, but nothing polices misuse of the Facilitator's discretion beyond the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group
assessments.quote: Emergency response is coordinated by the Emergency Response Group ("ERG"). The Emergency Response Group is a group of Facilitators, Aligned Delegates, and Ecosystem Actors that include domain experts in different areas of the Sky Ecosystem. The Emergency Response Group is tasked with reacting to emergency scenarios that are critical to the survival of the Sky Protocol.
assessments.description: Establishes the Emergency Response Group as the coordinator of emergency response, with a membership of Facilitators, Aligned Delegates, and Ecosystem Actors.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names defined actor categories and a clear role, but gives no membership count, selection criteria, or response deadline. 'Critical to the survival of the Sky Protocol' is a judgment standard, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is the defined escalation protocol the ERG operates within, so ERG failures could be escalated through it. Its consequences are not quantified for this paragraph, and escalation depends on someone invoking it.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership Criteria
assessments.quote: The membership of the Emergency Response Group may change at the discretion of Core GovOps, and as circumstances require. Generally, the Emergency Response Group should contain domain-expert Ecosystem Actors as well as governance decision-makers. The group must be able to diagnose a situation, suggest a short-term mitigation and act on such mitigation. The group should also be able to define the path forward for a long-term solution to the problem and act on it.
assessments.description: Sets discretionary membership and capability expectations for the Emergency Response Group, which must diagnose, mitigate, and act on incidents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names real capability obligations (diagnose, suggest short-term mitigation, act, define long-term path) but gives no thresholds, cadence, or verifiable membership criteria. Membership may change at Core GovOps' discretion and the group 'should' contain domain experts, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) defines the response protocol, but nothing penalizes a composition or capability shortfall in this paragraph. Membership is set by Core GovOps discretion, which is self-enforcement, so only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership
assessments.quote:
The membership of the Emergency Response Group is defined as Active Data in [A.1.9.1.2.2.0.6.1 - Emergency Response Group Current Membership](e9807449-fdc3-4860-8d53-c56181311618).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is Core GovOps.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.description: Defines Emergency Response Group membership as Active Data and assigns Core GovOps responsibility for updating it via the Direct Edit process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names a responsible actor (Core GovOps) and a referenced update protocol, but the membership itself is delegated to a linked Active Data document and no eligibility criteria, group size, or update cadence appear. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Core GovOps is both the responsible party and the only enforcer of its own Direct Edit updates, which is self-enforcement. The Emergency Response System and Agent Artifact Review do not reach membership accuracy, and no penalty or on-chain mechanism applies.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Team Members
assessments.quote:
Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, that team should assign two (2) of its own team members to be responsible for incident response.

A team may assign more than two (2) of its team members to be responsible for incident response at the discretion of Core GovOps.

To the extent possible, the selected team members should be in different timezones and jurisdictions for maximum operational and regulatory resilience.

The team members assigned to the Emergency Response Group should not be disclosed publicly under any circumstances as this could make them targets.
assessments.description: Specifies that team Emergency Response Group members assign two team members for incident response, with optional expansion and non-disclosure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The count of two assigned team members is concrete, but 'should' makes the core duty soft, and expansion beyond two is delegated to Core GovOps discretion. Timezone and jurisdiction diversity is qualified by 'to the extent possible' with no threshold.
metrics: Where an ERG Member is a team, assign two (2) team members for incident response
A team may assign more than two (2) at the discretion of Core GovOps
Selected members should be in different timezones and jurisdictions to the extent possible
Team members should not be disclosed publicly under any circumstances
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs emergency escalation, not staffing or disclosure of team members, and no penalty, conservatorship, or priced incentive attaches to failing to assign two members. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls would apply.

assessments.title: Additional Emergency Response Team Members
assessments.quote: Soter Labs is permitted to assign more than two (2) of its team members to the permissioned Emergency Response Communication Channels defined in [A.1.9.1.3 - Emergency Response Communication Channels](18418289-ada8-401d-a992-7e38b235c866), as well as any Emergency Response calls.
assessments.description: Permits Soter Labs to assign more than two team members to Emergency Response communication channels and calls.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a specific actor (Soter Labs) and a numeric baseline ('more than two (2)'), but sets no upper bound, cap, or criteria for how many members may be assigned. Whether a given assignment is permitted cannot be fully verified from the text.
metrics: more than two (2) Soter Labs team members assigned to Emergency Response Communication Channels and Emergency Response calls
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a permission rather than a constraint, and no penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism attaches to the number of assigned members. The Emergency Response System is the surrounding context, but nothing in the text links it to a violation of this permission.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegate Membership In Emergency Response Group
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegate membership in the Emergency Response Group is not automatic based on amount of delegated SKY or Ranked Delegate status. An Aligned Delegate seeking to participate in emergency response must be reviewed and approved by Core GovOps prior to joining the Emergency Response Group.

Core GovOps has discretion to approve or deny Aligned Delegate participation in the Emergency Response Group based on their assessment of the Aligned Delegate's competence and reliability.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps pre-approval of Aligned Delegates before they join the Emergency Response Group, based on discretionary competence and reliability.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The approval requirement and the named reviewer (Core GovOps) are concrete, but the admission criteria are purely judgmental ("competence and reliability", "discretion") with no thresholds, metrics, or review cadence. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Approval by Core GovOps required prior to joining the Emergency Response Group
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain gate, or escalation path is tied to an unapproved Aligned Delegate joining; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Signal Group
assessments.quote:
A unique Signal "Emergency Response" Group will be used for all incident response coordination.

TechOps Services will create the Signal Group and assign its administrators.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead shall manage access to the Signal Group. All Emergency Response Members must be added to the Group.

Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, the two (2) team members responsible for incident response are required to join the Signal Group.

The Signal Group should not be used for any purpose except communications concerning a potential emergency situation. The Group must be configured to have a four-week message retention.
assessments.description: Requires a dedicated Signal Emergency Response group for incident coordination, with access, membership, and four-week retention rules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligations are quantified: exactly two team members must join and messages must be retained for four weeks. Gaps include the soft 'should not be used' wording on group purpose and no cadence for verifying membership or access.
metrics: Two (2) team members responsible for incident response must join the Signal Group where a member is a team
Four-week message retention configured on the Group
All Emergency Response Members must be added to the Group
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph configures a communications channel and no penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to membership or retention failures. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) defines escalation but does not specify consequences for this channel's configuration.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.quote: Emergency Response Group Members must use an emergency contact mechanism to deal with emergencies. This emergency contact mechanism is selected and validated by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Group Members to use a validated emergency contact mechanism selected by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names a defined actor (Emergency Response Group Members) and selector (Protocol Security Workstream Lead), but gives no criteria for what counts as a valid mechanism, when it must be used, or how use is verified. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) defines an escalation protocol but attaches no consequence to failing to use the contact mechanism, and no penalty, artifact review, or emergency spell is tied to this duty. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Selection Criteria
assessments.quote:
A suitable emergency contact mechanism should meet the following criteria:

- The mechanism should use enterprise grade infrastructure with correspondingly high levels of uptime.
- The mechanism should not require personal information or KYC from users.
- The mechanism should allow segmenting of target user groups, so that required individuals are only notified when necessary.
- The mechanism should be able to bypass silent / do not disturb mode on devices to achieve an immediate response any time of day.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism minimizes data tracking of individual users.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism is open source.
assessments.description: Sets selection criteria for an emergency contact mechanism covering uptime, privacy, user segmentation, and bypassing do-not-disturb modes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The criteria are phrased as non-binding 'should' language, and the uptime and infrastructure criteria ('enterprise grade', 'correspondingly high levels of uptime') have no numeric threshold. Several criteria (no KYC, segmentation, DND bypass) are checkable, but a defender could argue the text does not bind any actor to a compliance outcome.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph governs the choice of a communication channel, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, artifact review, emergency spells) watches or penalizes whether a chosen mechanism meets these criteria; only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.quote: The currently approved emergency contact mechanism is PagerDuty.
assessments.description: Names PagerDuty as the currently approved emergency contact mechanism for the Emergency Response System.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names one concrete, checkable system (PagerDuty) but states a configuration fact rather than an obligation. It sets no response time, escalation cadence, or conditions for use, so a defender could argue it imposes no binding duty.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The parent Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) defines escalation outside the normal governance cycle, but nothing in the paragraph or the cited mechanisms attaches a consequence to failing to use or misusing this channel. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop reaches it.

assessments.title: Changes To Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may recommend changing the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5), but they must do so in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. The Core Facilitator’s recommendation is subject to a poll through the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator recommend changing the approved emergency contact mechanism, after consulting the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, subject to a weekly poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names actors (Core Facilitator, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and a process (Operational Weekly Cycle poll), but "in consultation with" has no defined form, depth, or completion criterion. The paragraph gives no thresholds, deadlines, or poll requirements, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The weekly poll is a procedural approval gate rather than a penalty or remedy for breach, and no emergency, penalty, or review mechanism in the catalog reaches a violation of this consultation and poll requirement beyond the catch-all misalignment reporting.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Fire Drills
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator may run firedrills to test the preparedness of individuals that have been added to the emergency contact mechanism. This will be done at the discretion of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator. The results of firedrills shall be published to maintain transparency.
assessments.description: Permits the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator to run discretionary fire drills on emergency contacts and publish the results.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors and a publication obligation exist, but the drills are optional ("may") and left "at the discretion" of the actors, with no cadence, thresholds, or deadline for publication. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism reaches a failure to run or publish drills; the only potentially applicable path is the generic misalignment and adjudication backstop.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation.

After an emergency situation has been declared, Core GovOps is responsible for coordinating emergency-situation processes to ensure they are civil, consistently applied and aligned. The Core Facilitator is responsible for publishing Polls and Executive Votes.

Any participant in the Sky Ecosystem, including Ecosystem Actors, Aligned Delegates or other community members, can request that the Core Facilitator declare an emergency. The Core Facilitator is granted broad discretion in handling such requests.
assessments.description: Assigns the Core Facilitator power to declare emergencies and Core GovOps duties to coordinate emergency processes, and lets participants request declarations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and roles are named, but there are no thresholds, criteria for declaring an emergency, or deadlines. Operative terms such as 'civil, consistently applied and aligned' and 'broad discretion' are judgment language, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is a defined escalation protocol run by Core GovOps, a body separate from the Core Facilitator, so it plausibly reaches failures of these roles. Its consequences for misusing or declining discretion are not quantified for this paragraph, and the 'broad discretion' language limits enforceability.

assessments.title: Considerations Before Expediting Protocol Changes
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is required to consider several important factors before expediting changes to the protocol:

- Potential for SKY holders to miss a poll or Executive Vote due to departure from the standard governance cycles.
- Expedited votes may not allow for sufficient discussion, leading to a sub-optimal solution.
- Increased governance burden on community and increased workload for domain teams.
- Frequent expedited votes may signal a lack of appreciation for a consistent and predictable governance process.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to weigh four listed governance factors before expediting protocol changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to consider factors is real, but it uses judgment language ('consider') over enumerated categories with no criteria, thresholds, or verifiable record of consideration. A Facilitator could argue compliance on any facts. No expedition trigger or documentation requirement is defined.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism verifies whether the Facilitator considered the factors before expediting. Emergency Spells and the Emergency Response System govern security threats and escalation, not this pre-decision consideration. Only the misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Incident Validation
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for determining whether a reported incident is a valid emergency; where possible, this can be done in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
assessments.description: Assigns the Core Facilitator responsibility for determining whether a reported incident is a valid emergency, with optional stakeholder consultation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A named actor and a real determination duty exist, but there is no criteria for what makes an incident a valid emergency, no deadline, and consultation is optional ('where possible'). Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is a defined escalation protocol that governs the emergency process this paragraph feeds, so a mis-determined or skipped validation could be escalated. The consequence is not quantified for this duty, and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Incident Categorization
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for categorizing emergencies according to their severity and other pertinent criteria.
assessments.description: Assigns the Core Facilitator responsibility for categorizing emergencies by severity and other pertinent criteria.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined actor and a real obligation are named, but the severity levels and the 'other pertinent criteria' are never specified. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System defines the escalation path that categorization feeds into, so a miscategorized emergency would plausibly fail to trigger the correct response. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on the process firing.

assessments.title: Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger
assessments.quote: Upon receiving notification from the Core Facilitator of a validated and categorized emergency situation, TechOps Services must trigger a notification in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2 - Emergency Contact Mechanism](3efb0238-aaae-4351-9ec9-31902f3a1394). All Emergency Response Group Members are required to acknowledge the incident in a timely manner through the Emergency Contact Mechanism. The notification must include a link to the official Emergency Response video call ("war room").
assessments.description: Requires TechOps to notify the Emergency Contact Mechanism after a validated emergency, with responder acknowledgment and a war-room link.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The steps are enumerated and checkable: a notification must be triggered, responders must acknowledge, and the notice must contain a war-room link. The acknowledgment deadline is only "in a timely manner", with no numeric window, so the timing magnitude is qualitative.
metrics: Notification triggered upon receiving Core Facilitator notice of a validated and categorized emergency
All Emergency Response Group Members must acknowledge the incident "in a timely manner" (no numeric deadline)
Notification must include a link to the official Emergency Response video call ("war room")
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is a defined escalation protocol outside the standard governance cycle that plausibly covers a failure to notify or acknowledge. No penalty is quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Video Call Coordination
assessments.quote: Emergency Response Group Members are required to promptly join the Video Call to coordinate incident response.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Group Members to promptly join the Video Call to coordinate incident response.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor and the obligation to join the incident-response Video Call are defined, but "promptly" has no time limit or other measurable criterion. A member who joins after several minutes could argue compliance either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is a defined escalation protocol for incident response and plausibly reaches a member who fails to join the coordination call. It sets no specific penalty or consequence for late or missing attendance, and escalation depends on someone raising the issue.

assessments.title: Known And Uncontentious Remedies
assessments.quote: If a remedy is known and uncontentious, the Core Facilitator shall coordinate with the necessary Ecosystem Actors to expedite an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to coordinate with Ecosystem Actors to expedite an Executive Vote when a remedy is known and uncontentious.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is a named actor doing a defined action, but "known and uncontentious" and "necessary Ecosystem Actors" have no criteria, and "expedite" has no deadline. Whether the Facilitator complied is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph sits inside the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d), but that system defines the escalation path without attaching a consequence to the Facilitator failing to coordinate. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism reaches this duty, so only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Emergency Declaration Procedure
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation at their discretion, either on their own initiative or in response to a request from a community member.

When declaring an emergency, the Core Facilitator should create a formal post on the Sky Forum, providing sufficient detail regarding the issue and explaining why immediate action is required. If the situation allows, the Core Facilitator should post the emergency declaration on the Sky Forum before taking action. If the urgency of the situation requires immediate intervention without delay, the Core Facilitator should create the Forum post as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, the emergency action.

There may be situations in which a public Emergency Declaration would be counterproductive to security objectives; the Core Facilitator is granted discretion in these matters.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator declare emergencies at discretion and asks for a Sky Forum post explaining the emergency, before or after action.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligations use judgment language: the Facilitator 'should' post 'sufficient detail' and act 'as soon as possible'. No deadline, threshold, or measurable content is stated, and the discretionary carve-out for security-sensitive cases leaves compliance arguable either way.
metrics: Forum post should be created before taking action if the situation allows
Forum post should be created as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, emergency action when immediate intervention is required
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines the declaration process itself, and the posting duty is a 'should' with no named enforcer, penalty, or escalation. The Core Facilitator effectively self-polices, and the only generic backstop is Reports of Misalignment, which is weak alone.

assessments.title: Record Retention
assessments.description: Says incident records should be retained after an incident for review, with the Core Facilitator deciding external sharing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is hedged as 'should' with a non-exhaustive 'may include but are not limited to' list. Item 1 is an explicit stub ('to be specified in a future iteration'), and there is no retention period, owner, or verifiable condition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Emergency Response System and Emergency Spells govern incident escalation, not record retention, and Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) covers agent artifacts rather than these incident records. Only the catch-all misalignment reporting reaches this text.

assessments.title: Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness
assessments.quote: Emergency preparedness is a critical priority. Core GovOps, in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, must regularly evaluate the emergency preparedness of the Emergency Response Group. This can be done through running fire drills or through extensive postmortems after an actual incident.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to regularly evaluate the Emergency Response Group's preparedness via fire drills or postmortems.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and an identifiable evaluation duty exist, but 'regularly' has no cadence and 'can be done through' makes the method optional. No thresholds or measurable outcomes are stated, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: regularly evaluate emergency preparedness (no cadence or deadline specified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. No penalty, escalation, or artifact review reaches Core GovOps' own evaluation duty; the only applicable backstop is the Reports of Misalignment catch-all, and the duty is effectively self-policed by Core GovOps.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures for Ecosystem Actor Individuals And Teams
assessments.quote:
For Ecosystem Actors appointed to the Emergency Response Group, fulfilling the responsibilities of this role is as critical to their overall performance evaluation as their customary deliverables.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is an Ecosystem Actor individual, the individual should be removed from the Group.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is part of an Ecosystem Actor team, the specific member who has failed to meet requirements should be removed from the Group.

If different Emergency Response Group Members from the same Ecosystem Actor team consistently fail to meet requirements, the Ecosystem Actor team as a whole should be removed from the Group.

The removal of a Member from the Group is done at the discretion of Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Ecosystem Actor is removed from the Emergency Response Group for deficient performance, Core GovOps must transparently announce this action via a post to the Sky Forum. Further, the removal must be incorporated into the evaluation of the Ecosystem Actor’s overall performance.

Core GovOps has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.description: Sets removal, Forum announcement, and performance-evaluation consequences for Emergency Response Group members who fail emergency-preparedness requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names enforcers (Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and removal outcomes, but its trigger is qualitative: 'non-negligible' deficiencies, 'consistently' failing, 'swift action', and 'clear documentation' have no thresholds or cadence. Removal is left to discretion ('should', 'may'), so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Removal of an individual Ecosystem Actor from the Emergency Response Group for deficient performance
Removal of the whole Ecosystem Actor team when different members from the same team consistently fail requirements
Public post to the Sky Forum announcing any Ecosystem Actor removal for deficient performance
Removal recorded in the Ecosystem Actor's overall performance evaluation
Documentation of all instances of Emergency Response Group Members' failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) is the parent escalation framework, and this rule gives a distinct enforcer (Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead) concrete remedies: group removal, a public Forum post, and a performance-evaluation entry. Mid rather than strong because the removal is discretionary ('should', 'may'), no penalty is quantified, and firing depends on those officers choosing to act.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures For Alignment Conservers
assessments.quote:
For an Alignment Conserver who has been appointed to the Emergency Response Group, the requirements of this role become as critical to the assessment of their overall performance as their customary obligations.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

Where the deficient Member is an Alignment Conserver, that Member should be derecognized pursuant to [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57).

Where the deficient Alignment Conserver is the Core Facilitator, the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps must reach consensus in order to initiate a derecognition proceeding against the Core Facilitator. Once this threshold is met, the procedure defined in [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57) should be followed. In the interim, Core GovOps selects an Operational Facilitator to step in temporarily and assist with coordinating emergency response.

The initiation of derecognition is done at the discretion of the Core Facilitator (or Core GovOps) and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, the Core Facilitator and Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Alignment Conserver is removed from the Emergency Response Group and derecognized for deficient performance, the Core Facilitator must transparently announce this action pursuant to [A.1.5.10.1 - Derecognition Notice](9c05207d-5e11-43ae-a8a3-1b61734d6ef9).

The Core Facilitator has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the Alignment Conserver’s derecognition and removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.description: Requires documenting and derecognizing Emergency Response Group Alignment Conservers who fail emergency-preparedness requirements, with discretionary initiation and announcement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations name defined actors (Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead, Core Facilitator) and a consensus condition, but 'non-negligible' deficiencies, 'swift' action, 'clear documentation' and discretionary initiation have no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria. A defender could plausibly argue compliance on the same facts.
metrics: Core GovOps and Protocol Security Workstream Lead must document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members' failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements
Core Facilitator derecognition of Core Facilitator requires consensus between Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps
Removal requires clear documentation supporting it
Derecognition must be transparently announced pursuant to A.1.5.10.1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Removal from the Emergency Response Group is a concrete remedy enforced by Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, who are distinct from the Conservers they evaluate, and it sits within the Emergency Response System escalation framework. However, initiation is at the enforcers' discretion, no penalty is quantified, and the Adjudication Process it runs through is only a catch-all.

assessments.title: Sky Core Governance Security
assessments.quote: This Article governs the correct and secure execution of Sky Governance processes for deploying and reviewing Executive Votes. This Article must protect against all forms of attacks, disruption and accidental failure by maximizing the transparency and resilience of the Sky Executive Process.
assessments.description: Scopes Article A.1.10 to securing Executive Vote deployment and review against attacks, disruption, and accidental failure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a posture statement with no metrics, thresholds, actors with defined duties, or verifiable conditions. 'Protect against all forms of attacks' and 'maximizing transparency and resilience' cannot be checked against any text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no consequence, and the Article's emergency and penalty mechanisms attach to specific sub-rules rather than to this scope statement. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops would reach it.

assessments.title: Spell Team Anonymity
assessments.quote: The Spell teams need not share their identities. Therefore, it is no longer a requirement that Spell crafting teams publish the deployer of a smart contract. The Spell Checklists have been amended accordingly.
assessments.description: Removes the requirement for Spell crafting teams to publish smart contract deployers; teams may stay anonymous.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete removed obligation (publishing the deployer) and a checklist amendment, so it is operative. However, it states no metric, threshold, or deadline, and 'share their identities' is undefined, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a permission and relaxes a duty, so no penalty, on-chain, or review mechanism attaches to a violation of it.

assessments.title: Executive Sheet
assessments.quote:
The Executive Sheet serves as a planning instrument and documentation for the agreed content of the Spell. It is therefore one of the foundational documents in the Executive Process. Each Spell has a dedicated Executive Sheet. The Governance Point creates a new Executive Sheet for each Executive Vote cycle, listing every executive item intended for inclusion in that cycle along with the provenance of each item. In this way, the Executive Sheet helps ensure transparency and verification in the Executive Process. Past Executive Sheets are preserved in order to provide a record of Executive Votes and their provenance.

The Executive Sheet (also referred to as the "exec sheet" or "sheet") is maintained on a large Google Sheets spreadsheet with several tabs. Each Executive Vote has its own tab, whose title is the designated Target Date for each Spell.

The Executive Sheet provides a publicly visible list of plain-English instructions outlining the executive actions performed in a given Spell. Each executive action is populated in the Executive Sheet under a column and broken down into input actions (high-level actions) and derived actions (resulting from input actions).

The Executive Sheet is used by several actors in the Executive Process. It is managed and populated by the Governance Point, used by stakeholders, who are required to provide confirmation for proposed executive items, and by the Spell Team. The Executive Sheet is the source of truth for the Spell Crafter who crafts the Spell based on its content. Only the Core Facilitator has write access to the Executive Sheet.
assessments.description: Defines the Executive Sheet as the per-Spell planning record, with one tab per Executive Vote and write access limited to the Core Facilitator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Several operative parameters are concrete and checkable: one sheet per Spell, one tab per Executive Vote titled by Target Date, and write access restricted to the Core Facilitator. The content requirements (listing every item with provenance, stakeholder confirmation) have no format, deadline, or completeness test.
metrics: Each Spell has a dedicated Executive Sheet
A new Executive Sheet is created for each Executive Vote cycle
Each Executive Vote has its own tab, titled with the Spell's Target Date
Only the Core Facilitator has write access to the Executive Sheet
Past Executive Sheets are preserved
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, or escalation mechanism in the catalog or the paragraph reaches sheet accuracy, completeness, or unauthorized edits; only the catch-all misalignment reporting applies.

assessments.title: Target Date
assessments.quote: The Target Date refers to the planned date when the Spell is expected to be made available to be voted on. The Target Date is decided by the Governance Point in collaboration with the Spell Crafter. Spells are usually deployed following a two-week cadence. Normally, the Target Date falls on Thursdays.
assessments.description: Defines the Target Date for spell voting availability, set by the Governance Point with the Spell Crafter on a usually two-week, Thursday cadence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two-week cadence and Thursday default are concrete, but both are hedged with "usually" and "normally," and the decision process ("in collaboration with") has no criteria or deadline. A defender could argue it is descriptive rather than binding.
metrics: Spells are usually deployed on a two-week cadence
Target Date normally falls on Thursdays
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or artifact review mechanism reaches a scheduling date; the paragraph is a definition, and only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Executive Document
assessments.quote:
The Executive Document (also referred to as the "Executive Copy," "executive," "Executive Proposal," or "exec doc") is a formal, plain-English Markdown document that serves as the primary communication tool for presenting the contents of an Executive Vote to the community. Created after the Executive Sheet is finalized, it provides a detailed breakdown of the actions proposed in the Executive Vote. Unlike the Executive Sheet, which organizes actions in a cell-based format, the Executive Document expresses these actions in sentence format for improved readability.

Each Executive Document corresponds to a specific Spell and describes the actions that the Spell will perform if executed. It is a critical tool for ensuring transparency, clarity, and alignment among stakeholders. The document serves as a proposal that can be voted on and either approved or rejected by Sky Governance. The Core Facilitator is responsible for producing and finalizing the Executive Document; and any changes must be made by them.

The Executive Document is designed to be accessible to both technical and non-technical members of the Sky Ecosystem. It enables Aligned Delegates and SKY holders to understand the actions that will be executed when the Spell is cast. Its contents are publicly visible on the Voting Portal, where Aligned Delegates review it before voting on the Spell. In addition to serving as a reference for voters, the Executive Document also guides the Spell Team in developing and finalizing the Spell, ensuring that the proposed actions are accurately implemented. The contents of the Executive Document are hashed and included within the Spell code to provide an additional layer of verification.
assessments.description: Defines the Executive Document as a plain-English Markdown proposal describing Spell actions, produced and changed only by the Core Facilitator and hashed into Spell code.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Core Facilitator) and a verifiable integrity step (contents hashed into Spell code), but gives no timing, finalization criteria, or hash-verification procedure. Most of the text is definitional rather than an operative obligation.
metrics: Document is a formal, plain-English Markdown document
Created after the Executive Sheet is finalized
Contents are hashed and included within the Spell code
Only the Core Facilitator may produce, finalize, or change the Executive Document
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The hash inclusion gives integrity verification but the paragraph attaches no consequence to a Core Facilitator altering the document, and no catalogued penalty, emergency, or artifact-review mechanism is stated to reach this rule. Only the misalignment-reporting catch-all applies.

assessments.title: Ecosystem Spell Validation
assessments.quote: Ecosystem Spell Validation (also referred to as "Spell validation" or "validation") refers to the process of performing a set of checks and high-level review of a specific Spell’s code as it exists on the blockchain (referred to as a "deployed Spell"). This process applies only to the deployed Spell and is not as comprehensive as the reviews conducted during the Spell development process by the Spell Reviewers. The purpose of Spell validation is to validate the safety of the current Spell in respect to its security impacts in relation to Sky Protocol smart contracts.
assessments.description: Defines Ecosystem Spell Validation as a limited high-level review of deployed Spell code for smart contract security impacts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines the process scope (deployed Spells only, less comprehensive than development review), which is concrete. However, the 'set of checks' and 'high-level review' are never enumerated or quantified, and no threshold, cadence, or pass/fail criterion exists.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional paragraph with no operative obligation, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, PSM, liquidation) reaches a violation of it; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Spell Team
assessments.quote: Each Executive Vote has a dedicated Spell Team, made up of Spell Crafters and Spell Reviewers. The Spell Team must include one Crafter, who is responsible for crafting the Spells. The Spell Team must also include at least two Reviewers, responsible for reviewing and confirming that the Spells are ready for the Executive Vote, at least one of whom should be a member of a different Ecosystem Actor than the Spell Crafter. A Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell. The Spell Team is a set of technical contributors working on developing all technical and smart-contract-related aspects of a particular Executive Vote, based on instructions set out by the Governance Point.
assessments.description: Requires each Executive Vote to have a Spell Team with one Crafter and at least two Reviewers, one from a different Ecosystem Actor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Headcounts are quantified (one Crafter, at least two Reviewers) and the cross-actor requirement is checkable. The 'should be' qualifier on the different-Ecosystem-Actor Reviewer softens that clause, and no cadence or verification step is stated.
metrics: Exactly one Spell Crafter per Spell Team
At least two Spell Reviewers per Spell Team
At least one Reviewer from a different Ecosystem Actor than the Crafter (stated as 'should')
A Crafter cannot also serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to Spell Team composition, and the only check is self-confirmation by Reviewers, which is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Spell Crafter
assessments.quote: The Spell Crafter (the Crafter) is the person or entity who parses the written instruction set of a proposed Executive to Solidity code in order to develop the Spell in the first instance. Every addition, modification, or removal of code or content within the Spell must be performed by the Crafter. The designated Spell Crafter must be rotated, such that the same person does not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes. The Spell Crafter is a member of the Spell Team for a particular Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Defines the Spell Crafter role, requires all Spell code changes be made by the Crafter, and mandates rotation between consecutive Executive Votes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rotation constraint is objectively checkable (same person may not craft Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes), and the Crafter's exclusive authority over Spell changes is clear. Gaps remain: 'person or entity' is undefined, and the text does not say how rotation is recorded or verified.
metrics: Same person may not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes
Every addition, modification, or removal of Spell code or content must be performed by the Crafter
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, review, or emergency mechanism is tied to Crafter rotation or exclusive authority; the only reach is the generic misalignment and adjudication backstop.

assessments.title: Spell Reviewer
assessments.quote: The Spell Reviewers (the Reviewers) are the people or entities responsible for reviewing the draft Spell as parsed by the Spell Crafter. The Reviewers are responsible for verifying the Spell, finding issues and catching bugs and mistakes in the Spell, and otherwise ensuring its quality. There is an important delineation between the function of Spell Crafters and Spell Reviewers: the Reviewers may not perform any addition, modification or removal of code or content within the Spell, although they may suggest changes to the Spell Crafter. Spell Reviewers are members of the wider Spell Team for a particular Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Defines Spell Reviewers as the parties who review draft Spells, and bars them from editing Spell code or content.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The bright-line prohibition on adding, modifying, or removing Spell code is checkable, but the core duties (verifying, catching bugs, ensuring quality) are judgment language with no metrics. The reviewer population is also left as 'people or entities' with no defined membership criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph cites no enforcement path, and the catalog's Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) is not shown to reach Spell Reviewers, so only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Governance Point And Governance Backup
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point is the Core Facilitator. Currently, the only Core Facilitator is JanSky. Each Spell also has a designated Governance Backup. The Governance Backup is required to assume the responsibilities of the Governance Point if the original Governance Point becomes unavailable, effectively stepping into the role as needed. The Governance Point is responsible for coordinating the Executive Vote and ensuring that the information in the Executive Sheet accurately reflects the progress of the Spell.

The Technical Point has domain expertise as the crafter of the smart contracts, but the Governance Point also has crucial context and should serve as a cross-check to the extent they can. The Governance Point is expected to ask questions where needed.
assessments.description: Defines the Governance Point (Core Facilitator) and Governance Backup roles, with duties to coordinate the Executive Vote and cross-check Spells.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The roles and some duties are named (Core Facilitator, Governance Backup, Executive Vote, Executive Sheet), but the operative standards are judgment language: 'to the extent they can', 'where needed', and 'ensuring' accuracy. No trigger defines when the Backup must assume the role ('becomes unavailable' is undefined), and no cadence or deadline is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or on-chain mechanism reaches a Governance Point's coordination or cross-check duties. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) concerns Agents' artifacts rather than this role, and the remaining route is the generic misalignment catch-all.

assessments.title: Role Of Governance Point And Backup
assessments.quote: The role of Governance Point and Governance Backup alternates from within the Core Facilitator. The positions rotate, following an internal schedule.
assessments.description: Specifies that the Governance Point and Governance Backup roles alternate within the Core Facilitator on an internal rotation schedule.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Core Facilitator) and an alternating rotation, but gives no cadence, order, or duration. The schedule is "internal" and undefined in the text, so a defender could argue any rotation complies.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or artifact-review mechanism targets whether the Governance Point and Backup roles rotate; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Responsibilities For Governance Point
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point has the following responsibilities in the Executive process:

- Gather the proposed content for the Executive sheet and prepare a draft of the Executive Vote.
- Align on Executive Vote contents with the relevant teams, and coordinate technical details.
- Ensure the contents of each Executive Vote are justified by processes or structures ratified by Sky Governance.
- Produce the text (Executive Document) that accompanies each Executive Vote and verify that the delivered code matches the code reviewed and approved on GitHub and that it contains all expected actions from the sheet.
- Publish the Executive Vote on the official Voting Portal.
assessments.description: Assigns the Governance Point duties for preparing, verifying, and publishing Executive Votes and Executive Documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates concrete steps, and the code-match check (delivered code equals GitHub-reviewed code and contains all sheet actions) is objectively verifiable. However, there are no deadlines or cadence, and duties such as aligning with relevant teams and ensuring justification by ratified processes are judgment-based.
metrics: Delivered Executive Vote code matches the code reviewed and approved on GitHub
Delivered code contains all expected actions from the Executive sheet
Executive Vote published on the official Voting Portal
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found: no penalty, conservatorship, or artifact review directly reaches this rule. Emergency Spells could theoretically halt a malicious or mismatched spell, but that is a protocol safeguard, not a consequence attached to the Governance Point's compliance, and the rest of the rule falls only under the catch-all misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Technical Point
assessments.quote:
The Technical Point role is filled by the Spell Team or the Spell Crafter from that group. For each Executive Vote, a Spell Team is selected from the Spell Roster to steward the Spell development process.

Within the Spell Team, the Spell Crafter serves as the primary point of contact for the Governance Point and any external parties. If the Spell Crafter is unavailable or if disagreements arise, the Governance Point’s secondary point of contact is the Spell Reviewers.

Input or opinions from external parties on technical details should be treated as informational and should not influence the Spell decision-making process.
assessments.description: Assigns the Technical Point role to Spell Team members, sets contact escalation to Spell Reviewers, and treats external technical input as informational.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are named (Technical Point, Spell Team, Spell Crafter, Spell Reviewers) and selection occurs per Executive Vote, but triggers such as 'unavailable' and 'disagreements' are undefined and the standard 'should not influence' is judgment-based with no verifiable test.
metrics: Spell Team selected for each Executive Vote
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or artifact-review mechanism is shown to reach role assignment, escalation, or the handling of external input; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could apply.

assessments.title: Spell Team Configuration
assessments.quote:
The Spell Team consists of the Crafter(s) and Reviewers for a designated Spell.

Currently, Sky has two teams of technical contributors for Spell development, Dewiz, and Sidestream. They rotate the responsibility of crafting and reviewing as follows:

- When Dewiz is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Dewiz member
    - Reviewing: one Dewiz member, one Sidestream member
- When Sidestream is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Sidestream member
    - Reviewing: one Sidestream member, one Dewiz member.
assessments.description: Defines Spell Team composition and the Dewiz/Sidestream rotation of crafting and reviewing roles for Spells.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Crafter and reviewer counts per Spell are stated exactly (one crafter, two reviewers, one from each team) with an explicit alternating rotation. Team membership is not defined beyond the two team names, and there is no verification cadence or record-keeping requirement.
metrics: Crafting: one member of the designated crafting team
Reviewing: two reviewers, one from each team (Dewiz and Sidestream)
Roles rotate between Dewiz and Sidestream depending on which team is crafting
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule is a process control with no stated consequence for a missing reviewer or wrong team composition. Its only reviewers are teammates, which is self-enforcement, and no catalogued mechanism (penalty, artifact review, emergency spell) is clearly triggered by a violation of team composition.

assessments.title: Shadow Delegates
assessments.quote: Shadow Delegates serve as alternative representatives for SKY holders who delegate their tokens. They are not officially recorded in the Atlas and do not receive any compensation from Sky. They may participate in governance decisions and vote on behalf of their delegators.
assessments.description: Describes Shadow Delegates as unrecorded, uncompensated alternative representatives who may vote for SKY holders who delegate to them.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines the role with concrete attributes (not recorded in the Atlas, no compensation, may vote on delegators' behalf), but states no thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions. It is a role description rather than a quantified obligation, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no penalty, escalation, or on-chain constraint on Shadow Delegate voting or on the delegation relationship, and no cited mechanism reaches it beyond the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops.

assessments.title: Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Prime Agents (see [A.0.1.1.42 - Prime Agent](a8454271-c090-4084-b022-4430e3def93c)) participate in the Executive Process by submitting their spell items for inclusion in the Executive Vote. A Prime Agent's spell items are the onchain changes that require a Spell to execute. These spell items are advanced through the Prime Spell Process, which is coordinated by the Executive Process Liaison (see [A.1.10.2.1.13 - Executive Process Liaison](abd8ac0d-1265-4a71-aaea-2fff6670eac5)) and scoped by the Strategic Team (see [A.1.10.2.1.14 - Strategic Team](f5decc3b-f22e-4ee8-a55d-d14eed218916)).
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit spell items via the Prime Spell Process for Executive Vote inclusion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real submission obligation and named actors (Prime Agent, Executive Process Liaison, Strategic Team) are present, but there are no thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria for what a compliant submission looks like. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a role description with no consequence for failing to submit spell items, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, artifact review) is tied to this submission duty. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop would reach it.

assessments.title: Recurring Items
assessments.quote: For each Executive Vote, the parameters listed in the subdocuments herein are always specified. It is the Spell Crafter who is responsible for identifying if the proposed contents of the Spell require the parameters to be set to "Yes" or "No".
assessments.description: Requires every Executive Vote to specify the listed parameters as Yes or No, with the Spell Crafter determining each value.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Spell Crafter) and a binary output (Yes/No), but the parameter set is delegated to unnamed subdocuments and the Spell Crafter's determination rests on judgment ('identifying if the proposed contents require'). No thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria appear in the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain control is tied to this rule, and the duty is self-policed by the Spell Crafter; the catch-all misalignment reporting alone does not raise it above weak.

assessments.title: Office Hours
assessments.quote:
Office hours are set to "Yes" if a Spell introduces major changes that can affect external parties, or if a stakeholder makes a specific request for the office-hours modifier to be switched on. Typical examples include collateral offboarding, onboarding new modules, oracle changes, and other actions that may have a significant impact on the protocol or its users.

While stakeholders can request that Office Hours be switched on, the final decision and responsibility for setting this parameter rests with the Spell Crafter. If the office hours modifier is on, the Spell can only be executed between 14:00 and 21:00 UTC, Monday - Friday. The purpose of this modifier is to ensure that Ecosystem Actors are available to address any issues that may arise during or shortly after the execution of the Spell. The Spell will have an extra restriction on top of the GSM Pause Delay, meaning it can only be cast during that timeframe, regardless of when it was approved.
assessments.description: Sets when a Spell may be cast: only 14:00–21:00 UTC Monday–Friday when the office-hours modifier is on, triggered by major changes or stakeholder request.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The execution window (14:00–21:00 UTC, Monday–Friday) and the named decision-maker (Spell Crafter) are concrete and checkable. The trigger for switching the modifier on relies on qualitative terms like "major changes" and "significant impact" with no defined criteria.
metrics: Spell execution window: 14:00–21:00 UTC
Execution days: Monday–Friday
Office-hours modifier set to "Yes" for major changes that can affect external parties or on stakeholder request
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The window is plausibly enforced by the Spell's on-chain casting check, but no citable mechanism UUID in the catalog or paragraph covers it. The trigger decision rests on the Spell Crafter's self-judgment, which is self-enforcement and therefore weak.

assessments.title: Global Line Modifier
assessments.quote: The Global Line Modifier, also referred to as the Global Debt Ceiling, defines the system-wide debt ceiling for Sky. It is set to "Yes" if there is a modification to any collateral type’s line that necessitates that the global Line is also modified.
assessments.description: Defines the Global Line Modifier flag, set to Yes when a collateral line change requires the system-wide debt ceiling to change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a binary Yes/No flag, but the trigger ('necessitates that the global Line is also modified') is a judgment call with no formula or threshold. No magnitudes, cadence, or defined actor are given.
metrics: Global Line Modifier set to "Yes" when a collateral-type line modification necessitates a global Line modification
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a definitional flag for an Executive Vote recurring item, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, liquidation, emergency spell, or review) reaches the accuracy of setting this flag. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Order Of Operations
assessments.quote: The Order of Operations parameter is relevant when actions within a Spell, or across multiple Spells, must be executed in a specific order to ensure that the correct final value is set. This applies to cases where dependencies, conflicting changes, or timing-sensitive modifications require precise sequencing to achieve the intended outcome. The Order of Operations parameter is set to "Yes" when actions must be executed in a specific order.
assessments.description: Defines a Yes/No Order of Operations parameter, set to Yes when Spell actions must execute in a specific sequence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter is binary and named, but whether sequencing is 'required' turns on judgment terms like dependencies, conflicting changes, and timing-sensitive modifications, with no criteria or measurable test. A defender could plausibly argue either that the flag was set correctly or that the trigger is too loose to apply.
metrics: Order of Operations parameter is set to "Yes" when actions must be executed in a specific order
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph is a disclosure flag inside the executive vote content, and no enforcement mechanism in the catalog or the text watches whether the flag is set correctly or whether sequencing is actually respected.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Deployment Verification
assessments.quote: For deployments of new modules such as an Allocation System Invocation or SP-BEAM, or to replace an old module, the process outlined in the subdocuments must be followed. The subdocuments provide additional detail regarding the smart contract deployment verification for each step in the Executive Process, where relevant. Unless otherwise stated, the normal process set out in [A.1.10.2.4 - Executive Process Breakdown](98298ab3-8d08-4c4f-b47b-81242a3e3903) applies.
assessments.description: Requires new or replacement smart-contract modules to follow the subdocument deployment verification process and the normal Executive Process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to follow a verification process is clear, but the paragraph itself states no thresholds, metrics, or deadlines and defers all operative detail to subdocuments not in the text. A defender could argue it does not yet bind anything concrete.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a module deployed without verification. The paragraph sets no specific consequence for skipping the verification steps, so the mechanism is only plausibly applicable.

assessments.title: Preparatory Phase for Module Deployment
assessments.quote: Before the Executive Process begins, the module is implemented, tested, audited as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6), and reviewed by relevant stakeholders to ensure readiness for inclusion. The subdocuments describe the crafting of an Atlas Edit Proposal for a technical deployment.
assessments.description: Requires modules to be implemented, tested, audited, and stakeholder-reviewed before the Executive Process begins.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule sets a clear sequencing gate and names an audit process by cross-reference, but 'tested' and 'reviewed by relevant stakeholders to ensure readiness' have no defined criteria, scope, or sign-off. A defender could plausibly argue a module is ready without meeting any measurable standard.
metrics: Module must be completed (implemented, tested, audited, stakeholder-reviewed) before the Executive Process begins

assessments.title: Requirements For Forum Post

assessments.description: Specifies the required contents of a Forum post that accompanies an executive vote proposing a deployed module.

However, it gives no deadlines or cadence, and key criteria are delegated or loose, such as constructor arguments being "as expected in the Init script" and "such as" lists.

assessments.title: Populating Content Regarding Module Deployment In Executive Votes
assessments.quote: The actions specified herein take place as part of the [A.1.10.2.4.2 - Governance Point Creates Executive Sheet Week 1 Monday (Step 2)](298819fe-cc26-49a8-a7cb-3ff83e55f291) step of the Executive Process.

assessments.title: Governance Point Includes Module Deployment In The Executive Sheet

assessments.description: Requires module deployments to appear in the Executive Sheet with linked Input and Derived Actions and their reasoning and authority URLs.

assessments.description: Places module deployment content into the executive document at Step 8 of the Executive Process.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Includes Module Deployment In The Executive Document
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator must include the module deployment in the Executive Document. The format for this content should be as specified below:
