assessments.title: Prime Spells
assessments.quote: This process will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: States that the Prime Spells process will be specified in a future Atlas iteration, with no operative requirement today.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The entire paragraph is an explicit stub deferring the process to a future iteration; there are no thresholds, actors, or verifiable conditions. Nothing currently binds any party.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph contains no operative obligation, and no mechanism in the catalog reaches a rule that does not yet exist; only the catch-all misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Purpose
assessments.quote: Prime Spell Security Enforcement establishes binding enforcement and formal recordkeeping for Prime Agent Spell security during the period when the Prime Spell Security Framework is progressively codified and operationalized in the Atlas. Its objective is to protect the Executive Process by ensuring that Prime Agents adhere to all applicable security requirements.
assessments.description: States the purpose of enforcing Prime Agent spell security requirements during the Prime Spell Security Framework's codification period.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a purpose statement with no thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or verifiable conditions. It promises 'binding enforcement and formal recordkeeping' without describing either.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no penalty, escalation, or enforcer, and no mechanism doc is cited in its text. Only the generic misalignment backstop could plausibly apply.

assessments.title: Obligation To Comply With Prime Spell Security Guidelines
assessments.quote: Prime Agents must adhere to all Prime Spell Security Guidelines as a condition of inclusion in an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to adhere to all Prime Spell Security Guidelines as a condition of inclusion in an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and the actor (Prime Agents) is defined, but the operative content is delegated to an external set of guidelines not stated in the text. No threshold, metric, or cadence is given, so a defender could argue that nothing specific binds them.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize interventions when security rules are violated or threatened, and Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry raises a Prime's insurance fees for poor security practice. Both plausibly reach guideline violations, but neither consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and the executive-vote inclusion gate is not itself a penalty.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Security Incidents
assessments.quote: Any breach by a Prime Agent of the Prime Spell Security Guidelines is designated a "Prime Spell Security Incident".
assessments.description: Designates any Prime Agent breach of the Prime Spell Security Guidelines as a Prime Spell Security Incident.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines an incident category by reference to the Prime Spell Security Guidelines, which are not specified here, and it gives no threshold, severity level, or deadline. Compliance turns on what the external guidelines require, so the operative rule is only partly verifiable from this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Labeling a breach an incident plausibly routes it into the Risk-Capital Incident Response framework, which allows penalties up to conservatorship. The Prime Spell Security Registry also prices insurance higher for poor security practice, which is a priced incentive reaching this rule. Neither mechanism quantifies a consequence specific to this designation, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Determination Of Occurrence Of Prime Spell Security Incident And Penalties
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps, in consultation with other appropriate stakeholders, have full discretion to determine whether a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred and to impose appropriate penalties.
assessments.description: Gives Core Facilitator and Core GovOps full discretion to determine Prime Spell Security Incidents and impose penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names defined actors and a real determination-and-penalty process, but it sets no criteria for what constitutes an incident and no penalty magnitudes, cadence, or deadlines. The phrase "full discretion" makes compliance arguable on any given facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph itself empowers a named enforcer distinct from the Prime to impose penalties, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Risk-Based Pricing of insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) plausibly reach for security incidents. The consequence is unquantified for this rule and no escalation path is defined, so it does not reach strong.

assessments.title: Penalties
assessments.description: Lists non-exhaustive penalty types that may be imposed on a Prime for a Prime Spell Security Incident.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names enumerated penalty categories (financial, queue deprioritization, vote exclusion, extra audits, support reduction) but gives no magnitudes, triggers, or decision criteria. The permissive phrasing "may include, without limitation" leaves whether any penalty applies largely to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) provide quantified financial penalties that could reach Prime security incidents, and Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) makes poor security practice raise insurance fees. However, the paragraph says penalties "may" be imposed, and no specific consequence is quantified for this rule, so escalation depends on discretion.

assessments.title: Prime Agent And Operational Executor Agent Produce Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.quote: After a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred, the Prime and its Operational Executor Agent must promptly produce a Prime Spell Security Incident Report using the designated template.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime and its Operational Executor Agent to promptly file a Prime Spell Security Incident Report after an incident.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and identifiable, but 'promptly' has no deadline or hour/day count, and the 'designated template' is not named or defined in the paragraph. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Capital Incident Response framework covers Prime incidents and lets Sky Core impose penalties up to conservatorship, which plausibly reaches a failure to report. The paragraph does not state any consequence for late or missing reports, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Delay In Submitting Or Failure To Thoroughly And Accurately Complete Report
assessments.quote: Unreasonable delay in submitting the Report, or failure to thoroughly and accurately complete it (including omission of relevant facts), as determined by the Core Council, constitutes a separate Prime Spell Security Incident and may result in additional penalties.
assessments.description: Makes unreasonable delay or incomplete, inaccurate Prime Spell Security Reports a separate security incident that may draw additional penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real, but 'unreasonable', 'thoroughly and accurately', and 'relevant facts' are judgment terms with no deadline or measurable standard. The Core Council's determination and the 'may result in additional penalties' language leave both the violation and the consequence open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Council, distinct from the Prime, classifies the late or deficient report as a Prime Spell Security Incident, which engages the Risk-Capital Incident Response framework and its penalties up to conservatorship. The penalty is discretionary and unquantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on the Council making that determination.

assessments.title: Core Spell Teams Review Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.quote: The relevant Core Spell Team, on behalf of the Core Council, must review this Incident Report for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.description: Requires the relevant Core Spell Team, for the Core Council, to review a Prime Spell Security Incident Report for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation names a defined actor (the relevant Core Spell Team) and a specific document, but "completeness and accuracy" has no criteria, deadline, or cadence. A reviewer could argue any cursory check satisfies the rule, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship apply to Primes and Operational Agents rather than to a Core Spell Team's review duty, and the Agent Artifact Review covers agents, not this review step. Only the Reports of Misalignment catch-all and self-policing by the team remain, which are weak.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Records Prime Spell Security Incident Report In Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.quote: All Prime Spell Security Incidents must be recorded by the Core Facilitator in the Incident Registry at [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f). Each Registry entry must identify the Prime Agent and its Operational Executor Agent, the incident date(s), a short description of the violation, the penalties imposed, and a link to the corresponding Prime Spell Security Incident Report.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to record every Prime Spell Security Incident in the Incident Registry with specified identifying and descriptive fields.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The required fields are enumerated and checkable, and the scope is 'All' incidents. However, there is no recording deadline or cadence, and the 'short description' requirement is qualitative.
metrics: Scope: all Prime Spell Security Incidents recorded in the Incident Registry
Each entry identifies the Prime Agent and its Operational Executor Agent
Each entry includes incident date(s)
Each entry includes a short description of the violation
Each entry includes the penalties imposed
Each entry links to the corresponding Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The registry feeds Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance (fd1f682c), so recorded security incidents raise a Prime's insurance fees, which gives the recording a priced consequence. Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach the penalties field, but no escalation is defined to ensure the Core Facilitator actually records incidents, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Prime Agent Credit Rating System
assessments.quote: The Registry shall serve as a critical input to the Prime Agent Credit Rating system and will determine Primes’ Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate when variable pricing is activated pursuant to [A.3.1.2.5.1 - Relationship To Base Rate](4659cbf0-78c2-469b-8432-883e5c931dd1).
assessments.description: Makes the Prime Spell Security Registry a critical input that sets Primes' Agent Credit Line borrow rate when variable pricing is active.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph assigns the Registry a determinative role in setting borrow rates, but gives no formula, weighting, or rate value. The operative rate logic is delegated to the cross-referenced A.3.1.2.5.1, and 'critical input' and 'when variable pricing is activated' leave compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Registry-driven rate setting is a priced incentive: poor security posture is expected to raise a Prime's borrowing cost, matching the Risk-Based Pricing mechanism. The consequence size is unquantified in this paragraph and depends on the referenced rate section, so it stays at mid.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance
assessments.quote: Insurance‑related fees charged by a Prime’s Operational Executor shall also be calculated using risk‑based pricing informed by the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry, including the severity, frequency, and recency of incidents.
assessments.description: Requires Prime insurance fees to be risk-priced using the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry's severity, frequency, and recency data.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete inputs (severity, frequency, recency) and the registry, but gives no formula, weighting, fee bounds, or update cadence. Compliance cannot be verified from the text alone.
metrics: Inputs: incident severity, incident frequency, incident recency from the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance mechanism (fd1f682c) is the rule itself as a priced incentive: poor security records raise a Prime's insurance fees. The rating is mid rather than strong because the fee magnitude for this rule is unquantified.

assessments.title: Review Of Prime Spell Security Registry By Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are expected to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry on an ongoing basis and to independently incorporate mitigations and controls based on relevant prior incidents into their Spell-development related processes.
assessments.description: Expects Prime Agents to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry ongoing and incorporate relevant incident mitigations into Spell development.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real but expressed in judgment language: "expected to review", "on an ongoing basis", and "independently incorporate" with no cadence, threshold, or verifiable measure of what counts as incorporation. A Prime could plausibly argue it complied with any reasonable review.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can assess whether a Prime's Spell-development processes reflect registry mitigations, with penalty assessment, though no consequence is quantified for this rule. Risk-Based Pricing of insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) gives a priced incentive for weak security practice, but it does not directly target failure to review the registry.

assessments.title: Escalated Penalties For Similar Prime Spell Security Incidents
assessments.quote: Where a new Prime Spell Security Incident reflects the same or a substantially similar circumstance as a previous Incident in the Registry, the new Incident shall be subject to an escalation multiplier applied to its financial penalty, as determined by the Core Council. This applies regardless of whether the earlier Incident involved the same Prime.
assessments.description: Requires escalating financial penalties for Prime Spell Security Incidents that repeat a substantially similar earlier Incident in the Registry, regardless of Prime.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an escalation multiplier applied to the financial penalty, but gives no value, formula, or bounds, and delegates the magnitude to the Core Council. 'Substantially similar' is undefined judgment language, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Escalation multiplier applied to the financial penalty for a new Incident matching a previous Registry Incident (value set by Core Council, not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) are the quantified financial penalty machinery this rule multiplies, and Risk-Based Insurance Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) prices repeated incidents. However, the multiplier itself is unquantified and depends on Core Council determination, so the escalation does not automatically fire.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.quote:
Prime Spell Security Incidents are recorded as Active Data in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Process Breakdown
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define the Prime Spell Process, the end-to-end procedure through which Prime Agents bring proposed actions through governance and into Sky Core Spells for on-chain execution. The Prime Spell Process spans four (4) weeks, from initial proposal through publication of the Sky Core Spell that includes the Prime Spell payload.

Two governance paths are accommodated. The Sky Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is not yet operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the Sky Core Atlas Edit Proposal process as specified in [A.2.2.6.2.3.2 - Atlas Edit Proposal Process For Prime Agents](364e52eb-4529-46a9-9852-edaaab88baeb). The Independent Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the voting process defined in the Prime Agent's [A.2.2.6.2 - Root Edit Primitive](78488c6b-d77f-4344-b954-476e415a2c7d). Any divergences between the governance paths are specified in the relevant sections.

The Prime Spell Process is organized into four (4) phases, one per week, specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the four-week, four-phase Prime Spell Process and the two governance paths by which Prime Agents ratify spell content.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The overall duration (four weeks) and phase count (four, one per week) are stated, which are concrete parameters. However, the phase contents are delegated to subdocuments, and divergences between the Sky Governance and Independent Governance paths are deferred to unspecified 'relevant sections'.
metrics: Prime Spell Process spans four (4) weeks, from initial proposal through publication of the Sky Core Spell
Organized into four (4) phases, one per week
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a process overview with no compliance obligation or consequence attached to the four-week timeline; no penalty, emergency, or on-chain mechanism reaches it, leaving only the catch-all misalignment backstop.

assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent's proposed Prime Spell content to be submitted, prioritized, and approved during week 0 of the process.

assessments.quote: The Prime Agent submits a Prime Spell Form to the Executive Process Liaison by Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 0. The Prime Spell Form initiates the Prime Spell Process for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle and specifies the proposed Prime Spell content. The Prime Agent must include the complexity score calculation for the proposed Prime Spell content in the Prime Spell Form. Items that introduce new code must have a completed audit as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) before submission.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to submit a Prime Spell Form by a set deadline, with a complexity score and completed audits for new code.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The submission deadline (Monday 16:00 UTC, week 0) is exact and verifiable. The complexity score calculation is required but its method is not defined here, and the audit requirement depends on a separate section and an undefined 'introduces new code' test.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Publishes Spell Actions On Sky Forum
assessments.quote:
Each proposed Prime Spell action must be included in a Forum post on the Sky Forum. Each Forum post must contain the Technical Scope, as specified in [A.1.10.2.5.2.1 - Technical Scope Template](b9ba6658-87a9-4421-9d20-386df8cea450), the Financial Risk Assessment, and, if relevant, a Technical Risk Assessment.

assessments.description: Requires financial risk assessment of Prime Agent Forum items, by Core Council Risk Advisor or a designated independent assessor, with a Thursday 16:00 UTC deadline.

assessments.title: Execution Of Agent Spells
assessments.quote: The execution of Agent Spells is described in the subdocuments herein. Two methods are available: direct execution in a Sky Core Spell and execution through StarGuard. Execution through StarGuard is the preferred method and any exceptions require valid reasoning.
assessments.description: Sets StarGuard as the preferred route for executing Agent Spells, with direct Sky Core execution allowed only on justified exceptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names two execution methods and a preference for StarGuard, but defers the operative detail to subdocuments. The exception standard, 'valid reasoning', is undefined and judgment-based, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could review how Agent Spells were executed and assess penalties, reaching a direct-execution violation. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and no automatic enforcement applies.

assessments.title: Execution Through StarGuard
assessments.quote: When the execution through the StarGuard method is used, the Agent Spells are whitelisted in Sky Core Spells and later executed using the StarGuard contract. The Sky Core Spell includes a whitelist of approved Agent Spells, which allows them to be executed via separate transactions. This enhances resilience and scalability, ensuring robust handling of payloads from multiple active Agents while minimizing risks to Sky Core.
assessments.description: Describes execution of Agent Spells via the StarGuard contract, using a whitelist approved within Sky Core Spells.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete mechanism (a whitelist in Sky Core Spells executed through the StarGuard contract) but gives no criteria for when the method applies, no whitelist contents or limits, and no measurable outcome. The 'enhances resilience' and 'robust handling' language is judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The whitelist is a structural control, but no citable mechanism doc attaches a defined consequence to a violation, and the catalog's catch-all and unrelated mechanisms do not reach this rule. None found.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The steps are concrete: named contracts, a single-Spell timing condition, and a named keeper job. However, the operative word is 'should' rather than 'must', and 'initialized' is undefined, so a defender could argue the rule does not bind.

assessments.title: StarGuard Functionality
assessments.quote: When initiated in a Sky Core Spell, the StarGuard whitelists relevant Agent Spells, enabling their secure execution. This whitelisting allows Agent Spells to run independently, supporting arbitrary complexity and custom features like office hours or expiration times. StarGuard also supports dropping a whitelisted Agent Spell, providing a mechanism to revoke access if needed for security or error correction. This is done via the `drop()` function.
assessments.description: Describes StarGuard whitelisting Agent Spells from Sky Core Spells and revoking them via drop().
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete control (whitelisting in a Sky Core Spell, the drop() function) and actors, but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria; revocation is only "if needed for security or error correction," which is judgment language. Whether it imposes a binding obligation is arguable, since it reads as a functional description.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes a capability and no consequence attaches to misuse or failure to revoke. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) cover pre-authorized interventions, but the text does not tie StarGuard whitelisting or drop() to that path, and the catch-all mechanisms alone would still be weak.

assessments.title: Responsibilities For Agents
assessments.quote: The Agents are required to include logic for the public view method `isExecutable()` in their Spell. This function is used to signal if the Spell is ready to be executed in a particular block or not. StarGuard cannot execute an Agent Spell if `isExecutable()` returns `False`. The value that must be returned for execution to be possible is `True`.
assessments.description: Requires Agent Spells to implement a public isExecutable() method returning True, which StarGuard checks before execution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The method name and the required return value (True) are exact and verifiable, and StarGuard's execution gate is stated. The rule leaves the internal logic that determines readiness undefined, so a defender could argue the substantive criteria are unspecified.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach an unauthorized whitelisting attempt. assessments.title: StarGuard Max Delay
assessments.quote: A configurable `maxDelay` sets the maximum duration between the whitelisting of the Agent Spell in the Sky Core Spell and the execution of the Agent Spell. This feature ensures Spells do not linger indefinitely, enforcing timely processing and reducing risks from delayed or forgotten actions. The recommended value for `maxDelay` is seven (7) days.
assessments.description: Defines a configurable maxDelay limiting the time between whitelisting and execution of an Agent Spell, recommended at seven days.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete configurable parameter (maxDelay) and a specific value (seven days), but the value is only 'recommended', so it is not a binding threshold. A defender could argue the parameter is advisory and does not yet bind compliance.

assessments.title: Requirements For Whitelisting
assessments.quote:
The requirements for whitelisting are:

- The address of the Agent Spell.
- The codehash of the Spell's bytecode.
- Confirmation that direct execution is not needed. If direct execution is needed, a valid reason must be provided.

This information must be provided by the Agent Spell reviewers to the Governance Point.

However, it sets no deadline or cadence, and the standard for a 'valid reason' for direct execution is undefined and left to judgment.
metrics: Provide the address of the Agent Spell

The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) may also apply to Agents, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Permissionless Execution
assessments.quote: The triggering of an Agent Spell is permissionless; anyone can initiate execution. A keeper job, StarGuardJob, allows keepers to monitor and execute eligible Spells at the earliest possible block.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes an open execution mechanism rather than an actor obligation, and no listed mechanism penalizes failure to trigger or execute promptly; Emergency Spells could pause a Spell but do not enforce permissionless execution.

assessments.title: Function Call For Execution
assessments.quote: Execution is initiated on the StarGuard contract via its `exec()` function, which performs necessary validation checks before calling the SubProxy’s `exec(spellDataCopy.addr, abi.encodePacked(StarSpellLike.execute.selector))` to perform the Spell's actions.
assessments.description: Specifies that spell execution is initiated via StarGuard's exec() after validation checks, which then calls SubProxy to run the spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete contracts, functions, and the exact SubProxy call signature, so the execution path is identifiable. However, the "necessary validation checks" are never enumerated or given criteria, so a third party cannot verify what gating occurs before execution.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The StarGuard validation step is on-chain, but the paragraph does not name a consequence for skipping or failing checks, and no catalogued mechanism UUID reaches this execution-mechanics rule. Enforcement found: none.

assessments.title: Validation Checks By StarGuard
assessments.quote:
The following checks are enabled by the contract:

- Verifies that the whitelisted Spell is executable only once, enforcing single-use to prevent replay attacks or unauthorized repeats.
- Verifies that the whitelisted bytecode codehash is valid, protecting against tampering or malicious alterations.
- Verifies that the Spell meets custom requirements (e.g., office hours) by confirming the `spell.isExecutable()` view function returns true.
- Verifies that StarGuard retains access to the SubProxy, ensuring no loss of control during the Agent Spell execution.
assessments.description: Lists contract-enabled StarGuard checks on whitelisted Spells: single-use execution, codehash validity, isExecutable gating, and retained SubProxy access.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each check is a binary, contract-verifiable condition (single execution, isExecutable() returns true, StarGuard retains SubProxy access). Gaps remain: "valid" codehash is not defined against a stated whitelist process, and "custom requirements (e.g., office hours)" is open-ended.
metrics: Whitelisted Spell is executable only once (single-use)
Whitelisted bytecode codehash is valid
spell.isExecutable() view function returns true
StarGuard retains access to the SubProxy during Agent Spell execution
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The checks are enforced by the StarGuard contract itself, which is strong in principle, but the contract is not in the catalog and no catalog or in-text mechanism UUID is cited; none found that is citable, so the rating defaults to weak.

assessments.title: Direct Execution Through Sky Core Spell
assessments.quote: When the execution through the Sky Core Spell method is used, the Agent Spells are executed directly in the Sky Core Spells.
assessments.description: Specifies that when execution through the Sky Core Spell method is used, Agent Spells run directly inside Sky Core Spells.

assessments.title: Sky Core Spell Executes Agent Spell
assessments.quote: Execution of an Agent Spell is initiated by the Sky Core Spell, which directly calls `exec()` on the Agent's SubProxy contract to perform the Spell’s actions in the same transaction. The SubProxy limits rights to the specific Agent, preventing access to Sky Core contracts. The current SubProxy contract is designed to execute the Agent Spell in the same transaction as the Sky Core Spell.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actors (Sky Core Spell, Agent SubProxy), the exact call (exec()), and a single-transaction execution requirement, all verifiable against contract code. The closing sentence hedges with "designed to," which leaves the obligation partly descriptive rather than a binding requirement.
metrics: Agent Spell execution occurs in the same transaction as the Sky Core Spell
SubProxy rights limited to the specific Agent; no access to Sky Core contracts
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SubProxy's rights restriction is contract-level isolation, but no catalog mechanism doc or UUID in the paragraph is tied to this rule, so none can be cited. Enforcement is therefore none found.

assessments.title: Novel Items
assessments.quote: Some onchain changes are considered novel and require specialized processes outside the regular Spell cadence, including a technical feasibility and implementation proposal phase prior to including the item in the Executive Vote process. The process for novel Spell items for Executive Votes is specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: States that some onchain changes are novel and need a specialized process, including a feasibility phase, before Executive Vote inclusion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real obligation, a technical feasibility and implementation proposal phase before Executive Vote inclusion, but gives no criteria for what makes a change novel and no timing or thresholds. It defers the operative process to subdocuments, so compliance is arguable from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph itself names no enforcement path, and no catalogued mechanism directly reaches the novel-item process; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Definition Of Novel Spell Item
assessments.quote: An item is considered novel if the request cannot use any of the code patterns already available in the `spell-mainnet` archive folder used on prior Spells.
assessments.description: Defines a Novel Spell Item as any executive item whose request cannot be satisfied by code patterns already in the spell-mainnet archive.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The definition names a concrete test (whether existing code patterns in the spell-mainnet archive can satisfy the request), so it is operative and checkable in principle. However, it does not specify how 'cannot use' is determined, who decides, or how pattern matching is evaluated, leaving the classification to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a definitional paragraph; no enforcement mechanism attaches to classifying an item as novel. The consequences of novelty (e.g., additional scrutiny in the Executive Vote) are defined elsewhere and are not reached by this text, so none found.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Or Core Facilitator Requests Inclusion Of Novel Item
assessments.quote: The process begins when a stakeholder's needs require an item that Core GovOps believes is novel in an upcoming Spell. Core GovOps submits a request to the Core Facilitator for inclusion of the item. The Core Facilitator also has the authority to independently request inclusion of a novel item.
assessments.description: Describes how Core GovOps or the Core Facilitator requests inclusion of a novel item in an upcoming Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and a sequence of steps are named: Core GovOps submits a request to the Core Facilitator, who may also request independently. Whether an item is novel depends on Core GovOps' belief, with no criteria, timing, or deadline.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sets no consequence for failing to follow the request process, and no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, emergency spells, artifact review) reaches a violation of it. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Confirms Whether Requested Item Is Novel
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Spell Teams, determines whether the requested item is novel. If the item is not considered novel, it is scheduled via the regular Spell process as specified in [A.1.10.2.4 - Executive Process Breakdown](98298ab3-8d08-4c4f-b47b-81242a3e3903). If the item is classified as novel, the Core Facilitator notifies the Core Spell Teams of this determination in the govops channel in Slack.
assessments.description: Core Facilitator classifies requested items as novel or not, routing each to the regular spell process or Slack notification.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actors and two outcome branches, but gives no criteria for what makes an item novel and no deadline or cadence for the determination or notification. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator classifies its own requests with only Core Spell Teams notified, which is self-enforcement. No penalty, escalation, or artifact review reaches this classification, leaving only the misalignment catch-all.

assessments.title: Core Spell Teams Conduct A Technical Feasibility Analysis And Develop An Implementation Proposal
assessments.quote: The Core Spell Teams conduct a technical feasibility analysis and develop an implementation proposal for the novel Spell item. One Spell Team may take the lead, or both teams may work in parallel and reconcile approaches. Both Spell Teams must agree on the implementation proposal. The proposal may include external audits as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) or other processes. The Core Facilitator and relevant domain experts, including those with technical expertise related to the novel item, can provide input on the implementation proposal. The Spell Teams deliver the implementation proposal to the Core Facilitator.
assessments.description: Requires Core Spell Teams to jointly produce a feasibility analysis and implementation proposal for a novel Spell item and deliver it to the Core Facilitator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and a sequence are defined (both Spell Teams must agree, then deliver to the Core Facilitator), but there are no deadlines, feasibility criteria, or measurable outputs. Whether the analysis is adequate is left to judgment, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph references the Audit Process but that is a process, not an enforcement mechanism. No penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or on-chain mechanism reaches a failure to deliver or agree on the proposal, and only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Obtains Approval From Relevant Stakeholders And Schedules Novel Spell Item
assessments.quote: After receiving the implementation proposal, the Core Facilitator shares it with the relevant stakeholders whose needs originated the request. The Core Facilitator works with these stakeholders to confirm that the implementation proposal addresses the needs that motivated the novel Spell item. After doing so, the Core Facilitator schedules the novel Spell item into the regular Spell cadence as specified in [A.1.10.2.4 - Executive Process Breakdown](98298ab3-8d08-4c4f-b47b-81242a3e3903).
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to share novel Spell proposals with stakeholders, confirm they meet needs, and schedule them.

assessments.title: Obtain Consensus On Content
assessments.quote:
Based on the review of requested and planned content, the teams must reach a consensus on which items to include in the Spell. In some cases, the Spell Crafter may request the removal of certain items if the Spell is deemed high risk, too big or contains novel code. Such removals typically affect non-critical items, such as internal payments. Content being removed from the Executive Sheet is added to the Executive Vote queue to be included in the next Executive Vote cycle.

Onboarding of sensitive modules is considered increasing the Spell's complexity in such a manner that the Spell Reviewers should only focus on this; therefore, non-crucial items should be removed from the Executive Sheet and included in the Executive Vote queue.

Where consensus cannot be reached, the procedure specified in [A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3.1 - Core Facilitator Final Inclusion Decision](4cbe3ee7-a64f-4e44-8cf5-25a09a87e233) applies.
assessments.description: Sets how teams reach consensus on Spell contents, removing high-risk or non-critical items to the Executive Vote queue and deferring deadlocks to the Core Facilitator.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator deadlock procedure (4cbe3ee7) is a tie-break for inclusion decisions, not a consequence for breaching the consensus rule, and no penalty, freeze, or conservatorship path reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Final Inclusion Decision
assessments.quote:
Where consensus cannot be reached on whether to include an item in the Spell, the disagreement must be raised in the govops channel in Slack so that the Spell Teams, Core GovOps, the Core Facilitator, and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead have visibility into the disagreement and the reasoning behind it. The Core Facilitator must hear all positions and make the final decision on whether to include the item. The Core Facilitator's decision is binding for the Executive Vote in question.

Routine coordination among the Spell Teams in their own working channels is expected. A disagreement over whether to include an item must not, however, be resolved in a way that excludes the Core Facilitator or that settles the matter privately and reports only the outcome. The positions of each party, and the reasoning through which the disagreement is resolved, must be visible in the govops channel in Slack.

assessments.title: Provenance
assessments.quote:
All actions in the Executive Sheet require sufficient provenance for their inclusion in the sheet and later in the Executive Vote. The legitimacy of a provenance is assessed on the basis of its mutability, visibility and resistance to compromise by external malicious actors. There are different ways of providing sufficient provenance, including "strong comment type" provenance, "onchain" provenance and "strong document type" provenance. These types of provenance are defined in the subdocuments herein.

If Executive actions and items do not have sufficient provenance, for example, "weak comment type", they cannot be included in the Executive Vote. If the Governance Point has any question whether a proposed Executive action has sufficient provenance, they must resolve that question of validity before including that action in the Executive Process.
assessments.description: Requires Executive Sheet actions to have sufficient provenance, otherwise excluding them from the Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The sufficiency test rests on judgment criteria (mutability, visibility, resistance to compromise) with no thresholds, and the provenance types are defined in subdocuments outside this text. The Governance Point's duty to resolve doubts is also open-ended, so a defender could argue the rule does not yet bind in a determinate way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Exclusion from the Executive Vote is a procedural gate, but no cited mechanism reaches a violation such as a Governance Point including unsupported provenance. The duty to resolve doubts is self-enforced by the same actor, so none found.

assessments.title: Weak Comment Type Provenance
assessments.quote: The provenance type "weak comment type provenance" refers to informal or editable comments made by stakeholders, which lack the security and visibility needed for Executive actions. For example, Discord messages, forum posts, or unverified social media comments are considered weak comment provenance, even if they relate to an action affecting the commenter (e.g., confirming a payment). Weak comment types are highly mutable, as they can often be edited or deleted without a public trace, and may not be visible to all ecosystem participants (e.g., requiring platform-specific accounts or access to private channels). They also have low resistance to compromise, relying on accounts without strong security protocols, making them vulnerable to malicious edits or takeovers by bad actors. As such, weak comment provenance does not qualify as sufficient and must not be used to authorize Executive actions.
assessments.description: Defines weak comment provenance (informal, editable stakeholder comments) and prohibits its use to authorize Executive actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a binding prohibition and concrete examples (Discord messages, forum posts, unverified social media), but its classification criteria ("informal", "lack the security and visibility needed", "low resistance to compromise") are qualitative. A reviewer could disagree on borderline sources, so the scope is not fully objective.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can review Executive Sheet confirmations, issue staged findings, and assess penalties, which could reach a weak-provenance authorization. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on a scheduled review rather than an automatic check.

assessments.title: OnChain Provenance
assessments.quote: The provenance type "onchain provenance" is one of the most legitimate types of provenance. Onchain information refers to information obtained from Sky Protocol-associated smart contracts and is considered practically immutable and publicly visible. Due to the design of these decentralized storage providers such as IPFS, information referred to by on-chain values or content hashes but stored on IPFS or other similar services is also considered practically immutable. The compromise resistance of on-chain values is very strong and relies on a compromised controller of a Sky Protocol-associated smart contract or severe supply chain attack to manipulate information.
assessments.description: Defines onchain provenance as practically immutable information from Sky smart contracts and IPFS-referenced content.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a definitional posture statement with no thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or defined actor obligations. Its claims ('very strong', 'practically immutable') are qualitative and there is nothing a regulated party must do to comply.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph imposes no operative obligation, and no enforcement mechanism in the catalog or cited text reaches it; it only classifies a provenance type.

assessments.title: Governance Point Must Ensure The Executive Sheet Is Completed
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point is responsible for ensuring that the Executive Sheet is fully completed and accurate. This includes the following:

- That all fields in the Executive Sheet are filled in with the required information, including URLs, figures, and confirmations. For any incomplete items (e.g., awaiting final figures), they must be marked with a `TODO` tag.
- That all items included in the Executive Sheet were discussed and approved during the GovOps meeting.
    - No approved items from the discussions can be omitted without a valid reason.
- That the financial transfers are accurate.
    - USDS transfers must be rounded up to the nearest whole number (no decimal points).
    - SKY transfers must be listed to exactly two decimal places.
    - Verify that the checksum for USDS and SKY transfers is accurate.
- The Spell items must be listed in order of importance for an average SKY voter except when there are order of operations concerns.
