An audit is required before new smart contract code is introduced to the Sky Ecosystem, including:

- Smart contracts and module onboardings
- Deployment and initialization scripts required to deploy and configure smart contracts, which must comply with the structure and requirements defined in [A.1.10.2.7.1.1 - Deployment And Initialization Script Standards](5f6012ba-450b-4620-baad-e602ee3e69f7)

This requirement does not extend to other code, such as off-chain services or user interfaces, unless separately specified.
assessments.description: Requires an audit before new smart contract code, including module onboardings and deployment scripts, enters the Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to audit before introduction is clear and the scope is enumerated, but no auditor, audit standard, depth, or pass criterion is defined. A defender could argue any audit satisfies the rule, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: An audit must be completed before new smart contract code is introduced to the Sky Ecosystem
Scope includes smart contracts, module onboardings, and deployment and initialization scripts
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry can raise a Prime's insurance fees for poor security practice, which plausibly reaches deploying unaudited code. Emergency Spells can freeze or pause when security rules are violated or threatened, but no consequence is quantified specifically for the audit requirement.

assessments.title: Deployment And Initialization Script Structure
assessments.quote:
Deployment logic and initialization logic must be structured as follows:

- Deployment logic must be extracted into a Solidity library that accepts constructor arguments and deploys the contract.
- Initialization logic must be extracted into a Solidity library that performs post-deployment configuration, including granting roles and setting state.
- The deployment script must orchestrate the deployment by calling the deployment and initialization libraries.

Deployment and initialization logic must be combined into a single library unless there is reasonable justification for separation.
assessments.description: Requires deployment and initialization logic to be split into separate Solidity libraries, orchestrated by a deployment script, unless justified otherwise.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates concrete artifacts (deployment library, initialization library, orchestrating script) and actions, so structural compliance is checkable. However, the exception for 'reasonable justification' is undefined, and the closing sentence requiring combination conflicts with the separation bullets.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sits under an audit trigger context, but no audit consequence, penalty, or emergency response is tied to this structural requirement; only the generic Adjudication/Misalignment catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: General Requirements
assessments.quote:
The following requirements apply to all deployment and initialization scripts:

- Libraries must not contain hardcoded addresses. All addresses and configuration values must be passed as parameters.
- All library functions must be tested. Test coverage must target 100%. Exceptions to this requirement must have reasonable justification.

Deployment verification, including confirmation of address correctness and on-chain state, is not within the scope of an audit of deployment and initialization scripts and must be performed as a separate deployment verification review.
assessments.description: Requires deployment and initialization scripts to avoid hardcoded library addresses and reach 100% test coverage, excluding deployment verification.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 100% coverage figure and the ban on hardcoded addresses are concrete and checkable. However, coverage is only a "target", and exceptions need only "reasonable justification", which is a judgment standard with no defined review path.
metrics: Test coverage must target 100% for all library functions
Libraries must not contain hardcoded addresses
Exceptions to the 100% coverage requirement must have reasonable justification
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can review deployment and initialization script artifacts and assess penalties, so it plausibly reaches these requirements. The paragraph does not quantify any consequence for a violation, and firing depends on a review being scheduled.

assessments.title: Deployment Script Requirements
assessments.quote:
Deployment scripts must satisfy the following requirements:

- Deployment scripts must yield ownership of deployed contracts to the relevant Governance proxy. Exceptions to this requirement must have reasonable justification.
- Top-level deployment scripts must be included in the audit scope. Auditors must at minimum verify constructor parameters.
assessments.description: Requires deployment scripts to transfer contract ownership to the Governance proxy and include top-level scripts in audit scope with constructor checks.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ownership-transfer and audit-scope obligations are concrete and checkable, and constructor-parameter verification is a named minimum. However, the ownership requirement is waived by an undefined 'reasonable justification' exception, and no audit cadence or deadline is stated.
metrics: Deployed contracts' ownership must be yielded to the relevant Governance proxy
Exceptions must have reasonable justification (unquantified)
Top-level deployment scripts must be included in the audit scope
Auditors must at minimum verify constructor parameters
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review deployment artifacts and assess penalties, plausibly reaching scripts that omit ownership transfer or audit scope. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could freeze contracts if an unowned deployment is treated as a threatened security violation, but no consequence is quantified for this rule and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Initialization Script Requirements
assessments.quote:
Initialization scripts must satisfy the following requirements:

- The initialization library must be directly importable by a compliant Spell without modifications. The execution context of the library is expected to be the relevant Governance proxy.
- Every initialization function must be audited.
- Top-level initialization scripts that exist solely for test environments must not be included in the audit scope.
assessments.description: Requires initialization scripts to be importable without modification, all initialization functions audited, and test-only scripts excluded from audit scope.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete artifacts (initialization library, initialization functions, test-only top-level scripts) and sets universal requirements ('every', 'must not be included'). However, the audit standard, depth, and completion criteria are undefined, and 'solely for test environments' and 'without modifications' have no objective test.
metrics: Initialization library must be directly importable by a compliant Spell without modifications
Every initialization function must be audited
Top-level initialization scripts existing solely for test environments must not be included in the audit scope
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps provides scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment by a party distinct from the actor, which can plausibly reach a non-audited or non-importable initialization script. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on the review being triggered.

assessments.title: Audit Request And Intake
assessments.quote:
The team responsible for the code to be audited fills in a standardized audit intake form containing, at minimum:

- The scope of the audit, identifying the specific contracts, scripts, or artifacts to be reviewed
- The repository URL and exact commit hash of the code to be audited, which must have been reviewed as specified in [A.1.10.2.7.2.1 - Code Review Requirement](4bead31b-adee-4121-a966-d0e1c31f91e2)
- Any context the auditor needs to understand the purpose and integration of the audited code within the Sky Ecosystem

Core GovOps compiles the completed intake forms and submits them to the auditor. The audit request must be submitted with sufficient lead time for the auditor to complete the review before the target Spell or deployment date.
assessments.description: Requires code teams to submit a standardized audit intake form with scope, reviewed commit, and context, and sets a lead-time requirement before deployment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The intake form has three enumerated minimum fields and requires an exact commit hash, which is verifiable. The lead time is only "sufficient" for the auditor, with no numeric deadline, so the timing obligation is delegated and not measurable.
metrics: Intake form contains at minimum: audit scope identifying specific contracts, scripts, or artifacts
Intake form contains repository URL and exact commit hash, reviewed per A.1.10.2.7.2.1
Intake form contains context on purpose and integration within the Sky Ecosystem
Audit request submitted with sufficient lead time before target Spell or deployment date (no duration stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Skipping or under-scoping the audit request is a security-practice lapse that the Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) can plausibly price upward, and Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) could reach a late or incomplete submission. Neither names a penalty for this specific intake rule, so the consequence is unquantified.

assessments.title: Code Review Requirement
assessments.quote: The commit hash submitted for audit must correspond to a Pull Request that has been reviewed and approved by at least one (1) member of the team responsible for the code who is not an author of the Pull Request. Evidence of the review and approval must be available to Core GovOps as part of the audit request and intake process specified in [A.1.10.2.7.2 - Audit Request And Intake](fcc17c4e-b1cd-4e62-bb2b-0aea02ee72d5).
assessments.description: Requires that audited commit hashes correspond to a PR approved by at least one non-author team member, with evidence available to Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified (at least one non-author reviewer, approval required) and the actor is defined as the responsible team. It lacks a deadline for producing evidence and does not define 'team responsible for the code', so a reviewer could argue about scope.
metrics: At least one (1) reviewer who is not an author of the Pull Request
Pull Request must be reviewed and approved before the commit hash is submitted for audit
Review and approval evidence must be available to Core GovOps as part of audit intake
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry makes weak code-review practice raise insurance fees, a priced incentive that plausibly reaches this rule. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check the audit evidence and assess penalties, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Audit Execution And Report Delivery
assessments.quote:
The auditor performs the audit against the scope and commit hash specified in the audit request. Upon completion, the auditor delivers an interim audit report containing, at minimum:

- A scope statement identifying the contracts, scripts, or artifacts reviewed
- The exact commit hash of the audited code
- All findings, categorized by severity
- Recommendations for remediation where applicable

The final audit report must be hosted on the auditor's website or another independently verifiable location. Internal documents, shared drives, or non-permanent links do not satisfy this requirement.
assessments.description: Requires auditors to audit against a specified commit hash, deliver interim reports with defined contents, and host final reports at verifiable permanent locations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete, checkable elements: an exact commit hash, enumerated report contents, and explicit exclusions for hosting (internal drives and non-permanent links). It sets no numeric threshold, no delivery deadline for the interim or final report, and no severity scale for the required categorization.
metrics: Audit performed against the scope and commit hash specified in the audit request
Interim audit report delivered upon completion
Interim report contains scope statement, exact commit hash, findings categorized by severity, and remediation recommendations where applicable
Final audit report hosted on auditor's website or another independently verifiable location; internal documents, shared drives, or non-permanent links do not satisfy
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could check whether audit reports meet the content and hosting requirements. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the paragraph does not state how a missing or non-compliant report is escalated.

assessments.title: Report Review And Acceptance
assessments.quote:
Upon delivery of the interim audit report, the team responsible for the audited code reviews the report and confirms that the audited scope and commit hash match the audit request. The audited artifact must not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote until the team has accepted the report.

An audit is considered complete when the final audit report is published at the independently verifiable hosting location specified in [A.1.10.2.7.3 - Audit Execution And Report Delivery](31544b57-28e8-4cee-b4ae-f73c2cacabad).

If the interim audit report identifies findings, the artifact must not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote until the remediation process specified in [A.1.10.2.7.5 - Findings Remediation](80eab9dd-3833-4418-9845-b648e19fb72f) is completed.
assessments.description: Requires audited artifacts to be accepted, scope- and commit-verified, and remediated before deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names verifiable checks (scope and commit hash matching the audit request, publication at a specified hosting location) and clear gating conditions. It sets no deadlines or numeric thresholds, and the 'team accepts the report' and 'remediation is completed' conditions are left to judgment.
metrics: Commit hash in the interim report matches the audit request
Audited scope matches the audit request
Artifact does not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote until the team accepts the interim report
Audit is complete only when the final report is published at the independently verifiable hosting location in A.1.10.2.7.3
Artifact does not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote while interim findings are unremediated under A.1.10.2.7.5
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with penalty assessment by an enforcer distinct from the actor, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can freeze an artifact when security rules are threatened, so both plausibly reach an artifact advancing without accepted or remediated findings. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the gate.

assessments.title: Findings Remediation
assessments.quote:
If the interim audit report contains findings, the team responsible for the audited code must address each finding based on its severity:

- Findings of low severity or below may be fixed or acknowledged. An acknowledged response must explain why the finding is accepted as-is, including the rationale and any mitigating factors.
- Findings of medium severity or higher must be fixed. The updated code must be re-audited through a new audit request as specified in [A.1.10.2.7.2 - Audit Request And Intake](fcc17c4e-b1cd-4e62-bb2b-0aea02ee72d5), and the re-audit must be completed as specified in [A.1.10.2.7.4 - Report Review And Acceptance](252e0d85-55ca-4fb5-8f44-a38b6ac65e81) before the audited artifact can proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote. Where the code was submitted by a Prime Agent, the Prime Agent is responsible for the cost of the re-audit.

All findings must be resolved or acknowledged before the audited artifact can proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote. The resolution status of each finding must be recorded in the final audit report or in a supplementary document referenced from the final audit report.
assessments.description: Requires teams to fix or acknowledge audit findings by severity, re-audit medium-or-higher fixes, and gate deployment on resolution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Severity tiers (low versus medium-or-higher) and a hard gate before deployment, Spell inclusion, or vote are concrete. Severity assignment, the acknowledgment standard ("rationale and mitigating factors"), and the Prime Agent's re-audit cost are unquantified or delegated, and no deadlines are stated.
metrics: Findings of medium severity or higher must be fixed and re-audited before deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote
Findings of low severity or below may be fixed or acknowledged with rationale and mitigating factors
All findings must be resolved or acknowledged before the artifact proceeds to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote
Resolution status of each finding recorded in the final audit report or referenced supplementary document
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) can review audited-artifact compliance and assess penalties, and Penalty Mechanisms can apply to Primes who skip re-audit, but neither is quantified for this rule. The Prime's re-audit cost is a real cost but not a defined penalty.

assessments.title: Audit Recordkeeping
assessments.quote: The Forum post for the associated Spell or deployment must include a link to each applicable final audit report, the audited commit hash, and confirmation that the deployed code matches the audited commit, as specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2.1 - Requirements For Forum Post](3d031b7c-1b1f-4f84-8668-1cdf43cb2ab2). Where a Technical Scope is submitted for the deployment, the final audit report and audited commit hash must also be included in the Technical Scope as specified in the same requirements.
assessments.description: Requires Spell Forum posts to cite final audit reports and audited commit hash, plus deployed-code confirmation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete, checkable artifacts (audit report link, commit hash, match confirmation, Technical Scope inclusion) with no numeric thresholds or deadlines. Gaps: "applicable" is undefined in this text, and the operative format is delegated to the external Requirements For Forum Post section.
metrics: Forum post includes a link to each applicable final audit report
Forum post includes the audited commit hash
Forum post includes confirmation that deployed code matches the audited commit
Where a Technical Scope is submitted, it includes the final audit report and audited commit hash
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a distinct enforcer with staged findings and penalty assessment, which could reach a missing or false audit record. The rule does not name this review and no consequence is quantified for this specific obligation, so it stays mid.

assessments.title: Pause Delay
assessments.quote:
The GSM (Governance Security Module) Pause Delay parameter sets the minimum amount of time after an Executive Vote has passed before changes will come into effect in the Sky Protocol.

Once an Executive Vote passes, the GSM Pause Delay must pass before the changes within that Executive Vote can affect the Sky Protocol. The Sky Protocol only has one GSM Pause Delay, and all parameter changes are subject to it. The GSM Pause Delay is usually expressed in terms of hours.

It is possible to move functionality outside of the GSM Pause Delay; however, this requires additional engineering work. A list of exceptional functionality can be found in [A.1.10.3.2 - Exceptions](6781594b-5dff-45ec-89a4-1c9684c4eed8).
assessments.description: Defines the GSM Pause Delay as a mandatory time lag between Executive Vote passage and the sky protocol changes taking effect.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The single GSM Pause Delay parameter and its role are named, but its magnitude is never stated; it is only 'usually expressed in terms of hours'. Exceptions are delegated to another document.
metrics: GSM Pause Delay: minimum time after an Executive Vote passes before changes take effect (usually expressed in hours; no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The delay is a contract timelock that physically blocks immediate execution, but no catalog mechanism directly enforces the delay itself. Emergency Spells are the pre-authorized intervention path that can pause changes during a threatened security event, so the rating is mid, not strong.

assessments.title: Pause Delay Adjustment
assessments.quote:
Adjusting the GSM Pause Delay parameter is a manual process that requires an Executive Vote. Changes to the GSM Pause Delay are subject to the pre-change GSM Pause Delay.

An increase to the GSM Pause Delay parameter should be considered if the risk of governance attack is considered especially high for whatever reason. In the past, the GSM Pause Delay has been increased due to the risk from flash loans combined with increased liquidity of the SKY token on the open market.

A decrease should be considered if time-critical governance actions are projected to be needed in the near future. For example, if extreme market volatility is expected, it may be beneficial to reduce the GSM Pause Delay temporarily to allow Governance to better react to changing conditions.
assessments.description: Requires an Executive Vote to change the GSM Pause Delay, with changes subject to the pre-change delay and judgment-based criteria for increases and decreases.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The process is concrete (manual, Executive Vote, pre-change delay applies), but no numeric delay values, bounds, or triggers are given. Increases and decreases are framed as things that "should be considered" under unquantified conditions like "especially high" risk or "extreme" volatility.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The pre-change delay acts as an in-text timelock on changes, but no citable catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph reaches this rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: Executive Drop Exception
assessments.quote:
The MCD_PAUSE contract manages the general governance timelock of the GSM Pause Delay; however, it also contains an in-built exception to its own rule.

The executive drop functionality allows a successful governance proposal to cancel a previous governance proposal that has not yet passed the GSM Pause Delay period and been executed. As in any other situation, the new Executive proposal must be the hat proposal, meaning more SKY is voting for it than is voting for any other Executive proposal.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to prevent a malicious attack on the protocol if they are able to exceed the attacker’s SKY weight before the GSM Pause Delay expires.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a malicious attacker may be able to delay or permanently block a legitimate governance proposal.
assessments.description: Allows a successful governance proposal to cancel a pending Executive proposal under the GSM Pause Delay if it holds the most SKY votes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 'hat proposal' criterion (more SKY votes than any other Executive proposal) is a verifiable comparison, but the eligible window is only loosely stated as 'has not yet passed the GSM Pause Delay period and been executed'. The threshold for 'exceeding the attacker's SKY weight' is not quantified.
metrics: New Executive proposal must be the hat proposal: more SKY voting for it than for any other Executive proposal
Cancellation must occur before the GSM Pause Delay expires
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines a governance power rather than a constraint on a party, and no citable mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or on-chain enforcement) attaches to misuse of the executive drop; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Oracle Freeze Exception
assessments.quote:
The OSM_MOM contract manages the freezing of Sky’s oracles. The freeze functionality allows a successful governance proposal to immediately freeze the oracle price for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. Once frozen, the oracle price will remain at its current value.

The oracle cannot be unfrozen without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay as part of a regular governance proposal.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that the oracles may be frozen by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.description: Lets a successful governance proposal freeze vault oracle prices, with unfreezing gated by the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor (a successful governance proposal), the OSM_MOM contract, and the scope (any or all vault types). The unfreeze constraint depends on the GSM Pause Delay, which is named but given no value here, so the operative magnitude is delegated.
metrics: Unfreezing an oracle requires waiting for the GSM Pause Delay as part of a regular governance proposal (duration not stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The GSM Pause Delay timelock is in-text but has no citable UUID, and no catalog mechanism reaches misuse of the freeze itself (an attacker-triggered freeze). Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The LINE_MOM contract manages the breaker for the Debt Ceilings of a configurable subset of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. This Debt Ceiling Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to reduce the debt ceilings of a pre-configured whitelist of vault types to zero without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay to expire.

The Debt Ceiling Breaker affects both the Debt Ceiling and the Maximum Debt Ceiling of a given vault type when activated, disabling the Dynamic Debt Ceiling functionality for that vault type if enabled. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected vault types must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The whitelist may be configured via a successful governance proposal, but must wait for the GSM Pause Delay before changes come into effect. The whitelist is defined in [A.1.10.3.2.3.1 - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception Whitelist](4937205a-5be0-4def-9b7f-00f9f3bff421) and can be changed via the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Lets a successful governance proposal zero the debt ceilings of whitelisted vault types immediately, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay via the LINE_MOM breaker.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative magnitude is exact: debt ceilings and maximum debt ceilings go to zero, with a named contract and whitelist. The GSM Pause Delay is referenced but its value is not stated here, and the whitelist is defined in another document.
metrics: Debt Ceiling and Maximum Debt Ceiling of whitelisted vault types reduced to zero on activation
Reversal requires an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay
Whitelist changes via governance proposal take effect only after the GSM Pause Delay
Whitelist changeable via the Operational Weekly Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The GSM Pause Delay is waived for the breaker itself, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, artifact review) reaches misuse of the breaker or unauthorized whitelist changes.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The CLIPPER_MOM contract manages the circuit breaker for vault types using Liquidations 2.0. The circuit breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to impose Sky Governance’s choice of limitations on liquidations for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol.

- Level 0 - Liquidations Enabled - The breaker is not tripped, new vaults can be liquidated and old liquidations can proceed.
- Level 1 - New Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations can take place.
- Level 2 - New Liquidations and Resets Disabled - No new liquidations can take place. No existing auctions can be reset if they expire.
- Level 3 - All Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations, no resets, no bidding in active auctions.

This functionality is exceptional because liquidations at non-market prices have the potential to be irreversibly damaging to both users and the Sky Protocol. The circuit breaker allows Sky Governance to attempt to limit the damage in the event of an issue affecting liquidations without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay.

Additionally, the contract allows for permissionless activation of the circuit breaker, if the price decrease in a collateral exceeds a preset percentage value between oracle price updates. The permissionless activation triggers the circuit breaker at Level 2 because both new auctions and resets reference the current oracle price.

When Level (0, 1, 2, 3) of liquidations circuit breaker is altered via Executive Vote, Sky Governance has the ability to set locked time, which is a specified duration which needs to pass before the liquidations circuit breaker can be triggered again via permissionless activation.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that liquidations may be halted by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.description: Defines the CLIPPER_MOM liquidation circuit breaker levels, its governance-set and permissionless activation, and locked-time rules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The four breaker levels are concrete and enumerated with clear effects. The permissionless trigger uses an unstated 'preset percentage' price drop and the locked time is a governance-set 'specified duration', so the key magnitudes are delegated.
metrics: Level 0-3 liquidation states (Level 2 triggered by permissionless activation)
Permissionless trigger when collateral price decrease exceeds a preset percentage between oracle price updates
Locked time: duration set by Executive Vote before permissionless re-triggering
Circuit breaker can bypass the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The breaker is itself enforced on-chain by CLIPPER_MOM, but no consequence attaches to misusing it. Emergency Spells (pre-authorized pauses on security threats) is the closest general halt mechanism, though it does not directly quantify breaker violations.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception Price Tolerance
assessments.quote:
Breaker Price Tolerance is a parameter which determines the condition for the permissionless activation of circuit breaker. Adjusting the Breaker Price Tolerance requires an Executive Vote, which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The Breaker Price Tolerance is expressed as a number between zero and one, and works with the following equation: `next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance`.

In instances where the price oracle model does not support the price delay function, the permissionless activation of the liquidation circuit breaker ceases to function, since there is no next oracle price.
assessments.description: Defines the Breaker Price Tolerance parameter that gates permissionless liquidation circuit breaker activation, and its governance adjustment rules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The activation condition is an explicit inequality (next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance) with the tolerance bounded between zero and one, and the no-next-price edge case is addressed. The tolerance's actual value is not stated, and the oracle inputs and the GSM Pause Delay length are not quantified in this text.
metrics: Breaker Price Tolerance is a number between zero and one
next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance
Adjusting the Breaker Price Tolerance requires an Executive Vote, subject to GSM Pause Delay
Circuit breaker ceases to function where the price oracle model does not support price delay (no next oracle price)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule governs a parameter and its activation formula; the GSM Pause Delay on adjustments is a governance timing delay not in the catalog, and no penalty, conservatorship, or emergency spell is tied to a violation of these parameter rules.

assessments.title: Direct Deposit Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The DIRECT_MOM contract manages the breaker for Direct Deposit Modules (D3Ms). The breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to disable any or all of the active D3Ms. In practice, this will set the bar parameter to zero, which (contrary to intuition) disables the module by setting the allowed Debt Ceiling to zero. At this point, no further USDS can be minted through the Direct Deposit Module. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected Direct Deposit Modules must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a given line of USDS credit is unexpectedly shut down. This has the potential to disrupt the protocol in question, which may impact Sky indirectly.
assessments.description: Allows a successful governance proposal to disable Direct Deposit Modules by setting bar to zero, halting their USDS minting.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The mechanics are concrete: the DIRECT_MOM contract, the bar parameter set to zero, and the resulting Debt Ceiling of zero. However, there is no criterion for when the breaker may be used, and reversal is delegated to an Executive Vote without stated magnitudes or deadlines.
metrics: bar parameter set to zero
allowed Debt Ceiling set to zero
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes a governance control rather than an obligation a regulated party could breach, and the GSM Pause Delay it references is not in the catalog or cited by UUID. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The SPLITTER_MOM contract allows for the disabling of the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay.

This functionality is available so that Sky Governance can react to emergencies regarding the Smart Burn Engine.

Since the Splitter contract also allocates USDS from the Surplus Buffer to USDS Staking Rewards, the activation of SPLITTER_MOM also disables these rewards. To reverse the effect, the `hop` parameter must be reconfigured, either with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay, or directly through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds, as specified in [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f).
assessments.description: Allows SPLITTER_MOM to disable the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay for emergencies, and specifies how the disablement is reversed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation and reversal path are identifiable, but 'emergencies' is undefined and 'within its bounds' is not quantified in this text. No thresholds, durations, or measurable criteria are stated, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The reversal path (Executive Vote or SBE-BEAM) corrects the disablement but imposes no consequence on misuse of SPLITTER_MOM. Emergency Response System governs emergency handling, not penalties for unjustified use, and no penalty or conservatorship mechanism reaches this exception.

assessments.title: PSM Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The LITE_PSM_MOM contract manages the breaker for swaps through the LitePSM. The PSM Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to halt swaps through the LitePSM.

The PSM Breaker can halt selling, buying, or both, independently. To reverse the effect, the halted parameter or parameters — `tin`, `tout`, or both, depending on which was halted — must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Lets a passed governance proposal halt LitePSM buying, selling, or both, with reversal via a delayed Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The controlled system (LITE_PSM_MOM), the parameters (tin, tout), the actor (a successful governance proposal), and the independent halt options are all named. The reversal is gated by the GSM Pause Delay, whose value is defined elsewhere and not stated here, and no cadence or timing applies.
metrics: Halt scope: selling (tin), buying (tout), or both, set independently
Reversal requires reconfiguring the halted parameter(s) via an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay (value not stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The breaker is a pre-authorized on-chain intervention that halts LitePSM swaps, which resembles the Emergency Spells mechanism (A.1.10.5). It is not a penalty for a violation, though, and the GSM Pause Delay that gates reversal is not in the catalog, so the consequence is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Modules
assessments.quote:
Bounded External Access Modules (BEAMs) are contracts that allow whitelisted operators to manage parameters in the Sky Ecosystem without needing to use the standard Executive Vote process. Thus, parameter changes enacted via these modules are not subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The actions of BEAMs are limited by risk parameters, which are set by Sky Core Governance. Changing these risk parameters typically requires an Executive Vote, unless the BEAM authorizes a standing actor to change them directly.
assessments.description: Defines Bounded External Access Modules, exempts their parameter changes from the GSM Pause Delay, and limits them by Sky Core risk parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a real obligation that BEAM actions are bounded by risk parameters, but it gives no numeric limits, no defined risk parameter values, and no criteria for whitelisting operators. 'Typically requires an Executive Vote' is hedged language a defender could read as non-binding.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph cites no enforcement mechanism UUID, and the catalog mechanisms (Emergency Spells, Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship) are not referenced in the text or clearly reached by the bounding rule; only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Module Risk Disclosure
assessments.quote:
BEAMs allow whitelisted operators greater flexibility to respond to market movements when setting parameters in the Sky Ecosystem. This flexibility introduces additional risk since operators are able to bypass the Executive Vote process when changing the parameters relevant to the BEAM that they operate.

This risk can be mitigated by limiting the frequency and size of modifications that can be made by operators in parameters controlled by Sky Core. All BEAMs should also have a related MOM contract that can deactivate the relevant BEAM in the event of an operator acting in a misaligned manner.

Any operator that fails to follow the defined procedures for a BEAM they are operating should be considered misaligned.
assessments.description: Describes risks of whitelisted BEAM operators bypassing Executive Votes, and requires frequency and size limits plus a MOM deactivation contract for each BEAM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires limits on the frequency and size of operator modifications and a MOM deactivation contract, but gives no numeric caps, cadence, or defined procedures. Misalignment is defined only by failure to follow undefined procedures, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The MOM contract's deactivation of a misaligned BEAM is a pre-authorized intervention that reaches operator misalignment, which fits Emergency Spells. It is not quantified and depends on someone triggering it, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) manages the parameters of the stUSDS system. Whitelisted operators can use the stUSDS BEAM to modify certain stUSDS parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The stUSDS BEAM modifies stUSDS parameters within specified ranges. See [A.4.4.1.3.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module](37f8f82e-7239-4cfb-8f95-d2cc40515cd9).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update stUSDS parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting stUSDS parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the stUSDS BEAM parameters and the STUSDS_MOM.
assessments.description: Lets whitelisted operators change certain stUSDS parameters within specified ranges without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (whitelisted operators), a controlled system (stUSDS BEAM), and a delay it bypasses, but the permitted parameters and the ranges are delegated to an external cross-referenced document. It gives no numeric bounds, cadence, or verifiable limit, so compliance cannot be checked from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize executive freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach malicious parameter-setting by operators. The consequence depends on someone triggering the spell, and the paragraph's own mitigations (the BEAM parameters and STUSDS_MOM) are not quantified here.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) manages certain parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. See [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a). Whitelisted operators can use the SBE-BEAM to modify the `kbump`, `burn`, and `hop` parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SBE-BEAM modifies these parameters, up or down, within specified bounds. See [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update Smart Burn Engine parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting Smart Burn Engine parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SBE-BEAM parameters and the SPLITTER_MOM, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.8 - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception](5247c795-7f9d-4d3f-a040-6bc9b070e2d4).
assessments.description: Allows whitelisted operators to modify Smart Burn Engine kbump, burn, and hop parameters within bounds, without the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor (whitelisted operators), the parameters (kbump, burn, hop), and the delay it bypasses, but gives no bound values or delay duration, deferring them to other documents. Its operative limit, 'within specified bounds', is not verifiable from this text alone.
metrics: Parameters modifiable: kbump, burn, hop
Adjustment bounded 'up or down, within specified bounds' (values not stated here)
Bypasses GSM Pause Delay (duration not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The text cites the Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception and SPLITTER_MOM as the mitigation for malicious parameter setting, a named circuit-breaker path that plausibly reaches the violation. No quantified penalty or defined escalation for operator misconduct is stated, so it rates mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Configurator Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.quote:
A Configurator Bounded External Access Module (cBEAM) is a whitelisted Operator. It can use the Configurator to adjust a Diamond PAU's rate limits or execute enabled controller actions, within the bounds BeamState sets, without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.4 - Configurator](45840a10-6c7c-453a-8218-4ab4d705012d).

This functionality allows Diamond PAU parameters to be adjusted more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by cBEAMs setting rate limits to undesirable values, whether by raising them excessively or lowering them to zero.

This risk is partially mitigated: BeamState's `hop` and `maxChange` parameters bound how far and how often a cBEAM can raise a rate limit; they do not bound decreases, which take effect immediately. The Core Council Multisig can immediately unpair a specific misbehaving cBEAM from its `RateLimits` contract or Controller to stop it from acting, and can separately remove its registration entirely, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6). Sky Governance can halt Configurator operations for all cBEAMs at once, through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71).
assessments.description: Allows whitelisted cBEAM operators to adjust Diamond PAU rate limits and controller actions within BeamState bounds, skipping the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the concrete parameters hop and maxChange in BeamState, but gives no values, so the magnitude and frequency of permitted increases are delegated to BeamState. Decreases are explicitly unbounded and take effect immediately, with no threshold or cadence stated.
metrics: BeamState `hop` parameter bounds how far a cBEAM can raise a rate limit (value not stated)
BeamState `maxChange` parameter bounds how often a cBEAM can raise a rate limit (value not stated)
Rate-limit decreases, including to zero, take effect immediately with no bound
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Council Multisig can immediately unpair a misbehaving cBEAM or remove its registration (Immediate Function Calls), and Sky Governance can halt all cBEAM operations via PASMom; these are named enforcers distinct from the cBEAM with concrete remedies. However, no quantified penalty applies and escalation depends on the Council or Governance acting on detected misuse, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Core Council Multisig Exception
assessments.quote:
The Core Council Multisig can act on BeamState without a separate Executive Vote for each change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754). Its immediate functions take effect directly, with no delay; its delayed functions take effect only after the Timelock's minimum delay has passed.

This functionality allows the Core Council Multisig to respond to cBEAM misbehavior, and to adjust BeamState's own parameters, more quickly than waiting for a separate Executive Vote.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by the Core Council Multisig itself.

The Core Council Multisig's immediate functions are bounded: they cannot register a new cBEAM, but can re-pair an existing one to a different `RateLimits` contract or Controller, or disable/halt existing PAS (Parallelized Allocation System) functionality.

The Core Council Multisig's delayed functions, once the Timelock is unpaused, are subject to the Timelock's minimum delay, and can be halted by Sky Governance triggering `pause()` through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71).

The PAS launches with the Timelock paused. Until it is unpaused, none of its delayed functions can take effect; they must instead go through an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.5 - Transitional Measures](d5240aa5-72c1-4f92-b22c-7a80a35d733c).
assessments.description: Lets the Core Council Multisig act on BeamState, with bounded immediate functions and timelock-delayed functions gated by PASMom pause.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The immediate functions are enumerated concretely (re-pair cBEAM to a different RateLimits contract or Controller, disable/halt PAS functions, but not register new cBEAM), and the actors and PASMom pause path are named. The operative timing parameter, the Timelock's minimum delay, is referenced but never given a value.
metrics: Timelock's minimum delay (value not stated; delayed functions take effect only after it passes)
Immediate functions take effect with no delay
Timelock launches paused; delayed functions require an Executive Vote until unpaused
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Sky Governance can halt delayed Core Council Multisig functions via pause() through PASMom, a named enforcer distinct from the multisig, which plausibly reaches malicious delayed actions. Immediate functions have no cited check, and no quantified penalty or remedy is stated for this rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The SPBEAM_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the SP-BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the SPBEAM_MOM is activated, the SP-BEAM will not be able to change any rates in the system, though Sky Governance retains the ability to modify rates directly through the usual Executive Vote process. To reverse the effect, the SP-BEAM's `bad` parameter must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance bypass the GSM Pause Delay to disable the SP-BEAM rate-setting module during emergencies, with reversal requiring a delayed Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The contract (SPBEAM_MOM), the actor (Sky Governance), the effect (SP-BEAM cannot change rates), and the reversal path (reconfiguring the `bad` parameter by Executive Vote) are named. The operative delay magnitude is delegated to the GSM Pause Delay, and no trigger criteria or time limits are stated.
metrics: Bypasses the GSM Pause Delay (magnitude defined elsewhere)
Reversal requires an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes a pre-authorized executive kill switch for an emergency, which is the Emergency Spells mechanism reaching SP-BEAM operator misbehavior. Its consequence is unquantified and it is a privileged governance power rather than an automatic constraint on Sky Governance's own bypass.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.quote:
The STUSDS_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module or set the `cap` or `line` stUSDS parameters to zero.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the stUSDS BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the STUSDS_MOM is activated to disable the stUSDS BEAM, the stUSDS BEAM will not be able to change any stUSDS parameters in the system, though Sky Governance retains the ability to modify stUSDS parameters directly through the usual Executive Vote process. Reversing a disabled stUSDS BEAM requires reconfiguring the rate setter's `bad` parameter with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay. Reversing a `cap` or `line` set to zero requires reconfiguring both the stUSDS parameter and the rate setter's corresponding `maxCap` or `maxLine` parameter, likewise with an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance bypass the GSM Pause Delay to disable the stUSDS BEAM or zero its cap or line parameters in emergencies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete contracts and parameters (STUSDS_MOM, cap, line, bad, maxCap, maxLine) and the reversal steps. However, the GSM Pause Delay is referenced without a value, and no numeric thresholds or deadlines are stated in this text.
metrics: Bypasses the GSM Pause Delay (duration defined elsewhere, no value stated here)
Sets stUSDS cap or line parameters to zero
Reversal requires an Executive Vote subject to the GSM Pause Delay
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The bypass is itself a pre-authorized emergency intervention against a BEAM operator that is hacked or malicious, which maps to the Emergency Spells path for security violations. The consequence for misuse is not quantified, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: PASMom Exception
assessments.quote:
The PASMom contract (`PAS_MOM`) allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to halt Configurator operations or pause the Timelock governing changes to the PAS. This is a Sky Governance action taken independently of both the Core Council Multisig and cBEAM; neither can trigger the PASMom contract itself. For PASMom's on-chain relationship to BeamState and the Timelock, see [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8).

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency. If a cBEAM is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can trigger `stop()` through the PASMom contract, preventing all cBEAMs from executing any action through the Configurator; restarting is done via the Core Council Multisig proposing `start()` through the Timelock once it is unpaused, or otherwise via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.5 - Restart After Halt](e049feea-5af3-4a8d-8766-36e348fd5d7b).

If the Core Council Multisig is compromised or acting maliciously, Sky Governance can trigger `pause()` through the PASMom contract, preventing the Timelock from scheduling or executing the Core Council Multisig's delayed proposals; reversing this requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Governance bypass the GSM Pause Delay to stop or pause Configurator and Timelock operations via PASMom, and sets restart and reversal paths.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the contract, functions (stop, pause, start), actors, and restart and reversal routes, which are concrete and checkable. The trigger is qualitative ("compromised or acting maliciously") and no thresholds, timing, or delay values are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph grants a power rather than constraining behavior, and the only check is an Executive Vote to reverse the pause, which is a governance control rather than a consequence for misuse. The Emergency Response System and Emergency Spells are not cited in the text and do not clearly reach misuse of PASMom itself.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Features
assessments.quote: The `lerp` must be activated in an Executive Vote but can thereafter change the value of the designated parameter without additional Executive Votes. Each `lerp` instance is defined in terms of a `start` value, representing the desired starting value, an `end` value, representing the desired ending value, and a `duration` over which the parameter will be adjusted between the starting value and the ending value. Any user can then permissionlessly call `tick` to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed.
assessments.description: Defines how the Linear Interpolation Module activates via Executive Vote and gradually adjusts a governance parameter between start and end values over a duration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete parameters (start, end, duration, tick) and a linear interpolation mechanic, so the adjustment path is identifiable. However, no duration bounds, units, or tick cadence are given, and the start and end magnitudes are left to each instance.
metrics: start: desired starting value of the governance parameter (no value specified)
end: desired ending value of the governance parameter (no value specified)
duration: period over which the parameter is linearly adjusted (no value or units specified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Activation requires an Executive Vote, but that is a gating step rather than an enforcement consequence for misuse, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, liquidation, emergency spell, artifact review) is shown to reach how a lerp adjusts parameters after activation. Only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Parameters
assessments.quote:
Each `lerp` instance has the following parameters:

- `target` - The target contract in which a parameter is being changed
- `what` - The name of the parameter being changed
- `startTime` - The starting time of this `lerp` instance
- `start` - The starting value of that parameter
- `end` - The ending value of that parameter
- `duration` - How long this `lerp` instance will run for
- `done` - Indicates whether this given `lerp` instance is completed or not
assessments.description: Defines the seven fields each Linear Interpolation Module (lerp) instance uses to schedule gradual parameter changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete fields (target, what, startTime, start, end, duration, done) but states no thresholds, formulas, bounds, or deadlines, and it imposes no operative obligation on any actor. A defender could argue it is descriptive only and binds no one.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The lerp interpolation is contract-executed, but the paragraph is a data-structure definition with no violation mode, and none of the catalog mechanisms (penalties, liquidation, PSM, emergency spells, artifact review) reaches it.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Authorization
assessments.quote: The Facilitators responsible for the Scope that governs the parameter to be adjusted by the Linear Interpolation Module, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, may recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments.
assessments.description: Permits Scope Facilitators, consulting the Core Council Risk Advisor, to recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors are defined (Facilitators responsible for the governing Scope, Core Council Risk Advisor), but the rule is a permissive recommendation with no criteria for when a recommendation is appropriate, no consultation standard, and no thresholds. Compliance is arguable on any facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule governs an optional recommendation rather than a prohibited act, and no penalty, emergency, or artifact-review mechanism in the catalog or the paragraph text reaches it; only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Consideration
assessments.quote: The Facilitators must take into consideration the benefits and costs with using the Linear Interpolation Module. A longer `duration` has the benefit of adjusting the parameter more slowly, giving users more time to adjust. However, the drawback of a longer `duration` is that the parameter will not reach its desired `end` value for a longer period of time. When the cost of a parameter not being at its desired value is high, use of the Linear Interpolation Module is not appropriate, and the parameter should be adjusted to its desired value following the required process.
assessments.description: Requires Facilitators to weigh costs and benefits of using the Linear Interpolation Module and avoid it when non-desired parameter values are costly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real (consider trade-offs; use the required process when costs are high), but it relies on judgment language such as "take into consideration" and "high" cost, with no threshold, metric, or cadence. A Facilitator could plausibly argue compliance on any facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or on-chain mechanism reaches a Facilitator's cost-benefit judgment on using the module, so only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Governance Process For Linear Interpolation Module
assessments.quote: The process to utilize the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust a parameter must follow the same governance process required to modify the designated parameter. If the parameter can be updated directly through an Executive Vote, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust it may also be included directly in an Executive Vote. If modifying the parameter requires a prior Governance Poll, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module for that parameter must also be preceded by a Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Requires Linear Interpolation Module parameter adjustments to follow the same governance process, Executive Vote or Poll, as the parameter itself.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete processes (Executive Vote, Governance Poll) and a clear conditional mapping, but the operative requirement is delegated to whatever process the designated parameter already uses. It gives no thresholds, deadlines, or cadence of its own.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, on-chain, or emergency mechanism reaches a violation of this process-mapping rule. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, and governance votes self-enforce.

assessments.title: Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.1 - Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig](21fa6749-6209-4280-9b5f-b2a73d400421)) can freeze SkyLink bridges deployed in the Sky Ecosystem without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function.
assessments.description: Lets the Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig freeze SkyLink bridges outside Spells and requires forum reporting of its actions.

metrics: Each multisig action, including function calls and parameters, must be reported on the Sky Forum within a reasonable time frame
Reportable actions include activating or disabling the freeze function
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain control reaches a missed or late forum report. Only the generic Reports of Misalignment catch-all applies, which is always weak.

The Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.2.3.1.1 - Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig](8e618196-257a-49d8-834d-665dba345fcd)) can freeze the Solana SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

The Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.3.3.1.1 - Avalanche SkyLink Freezer Multisig](0b1162f6-6a30-4a30-b693-68e077093e7c)) can freeze the Avalanche SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

assessments.title: Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.4.3.1.1 - Plasma SkyLink Freezer Multisig](f833edaa-9f5f-4445-afcb-a9cfc3620b10)) can freeze the Plasma SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The freeze authority and the reporting channel (Sky Forum post covering function calls and parameters) are named and concrete.
