metrics: Each action by the multisig, including function calls and parameters, must be reported on the Sky Forum within a reasonable time frame
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Spells mechanism addresses security violations such as freezes, not failure to report multisig actions, and no penalty, review, or escalation path is tied to the reporting duty; only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Multisig Freeze Of SparkLend
assessments.quote:
In addition to the SparkLend Freezer Mom contract defined in [A.1.10.3.2.7 - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception](645443f1-9004-48d3-868c-139b608bb1f9), an external SparkLend Security Access Multisig has been established that allows for pausing and/or freezing SparkLend markets. The SparkLend Security Access Multisig can enable or disable the SparkLend Freezer Mom contract without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the pause or freeze function.
assessments.description: Requires the SparkLend Security Access Multisig to report each pause or freeze action and its parameters on the Sky Forum within a reasonable time.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (the SparkLend Security Access Multisig), the controlled actions (pause/freeze), and the reporting venue (Sky Forum) are concrete and checkable. The reporting deadline is only "a reasonable time frame," a delegated judgment that a defender could stretch, so the timing is not quantified.
metrics: Each multisig action, including function calls and their parameters, must be reported
Reporting must occur "within a reasonable time frame" (no numeric deadline)
Reports must be posted on the Sky Forum
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps is a scheduled, third-party review with staged findings and penalty assessment, and it could reach a missing or late action report. The consequence is not quantified for this specific reporting duty, and firing requires the review to actually examine the forum record.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The SparkLend Security Access Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or SparkLend users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit).

The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior.

The Multisig can also be used in cases where a vulnerability or exploit is discovered in other protocols using the same codebase as SparkLend, and a timely action can prevent or mitigate the damage.

The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with the requirements defined herein.
assessments.description: Restricts use of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig to urgent exploit-prevention situations and defines the Core Council's oversight duty.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule sets out qualitative criteria such as 'urgent or emergency', 'potential to harm', and whether an Executive Vote's preparation time would leave the ecosystem vulnerable. It gives no numeric threshold, time limit, or measurable test, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can reach Spark Agent's multisig use through scheduled review, staged findings, and penalty assessment by a body distinct from the actor. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and the review depends on the Core Council or GovOps raising the matter.

assessments.title: Facilitators Must Exercise Due Caution In Reviewing Use Of Multisig
assessments.quote: The list of instances justifying use of the multisig in the Target Document is not intended to be exhaustive. However, the Core Council must exercise due caution in reviewing and validating use of the multisig in edge cases, i.e., use of the multisig that falls outside of the examples provided in the Target Document. In such "edge cases," the Core Council must ensure that a postmortem is publicly published on the Sky Forum which justifies the use of the multisig. The Core Council should also consider proposing an edit to the Target Document so that the edge case is explicitly included in the examples provided in the Target Document.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council to exercise caution on edge-case multisig use and publish a Sky Forum postmortem justifying it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The postmortem publication on the Sky Forum is a concrete, checkable artifact, but no deadline or cadence is set, and the 'due caution' standard and the definition of an edge case (anything outside examples in another document) remain judgment-based. The edit proposal is only 'should consider', which is non-binding.
metrics: Postmortem publicly published on Sky Forum for each edge-case multisig use
Edge case = multisig use outside the examples in the Target Document
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or review mechanism in the catalog reaches the Core Council's postmortem duty; the Core Council polices itself, and only the misalignment-report catch-all applies.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has a 3/5 signing requirement.
assessments.description: States the current signing threshold of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig as 3 of 5 signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 3/5 threshold, the signer count, and the named multisig are all concrete and checkable on-chain. It is a descriptive statement of current state rather than an obligation, and it gives no cadence, change-control process, or rule for when the threshold must be revisited.
metrics: Signing requirement: 3 of 5 signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The threshold is enforced by the multisig contract when transactions execute, but the paragraph does not regulate changes to it, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, insurance pricing) is shown to reach a reduction in the threshold.

assessments.title: SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. The Core Facilitator should consider preparing an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.
assessments.description: Requires Governance Poll approval for SparkLend Security Access Multisig signer changes, with narrow self-report exceptions and expedited escalation for unratified changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actors (signers, Core Facilitator, Sky Governance), the approval channel (Governance Poll), and the exception procedure (public Sky Forum post). Operative timing and escalation are qualitative: 'as soon as possible', 'immediately', and 'should consider preparing' an Executive Vote, with no thresholds or deadlines.
metrics: Signer modifications require Governance Poll approval
Exceptions limited to self-reported loss of key access or explicit removal request, communicated via public Sky Forum post
Replacement of affected signer 'as soon as possible'
Unratified or non-exception signer changes to be questioned 'immediately' and treated as malicious
Core Facilitator 'should consider' preparing an expedited Executive Vote to remove external security access
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive freezes when security rules are violated, and the Emergency Response System (A.1.9) gives an escalation path outside the normal governance cycle, which together plausibly reach unratified multisig signer changes. However, the paragraph's escalation is hedged ('should consider') and no quantified consequence applies to this rule, so firing depends on someone volunteering it.

assessments.title: Emergency Spells Definition
assessments.quote: Emergency Spells are expedited ad hoc Spells that, while typically compliant with all customary quality-assurance processes, do not adhere to the normal Spell cadence. Emergency Spells solve the root issue of an emergency / urgent situation impacting the Protocol and are used when a rapid response time is needed. The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps are responsible for managing the use of Emergency Spells pursuant to [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b) and [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48).
assessments.description: Defines Emergency Spells as expedited, off-cadence Spells for urgent Protocol situations, assigning management duties to Core Facilitator and Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors (Core Facilitator, Core GovOps) and cross-references two sub-sections, but gives no thresholds or deadlines. Terms such as 'typically compliant', 'emergency / urgent situation' and 'rapid response time' are undefined, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) are the intervention instrument itself, not a consequence for misusing them; no penalty, review, or automatic mechanism is tied to the duty to manage their use. The cross-referenced sub-sections are not catalog mechanisms.

assessments.title: Standby Spells Definition
assessments.quote:
Sky Protocol uses circuit-breakers to mitigate undesired scenarios, which circuit-breakers are called MOM contracts. MOM contracts must first be triggered through a Spell, after which they bypass the GSM Pause Delay and can immediately act on the Protocol. See [A.1.10.3.2 - Exceptions](6781594b-5dff-45ec-89a4-1c9684c4eed8).

In emergency scenarios, time is a scarce resource. Therefore, Standby Spells are used in validated emergency scenarios to trigger a MOM contract. In an emergency situation, Spell teams can then focus on crafting an ad hoc Emergency Spell to solve the root cause of an issue, if appropriate. Due to Standby Spells, it is no longer necessary in an emergency for Spell teams to spend time crafting and reviewing a Spell whose sole purpose is to trigger a mitigation of the issue, i.e., the MOM contract.

Standby Spells open new attack vectors that must be mitigated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb).
assessments.description: Defines Standby Spells as pre-authorized spells that trigger MOM circuit-breaker contracts in validated emergencies, bypassing the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule establishes an operative pathway: MOM contracts are triggered only by a Spell and bypass the GSM Pause Delay. However, the key gating condition, 'validated emergency scenarios', has no defined criteria, validator, or threshold, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) are the parent pre-authorized intervention channel that a Standby Spell instantiates, so misuse of an emergency trigger is plausibly reached by that framework. The consequence for misusing a Standby Spell is not quantified or specifically defined here.

assessments.title: Standby Spell Incorporation Into New MOM Contracts
assessments.quote: Each new MOM contract created must incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory, which can be used to create new Standby Spells that can trigger the MOM contract. With a Standby Spell per every MOM contract, the generation of technical debt can be avoided.
assessments.description: Requires every new MOM contract to incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory that can trigger it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The one-per-contract requirement is concrete and countable, so a third party could check whether each new MOM contract has a Standby Spell or factory. However, the text does not define what counts as incorporation or what the spell must be able to do beyond triggering the contract, and it gives no deadline or verification process.
metrics: Each new MOM contract created must incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory
One Standby Spell per MOM contract (or a factory able to create them)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Standby Spells are Emergency Spells, and Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a MOM contract deployed without a trigger. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and firing depends on someone identifying the omission and escalating it.

assessments.title: Available Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The currently available Standby Spells are defined in the subdocuments herein. The following list of Standby Spells is not exhaustive: that is, the Core Facilitator, in collaboration with the Emergency Response Group and Spell teams, has the discretion to develop and use a Standby Spell that is not listed in the subdocuments below. When that occurs, however, the Core Facilitator must ensure that the new Standby Spell is subsequently added to the subdocuments below.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator develop unlisted Standby Spells and requires that each be added to the subdocuments afterward.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Core Facilitator) and a real obligation to add new spells to the subdocuments, but it sets no deadline or cadence for adding them and no criteria for when discretion applies. Compliance is arguable, since the Facilitator could claim adding a spell later satisfies the rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule concerns documentation of Standby Spells, and no mechanism watches whether the Facilitator adds new spells to the subdocuments; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Single-Collateral Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The subdocuments herein define currently available single-collateral Standby Spells. For each instance of use, single-collateral Standby Spell contracts require a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory.
assessments.description: Defines available single-collateral Standby Spells and requires a factory deployment transaction for each use.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete mechanical step, a factory deployment transaction for each instance of use, which a third party could check on-chain. However, it mainly points to subdocuments for the actual spell list and states no thresholds, limits, or cadence, and it reads as architectural description, so a defender could argue it imposes little binding obligation.
metrics: Each instance of use of a single-collateral Standby Spell requires a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The per-use factory deployment is a structural gate that makes each use a discrete, on-chain-visible action, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) are the pre-authorized intervention machinery that would reach misuse of these spells. The paragraph states no quantified consequence for bypassing the factory requirement, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: SingleOsmStopSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to freeze an OSM for a single collateral. If the oracle price provider fails for any reason, Governance can act before the OSM registers the next price; this allows for the problem to be fixed with no impact on the system.
assessments.description: Describes a standby emergency spell that lets governance freeze one collateral's OSM price feed after an oracle failure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The spell's scope is named (one OSM, one collateral) and it has a timing condition, freezing before the next price is registered. However, the trigger is open-ended ("fails for any reason") and no failure threshold, detection metric, or response deadline is stated.
metrics: Freeze must take effect before the OSM registers the next price
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The spell is itself a pre-authorized Emergency Spells freeze that governance can execute when the oracle feed is threatened, so it reaches this oracle-failure case. Firing still depends on someone invoking it, and no automatic trigger or quantified consequence is defined.

assessments.title: SingleDdmDisableSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to disable a D3M integration. If a D3M partner is experiencing a problem such as a hack, this emergency Spell can be used to prevent abuse. While it cannot recover Dai already injected into the compromised protocol, the Emergency Spell can prevent additional exposure.
assessments.description: Authorizes a standby emergency spell to disable a D3M integration when a partner protocol is compromised, such as by a hack.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete tool (SingleDdmDisableSpell) and its target (a D3M integration), but the trigger is judgment language ("experiencing a problem such as a hack") with no defined severity, detection criteria, or decision actor. Compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Spells mechanism (A.1.10.5) is the pre-authorized executive path that reaches this rule: it lets the integration be frozen or disabled when a partner's security is threatened. The remedy is concrete, but the paragraph does not define when it fires or who escalates, so it is not strong.

assessments.title: SingleLitePsmHaltFactory
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to halt a LitePSM completely.
assessments.description: Describes a standby spell that can be used in an emergency to fully halt a LitePSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete action (complete halt of a LitePSM) and a controlled system, but gives no trigger criteria for 'emergency', no authorised actor, and no scope or duration of the halt. Whether it binds anyone on specific facts is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The halt is itself an Emergency Spell (A.1.10.5), a pre-authorised executive intervention that reaches LitePSM security violations. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and firing depends on executive action being taken.

assessments.title: Grouped Standby Spells
assessments.quote: The subdocuments herein define currently available grouped Standby Spells. For each instance of use, grouped Standby Spell contracts require a transaction to deploy the Standby Spell from a factory. Unlike single-collateral Standby Spells, a grouped Standby Spell is configured at the time of deployment with a specific list of collaterals it can operate on. This setup enables a single grouped Standby Spell to operate on multiple related collaterals.
assessments.description: Defines grouped Standby Spells as factory-deployed per use, configured at deployment with a fixed list of collaterals.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text names a concrete procedure (one factory deployment transaction per use, collateral list fixed at deployment), but it is largely descriptive. It sets no thresholds, limits on collateral count, or verifiable criteria for compliance, so a defender could argue it imposes no binding obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph describes deployment structure and states no consequence for deploying outside the factory or mis-configuring the collateral list. The Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) governs spell use in general but does not reach this descriptive rule.

assessments.title: GroupedLineWipeSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell will perform a Line MOM Wipe (set debt ceiling to zero) for the specified collaterals. It can be used if the specified collaterals fail - for example, if a stablecoin depegs or the protocol that provides the token is hacked. Users will still be able to exit their positions, but no new debt will be allowed to be created for the collaterals.
assessments.description: Defines a standby spell that sets the debt ceiling to zero for specified collaterals when they fail.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative action is concrete: the debt ceiling is set to exactly zero for named collaterals. The trigger is qualitative, with 'fail' and 'for example' (depeg, hack) and no threshold, so when the spell may be used is left open.

Use permitted if the specified collaterals fail (no numeric trigger)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The spell is itself a pre-authorized Emergency Spell (A.1.10.5) that executes an intervention on the debt system when collateral security is threatened. It is mid rather than strong because it needs someone to deploy it and the trigger is not defined.

assessments.description: Permits a Standby Spell to be used in an emergency to disable the Smart Burn Engine.

assessments.title: SPBEAMHaltSpell
assessments.quote: This Standby Spell can be used in an emergency to disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM). After this Standby Spell is invoked, the SP-BEAM will no longer be able to set rates in the system. Invoking the Standby Spell has no impact on rates, which remain at pre-invocation levels until adjusted by Sky Governance via an Executive Vote.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Spells mechanism (A.1.10.5) provides pre-authorized executive intervention to halt a module when security is threatened, which reaches SP-BEAM misbehaviour. Invocation is discretionary and the trigger is not defined, so the escalation is not automatic.

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the Standby Spell process is as follows:

- Standby Spells can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).

The decision to initiate the process to use a Standby Spell is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).

- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use a Standby Spell in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.

- After the decision to use a Standby Spell is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).

- After the Core Facilitator decides to use a Standby Spell, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).

- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the Standby Spell and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.
assessments.description: Sets the Core Facilitator's responsibilities for deciding, communicating, documenting, and actioning Standby Spells in an emergency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core Facilitator, TechOps Services) and named channels (Emergency Response Signal Group, war room call) are concrete and steps are enumerated. However, timing is only 'promptly' with no numeric deadline, and consultation is softened to 'where possible' and 'should'.
metrics: Documentation of decision 'promptly' after first reached on a video call
TechOps trigger of incident 'promptly' after the Core Facilitator decides to use a Standby Spell
Consultation with Scope Advisor(s) 'where possible'
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Facilitator is the actor whose conduct is governed, and no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain control reaches a violation of these communication or documentation steps. The Emergency Spells mechanism is the instrument being regulated, not an enforcer of this rule.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote: Core GovOps must promptly acknowledge receipt of the Core Facilitator's decision to use a Standby Spell. This acknowledgment must take place in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to promptly acknowledge the Core Facilitator's Standby Spell decision in the designated Emergency Response Signal Group channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The acknowledgment channel is concretely identified by cross-reference to A.1.9.1.3.1 Emergency Response Signal Group, and the actor is defined. However, "promptly" has no numeric deadline or measurement cadence, so timeliness is qualitative.
metrics: Acknowledgment must be made promptly (no numeric deadline stated)
Acknowledgment must occur in the Emergency Response Signal Group channel (A.1.9.1.3.1)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) governs the signal channel and defines an escalation protocol outside the standard governance cycle, which a missed acknowledgment could stall. No quantified penalty applies to this specific acknowledgment duty, and escalation would depend on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Standby Spell
assessments.quote:
Two Authorized Representatives, as defined in the subdocument below, from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Standby Spell.

This validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). assessments.title: ADs' Role In Standby Spells
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use a Standby Spell unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use a Standby Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Standby Spell. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell](4cf98145-079f-44e0-9a2b-1d7b16037f4a).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the Standby Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.

assessments.title: Deployment Of Emergency Drop Spells

```solidity
function deploy(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta) public returns (address _spell)
```

The parameters of the `deploy` function are defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Protego Usage
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the usage of Protego is as follows:

- Protego can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).
- The decision to initiate the process to use Protego is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).
- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use Protego in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.
- If the decision to use Protego is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
- After the Core Facilitator decides to use Protego, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the usage of Protego and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.

Compliance on the same facts is arguable, so the score is capped at 2.

The Emergency Response System and Emergency Spells define escalation and intervention, but no mechanism penalizes a Core Facilitator's procedural lapses (missed documentation, unvalidated trigger, or failure to consult) beyond the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells are the pre-authorized intervention path when security rules, including spell-validation rules, are violated or threatened, so an unauthorized validation could trigger it. The consequence is not quantified for this roster and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Custom Spell Voting For Protego Usage
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may use the Custom Spell Voting Page when it is beneficial to coordinate voting without using the standard Spell process. The Core Facilitator must not use this method unless domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group have recommended this approach; such a recommendation must be explicitly documented in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Restricts the Core Facilitator's use of the Custom Spell Voting Page to cases where Emergency Response domain experts recommend it, documented in a named channel.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The gating condition is concrete and checkable: an explicit recommendation by domain expert Ecosystem Actors, documented in a named channel. However, "when it is beneficial" is judgment language, and there is no count of required experts, no deadline, and no verification cadence.
metrics: Recommendation from domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group is required before use
Recommendation must be explicitly documented in the Emergency Response Signal Group communication channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) and the Emergency Response System (A.1.9) provide a pre-authorized intervention and escalation path that plausibly reaches unauthorized use of the Protego voting method. The consequence for a breach is not quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: ADs' Role In Protego Usage
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use an Emergency Drop Spell, or to give authority to the Protego contract, unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5);
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use Protego or an Emergency Drop Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell, if applicable. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell](a15e7cd9-ea93-48ac-b53a-afc476ca2d05).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the usage of Protego or the Emergency Drop Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.
assessments.description: Requires Atlas Delegates to confirm specified notifications and GovOps validation before voting to use Protego or an Emergency Drop Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The pre-vote gating conditions are verifiable, naming specific channels (A.1.9.1.3.1, A.1.9.1.5.3) and an authorized-representative list, with a required written form for validation. Gaps remain: the post-confirmation duty to vote 'promptly' or resolve 'speedily' has no time bound, and the authorized validator list is delegated to another document.
metrics: Post-confirmation vote must occur 'promptly' (no duration specified)
Concern resolution must be 'speedy' (no duration specified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, on-chain gate, or named enforcer distinct from the ADs watches this confirmation duty; the only reachable path is the misalignment catch-all, and confirmation is largely self-attested by the ADs themselves.

assessments.title: AD Reliance On Core GovOps In Emergency Drop Spell Process Where Core GovOps Is Nonresponsive
assessments.quote: There is an exception to the requirement that two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of an Emergency Drop Spell. In situations where the Authorized Representatives have failed to respond to the emergency situation, the Core Facilitator may temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator the sole authority to validate the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). The Core Facilitator must communicate this in writing in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator sole authority to validate an Emergency Drop Spell when Core GovOps Authorized Representatives are unresponsive, and requires written notice.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the actors (Core Facilitator, Operational Facilitator, Core GovOps ARs) and a specific secure channel by reference, so the written-notice duty is checkable. The trigger ('failed to respond to the emergency situation') and the duration ('temporarily') have no time limit, cadence, or threshold, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Core Facilitator must communicate the grant in writing in the secure channel specified in A.1.9.1.3.1 (Emergency Response Signal Group)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) provides a defined escalation protocol for emergency grants, and Core GovOps artifact review (A.1.14.2.10) could check the required written notice and the grant's use. Neither sets a quantified consequence for this exception, and firing depends on review or escalation being triggered.

assessments.title: Misalignment To Vote For Unvalidated Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.quote: It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for an Emergency Drop Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated.
assessments.description: Defines a vote for an unvalidated Emergency Drop Spell as severe misalignment for Aligned Delegates, with derecognition and buffer confiscation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Aligned Delegate), the prohibited act, and concrete remedies (immediate derecognition, full AD Buffer confiscation) are stated. However, the validation standard that defines a breach is delegated to a cross-referenced section, and 'should' softens the confiscation obligation.
metrics: immediately derecognized
full AD Buffer confiscated (should be)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states concrete remedies (derecognition, full buffer confiscation), and Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) plus Penalty Mechanisms can reach security-rule violations. No named enforcer or escalation path is stated here, and the confiscation is 'should' rather than mandatory, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Protego Usage Accountability
assessments.quote: Breach of any requirement concerning Emergency Spells - including usage of Protego - constitutes misalignment and must be addressed pursuant to [A.1.9.1.6 - Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness](8df982ee-754c-4cd9-a5f9-ce1c30e06cf8).
assessments.description: Classes breaches of Emergency Spell requirements, including Protego usage, as misalignment routed to an accountability process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph creates a real routing obligation (breach is misalignment and must be handled under a named accountability rule), but it sets no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria for what counts as a breach. The operative content lives in the referenced A.1.9.1.6 document, which is not reproduced here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The only consequence path is the misalignment catch-all (Reports of Misalignment / Adjudication), which is weak alone. The linked accountability document 8df982ee is named but its penalties or escalation are not described in this text, so no specific mechanism is shown to reach this rule.

assessments.title: Emergency Process For Misaligned Agent Artifacts
assessments.quote: In an emergency situation (see [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)), Sky Core has the discretion to immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function if it reasonably suspects that the Artifact is contributing towards a significant or system-level risk. Sky Core must act in good faith when exercising its discretion in emergency situations.
assessments.description: Lets Sky Core immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function in an emergency it reasonably suspects poses significant risk, acting in good faith.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative trigger is judgment language: "reasonably suspects" and "significant or system-level risk" have no defined criteria or thresholds. The emergency definition is delegated by cross-reference to A.1.9.1.1, and "immediately" is the only timing term, with no deadline or notice requirement.
metrics: "immediately" suspension timing (no defined deadline or notice period)
"reasonably suspects" standard for triggering suspension
"significant or system-level risk" threshold (undefined)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is itself the remedial power: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) pre-authorize executive suspensions when security rules are threatened, and the Emergency Response System (A.1.9) supplies an escalation path outside the standard governance cycle. Neither quantifies a consequence for the Artifact, and invoking the suspension depends on Sky Core deciding to act.

assessments.title: Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain a `Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Requires every Agent Artifact to include a direct-child Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response document describing ecosystem-wide emergency protocol.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a verifiable structural requirement: the document must exist as a direct child of a named parent. The substantive obligation, a protocol that is 'applicable' to ecosystem-wide situations, has no defined content, criteria, or triggers, so a defender could argue compliance by including any such document.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment, which would plausibly catch a missing required omni document. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and the review's escalation has to be triggered.

assessments.title: Agent Emergency Response
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain an `Agent-Specific Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations solely impacting the Agent, versus the broader Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Requires every Agent Artifact to include an Agent-Specific Emergency Response document as a direct child of Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The structural requirement (a named document placed as a direct child of a named parent) is verifiable from the artifact tree. The operative content obligation, to specify an emergency response protocol for Agent-only versus ecosystem-wide situations, has no thresholds, required elements, or criteria, so compliance with the content is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a distinct enforcer that can find a missing required Omni Document and assess penalties. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on the review being run.

assessments.title: Executor Agent Facilitators
assessments.quote: Executor Agent Facilitators are Facilitators that carry out specific activities on behalf of Executor Agents. Whenever an Executor Agent must interpret an Artifact, that interpretation must be done by the Facilitator. Whenever an Executor Agent has privileged access to smart contracts of Sky or an Agent, that access must be held by the Facilitator. Facilitators use this access to carry out the Executor Agent’s operational responsibilities as directed by GovOps, unless the Facilitator believes that GovOps is misaligned.
assessments.description: Requires Executor Agent Facilitators to interpret Artifacts and hold privileged smart-contract access for Executor Agents, using it as GovOps directs unless misaligned.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Role allocation is concrete: Facilitators must interpret Artifacts and hold privileged access. However, 'specific activities' is undefined and the 'unless the Facilitator believes GovOps is misaligned' exception is purely subjective, with no thresholds, metrics, or cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when security rules covering privileged contract access are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches misuse of that access. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the paragraph itself only offers the misalignment catch-all.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer
assessments.quote: The Demand Side Buffer is the account used for disbursement of Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments. The Demand Side Buffer is controlled by a multisig as specified in the documents herein. The balance of this account may be topped up through an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Describes the Demand Side Buffer account used for Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payouts, its multisig control, and Executive Vote top-ups.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (a multisig) and a process (Executive Vote top-ups), but gives no thresholds, caps, or cadence. Control is delegated to 'the documents herein' without stating the operative signing or disbursement criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Multisig control is self-enforcement by the custodian, and Executive Vote top-ups are a governance process with no stated consequence for misuse. No cited mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or artifact review) is shown to reach disbursement misconduct from this text.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Demand Side Buffer Multisig has a 2/3 signing requirement.
assessments.description: Requires the Demand Side Buffer Multisig to use a 2-of-3 signing threshold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 2/3 threshold is a concrete, verifiable parameter that a third party could check on-chain. It does not name the signer set or the scope of transactions the threshold covers.
metrics: Signing requirement: 2 of 3 signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. A multisig threshold is arguably self-enforcing on-chain, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph reaches this rule, so it is rated weak.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote: The signers of the Demand Side Buffer Multisig must use the Multisig to disburse Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments in accordance with the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires Demand Side Buffer Multisig signers to use the multisig to disburse Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments per the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Demand Side Buffer Multisig signers) and a controlled system, but has no threshold, cadence, or deadline. Its operative standard, 'in accordance with the Atlas', is delegated to other text, so compliance is arguable on the paragraph alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized freezes or pauses when security rules are violated, which could reach unauthorized multisig disbursements. No quantified penalty applies to this rule, and firing depends on someone escalating a violation as a security breach.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Modification
assessments.quote: Operational GovOps Soter Labs can change the signers of the Demand Side Buffer Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least three (3) signers and at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions.
assessments.description: Lets Soter Labs change Demand Side Buffer Multisig signers at any time, provided at least three signers and a two-thirds execution threshold remain.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Operational GovOps Soter Labs) and gives exact numeric constraints: at least three signers and at least two-thirds of signers required to execute. A third party could verify compliance from the multisig's configuration alone.
metrics: at least three (3) signers
at least two-thirds of signers required to execute transactions
signer changes permitted at any time
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a separate enforcer with penalty assessment and could reach a signer change that breaks the minimum-signer or threshold limits. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could freeze the multisig if a security rule is threatened. Neither states a quantified consequence for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Auxiliary Accounts
assessments.quote:
Operational GovOps Soter Labs may establish auxiliary accounts on other blockchains to facilitate efficient distribution of Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments to Integrators operating on those blockchains. Operational GovOps Soter Labs may move funds from the Demand Side Buffer Multisig to auxiliary accounts as necessary to facilitate such payments. Each auxiliary account must conform to the same standards as the Demand Side Buffer Multisig, specifically:

- a minimum of three (3) signers;
- at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions; and
- all signers are controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.
assessments.description: Permits Soter Labs to create multisig auxiliary accounts on other chains and sets minimum signer count, approval threshold, and control requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligations are quantified: at least three signers, at least two-thirds of signers required to execute, and all signers controlled by Soter Labs. Gaps remain: 'as necessary' is undefined, 'controlled by' is not operationalized, the 'same standards' are incorporated by reference to the Demand Side Buffer Multisig, and no review cadence is stated.
metrics: minimum of three (3) signers
at least two-thirds of signers required to execute transactions
all signers controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review Operational GovOps' configuration of auxiliary accounts with penalty assessment, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can freeze funds if signer-security rules are violated or threatened. Neither consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and invoking either requires an escalation step.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Target Chain Identification And Feasibility Analysis
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent researches potential target blockchains for token bridging, including evaluation of user base, DeFi ecosystem, and bridging security requirements. The Prime Agent confirms that the target chain supports LayerZero or can be integrated easily with the LayerZero Omnichain Fungible Token standard. The Prime Agent also estimates potential use of the token on the target chain to justify the bridge deployment and audit costs. The output of this step is a preliminary decision to proceed with deploying a bridge to the target chain including a scope of work for the bridge deployment and estimated audit costs.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to research target chains for token bridging and output a preliminary deployment decision with scope and audit cost estimates.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor, enumerated research steps, and a defined output (a preliminary decision with scope and audit cost estimate). The operative criteria are judgment language, such as 'evaluation of user base', 'can be integrated easily', and 'estimates potential use', with no numeric thresholds, cost bounds, or deadlines.
metrics: Target chain must support LayerZero or be integrable 'easily' with the LayerZero OFT standard (no threshold for 'easily')
Output must include a scope of work and estimated audit costs (no value or cap specified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The output is a documented deployment decision and cost estimate, which Core GovOps artifact review could examine and assess for penalties. No consequence is quantified for this specific research step, and the review would need to be triggered.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Initial Alignment With Operational GovOps
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent presents the bridging plan to Operational GovOps, including a technical summary, proposed timeline, and estimate of audit costs. The Prime Agent and Operational GovOps also discuss any guidelines in the Atlas or the Agent Artifact that may affect bridging. The Prime Agent receives early feedback on the plan and modifies it accordingly. The output of this step is an informal agreement to proceed with developing a bridge deployment along with any documented conditions or feedback from Operational GovOps.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to present a token bridging plan to Operational GovOps and reach an informal agreement before bridge development.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors and enumerates steps (presentation, discussion, feedback, plan modification), but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria for the plan's contents. The output, an 'informal agreement', and 'early feedback' are judgment-based, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The step is a procedural alignment meeting with no penalty, escalation, or on-chain control attached. Violation would only reach the generic misalignment catch-all, and the Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) does not clearly cover this pre-development alignment step.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Audit Preparation And Proposal Of Costs
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent contacts a reputable third-party security audit firm for reviewing the bridge implementation. The Prime Agent negotiates audit scope, timeline, and fees with the audit firm. The Prime Agent documents the projected cost for the bridge, including development, audit, and deployment costs, for future reimbursement. The outcome of this step is a formal agreement with the audit firm and a detailed cost breakdown for bridge deployment and auditing.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to engage a reputable audit firm, negotiate audit terms, and document projected bridge costs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor and enumerates process steps, but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or cost limits. 'Reputable' and 'detailed cost breakdown' are judgment terms with no defined criteria, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine the audit agreement and cost breakdown, which are the rule's outputs, and the Penalty Mechanisms could reach a failure to document costs for reimbursement. Neither consequence is quantified for this specific step.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Bridge Deployment And Initial Audit
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent, through Operational GovOps, deploys the Token SkyLink contract on the target chain. The Prime Agent shares the Token SkyLink contract’s final address with the audit firm for verification. Operational GovOps confirms that the bridge contract address and references match the updated Prime Agent Artifact. The audit firm completes and updates the bridging audit registry with the results of the audit. The output of this step is a deployed bridge contract with audit results uploaded to the bridging audit registry.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent and Operational GovOps to deploy the Token SkyLink bridge contract, verify its address, and have an audit firm record results.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors (Prime Agent, Operational GovOps, audit firm) and an ordered sequence of steps, but sets no deadline, no audit pass or fail criteria, and no verification standard beyond address and reference matching. Whether the audit was properly completed is therefore arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review the updated Prime Agent Artifact that Operational GovOps must match, with penalty assessment. Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance (fd1f682c) prices poor security practice in Prime fees, which plausibly reaches an unsound bridge deployment. Neither is quantified for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Activation On New Chain
assessments.quote: Core GovOps formalizes the audit results with a Sky Core Executive Vote to fully activate bridging functionality. Operational GovOps updates the Prime Agent Reimbursement Module to begin counting any bridged tokens toward the incremental reward. The output of this step is fully enabled bridging on the target chain with the Prime Agent Reimbursement Module updated to track bridging based rewards.
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to formalize audit results via an Executive Vote before fully activating token bridging on a new chain, and Operational GovOps to update reward tracking.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors and an ordered sequence (audit, Executive Vote, reimbursement module update) are present, but the paragraph sets no criteria for what audit result is sufficient to activate bridging and no deadline. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could pause bridging activated without a passing audit. Nothing in the paragraph itself ties the activation step to that mechanism, and no consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: List of Active Token SkyLink Deployments
assessments.quote: The Token SkyLink Primitive must list each active Token SkyLink deployment. The listing must include the following information: (1), the token being bridged, (2) the target chain of the bridge, (3) the address of the bridge contract on the Ethereum Mainnet, (4) the address of the bridge contract on the target chain, (5) the audit of the bridge contract, (6) the bridge parameters, (7) the total bridge deployment and audit costs, and (8) the amount of bridge deployment and audit costs that have been reimbursed to date.
assessments.description: Requires the Token SkyLink Primitive to list each active bridge deployment with eight specified information fields.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete: each active deployment must be listed with eight enumerated fields, which a third party could check for presence. Gaps include no update cadence, no location or format for the listing, and undefined terms such as 'bridge parameters' and 'audit'.
metrics: Each active Token SkyLink deployment must be listed

Eight required fields: bridged token, target chain, Ethereum Mainnet bridge contract address, target-chain bridge contract address, bridge contract audit, bridge parameters, total deployment and audit costs, amount of costs reimbursed to date
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can review published listings and assess penalties, which plausibly reaches a missing or incomplete deployment listing. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and firing depends on a review being scheduled and escalated.

assessments.title: Base Tracking Methodology
assessments.quote: The Tracking Methodology for Base is to specify the Reward Code as a parameter in calls to the Base PSM contract. Conversions from USDS or USDC to sUSDS are considered "deposits" and net deposits are calculated using an approach similar to that on Ethereum Mainnet.
assessments.description: Specifies how Base distribution-reward tracking records PSM calls, deposits, and net deposits, using a Reward Code parameter.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Reward Code parameter in Base PSM calls and the definition of USDS/USDC-to-sUSDS conversions as deposits are concrete and checkable. Net deposit calculation is delegated to an approach 'similar to that on Ethereum Mainnet' with no formula or thresholds.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a reward-accounting methodology with no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism tied to correct tracking; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Allocation System Primitive
assessments.quote: The Allocation System Primitive is the base mechanism that enables Prime Agents to put up Risk Capital to deploy USDS collateral into different opportunities that provide risk-adjusted return, by borrowing at the Base Rate from Sky, and following Asset Liability Management restrictions on the liquidity of deployed assets.
assessments.description: Defines the Allocation System Primitive as the mechanism letting Primes deploy USDS by borrowing at Base Rate under ALM liquidity restrictions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real obligation exists (borrow at the Base Rate from Sky and follow ALM liquidity restrictions), but the Base Rate value and the ALM restrictions are not quantified in this paragraph. Compliance could be argued either way without the referenced parameters.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules, which plausibly covers the Prime's Risk Capital-backed allocation and ALM restrictions. The consequence is not quantified for this paragraph's rule, so it rates mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Designation Process
assessments.quote: Sky Direct Exposures are designated by the Core Facilitator in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor via posts to the Sky Forum under the "Sky Core" category. Sky Direct Exposures are recorded in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.2.0.6.1 - List Of Current Sky Direct Exposures](5f368e33-7a82-4244-a9ba-f285193ec043) and must specify the asset that is being designated as a Sky Direct Exposure and the Prime Agent responsible for implementing the exposure.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to designate Sky Direct Exposures via Sky Forum posts and record them with asset and responsible Prime Agent.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core Facilitator, Core Council Risk Advisor), a defined channel (Sky Forum), and required record fields are specified. However, there are no designation criteria, no meaning for 'in consultation', and no deadlines.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism reaches the designation act itself. The referenced list UUID is a record, not an enforcement mechanism, so only the misalignment catch-all applies.

assessments.title: Current Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.quote:
The list of current Sky Direct Exposures is defined as Active Data in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.2.0.6.1 - List Of Current Sky Direct Exposures](5f368e33-7a82-4244-a9ba-f285193ec043).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.description: Designates the Core Facilitator as responsible for updating the list of current Sky Direct Exposures via the Direct Edit protocol.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Core Facilitator) and a referenced update procedure (Direct Edit), but gives no thresholds, cadence, or deadlines. Compliance depends on what the referenced Active Data and Direct Edit protocol contain, which this text does not state.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Direct Edit protocol is referenced but is not a catalog enforcement mechanism, and the only UUID in the text points to the list itself. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Rate Limits
assessments.quote:
Rate limits set the maximum allowable amount of tokens that can be processed for specific operations within a given time period. Each rate limit contains the rate limit data: `maxAmount`, `slope`, `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated`. The current rate limit is calculated using the formula:

`currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount)`.

The rate limit data `maxAmount` and `slope` are configurable parameters that are set and modified by Governance. The rate limit data `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated` are internal state data dynamically tracked by the Rate Limiter to perform its calculations.

Rate limits set caps on the rate of allocation to a given Instance, they do not act as a limit on the total amount that may be allocated to that Instance.
assessments.description: Defines on-chain rate limits capping how much of a token can be processed per time period, with a time-decay formula and governance-set parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The exact formula for currentRateLimit is given, and the four state variables are named. However, the governance-set values for maxAmount and slope are not stated, and the paragraph does not define the tokens or operations covered or the time units of slope.
metrics: currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount)
maxAmount: governance-configurable cap on allowable amount
slope: governance-configurable rate of increase per unit time
lastAmount and lastUpdated: internal Rate Limiter state, no stated values
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The formula is applied by the Rate Limiter in code, which is a form of automatic constraint, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph is tied to it, so none found that is citable. Without a citable mechanism, the rating is weak.

assessments.title: MaxAmount
assessments.quote: `maxAmount` sets a hard cap on the level of allocation to an Instance at any given time. It sets the absolute rate limit regardless of how much time has passed since the last allocation. For example, if `maxAmount` is set to 1,000,000 tokens, the rate limit will increase over time at the rate determined by the `slope` until it reaches 1,000,000 tokens. At this point the rate limit will stop increasing, but it will resume increasing once an allocation to the Instance has been made.
assessments.description: Defines maxAmount as a hard cap on allocation to an Instance, with the rate limit rising at slope until reaching it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The cap is a named parameter with a clear accumulation formula (rate limit grows at slope until maxAmount, then resumes after an allocation), and a worked example of 1,000,000 tokens. The slope is defined elsewhere without a value, and the rule does not state the cadence of the accrual or the governance-set value of maxAmount itself.
metrics: maxAmount: hard cap on allocation level to an Instance at any time
Rate limit increases over time at the rate set by slope until it reaches maxAmount
Rate limit resumes increasing after a new allocation to the Instance
Example: maxAmount = 1,000,000 tokens
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule is a parameter-level rate limit with no penalty, liquidation, or escalation path cited, and no catalog mechanism reaches allocation-cap violations. The on-chain implementation is implied but not documented in this paragraph, so it cannot be cited.

assessments.title: Outflow Rate Limits
assessments.quote:
Outflow Rate Limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced from a scope. "Outflow" means movements that lower exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as withdrawals, redemptions, or unwind operations.

Outflow limits are often configured more permissively to prioritize safety and fast exits. When outflow limits are "unlimited," the rate limits contract simply does not apply a cap in that direction.
assessments.description: Defines outflow rate limits as caps on how fast allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced, and notes that unlimited outflow means no cap.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is definitional: it names outflow rate limits and what "outflow" covers, but states no cap value, rate, window, or formula. Nothing in the text can be checked for compliance, so a defender could argue it imposes no obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph mentions a rate limits contract that applies no cap when unlimited, but describes no consequence for breaching a configured limit, and no catalog mechanism is tied to outflow rate limits.

assessments.title: MaxSlippage
assessments.quote: `maxSlippage` is a configurable parameter that sets the maximum allowed price impact or deviation from expected output when executing trades or liquidity operations in a pool. `maxslippage` is expressed as a decimal and must be a non-zero value. This protects against excessive price impact during volatile market conditions.

assessments.title: Hop Definition
assessments.quote:
The `hop` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive increases any cBEAM makes to the same rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope`. Its value is set per `RateLimits` contract, but the interval is tracked independently for each rate limit within it, so increasing one rate limit does not affect when another can next be increased. A decrease is not subject to `hop`.

Changes to the `hop` parameter are proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), or made directly via an Executive Vote at any time, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4 - PAS](989171ed-5424-42ee-83f4-199e1149699c).
assessments.description: Sets a minimum per-rate-limit interval between cBEAM increases to maxAmount or slope, exempts decreases, and governs who may change hop.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a formula-like constraint: a per-rate-limit minimum interval in seconds applies to increases only, with decreases exempt. The hop value itself is not stated and is delegated to each RateLimits contract's setting, and no default or bounds are given.
metrics: Minimum time interval in seconds between consecutive increases to the same rate limit's maxAmount or slope
Interval tracked independently per rate limit within each RateLimits contract
Decreases to maxAmount or slope are not subject to hop
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The hop constraint is likely enforced by the RateLimits contract on-chain, but no catalog mechanism documents that. Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) is the only cited path that could freeze or pause a cBEAM that breaches a security rule, and the text does not say the spell fires on a hop violation, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Max Change Definition
assessments.quote:
The `maxChange` parameter, defined per `RateLimits` contract, bounds how far a cBEAM may raise a rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope` in a single adjustment: the new value cannot exceed the higher of the current value multiplied by `maxChange`, or that rate limit's own registered default.

`maxChange` itself can only be set to zero or to `WAD` (`10**18`, a multiplier of one (1)) or more; it cannot be set to a fractional multiplier below one (1).

Changes to the `maxChange` parameter are proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), or made directly via an Executive Vote at any time, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4 - PAS](989171ed-5424-42ee-83f4-199e1149699c).
assessments.description: Caps how much a cBEAM can raise a rate limit's maxAmount or slope per adjustment, and sets maxChange's minimum value.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The cap formula (new value at most the higher of current × maxChange or the registered default) and the lower bound (zero or at least WAD) are explicit and checkable. Gaps remain: 'cBEAM' and 'registered default' are defined elsewhere, and the text gives no cadence for 'single adjustment'.

assessments.title: Locked Unlimited Rate Limit Definition
assessments.quote:
A rate limit is locked as unlimited, and a cBEAM must keep it at a `maxAmount` equal to the maximum uint256 value with a zero slope, in either of two (2) cases:

- It has a default of that same value.
- It already holds that value on the `RateLimits` contract and has no default at all. A rate limit that is already unlimited is locked the same way whether or not it was ever registered.

Registering a default other than the unlimited value removes that lock.
assessments.description: Locks cBEAM rate limits at unlimited uint256 maxAmount with zero slope when defaulted or already unlimited on RateLimits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives exact values (maxAmount equal to the maximum uint256, zero slope), names the actor (cBEAM), and enumerates two conditions that trigger the lock. A third party could verify compliance from the text alone.

slope equals zero
lock applies when default equals the maximum uint256 value

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach an unauthorized change to a locked rate limit. No consequence is quantified for this rule, and firing requires escalation.

assessments.title: Core Council Multisig
assessments.quote:
The Core Council Multisig (`coreCouncil`) can call any of BeamState's immediate functions directly, without a Spell, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6), including halting Configurator operations as an emergency action. Sky Governance can independently halt Configurator operations or pause the Timelock through the PASMom contract, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71) and [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8).

The Core Council Multisig proposes and can cancel changes to BeamState's delayed registries and bounds on the Timelock, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3 - Delayed Function Calls](4a388764-7469-4efb-84f0-6b91278428fb). The Core Council Multisig also proposes restarting Configurator operations, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.5 - Restart After Halt](e049feea-5af3-4a8d-8766-36e348fd5d7b). Once the minimum delay has passed, any address may execute the proposed change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.2 - Timelock](a824d088-be58-4163-b382-54a95a728103); proposing, cancelling, and executing are all blocked while the Timelock is paused.
assessments.description: Defines Core Council Multisig powers to call immediate functions, propose and cancel delayed changes, and restart Configurator operations, subject to Timelock and PASMom controls.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Core Council Multisig, Sky Governance), enumerated powers, and named Timelock and PASMom controls are concrete, but the minimum delay is never given a value and the operative magnitudes are delegated to referenced sub-paragraphs.

The consequence is delay and pausing rather than a quantified penalty, so mid.

assessments.title: Timelock
assessments.quote:
The Timelock gates delayed changes to BeamState's registries and bounds: the Core Council Multisig proposes and can cancel a change, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), and once the minimum delay has passed, any address may execute it, since the Timelock's `EXECUTOR_ROLE` is granted to `address(0)`, making execution permissionless. Proposing, cancelling, and executing are all blocked while the Timelock is paused; only unpausing restores them. The minimum delay is fourteen (14) days.

The Timelock's `PROPOSER_ROLE` and `CANCELLER_ROLE` are held by the Core Council Multisig. Its `PAUSER_ROLE`, which can pause the Timelock, is held by PASMom, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.6 - PASMom](88e11076-5fe1-42a5-b2ba-bdb1bc929ec8). The Timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which can grant and revoke its other roles and change its minimum delay, is held by the Sky Pause Proxy.
assessments.description: Describes Timelock delay, proposer, canceller, executor, and pauser roles gating changes to BeamState registries.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 14-day minimum delay and named role holders (Core Council Multisig, PASMom, Sky Pause Proxy) are concrete and checkable against contract state. Minor gaps: DEFAULT_ADMIN can change the minimum delay, so the 14 days is not fixed, and no cadence or verification process is stated.
metrics: Minimum delay is fourteen (14) days
EXECUTOR_ROLE granted to address(0), making execution permissionless after the delay
Proposing, cancelling, and executing blocked while the Timelock is paused
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The delay and role gating are code-enforced, but no catalog mechanism describes the Timelock itself. Emergency Spells (pause by PASMom) plausibly reaches a violation, but the delay can be altered by DEFAULT_ADMIN, so the consequence is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Restart After Halt
assessments.quote:
Restarting Configurator operations after a halt is done via BeamState's `start()` function, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.8 - Start Function Call](032164e4-cf66-4e79-bb8c-18f095a1cdef). `start()` is proposed by the Core Council Multisig, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.1 - Core Council Multisig](666cf6b3-6d7a-40f7-99fb-b6e2e4375754), and takes effect only after a minimum delay has passed since being proposed. While the Timelock is paused, `start()` cannot take effect this way; restarting instead requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.5 - Transitional Measures](d5240aa5-72c1-4f92-b22c-7a80a35d733c).

Unpausing the Timelock does not route through this minimum delay, since it is gated by the Timelock's own access control rather than BeamState's role system. This holds regardless of how the Timelock came to be paused, and requires an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll — the same process specified for reversing PASMom's `pause()` in [A.1.10.3.2.13 - PASMom Exception](2171fb2b-de83-44f2-92bf-26b59a1e8c71).
assessments.description: Specifies how Configurator operations are restarted after a halt, via BeamState start() or an Executive Vote, and how the Timelock is unpaused.
