assessments.title: Operator Execution
assessments.quote:
An Operator exercises a rate limit adjustment by calling the Configurator directly. A rate limit locked as unlimited, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.3 - Locked Unlimited Rate Limit Definition](92a74fe1-3115-4cd7-bbf8-4e16fb4b0aa8), cannot be raised or lowered. Otherwise, an Operator may lower a rate limit's `maxAmount` or `slope` to any value, including to zero, at any time. It may raise either value up to the bound set by [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.2.1 - Max Change Definition](942d6607-b92c-4779-8012-ea3b259ebf2b), and only after the interval set by [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.1.1.1 - Hop Definition](dc0e3a84-b542-4985-a41b-7ae2a3921cf3) has passed since its last raise to that rate limit.

An Operator exercises a controller action by calling the Configurator to execute an enabled action on its paired Controller.

Both are unaffected by whether the Timelock is paused, but are blocked while Configurator operations are halted, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.4.10 - Stop Function Call](52895c20-8322-4cbf-800f-8ea107f00f85).
assessments.description: Governs Operator rate-limit changes and controller actions via the Configurator, including bounds on raises and halt conditions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Lowering is unrestricted and raising is bounded by a referenced Max Change Definition and Hop interval, but neither magnitude appears in this paragraph. The Locked Unlimited and Stop Function conditions are clear, while the operative limits are delegated to other documents.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The raise bound (Max Change) and cooldown (Hop) are contract-level constraints on the Configurator, so an out-of-bounds or too-early raise is blocked on-chain rather than policed by people. The Stop Function Call (52895c20) adds an emergency halt path that also reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Transitional Measures
assessments.quote:
The PAS launches with the Timelock paused, as a transitional measure, via the August 27, 2026 Executive Vote. This means that, while the Timelock is paused, the functions described below, which the Core Council Multisig otherwise proposes through the Timelock, cannot take effect. Any updates instead require an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll:

- `setHop()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.1 - Set Hop Function Call](8ead8771-c769-48d0-af2a-802099c61d42).
- `setMaxChange()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.2 - Set Max Change Function Call](da93e0a7-5fa1-4d93-af72-24557fbd9f24).
- `addRateLimits()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.3 - Add Rate Limits Function Call](87da775d-430e-4db9-b58e-bbcf323e375a).
- `addController()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.4 - Add Controller Function Call](2ef770b2-3636-4545-9aad-0f7cf94c0619).
- `addInitRateLimits()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.5 - Add Init Rate Limits Function Call](bbdf1e6a-821b-43ec-aabf-e43a3bd6e113).
- `addInitControllerActions()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.6 - Add Init Controller Actions Function Call](010a904e-e0e0-4c1d-8460-b8e3118b680f).
- `addCBeam()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.7 - Add cBEAM Function Call](33d6773e-d3d8-4141-943b-bfac186574b1).
- `start()`, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.3.8 - Start Function Call](032164e4-cf66-4e79-bb8c-18f095a1cdef).

The Core Council Multisig also cannot cancel an already-proposed delayed change while the Timelock is paused; only unpausing it, via an Executive Vote, restores that ability.

The Core Council Multisig's immediate functions, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.4.3.4 - Immediate Function Calls](2c82cfd0-7a9a-464f-844d-ebc43b31c2a6), are unaffected by the Timelock being paused, since they do not route through it.
assessments.description: Sets the Timelock to launch paused, blocking eight Core Council Multisig functions and delayed-change cancellation until an Executive Vote unpauses it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Core Council Multisig), a dated Executive Vote (August 27, 2026), and eight enumerated functions with cross-referenced specs. It lacks any stated end condition or review cadence for the transitional pause, so the duration is left open.

Immediate Function Calls unaffected by pause
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The pause is a contract-level state that physically prevents the listed functions and delayed-change cancellation from taking effect, which is self-executing for those paths. The only catalog pause machinery is Emergency Spells, which reaches the pause state only loosely since this pause is a transitional executive measure, and no quantified consequence applies to the rule's violation modes.

assessments.title: Add Liquidity To Uniswap v3 Position
assessments.quote: The Uniswap v3 Facet's `addLiquidity` function attempts to deposit the target amounts of the pool's two (2) tokens on behalf of the ALM Proxy. To open a new position, it calls the Uniswap v3 position manager's `mint` function. To add to an existing position, it calls the position manager's `increaseLiquidity` function instead — but only after confirming the ALM Proxy is the current owner of that position. Depositing into a tick range does not necessarily use the full target amount of both tokens; the Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amounts actually deposited by comparing the ALM Proxy's token balances before and after the call, rather than relying on the target amounts or the position manager's own return values. The deposit does not complete unless the tick bounds fall within the configured bounds for the pool. Before depositing, the Uniswap v3 Facet checks the specified minimums against expected amounts derived from the pool's time-weighted average price, not its current spot price. assessments.title: Rate Limit
assessments.quote:
The aggregate withdrawal limit sums one unit of either pool token as equivalent, so it is only meant to work with a stable-stable pool. Using it on a pool with two tokens of different value would produce a cap unrelated to actual exposure.

Removing liquidity is subject to three (3) on-chain withdrawal rate limits, each identified by `LIMIT_UNISWAP_V3_WITHDRAW`. One is the aggregate limit described above, metered in a normalized unit summed across both pool tokens. The other two are per-token limits, one for each of the pool's two (2) tokens, each metered in that token's own unit. All three limits are enforced automatically within the call; the transaction reverts if the amount attributed to any of the three exceeds its current rate limit.

These limits meter only the amount returned by decreasing liquidity. Fees already accrued on the position are collected in the same call but are not counted against them.

assessments.title: Remove Liquidity From Uniswap v3 Position
assessments.quote: The Uniswap v3 Facet's `removeLiquidity` function first confirms the ALM Proxy is the current owner of the position, then decreases the specified amount of liquidity from it. It does this by calling the Uniswap v3 position manager's `decreaseLiquidity` function. Before the decrease, the facet collects any fees the position has already accrued. The `decreaseLiquidity` call itself does not transfer any tokens to the ALM Proxy; it only credits the withdrawn amounts to the position as tokens owed. After the decrease, the facet collects again, and this second collection is what delivers the withdrawn principal to the ALM Proxy. The withdrawal does not complete unless the resulting amounts satisfy the specified minimums, and those minimums must in turn satisfy the configured maximum slippage for the pool. Unlike the deposit-side check on adding liquidity, this check is against the amounts actually withdrawn, measured after the decrease and both collections have already executed; it is not checked against an independent price reference computed before execution.

If the swap reaches this price limit before selling the full specified amount, execution stops without reverting, and part of the specified amount goes unsold. The Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amount actually sold by comparing the ALM Proxy's balance of the given token before and after the swap, and applies the Rate Limit against that measured amount rather than the specified amount. The swap does not complete unless the specified tick deviation falls within the configured maximum for the pool and the amount received is at least the specified minimum, which must be a non-zero value. The maximum tick deviation is the only governance-configured control on the swap's execution quality; the minimum amount received has no equivalent governance floor beyond being non-zero.

assessments.title: Role Configuration
assessments.quote:
Morpho vaults must use the following role configuration:

- The Owner role must be held by the relevant Prime Agent's SubProxy.
- The Curator role must be held by a Multisig jointly controlled by the Operational Executor Agent and either the relevant Prime Agent or an external curator. The Multisig must require a 2 of 2 signer approval threshold.
- The Allocator role may be held by an externally owned account or Multisig controlled by the relevant Prime Agent or an external curator, or by the Morpho Public Allocator contract. Where the Morpho Public Allocator contract holds the Allocator role, any emergency action that withdraws vault assets from a market must also set the Public Allocator's caps for that market to zero, so that the Public Allocator cannot reallocate assets back into that market.
- The Sentinel role must be held by at least one (1) address controlled by the Operational Executor Agent, using a signer set separate from the signer set controlling the Curator role. Additional Sentinel addresses may be designated. These additional Sentinel addresses are recommended but not required, and no restriction applies to who may control them. Any automated monitoring solution serving as a Sentinel must be capable of automatically revoking pending actions when it detects a threat.
assessments.description: Specifies required role holders, multisig thresholds, and Public Allocator cap handling for Morpho vault Owner, Curator, Allocator, and Sentinel roles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Core obligations are quantified: the Curator Multisig requires a 2-of-2 threshold, at least one Sentinel address is mandated, and Public Allocator caps must be set to zero on emergency withdrawals. Gaps remain: "external curator" is undefined, the threat-detection trigger for automatic revocation has no criteria, and no verification cadence is stated.

At least one (1) Sentinel address controlled by the Operational Executor Agent
Public Allocator caps for the withdrawn market must be set to zero on emergency action

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can freeze or pause when security rules are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches a misconfigured Curator or Sentinel. Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry raises insurance fees for poor security practice, but neither consequence is quantified for this specific role configuration rule.

WBTC maximum liquidation LTV: 86%
sUSDS maximum liquidation LTV: 96.5%
Instance Financial CRR must account for any difference between the 86% limit and the risk-model limit for cbBTC, WBTC, and stETH
Unlisted collateral requires due diligence and Core Council approval before adoption
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Positions that breach the liquidation LTV limit are liquidated under the contract-enforced Liquidation Penalty, an on-chain automatic cost that applies to collateral-limit violations without a human in the loop.

assessments.title: Multi-Source Oracle Methodology
assessments.quote: Oracle-based market pricing must use Chainlink, RedStone, and Chronicle as its sources. When all three (3) sources are available and valid, the median of those sources must be used. If only two (2) valid sources are available, the average of those sources must be used. If only one (1) valid source is available, a credible fallback source must be used.
assessments.description: Requires oracle prices to come from three named sources, aggregated by median, average, or fallback depending on how many are valid.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The aggregation logic is enumerated by source count (3 median, 2 average, 1 fallback), but 'valid' and 'credible' are undefined and no rule covers zero valid sources. Staleness, deviation, and cadence thresholds are absent.
metrics: Three sources: Chainlink, RedStone, Chronicle
All three available and valid: use median
Two valid sources: use average
One valid source: use a credible fallback source
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can freeze or pause when a security rule is violated or threatened, which could reach manipulated or misapplied oracle pricing. No quantified penalty attaches to using the wrong source or aggregation method, so the rating is capped at mid.

assessments.title: Eligible Collateral Oracle Methodologies
assessments.quote:
The following pricing methods apply to eligible collateral assets and must comply with the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1 - Multi-Source Oracle Methodology](191fbabc-d4e1-4ec4-9ea8-35b80eb809b0) for any market-pricing component:

- ETH: oracle market pricing.
- cbBTC: BTC oracle market pricing.
- stETH: the wstETH-to-ETH contract exchange rate multiplied by the ETH oracle market price.
- WBTC: oracle market pricing.
- sUSDS: the sUSDS-to-USDS contract exchange rate multiplied by the USDS oracle market price.
assessments.description: Specifies oracle and exchange-rate pricing formulas for ETH, cbBTC, stETH, WBTC, and sUSDS eligible collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each asset has an explicit pricing formula, and the stETH and sUSDS formulas multiply named contract exchange rates by named oracle prices. The base 'oracle market pricing' is delegated to A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1 without a stated value, source, or update cadence.
metrics: ETH price = oracle market price
cbBTC price = BTC oracle market price
stETH price = wstETH-to-ETH contract exchange rate × ETH oracle market price
WBTC price = oracle market pricing
sUSDS price = sUSDS-to-USDS contract exchange rate × USDS oracle market price
Market-pricing components must comply with the Multi-Source Oracle Methodology (A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Collateral prices feed the on-chain Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b), which automatically penalizes positions that breach collateral requirements, so mispricing has a contract-level cost. The rule has no specific consequence of its own, and the penalty is not quantified for pricing-method violations.

assessments.title: Temporary Single-Source Oracle Exception
assessments.quote: A single-source Chainlink oracle may be used temporarily for a major collateral asset. Such a configuration should migrate toward the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.2.3.1 - Multi-Source Oracle Methodology](191fbabc-d4e1-4ec4-9ea8-35b80eb809b0), following the structure used by SparkLend and on a schedule coordinated with the affected Prime Agent to avoid unnecessary operational disruption.
assessments.description: Permits a temporary single-source Chainlink oracle for a major collateral asset and says it should migrate to multi-source oracles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The exception has no duration, no defined threshold for 'major collateral asset', and no migration deadline. 'May' and 'should' are non-binding, and the timing is delegated to coordination with the affected Prime Agent, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Spell Security Registry's risk-based insurance pricing raises a Prime's fees for poor security practice, which can reach a single-source oracle configuration. The paragraph sets no consequence or deadline for this rule, so the mechanism is only plausibly applicable.

assessments.title: New Collateral Oracle Approval
assessments.quote: The oracle methodology for any new collateral asset requires due diligence and approval by the [A.0.1.1.46 - Core Council](5a03a0c4-a47a-409c-9b23-52ac93e63d45) before adoption.
assessments.description: Requires Core Council due diligence and approval of a new collateral asset's oracle methodology before adoption.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real gate exists with a named approver (Core Council) and a timing point (before adoption), but 'due diligence' has no criteria, checklist, or threshold, so compliance on the same facts is arguable. No cadence, deadline, or measurable condition is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states an approval gate but names no penalty, escalation, or remedy for adopting an oracle without approval, and no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, emergency spells, artifact review) is tied to this rule. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop would reach it.

assessments.title: Interest Rate Requirements
assessments.quote: Morpho Blue variable-rate markets must use the Morpho Adaptive Curve Interest Rate Model (https://docs.morpho.org/developers/contracts/irm/#adaptivecurveirm). Morpho Midnight fixed-rate markets use market-set rates rather than an interest rate model. A maker posts an offer at a price in a fixed-maturity market, and the implied fixed rate for the remaining term is locked when a taker executes the offer.
assessments.description: Requires Morpho Blue variable-rate markets to use the Adaptive Curve IRM and describes market-set fixed rates in Midnight.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific interest rate model (Morpho Adaptive Curve IRM, with a reference URL), so a third party could check market configuration. It states no numeric parameters, and the Midnight clause is descriptive rather than a binding obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism reaches the choice of interest rate model in a Morpho market; liquidation and penalty machinery govern collateral and Risk Capital breaches, not market configuration.

assessments.title: Vault Timelock Requirements
assessments.quote:
Morpho vaults must use at least the following timelock delays for protected functions:

| Action | Minimum Timelock Delay |
| --- | --- |
| Abdicate | seven (7) days |
| Add adapter | seven (7) days |
| Increase absolute cap | seven (7) days |
| Increase relative cap | seven (7) days |
| Increase timelock duration | seven (7) days |
| Remove adapter | seven (7) days |
| Set adapter registry | seven (7) days |
| Set management fee | three (3) days |
| Set management fee recipient | three (3) days |
| Set performance fee | three (3) days |
| Set performance fee recipient | three (3) days |
| Set receive assets gate | seven (7) days |
| Set receive shares gate | seven (7) days |
| Set send assets gate | seven (7) days |
| Set send shares gate | seven (7) days |

The following functions must not be subject to a timelock delay:

- Adding or removing an allocator, so that a compromised allocator can be removed immediately.
- Setting the force deallocate penalty, so that a penalty can be introduced immediately in response to a griefing attack.

Decreases to absolute or relative caps may be executed without delay. A decrease to a function's timelock duration is subject to that function's then-current timelock delay. For the Set adapter registry, Set receive assets gate, Set receive shares gate, and Set send shares gate functions, permanently abdicating the function is accepted in place of the timelock delay.
assessments.description: Sets minimum timelock delays for protected Morpho vault functions and bars timelocks on allocator changes and force-deallocate penalty settings.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each protected action has an exact minimum delay in days (3 or 7), with explicit exemptions and rules for decreasing caps and timelock durations. A third party could check compliance directly against the table and bullet list.

Add adapter: minimum 7 days

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a vault that shortens or bypasses its protected-function delays or a compromised allocator. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the on-chain timelock itself has no citable catalog entry.

assessments.title: Adapter Timelock Requirements

Adapters used by Morpho vaults must use at least the following timelock delays for protected adapter functions:

| Action | Minimum Timelock Delay |

assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each protected function has a numeric minimum delay in days, which is verifiable. The rule does not define 'protected adapter functions' beyond the table, and it does not name who certifies compliance.

assessments.title: Eligible Chains
assessments.quote: Morpho vaults may initially be deployed on Ethereum Mainnet, Base, and Robinhood Chain. Deployment on any other chain requires a risk review.
assessments.description: Limits initial Morpho vault deployment to three named chains and requires a risk review for any other chain.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The permitted chains are enumerated concretely, but 'initially' has no defined end point and the 'risk review' required for other chains has no defined reviewer, criteria, or deadline. Compliance for non-listed chains is therefore only partly checkable from the text.
metrics: Initial permitted deployment chains: Ethereum Mainnet, Base, Robinhood Chain
Deployment on any other chain requires a prior risk review (no criteria, reviewer, or deadline stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess deployment configuration with staged findings and penalty assessment, and Emergency Spells can freeze deployments when security rules are violated or threatened. Neither is tied to this chain list, and the consequence for an unreviewed chain deployment is unquantified, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Transition And Compliance
assessments.quote:
Notwithstanding the other requirements of the Morpho Vault Curation Framework, Morpho vault exposure existing as of August 17, 2026, must be migrated to new vaults or upgraded to comply with the framework no later than the execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote. Migration may be staged to account for underlying market utilization and existing vault configurations, but must be completed by that time.

Following the execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote, noncompliant Morpho vault allocations are subject to the Instance Financial CRR specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.3.8.2 - Noncompliant Morpho Vault Allocations](20aa9663-214b-46f5-8b37-53be387b996b).
assessments.description: Requires existing Morpho vault exposure to be migrated or upgraded to framework compliance by the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Two hard dates are stated: existing exposure as of August 17, 2026, and completion by execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote. Compliance itself is delegated to the Morpho Vault Curation Framework, and staging is left open-ended, so the interim standard is not defined.

Migration must be completed no later than execution of the October 8, 2026 Executive Vote
Post-October 8, 2026 noncompliant Morpho vault allocations are subject to the Instance Financial CRR in 20aa9663-214b-46f5-8b37-53be387b996b
assessments.enforcementReasoning: After the October 8, 2026 vote, noncompliant allocations face the Instance Financial CRR (20aa9663), a capital requirement whose penalty machinery (Penalty Mechanisms, b8ee2d12) plausibly reaches the violation. The consequence is not quantified in this paragraph, and before the deadline there is no enforcement path.

assessments.title: Pull Request Approval Requirements

Gaps remain: "Prime Agent Liquidity Layer repositories" is not defined by enumeration or criteria, and approval quality (e.g., code-owner or reviewer independence from the author) is unspecified.

assessments.title: Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig
assessments.quote: Each Liquidity Layer must include at least one (1) Freezer Multisig, holding the emergency authority to remove a compromised or malicious address authorized to submit allocation operations. Each Freezer Multisig must use the default configuration specified in the documents herein unless a deviation has been approved as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3 - Default Configuration Deviations](3b9336c2-53c8-4967-ab45-a2f8c5a36556).
assessments.description: Requires each Liquidity Layer to have at least one Freezer Multisig able to remove compromised allocation addresses, using default configuration unless deviation is approved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The minimum count of one Freezer Multisig per Liquidity Layer is concrete and checkable. The default configuration is delegated to other documents, and the deviation approval process is only cross-referenced without stated criteria.
metrics: At least one (1) Freezer Multisig per Liquidity Layer
Each Freezer Multisig uses the default configuration unless a deviation is approved per A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain check, or escalation is attached to lacking a Freezer Multisig or deviating from default configuration; the deviation cross-reference (3b9336c2) is an approval path, not an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Freezer Multisig has a default 2/5 signing requirement. This default is below the baseline threshold specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98) and applies under the standing exemption for emergency-response Multisigs specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.2.1 - Emergency-Response Multisig Threshold Exception](55f1c795-0653-4dda-9f05-b3068d2608e3).

However, the baseline threshold it is said to fall below is defined only by reference to another paragraph without a value here, and the exemption's scope is delegated to that paragraph, so compliance cannot be fully checked from this text alone.
metrics: Freezer Multisig default signing requirement: 2 of 5 signers
Baseline threshold (A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1): value not stated in this paragraph

Emergency Spells (b8266c11) govern the freezer's emergency actions and could reach a threshold violation, but no consequence is quantified for this specific signing rule.

assessments.title: Required Signers

It is still a default, and the text does not say how or when composition may deviate, how often it is verified, or what happens if a signer is unavailable.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named approvers and a recording step are concrete, but there is no approval criterion, threshold, deadline, or definition of what counts as a deviation. Compliance depends on undefined judgment in the approval.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The approval gate names Core GovOps and the Workstream Lead, but no consequence is stated for unapproved deviations. No catalog mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, artifact review) is shown to reach this rule, so only the catch-all backstop applies.

The list of approved deviations is defined as Active Data in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.6.2.1.3.1.0.6.1 - Approved Deviations](c304cb9f-ab10-4d5b-8f94-588170b36a9e).

No penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or artifact review is cited as reaching edits to this list, and the referenced UUIDs are data and definition documents rather than enforcement mechanisms.

assessments.title: Initial Concept And Feasibility Discussions
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent identifies a yield opportunity on a target chain that can exceed the Base Rate. The Prime Agent estimates Required Risk Capital (RRC) and Asset Liability Management requirements associated with the opportunity and evaluates options for fulfilling them. The Prime Agent also considers exchange and bridging costs, if applicable. Based on this, the Prime Agent develops a net yield target for the opportunity factoring in all of these costs. The output of this step is an internal meeting note summarizing the idea as well as estimates of Required Risk Capital, Asset Liability Management, and exchange / bridging costs.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to identify a yield opportunity above the Base Rate and document RRC, ALM, cost estimates, and a net yield target in a meeting note.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete outputs (RRC, ALM, exchange/bridging costs, net yield target, internal meeting note) but every operative step uses judgment language ('identifies', 'estimates', 'evaluates', 'considers') with no threshold, formula, or deadline. A Prime could argue it complied by writing any note with any estimates.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The meeting note and RRC estimates are agent artifacts that Core GovOps Artifact Review can examine with penalty assessment, and the RRC estimates feed Risk Capital rules backed by Penalty Mechanisms. The consequence is not quantified for this specific step, so it stays mid.

assessments.title: Preliminary Required Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management Arrangement
assessments.quote: If necessary, the Prime Agent reaches out to other Prime Agents that could provide Junior Risk Capital (JRC) / Senior Risk Capital (SRC) or assume Asset Liability Management obligations. The Prime Agent negotiates with these other Prime Agents and documents these potential deals. The output of this step is an informal confirmation of JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management transfer details.
assessments.description: Lets a Prime Agent seek other Primes to provide JRC/SRC or assume ALM obligations, then document an informal confirmation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The outreach, negotiation, and documentation steps are named, but the trigger 'if necessary' is undefined and nothing sets thresholds, deadlines, or documentation standards. The stated output is an 'informal confirmation', so compliance is arguable on any facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph creates no binding transfer, and the informal output is not tied to the Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship, or artifact review. No citable mechanism reaches this preliminary outreach step.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Preparation Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.quote:
The Capital and Operational Plan ("C&O Plan") articulates the Prime Agent’s strategy for a proposed new Allocation Instance or a modification to an existing Instance. In addition to articulating the Instance’s strategic objectives and operational parameters, the C&O Plan includes a pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate and a strategy for ensuring sufficient Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage.

The C&O Plan is the major input into the Artifact Edit Proposal that codifies the new or modified Instance. Following the approval of such a proposal by Prime governance, the details and commitments outlined in the C&O Plan are formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document of the Prime Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents' Capital and Operational Plans to include a pro-forma RRC estimate and a TRC coverage strategy, integrated into their artifacts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names required components (a pro-forma RRC estimate and a TRC coverage strategy) but gives no thresholds, formulas, cadence, or standard for sufficiency. A Prime could arguably satisfy it with any estimate and any strategy, so compliance is judgment-based.
metrics: Pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate included in the C&O Plan
Strategy for ensuring sufficient Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage included in the C&O Plan
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can examine whether the approved plan details were integrated into the Instance Configuration Document, and the Penalty Mechanisms can reach Risk Capital shortfalls that stem from a deficient plan. The consequence is not quantified for this specific content requirement, and escalation depends on a review being triggered.

assessments.title: Pro-Forma Instance RRC Estimate
assessments.quote: As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must prepare an initial pro-forma Instance Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate. This estimate serves as the basis for the Prime’s capital planning prior to the availability of official RRC figures from Sky Core. The estimate must strictly adhere to the implementation of RRC-models defined in [A.3.2 - Risk Capital](55999acf-75fe-4adf-8584-9746ef50d3e4).
assessments.description: Requires Primes to prepare a pro-forma Instance RRC estimate in line with the RRC models in A.3.2 before official Sky Core figures are available.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to produce an estimate and adhere to A.3.2 RRC models is concrete, but the paragraph states no numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines. Its only timing condition, 'prior to the availability of official RRC figures', is open-ended, and 'strictly adhere' depends on an external model definition.
metrics: Estimate prepared prior to the availability of official RRC figures from Sky Core
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The estimate feeds Risk Capital planning, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) for Primes not following Risk Capital rules plausibly reach a failure to adhere to A.3.2 models. Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could assess the estimate, but neither mechanism quantifies a consequence for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) Coverage Strategy
assessments.quote:
As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must articulate its strategy for ensuring its Total Risk Capital (TRC) adequately covers the pro-forma Instance RRC of a new or modified Instance and the resulting impact on its Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s notional TRC coverage strategy must outline how this new Instance’s RRC will be notionally accounted for or supported by the Prime’s overall TRC pool. If the Prime’s current TRC is not sufficient to cover its estimated increased Aggregate RRC, the strategy should outline the Prime Agent’s intended steps for acquiring additional JRC/SRC.

For instance, this risk-capital acquisition strategy could involve:

1. Renting Junior Risk Capital (JRC)
    - Sourcing Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) by renting it from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
    - Sourcing Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) from external capital providers.
2. Sourcing Senior Risk Capital (SRC):
    - Originating SRC through the Sky monthly auction.
    - Renting OSRC from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
3. Increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): A Prime might have plans to bolster its own IJRC through retained earnings or other internal means.
4. Decreasing exposure in an existing Instance(s) to lower Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s capital-acquisition strategy should indicate how the Prime will remain in compliance with all relevant Atlas rules, such as sourcing ratios that constrain how much Senior Risk Capital can be "enabled" or counted toward a Prime’s Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
assessments.description: Requires Primes to articulate a strategy for covering new or modified Instance RRC with Total Risk Capital, including acquiring JRC or SRC if short.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to articulate a TRC coverage strategy is real, but it is expressed in judgment language ("should outline", "could involve", "for instance") with no coverage ratio, deadline, or measurement cadence. The sourcing-ratio limits are delegated to an external section, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Capital & Operational Plan that contains this strategy is subject to Core GovOps artifact review with penalty assessment, and a TRC shortfall falls under Risk Capital penalty machinery. Neither consequence is quantified for this specific articulation duty, and firing depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Additional Elements Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.quote:
The Capital & Operational Plan includes the following additional elements:

- Operational Parameters: defines the Instance’s target chain(s), protocols, initial capital, maximum deposit sizes, and any other parameters that underpin the pro-forma RRC calculation.
- Data Submission Protocol: defines how yields, Required Risk Capital usage, ALM costs, exchange data, etc. will be reported and audited.
- Emergency Procedures: defines mechanisms to be triggered if security or risk capital thresholds are breached, such as a kill switch or partial freeze.
- Asset Liability Management (ALM) Strategy: details if the Prime will meet its ALM requirements through its own direct asset management or by transferring its obligations to another Prime Agent via the ASC Rental Primitive. If the latter, the C&O Plan must reference the governing Ecosystem Accord and its key terms.
- Performance-based Adjustments: define the conditions or KPIs that allow adjustments to Instance deposit caps or yield expansions without requiring a formal Artifact edit.
assessments.description: Lists five elements a Prime's Capital & Operational Plan must include: parameters, data reporting, emergency procedures, ALM strategy, and performance adjustments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates required C&O Plan sections, which is a real obligation, but it sets no thresholds, cadences, or deadlines. Terms like 'defines mechanisms', 'details if', and 'define the conditions or KPIs' leave content and sufficiency open, so a Prime could arguably comply by listing headings.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reaches a C&O Plan that omits required elements, through staged findings and penalty assessment. The consequence is not quantified for this paragraph, and firing depends on the review being scheduled and escalated.

assessments.title: Preliminary Informal Check With Operational GovOps
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent presents the Capital and Operational Plan for the Allocation Instance to Operational GovOps, including any associated JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management arrangements. Operational GovOps reviews and either provides an informal greenlight or requests modifications to the Plan. The output of this step is Operational GovOps approval to proceed with a request to revise the C&O Plan, as applicable.
assessments.description: Requires a Prime Agent to present its Capital and Operational Plan to Operational GovOps for an informal greenlight or modification request before proceeding.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines actors (Prime Agent, Operational GovOps) and a sequenced step with a stated output, but sets no thresholds, deadlines, review cadence, or criteria for granting a greenlight. Whether the step was properly performed is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, or structural mechanism reaches a failure to present the plan or proceed without informal greenlight; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Agent Inputs
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent drafts an update to the Prime Agent Artifact adding the Allocation Instance to the list of active Allocation Instances and including the information specified in [A.2.2.10.1.2.6 - List Of Allocation Instances](e4975062-6d19-438b-a5d5-cfc1a7fd8cb9). The Prime Agent submits the draft to the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is a draft Prime Agent Artifact update in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to draft an Artifact update adding a new Allocation Instance and submit it to Powerhouse.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Prime Agent), system (Powerhouse), and steps are named, but the required content is delegated by cross-reference to A.2.2.10.1.2.6 and no deadline or cadence is stated. Compliance can be checked as a process step, but not against a quantified standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review of Prime Agent artifacts with staged findings and penalty assessment, so it plausibly reaches a missing or inaccurate allocation-instance update. The consequence is not quantified for this specific step.

assessments.title: Validation And Off-Chain Vote
assessments.quote: The Operational Executor Facilitator reviews the proposal to ensure that it is complete and aligned with the Atlas. The Operational Executor Facilitator then initiates an off-chain snapshot vote, following the quorum and majority rules in the Prime Agent Artifact. When complete, the result of the vote is recorded in the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is the snapshot vote result recorded in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.description: Requires the Operational Executor Facilitator to review a proposal, run an off-chain snapshot vote, and record the result in Powerhouse.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The steps are enumerated (review, initiate snapshot vote, record result), but the completeness and Atlas-alignment review has no criteria, and the quorum and majority thresholds are delegated to the Prime Agent Artifact. A defender could plausibly argue the review was satisfied on any facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment by a party distinct from the Facilitator, and it could reach a deviation from the quorum and majority rules in the Prime Agent Artifact. No consequence is quantified for this specific vote procedure.

assessments.title: Official Update of Artifact
assessments.quote:
If the Allocation Instance is successfully approved, the Operational Executor Facilitator finalizes and publishes the update to the Prime Agent Artifact, making it effective in the Atlas. The output of this step is an updated Prime Agent Artifact with the new Allocation Instance.

Once a new Instance is deployed, its data is integrated into risk-capital monitoring systems and its RRC will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This official RRC figure supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC.
assessments.description: Requires publishing approved Allocation Instances to the Prime Agent Artifact and tracking their official RRC, which supersedes the pro-forma figure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete: a named actor (Operational Executor Facilitator) must publish an updated artifact, and the official RRC supersedes the pro-forma figure. However, there is no deadline, no defined meaning of 'integrated' into monitoring systems, and no cadence or threshold, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The official RRC figure sets the Risk Capital a Prime must hold, so a mismatch or failure to track it can reach the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which apply to Risk Capital rule breaches. The penalty is not quantified for this publication step, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Instance Setup Deployments
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define how the deployment of an Allocation Instance is executed on-chain. In the short-term, an Allocation Instance may also be deployed using the process for Interim Deployments specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.2 - Interim Deployments](9b3edbbf-89d1-42da-a9c3-18f858f8471f).

The Prime Agent must subsequently prepare a pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate, which must be approved by the Core Council Risk Advisor, before the parameters of the Instance can be updated for normal operation.
assessments.description: Requires a Prime Agent to obtain Core Council Risk Advisor approval of a pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate before normal-operation parameter updates.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors and a concrete approval gate with a named artifact, but gives no threshold, formula, or deadline; 'subsequently' is undefined. Deployment mechanics are delegated by reference to other sections, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (A.3.2.2.7.2) are designed to incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules and could plausibly reach skipping the estimate or approval gate. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, so it rates mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Conduit Development And Testing
assessments.quote: Once formally validated, the Prime Agent implements the new Allocation Instance based on the specifications in the Prime Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps must test the Allocation Instance with minimal funds from the Prime Agent’s Central Allocation Buffer, verifying deposit / withdrawal logic, slippage constraints, and oracle checks. If this testing is successful Operational GovOps confirms that the Allocation Instance satisfies all risk constraints specified in the Prime Agent Artifact. The output of this step is validated contracts for the Allocation Instance and a green light to proceed with a scaled deployment.
assessments.description: Requires Operational GovOps to test a new Allocation Instance with minimal funds before a scaled deployment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors, a funding source (Central Allocation Buffer), and test categories (deposit/withdrawal logic, slippage, oracle checks), but gives no amount for 'minimal funds', no slippage or oracle tolerance, and no definition of a 'successful' test. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps can review the Prime Agent's implementation against its artifact with staged findings and penalty assessment, and Penalty Mechanisms can impose quantified penalties on Primes and Operational Agents for breaching risk rules. Neither is tied to this testing step specifically, and escalation depends on someone initiating review, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Initial Deployment and Required Risk Capital / Asset Liability Management Execution
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent finalizes JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management Arrangements. Operational GovOps records these arrangements in the Powerhouse interface. If Operational GovOps is charged with operationalizing an Instance, it deploys funds from the Prime Agent’s Operational Buffer into the Allocation Instance, performing any necessary DEX exchanges. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.1 - Operationalization Of Allocation Instances](989512c2-4fa1-46b8-947c-00e3c0b56024). In doing so, Operational GovOps follows instructions in the Agent Artifact regarding the amount of capital to deploy and slippage tolerances. The output of this step is a fully deployed Allocation Instance conforming to Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements.
assessments.description: Describes Prime Agent and Operational GovOps steps to deploy Operational Buffer funds into Allocation Instances per Agent Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real deployment process and actors but states no thresholds. Deployment amount and slippage tolerance are delegated to the Agent Artifact, and 'conforming to Risk Capital requirements' is not defined here, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a separate enforcer that assesses penalties, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can apply to Operational Agents who breach Risk Capital rules. Neither is quantified for deployment amount or slippage violations, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Operationalization Of Allocation Instances
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams may choose to directly operationalize their Allocation System Primitive Instances ("Instances") using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts. Alternatively, Prime Agents may elect to have the Instances operationalized by their Operational Executor Agent. This constitutes an exception to the general rule that Operational Executor Agents operationalize all Sky Primitives on behalf of Prime Agents. See [A.1.14.3.4 - Agent Role Delineation](fdf32ca5-5e2e-481e-9047-4d1599547216).

For Prime Agent teams that operationalize their Instances, they will be required to formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies; should an Instance under-perform these KPIs, Operational GovOps is authorized to step in and operationalize the Instance(s) via a back-up strategy that is defined in the Agent Artifact. Additional logic on this point will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Lets Prime teams run proprietary Instance strategies, requires them to set KPIs, and authorizes Operational GovOps to step in on underperformance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors and a real obligation to formulate KPIs, but gives no KPI content, underperformance threshold, or measurement cadence. The 'under-perform' trigger is judgment language, and the paragraph explicitly defers the operative logic to a future iteration, so a Prime could reasonably argue it does not yet bind.
metrics: Prime Agent teams must formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies (no thresholds stated)
Trigger: an Instance that under-performs these KPIs (threshold undefined)
Operational GovOps may operationalize the Instance via a back-up strategy defined in the Agent Artifact
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check the KPIs and back-up strategy in the Artifact with staged findings and penalty assessment, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can attach to Primes and Operational Agents. The consequence is not quantified for KPI under-performance, and firing depends on a review being initiated.

assessments.title: Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard
assessments.quote:
The Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard serves as the official system for determining and disseminating RRC figures for Prime Agents and their Allocation System Primitive Instances.

Prior to the full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system, Prime Agents must utilize the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for their official Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC. Data from this source is to be used for all internal TRC management, required reporting and compliance assessments.

The Sky Core RRC Dashboard is located at [https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital](https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital).
assessments.description: Designates the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for Prime Agents' Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Prime Agents), a specific source (the dashboard at a stated URL), and its uses (TRC management, reporting, compliance). It gives no RRC formula, threshold, or update cadence, and the start condition 'prior to the full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system' is undefined, so a Prime could argue the duty does not yet bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Using non-authoritative RRC figures could mis-state capital compliance, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and conservatorship for breach of capital requirements (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach that failure. Neither mechanism is quantified for this data-sourcing rule specifically, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Interim Notice Regarding RRC Dashboard Coverage
assessments.quote: Some Allocation System Instances displayed on the RRC Dashboard concern asset types whose risk models have not yet been fully developed. See [A.3.2.1.1.4.3 - Financial Risk Models](2af9fa64-ab25-4017-920c-f1c07dff4c06). An active Instance’s respective Instance Configuration Document will specify its `RRC Framework Full Implementation` status as either `Covered` or `Pending`.
assessments.description: Requires Instance Configuration Documents to state RRC Framework implementation status as Covered or Pending for certain dashboard instances.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a specific field (RRC Framework Full Implementation) and two enumerated values, but gives no criteria for assigning Covered versus Pending. It also sets no deadline, cadence, or threshold, and 'some' instances is left undefined.
metrics: RRC Framework Full Implementation status must be either Covered or Pending in each active Instance's Instance Configuration Document
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a disclosure notice with no penalty, emergency, insurance, or on-chain mechanism tied to the accuracy of the status field; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops could apply.

assessments.title: Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams are responsible for managing their Total Risk Capital (TRC) to continuously meet their Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC). The accounting of TRC considers all on-chain holdings and any off-chain agreements, encumbrances, or conditions that may affect the immediate availability or eligibility of capital for RRC coverage. For a definition of Total Risk Capital, see [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).

The documents herein define requirements and standards for a Prime Agent’s internal TRC management systems.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to continuously meet Aggregate Required Risk Capital using Total Risk Capital, counting on-chain and off-chain encumbrances.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Prime Agent teams) and the operative standard (continuously meet Aggregate RRC), but gives no numeric threshold or measurement cadence. The accounting scope ('any... that may affect' availability) is judgment-based, and TRC is delegated to another document.
metrics: Total Risk Capital must continuously meet Aggregate Required Risk Capital (no numeric threshold or measurement cadence stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Capital Incident Response lets Sky Core impose penalties up to conservatorship when Risk Capital is short, and Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements cover Prime breaches of RRC coverage. The enforcer is Sky Core, distinct from the Prime, with concrete remedies.

assessments.title: Objective of Prime TRC Management
assessments.quote:
To comply with Atlas risk capital requirements, Prime Agent teams must establish, maintain, and operate an internal system for TRC management. A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should enable proactive operational risk management. This entails ongoing capital adequacy assessment and strategic capital allocation planning for current and future Allocation System Primitive Instances, including the ability to perform scenario analyses for potential deployments or market stresses.

Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable them to maintain continuous sufficiency of the Prime Agent’s held TRC against its official Aggregate RRC. This requires real-time or near real-time comparison and internal alerting mechanisms to prevent and address potential shortfalls.
Primes must ensure that their internal TRC management systems maintain comprehensive, verifiable internal records of all TRC components, related transactions, and compliance activities to support internal governance and external verification processes, such as the submission of TRC Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to run an internal TRC management system covering capital adequacy, continuous sufficiency against Aggregate RRC, and verifiable records.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph uses judgment language such as "should enable", "proactive", and "comprehensive, verifiable" records without any numeric threshold or formula. Its only time-related terms, "real-time or near real-time" and "continuous", give a cadence but no measurable tolerance.
metrics: Continuous sufficiency of held TRC against official Aggregate RRC
Real-time or near real-time comparison of TRC against Aggregate RRC
Internal alerting to prevent and address potential shortfalls
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A shortfall of held TRC against Aggregate RRC is a risk-capital breach that would reach the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and, for serious cases, conservatorship (5c3dd35a). The penalty amounts are not quantified for this rule, and the internal-system and record-keeping duties are only indirectly covered; the TRC Report (41ca2085) is the reporting channel.

assessments.title: Minimum Capabilities of Prime TRC Management Systems
assessments.quote:
A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should possess the following capabilities to meet the objectives outlined in [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Objective of Prime TRC Management](9a8120c4-0a5b-426f-97a5-283c708413f5).

1. Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable compliant sourcing and tracking of all TRC components, including Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC), Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC), and Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). Compliance in this context includes strict adherence to eligibility criteria and capital-sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal, Senior Per Junior) as defined in the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
The system must provide real-time or near real-time tracking of all held Total Risk Capital (TRC) components. This includes, for each TRC component:
    - Accurate valuation of the assets comprising each component.
    - Clear identification of the source of each component (e.g., Prime’s own SubProxy for IJRC, specific Ecosystem Accord references for rented PEJRC or OSRC, TEJRC encumbrance details, OSRC origination details).
    - Verification of each TRC component’s eligibility status according to Atlas rules. This includes tracking whether capital is “enabled” or “active” for RRC coverage purposes (e.g., based on Ecosystem Accord status, compliance with sourcing ratios, etc.).
    - Distinction between capital directly held by the Prime Agent and capital that is encumbered (e.g., PEJRC where the lending Prime retains custody but the capital is contractually committed).
2. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable dynamic-state accounting. The system must account for TRC components that are in dynamic, pending, or off-chain states, as these can impact the true risk capital available to a Prime Agent. This includes:
    - Pending transactions such as PEJRC or OSRC rental Ecosystem Accords that have been committed to by the parties, but not yet codified in the Atlas.
    - Capital in transit, e.g., assets that are committed to be IJRC, but currently moving between chains via bridges or locked in Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) messages awaiting finality.
    - Operational expenditures funded by TRC components (typically IJRC), such as blockchain transaction fees, oracle service fees, audit costs, and other operational overhead that reduces available risk capital. The system should track these expenditures in real-time or near real-time.
    - Any off-chain factors that could impair the immediate deployability or availability of TRC components.
3. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable continuous capital adequacy monitoring. The system must enable the near real-time comparison of the Prime Agent's internally tracked and calculated TRC against its official Aggregate RRC, as obtained from the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This core functionality is essential for the Prime Agent to proactively monitor its capital adequacy, identify potential or actual TRC shortfalls, and make timely operational and capital management decisions to maintain compliance.
4. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should define a RRC-incident (e.g., TRC shortfall) response protocol. The system should enable internal alerting mechanisms that detect when a Prime Agent’s TRC approaches predefined internal buffer thresholds relative to its Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9). The system should also detect an actual shortfall where the Prime Agent’s held TRC falls below its Aggregate RRC. Furthermore, Prime Agent teams should establish and document internal processes for responding to such alerts. Such internal processes should include: 1) internal escalation and assessment of the shortfall’s cause and magnitude; 2) formulation of potential responses or corrective actions, which may include sourcing additional TRC, reducing risk-weighted exposures, or other measures; 3) internal decision-making framework for the evaluation of potential responses and selection of the most appropriate one; and 4) notifying any pertinent parties (Operational GovOps) as needed for the purpose of planning or implementing follow-up action.

Prime Agent teams' internal decision-making framework may consider the economic trade-offs of various actions, including the strategic acceptance of penalties for a TRC shortfall where such an approach is determined to be economically advantageous compared to immediate rebalancing (e.g., avoiding excessive transaction costs or market impact).
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents' internal TRC systems to track capital components, dynamic states, RRC adequacy, and shortfall response.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete components and a required comparison against Aggregate RRC, but gives no numeric buffer thresholds, no ratio values, and only a vague 'real-time or near real-time' cadence. Most obligations are 'should' capabilities whose adequacy is open to judgment.
metrics: Tracking of TRC components in real-time or near real-time
Near real-time comparison of internally tracked TRC against official Aggregate RRC from the Sky Core RRC Dashboard
Alerts when TRC approaches predefined internal buffer thresholds relative to Aggregate RRC (thresholds not stated)
Detection of actual shortfall where held TRC falls below Aggregate RRC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) reach TRC shortfalls that these systems are meant to detect, but not the system-capability requirements themselves. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could check the documented processes, though no quantified consequence attaches to this rule specifically.

assessments.title: Primes’ TRC Report
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to provide an accurate and verifiable attestation of their TRC composition and adherence to capital requirements.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic TRC Reports attesting to their capital composition and capital-requirement adherence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: An identifiable reporting obligation exists, but "periodic" has no cadence or deadline, and "accurate and verifiable attestation" names no fields, thresholds, or format. A Prime could arguably comply with any report it submits, so the rule is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The report attests to adherence to capital requirements, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) for Risk Capital rules and the conservatorship escalation for capital-requirement breach (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach a failure to report or a misreported composition. Neither quantifies a consequence for the reporting duty itself, and firing depends on the reporting gap being surfaced.

assessments.title: Mandate and Rationale
assessments.quote:
Prime Agents are required to periodically submit TRC Reports to Core GovOps. This report serves a dual purpose. It provides a verifiable snapshot of the Prime Agent's TRC composition and key capital ratios as of the end of the reporting period; and second, it provides a formal attestation regarding the Prime Agent's maintenance of TRC at or above its dynamically changing Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC) throughout the entire reporting period. See [A.3.2.1.1.2 - Aggregate RRC](6aed5cc1-9671-4b73-88a9-fdd86ac93ece).

This comprehensive reporting, encompassing both an end-of-period statement and disclosures of any intra-period events affecting TRC, is essential. On-chain data alone (such as that captured by the planned OVRC system) cannot definitively prove the full eligibility and unimpaired availability of a Prime Agent's capital position for continuous RRC coverage, nor can it capture all off-chain factors. These factors include, but are not limited to, whether assets are subject to Prime-initiated off-chain contractual pledges, if the economic value or redeemability of its bridged assets is compromised by issues with their originating bridge, or if its assets are encumbered by derivative structures or other off-chain commitments that would impair their immediate use at any point during the period.

The TRC Report serves as an important basis for Core GovOps’ verification procedures. This entails: 1) reconciling reported end-of-period TRC components against the Sky Atlas, on-chain data, and other relevant sources to validate the period-end capital position and adherence to Atlas-defined capital requirements; and 2) reviewing Prime Agents’ attestations and disclosures regarding its TRC management and any material events throughout the reporting period to assess continuous compliance with its dynamically changing Aggregate RRC. The outcome of this validation is a critical input for the monthly settlement cycles, which latter includes the determination and retroactive application of penalties for any identified discrepancies or violations of capital requirements during the period.

The long-term vision is for the Powerhouse system to enable the automation of TRC data aggregation and verification. The Powerhouse system will have capabilities such as directly querying Prime Agent SubProxy accounts for IJRC assets, programmatically accessing and interpreting Ecosystem Accords recorded in the Atlas, interfacing with TEJRC and OSRC smart contract systems, and automatically applying Atlas-defined eligibility rules. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.1 - Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)](8048bdf0-84b7-4546-8f1a-98b62d073c84). Even in this advanced state, the TRC Report, or a similar form of periodic attestation, may remain necessary to cover elements of TRC verification that are not fully able to be automated or require explicit Prime Agent declaration.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic TRC Reports attesting end-of-period capital and continuous coverage of Aggregate RRC, verified by Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete metric, TRC at or above the dynamically changing Aggregate RRC throughout the period, and ties verification to monthly settlement. However, the reporting cadence is only "periodically", the reporting period is not defined here, and the RRC magnitude is delegated to A.3.2.1.1.2.
metrics: TRC at or above Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC) throughout the entire reporting period
End-of-period TRC composition and key capital ratios snapshot
Reporting submitted periodically to Core GovOps
Verification outcome feeds monthly settlement cycles
Retroactive penalties for identified capital discrepancies or violations during the period
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps (a named enforcer distinct from the Prime) reconciles and verifies the TRC Report, and the text states its outcome drives retroactive penalties in monthly settlement. This reaches misreported or insufficient TRC via the Penalty Mechanisms, with conservatorship available for breach of capital requirements.

assessments.title: TRC Report Contents
assessments.quote:
The Total Risk Capital (TRC) Report submitted by a Prime Agent must provide an accurate and verifiable breakdown of all TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the specified reporting period. The TRC Report should include the following essential information:

- Aggregate TRC Value As of End of Period: The total declared value in USD of all eligible TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the reporting period.
- Detailed Breakdown of TRC Components As of End of Period: For each category of TRC held, the report must detail the following values as of the end of the reporting period:
    - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): The total amount of IJRC, a breakdown of its constituent asset types, and their respective values in USD.
    - Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC): The total amount of PEJRC. For each portion of PEJRC sourced from another Prime Agent, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date of the arrangement, and a direct reference to the Ecosystem Accord that governs the PEJRC arrangement.
    - Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC): The total amount of TEJRC. For each TEJRC source, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the TEJRC smart contract or facility and any relevant encumbrance identifier.
    - Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC): The total amount of OSRC. The report must specify the amount originated directly by the Prime Agent from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool and any amount of OSRC rented from other Prime Agents. For any rented OSRC, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date, and a direct reference to the pertinent Ecosystem Accord.
    - Key Ratio Inputs and Computed Totals (Prime Internal Calculation) As Of End Of Period: Based on the component values reported above (as of the end of the reporting period), the report must include key figures used in and resulting from the Prime Agent's internal capital adequacy calculations. These figures reflect the capital structure and ratios as of the end of the reporting period and include:
        - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
        - External Junior Risk Capital (EJRC) generated via External Per Internal Ratio (Prime External Junior Risk Capital + Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital sourced via the EPI ratio still carries Senior Per Junior or SPJ capacity)
        - EJRC-via-SPJ (sourced by spending SPJ capacity; zero-SPJ-capacity thereafter)
        - Enabled Senior Risk Capital (SRC)
        - Total Senior Per Junior capacity
            - Allocation of SPJ capacity to 1) enable SRC; or to 2) source EJRC
        - Prime-computed eligible Total Risk Capital (IJRC + EJRC-via-EPI + EJRC-via-SPJ + enabled SRC)
        - Official Aggregate RRC
        - Capital buffer = TRC – Aggregate RRC
        - Effective ratios
            - EPI = EJRC-via-EPI ÷ IJRC
            - SPJ utilisation:
                - enabled SRC ÷ total SPJ capacity
                - EJRC-via-SPJ ÷ total SPJ capacity
- Dynamic Period Attestation and Disclosures: In addition to the end-of-period snapshot figures, the TRC Report must include an Attestation from the Prime Agent confirming it maintained TRC at or above its Aggregate RRC at all times throughout the entire reporting period. In addition, the TRC Report must include disclosure of any events, Prime-initiated off-chain contractual obligations, impairments to the value or redeemability of held assets (such as RWA backing or bridged asset viability), encumbrances, or other conditions that occurred at any point during the reporting period which materially affected its TRC, even if such conditions were temporary or not continuously visible to on-chain monitoring systems. This disclosure must include the nature of the event/condition, its precise timing and duration, and its quantified impact on the Prime Agent's TRC.
assessments.description: Specifies required contents of a Prime Agent's TRC Report, including component breakdowns, ratio inputs, and an attestation of TRC at or above Aggregate RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Most required fields are concrete and checkable: USD amounts, counterparty identifiers, expiry dates, Ecosystem Accord references, and explicit formulas for capital buffer and EPI/SPJ ratios. Gaps remain: no reporting deadline or cadence, and the disclosure of 'materially affected' conditions is left to judgment.
