No consequence is quantified for false or incomplete reporting specifically, and enforcement depends on a review being triggered.

assessments.title: Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)
assessments.quote:
An autonomous monitoring system must be designed and implemented to enable continuous tracking of Prime Agents’ on-chain verifiable risk-capital components in near real-time. The on-chain, verifiable risk-capital components that can be tracked by such a monitoring system in real time are termed "On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital" (OVRC).

OVRC is not necessarily equivalent to Total Risk Capital (TRC). A Prime Agent’s actual TRC cannot be determined definitively without accounting for off-chain agreements, encumbrances or other relevant conditions affecting capital eligibility or availability, which conditions must be disclosed in the TRC Reports submitted by Prime Agents. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).

Where the OVRC of a Prime Agent is less than its Aggregate RRC, the shortfall will be logged and penalty accrual will commence on a pro-rata, per-second basis for the duration and magnitude of the observed shortfall, according to the penalty schedule defined in the Atlas. Thus, this on-chain monitoring system serves as an interim penalty ledger.
assessments.description: Requires an autonomous system to continuously track Prime Agents' on-chain verifiable risk capital and accrue penalties on shortfalls against Aggregate RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the OVRC metric, the comparison against Aggregate RRC, and a per-second pro-rata accrual cadence, but "near real-time" is undefined and penalty magnitude is delegated to a schedule "defined in the Atlas" without values.
metrics: OVRC of a Prime Agent less than its Aggregate RRC triggers a logged shortfall
Penalty accrual on a pro-rata, per-second basis for the duration and magnitude of the shortfall
Continuous tracking "in near real-time"
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph itself triggers automatic per-second penalty accrual on shortfalls, which reaches the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) that incentivize Primes to meet Risk Capital rules. The consequence magnitude is delegated to an external penalty schedule and no conservatorship or escalation is stated here, so mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Validation of TRC Report In General
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc). The protocol for validation of Primes’ TRC reports is defined in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic TRC Reports to Core GovOps, with validation delegated to other documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real submission obligation exists, naming the actor (Prime Agents) and recipient (Core GovOps), but 'periodic' has no cadence or deadline. The validation protocol is only referenced ('defined in the documents herein') and no validation criteria appear in this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms quantify financial penalties for Primes that fail Risk Capital rules, and TRC reporting feeds those rules, so non-submission plausibly reaches them. The paragraph never states a consequence for missed reports, so escalation depends on the penalty machinery being invoked.

assessments.title: Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process
assessments.quote:
Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Primes on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process.

Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas.

Core GovOps validates the Prime Agent's reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Prime Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of "eligible assets" for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.1.1 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)](8728abee-0dc5-449b-b4c2-78698da16f10).

For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Prime, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components.

Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Prime Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Prime Agent's TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Prime Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations.

Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Prime Agent's compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)).
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to validate Prime TRC Reports against on-chain state, Atlas records, and capital sourcing ratios.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph enumerates concrete verification steps, including reconciling IJRC against SubProxy on-chain balances and cross-referencing TEJRC and OSRC contracts. However, it sets no cadence for 'regular basis', leaves the EPI and SPJ ratio values to the Atlas, and makes supplementary evidence requests optional ('may include').
metrics: TRC Reports received 'on a regular basis' (no cadence specified)
Compliance with Aggregate RRC 'throughout the entire reporting period' (no threshold stated)
Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios, e.g., External Per Internal (EPI) and Senior Per Junior (SPJ) (values defined elsewhere)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps is a named enforcer distinct from the Prime, and its validation can surface intra-period RRC shortfalls that feed the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship path. The paragraph itself states no penalty or escalation, so firing depends on someone escalating a finding.

assessments.title: Finalized Determination Of TRC Position And Penalties
assessments.quote:
After reaching a definitive accounting of Prime Agents’ capital position and TRC adequacy, penalties are finalized by Core GovOps. This involves reconciling the interim penalty ledger (derived from the OVRC system) with the definitive TRC history, which incorporates all validated information from the TRC Report including any intra-period shortfalls.

1. If the validated TRC Report indicates that the Prime Agent's TRC was below its Aggregate RRC during the reporting period, and this actual shortfall was more severe than, or not detected by, the OVRC monitoring system, then penalties will be finalized as follows: if the OVRC system had already accrued penalties, these will be adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall; if the OVRC system had not detected a shortfall, penalties will be assessed and applied retroactively based on the full duration and magnitude of the actual shortfall.
2. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC shortfalls were identical in duration and magnitude to those logged by the OVRC monitoring system throughout the reporting period: the penalties accrued in the interim penalty ledger will be confirmed and finalized.
3. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC was higher than a misleading OVRC reading during a specific portion of the reporting period which led to an erroneously logged penalty: Core GovOps will adjust or void the penalty accordingly.
assessments.description: Finalizes Prime Agent penalties by reconciling the interim OVRC ledger with validated TRC history, adjusting or voiding penalties as shortfalls warrant.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Core GovOps), a comparison (TRC versus Aggregate RRC), and enumerated adjustment outcomes, with upward adjustment tied to the actual shortfall. The penalty magnitude and any finalization deadline are not stated, so the consequence is delegated.
metrics: TRC below Aggregate RRC during the reporting period
Shortfall duration and magnitude matched against OVRC-logged shortfall
Penalties adjusted upwards to match actual shortfall
Penalties assessed retroactively on full duration and magnitude of actual shortfall
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) are the quantified financial penalties that this paragraph finalizes, and Core GovOps is a named enforcer distinct from the Prime Agent. The magnitude for this rule is not quantified in the text, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Risk-Capital Incident Response
assessments.quote:
Where a Prime Agent’s Allocation System Instances are operationalized by its Operational Executor Agent, the management of and response to Required Risk Capital (RRC)-related incidents requires a defined framework within each Prime Agent's Artifact (the Multi-Instance Coordinator Document for the Allocation System Primitive) and its associated Executor Accord.

While the Prime Agent's strategic team ("Prime Team") determines the specific rectification strategy for an RRC incident—considering its holistic portfolio, prevailing market conditions, and the potential for strategic acceptance of penalties—this discretion is exercised subject to the authority of Sky Core to impose penalties and take corrective measures, up to and including the conservatorship of a Prime Agent, to protect the ecosystem and make any losses whole.

This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Defers the Prime Agent's Required Risk Capital incident response framework, leaving Sky Core penalty and conservatorship authority as the only operative consequence.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states that the response framework will be developed in a future iteration, so no incident definition, timeline, or threshold exists. It names actors (Prime Team, Sky Core) and remedies (penalties, conservatorship) but gives no magnitudes or criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Sky Core's authority to impose penalties and conservatorship for RRC incidents reaches this rule via the Risk-Capital Incident Response, Penalty Mechanisms, and Conservatorship mechanisms. The escalation path is not defined for this paragraph, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Instance Operational Conformance
assessments.quote: Operational deviation from Artifact specifications can render an Instance’s RRC, and thus the Prime’s Aggregate RRC, invalid. Prime Agents must therefore ensure that each Allocation System Instance adheres to its respective Instance Configuration Document. Whether a Prime self-operationalizes its Allocation System or contracts with an Operational Executor Agent, its Agent Artifact must define processes for monitoring for, and addressing deviations of, Instance operational conformance. This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep each Allocation System Instance conformant to its Instance Configuration Document and define monitoring processes for deviations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a real obligation (adherence to the Instance Configuration Document and defined monitoring and deviation-handling processes), but gives no threshold, cadence, tolerance, or deadline. The closing sentence defers development to a future iteration, so a Prime could reasonably argue the duty is not yet operative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph ties Instance deviations to invalid RRC, so the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can plausibly reach a violation, and Agent Artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check the required monitoring processes. Neither consequence is quantified for this rule, and no escalation path is stated in the text.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management
assessments.quote: Requirements and infrastructure related to Asset Liability Management shall be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Placeholder stating that Asset Liability Management requirements and infrastructure will be defined in a future Atlas iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is an explicit stub that defers all requirements to a future iteration, with no thresholds, metrics, actors, or deadlines. There is nothing currently verifiable to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No obligation exists today to enforce, and no catalog mechanism is tied to this paragraph's text; the only applicable backstop is the generic misalignment or adjudication process.

assessments.title: Allocation Instance Adjustments, Scaling, And Settlement
assessments.quote: On an ongoing basis, the Prime Agent team or Operational GovOps operates the Allocation Instance, scaling exposure up and down. Any change to the Allocation Instance outside of the limits specified in the Prime Agent Artifact or requiring judgment on the part of Operational GovOps (where the Allocation System Instance is operationalized by the Operational Executor Agent) requires a new vote of Prime Agent token holders. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.3.1 - Modification Of Existing Instances](c1b5708c-e88f-45e0-92e1-b76e68b34f13). As part of monthly and quarterly settlement cycles, Core GovOps reviews yields and obligations, applying penalties retroactively for any previously undisclosed violations. In the event of any such violations, Operational GovOps may be required to take escalatory steps based on the fallback strategy in the Prime Agent Artifact.
assessments.description: Requires Prime or Operational GovOps to run allocation scaling, with out-of-limit changes needing a new vote, and monthly and quarterly settlement reviews with penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names actors and a monthly and quarterly settlement cadence, and gates changes behind a new token-holder vote. The operative limits are delegated to the Prime Agent Artifact, penalty magnitudes are unstated, and escalation is hedged as 'may be required'.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps, a distinct enforcer, reviews settlement and applies retroactive penalties, which the Penalty Mechanisms reach. The penalty size is unquantified for this rule, and escalation is conditional ('may be required') on the artifact's fallback strategy.

assessments.title: Modification Of Existing Instances
assessments.quote: When a Prime Agent wishes to modify an existing Allocation System Primitive Instance in a manner that cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters defined in its Agent Artifact, the Prime Agent must initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal process as detailed herein.
assessments.description: Requires a Prime Agent to start an Artifact Edit Proposal when changing an Allocation System instance beyond its Agent Artifact parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor and the required process are named, but the trigger ('cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters') is judgment-based and the parameters and the Artifact Edit Proposal process are defined elsewhere, with no thresholds or deadlines here. A Prime could plausibly argue that a given change was accommodated within existing parameters.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, third-party review of Agent Artifacts with staged findings and penalty assessment, which could catch an out-of-parameter modification made without an edit proposal. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule and the paragraph does not reference that review.

assessments.title: Conditions Requiring Artifact Edit Proposal
assessments.quote:
An Artifact Edit Proposal is mandatory for an Instance modification under the following conditions:

1. a desired modification to the Instance's operational parameters falls outside the pre-defined operational ranges codified in the respective Instance Configuration Document or other applicable Artifact Documents; or
2. a desired modification, even if notionally within defined ranges in the Artifact, is determined by Operational GovOps to materially alter the Instance's risk profile in a way that could invalidate the underlying Capital and Operational Plan and, consequently, the premises driving the current Required Risk Capital (RRC) for that Instance. Operational GovOps retains the discretion to require an Artifact Edit Proposal if a proposed change, regardless of its fit within existing operational ranges, is determined to pose a material change to the assessed risk.
assessments.description: Requires an Artifact Edit Proposal for Instance modifications that exceed codified operational ranges or materially change the risk profile, at Operational GovOps' discretion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Condition 1 has an objective trigger (outside ranges codified in named Artifact Documents), but no range values appear in the text. Condition 2 turns on Operational GovOps' determination of material risk change and discretionary override, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Modification falls outside pre-defined operational ranges in the Instance Configuration Document or other applicable Artifact Documents
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review by a separate enforcer with penalty assessment, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) attach to Primes and Operational Agents who breach Risk Capital rules, which this rule relates to via RRC premises. No quantified consequence is stated for failing to file an Artifact Edit Proposal, and escalation depends on review or a report being triggered.

assessments.title: Revision of Capital and Operational Plan for Instance Modification
assessments.quote:
Prior to submitting an Artifact Edit Proposal for an Instance modification, the Prime Agent must revise the Capital and Operational Plan (C&O Plan) associated with that Instance to reflect the desired new state.

The revised Capital and Operational Plan for an Instance modification must include the following information:

1. Updates to the Instance's strategy and operational parameters;
2. A new pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate specifically calculated to reflect the Instance's proposed modified state; and
3. A revised notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage strategy, detailing how the Prime Agent will manage any changes to the Instance RRC and the consequential impact on its Aggregate RRC, including plans for acquiring additional JRC or SRC if necessary.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to revise the Capital and Operational Plan with updated strategy, pro-forma RRC, and TRC coverage before proposing an Instance modification.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete required components (strategy and operational parameter updates, a pro-forma RRC estimate, a revised TRC coverage strategy) and a sequencing gate ('prior to submitting'). It gives no numeric thresholds, formulas, cadence, or criteria for adequacy of the strategy or coverage plan, so a checker can confirm presence of the items but not sufficiency.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The plan is a risk-capital artifact, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) for Risk Capital rule breaches and Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a missing or inadequate revised C&O Plan. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Post-Approval Integration and RRC Update
assessments.quote:
If the Artifact Edit Proposal for the Instance modification is approved through the Prime Agent’s governance process, the relevant content from the revised Capital and Operational Plan is formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document within the Prime Agent's Artifact.

Once the modified Instance is operational under its new, approved parameters and its data is integrated into the ecosystem’s monitoring systems, its adjusted Required Risk Capital (RRC) will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. This official RRC figure then supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC that was part of the modification proposal.
assessments.description: Requires approved Instance modifications to integrate revised plan content and set official RRC via the Sky Core dashboard, superseding pro-forma RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph establishes a real obligation (integrate approved plan content; official RRC supersedes the pro-forma figure) but gives no RRC formula, threshold, or deadline for when integration or determination must occur. 'Once operational' and 'integrated into monitoring systems' are open-ended, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms plausibly reach a Prime that fails to integrate approved parameters or relies on a stale pro-forma RRC, since they incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules. The consequence is not quantified for this specific paragraph, and no escalation path is stated in the text.

assessments.description: Requires the Allocation System Primitive to be in the Globally Activated state.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete, binary state and a specific component, so compliance is checkable as a status flag. However, the operative meaning of 'Globally Activated' is not defined in the paragraph and no activation criteria or verification steps are stated.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states an activation precondition, and no citable mechanism attaches a consequence to operating without global activation; the catch-all backstops alone would be weak.

assessments.title: Required Allocation Instance Parameters

assessments.title: Required Allocation Instance Allocation Strategy
assessments.quote: For each Allocation Instance, the Prime Agent Artifact must specify the strategy documents contained herein. These strategy documents must describe in detail how the Allocation Instance should be operated so that the Operational Executor Agent that the Prime Agent has contracted with can operate the Allocation Instance without further input from the Prime Agent or having to make "judgment calls". To the extent that the Prime Agent’s strategy cuts across different Allocation Instances, the Prime Agent may include a single set of strategy documents covering all Allocation Instances.
assessments.description: Requires each Allocation Instance's Prime Agent Artifact to include detailed operating strategy documents that an Operational Executor can follow without judgment calls.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real (strategy documents must exist per Allocation Instance), but 'in detail' and 'without further input or judgment calls' are qualitative standards with no measurable threshold, checklist, or verification criteria. A Prime could plausibly argue its documents suffice on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review of the Prime Agent Artifact by a separate enforcer, which can reach missing or inadequate strategy documents, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could follow. The penalty is not quantified for this specific rule, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Required Allocation Instance Asset Liability Management Strategy
assessments.quote: The allocation strategy for each Allocation Instance should specify how Operational GovOps should adjust the amount of funds allocated to the Conduit based on performance, market conditions, or other factors. It should also specify limits to the amount by which the allocation can be adjusted before a vote of Prime Agent token holders is required.
assessments.description: Requires each Allocation Instance strategy to specify GovOps allocation adjustment rules and limits before Prime token holder vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete actors and a vote trigger, but the adjustment limits that would trigger a token-holder vote are left unspecified, and the adjustment factors (performance, market conditions, other factors) have no criteria. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
metrics: limits to the amount by which the allocation can be adjusted before a vote of Prime Agent token holders is required
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) plausibly reaches a missing or deficient allocation strategy, since it is an agent artifact with staged findings and penalty assessment. No quantified consequence is tied to this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the adjustment limits.

assessments.title: Required Allocation Conduit Asset Liability Management Strategy
assessments.quote: The asset liability management strategy for each Allocation Instance must specify what steps Operational GovOps should take to ensure that the Prime Agent continues to satisfy its Asset Liability Management obligations as the amount of funds allocated to the Conduit changes.
assessments.description: Requires each Allocation Instance's ALM strategy to specify steps Operational GovOps takes to keep the Prime compliant as Conduit funds change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete artifact (the ALM strategy per Allocation Instance) and a defined actor (Operational GovOps), but the required steps are unspecified and no threshold, metric, or cadence is given. A defender could argue that any listed set of steps satisfies the text, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) can assess whether the ALM strategy specifies the required steps, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could plausibly reach Operational GovOps for deficient risk-capital-related artifacts. Neither is quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on the review being triggered.

assessments.title: Required Allocation Instance Fallback Strategy
assessments.quote: The fallback strategy for each Allocation Instance must specify how Operational GovOps should determine when an emergency situation is occurring regarding the Allocation Instance and what actions it should take to protect the Prime Agent from losses associated with the Allocation Instance. The fallback strategy must include emergency measures for Operational GovOps to reduce exposure to, drain, and ultimately shut down the Allocation Instance if Required Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management obligations are breached.
assessments.description: Requires each Allocation Instance to have a fallback strategy for detecting emergencies and reducing, draining, and shutting down the instance after Risk Capital or ALM breaches.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Operational GovOps), a trigger (breach of Required Risk Capital or ALM obligations), and enumerated steps (reduce exposure, drain, shut down). It gives no thresholds, no criteria for determining an emergency, and no deadlines, and leaves the content of the strategy itself unspecified, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) provides a defined incident framework in which Sky Core may impose penalties up to conservatorship for losses, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) apply to Risk Capital rule breaches. These plausibly reach a breach of the Risk Capital obligations this rule references, but no consequence is quantified for failing to maintain a fallback strategy itself, and escalation depends on someone invoking it.

assessments.title: Step 0: Net Revenue
assessments.quote:
The sole function of Step 0 is to establish the Net Revenue of the Sky Protocol. It performs no allocations to downstream functions or buffers, unlike subsequent steps for which this Net Revenue serves as the input.

Net Revenue is calculated for a single calendar month. Income from and Expenses owed to Prime Agents that settle through the Monthly Settlement Cycle are recognized in the month covered by that cycle. Where an amount recognized in an earlier month is subsequently adjusted, the adjustment is likewise recognized in the month covered by the cycle that settles it, and the earlier month's Net Revenue is not changed, as specified in [A.2.4.1.2.1.4 - True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle](de1592f5-dbce-46de-913f-6ec9589d36e8). Stability Fees on crypto vaults, legacy Real World Assets, and the SKY-Backed Borrowing vaults are recognized as they accrue, as are the interest expenses of the Sky Savings Rate, the Dai Savings Rate, and stUSDS. All other items of Income and Expense are recognized when USDS or DAI enter or leave the Sky Surplus Buffer. Transfers out of accounts other than the Sky Surplus Buffer are not recognized as Expenses, except as provided in [A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1.6.4 - Expense Recognition For Legacy Account Consolidation](1760b35f-da5a-4504-a014-dd7a611b4c0e).
assessments.description: Defines how Net Revenue is recognized by calendar month, including timing rules for Stability Fees, savings-rate interest, and Surplus Buffer flows.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Recognition timing is concrete: a single calendar month, Monthly Settlement Cycle attribution, accrual-based recognition for named fee and interest streams, and recognition when USDS or DAI enter or leave the Sky Surplus Buffer. Gaps remain: no Net Revenue formula is stated, and the 'all other items' catch-all depends on referenced sections.
metrics: Net Revenue calculated for a single calendar month
Income and Expenses from Prime Agents recognized in the month covered by the Monthly Settlement Cycle that settles them
Stability Fees and savings-rate interest recognized as they accrue
All other Income and Expense recognized when USDS or DAI enter or leave the Sky Surplus Buffer
Transfers out of accounts other than the Sky Surplus Buffer are not recognized as Expenses, except as provided in A.2.3.1.2.2.2.1.6.4
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. This is an accounting recognition rule with no penalty, on-chain automatic consequence, or named enforcer tied to misstated Net Revenue; the cited UUIDs are cross-references to other rules, not enforcement mechanisms.

assessments.title: Internal Senior Risk Capital Income
assessments.quote: Internal Senior Risk Capital income is the revenue attributed to Sky from the total payments made by Primes for Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). ISRC itself is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital, as specified in [A.2.3.1.3 - Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital](ac7a6636-acbc-40c9-abc1-4543c0beb300). While Primes pay a single clearing price for their OSRC based on the monthly Origination Process, the total revenue received by Sky is subsequently allocated proportionally, with the portion corresponding to ISRC's share of the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool designated as ISRC Income.
assessments.description: Defines Internal Senior Risk Capital income as Sky's revenue from Prime OSRC payments, allocated proportionally by ISRC's share of TSRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The proportional allocation by ISRC's share of TSRC is a stated formula with defined terms and a monthly origination cadence. The clearing price and the TSRC/ISRC values are defined elsewhere or unquantified here, so the magnitudes are not stated in this paragraph.
metrics: Revenue allocated proportionally by ISRC's share of the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool
Primes pay a single clearing price for OSRC set through the monthly Origination Process
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This paragraph is an income-attribution definition with no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism tied to its allocation rule, and it does not reference any citable enforcement machinery.

assessments.title: External Senior Risk Capital Fees
assessments.quote: External Senior Risk Capital Fees are levied by Sky and calculated as 5% of the net interest earnings generated by the External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) pool each Monthly Settlement Cycle. These earnings represent the portion of the total revenue from Primes' Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) payments that is attributed proportionally to ESRC, based on its contribution to the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool for that cycle. This 5% fee is deducted before the remaining ESRC earnings contribute to the srUSDS conversion rate. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.2 - ESRC Earnings Fee](559f6fb6-daf6-41b2-9882-53a91aaf132f).
assessments.description: Sets External Senior Risk Capital fees at 5% of monthly ESRC net interest earnings, deducted before srUSDS conversion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified (5% fee, monthly cycle, deduction before srUSDS conversion). The earnings attribution is described only as proportional to ESRC's share of TSRC, with no explicit formula or input values.
metrics: Fee = 5% of net interest earnings generated by the ESRC pool
Calculated each Monthly Settlement Cycle
Fee deducted before remaining ESRC earnings contribute to srUSDS conversion rate
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Sky levies the fee itself, which is self-enforcement, and no catalog mechanism (penalty, liquidation, emergency spell, artifact review) reaches an underpayment or miscalculation of this fee. The cited ESRC Earnings Fee doc is a reference, not an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Step 1: Security And Maintenance
assessments.quote: All of the Net Revenue from Step 0 (see [A.2.3.1.2.1.1 - Net Revenue](bddce7bf-c568-444b-b196-e15a99016696)) becomes Step 1 Capital. Twenty percent (20%) of Step 1 Capital is allocated for security and maintenance of the Sky Ecosystem as specified in the documents herein. The remaining eighty percent (80%) of Step 1 Capital becomes Step 2 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.description: Splits Step 1 Capital from Net Revenue, allocating 20% to security and maintenance and 80% to Step 2 Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is a fixed 20%/80% split of Step 1 Capital, which is verifiable from the text. The use of the 20% is delegated to 'the documents herein' and no measurement cadence or timing is stated.
metrics: Net Revenue from Step 0 becomes 100% of Step 1 Capital
20% of Step 1 Capital allocated for security and maintenance
80% of Step 1 Capital becomes Step 2 Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. This is an internal allocation split with no on-chain constraint, penalty, or named enforcer tied to the 20%/80% division. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could apply.

assessments.title: Fortification Foundation Allocation
assessments.quote: Ten percent (10%) of Step 1 Capital is allocated to the Fortification Foundation, covering legal defense, resilience, and unquantifiable risk management. See [A.2.13.1.2 - Fortification Foundation Grants](ec2ebbba-6944-44cb-a04d-4572c6bea1e7). Until the Fortification Foundation is fully operational, this allocation may be directed to the Sky Frontier Foundation on an interim basis to support protocol development and growth.
assessments.description: Allocates 10% of Step 1 Capital to the Fortification Foundation, with an interim option to direct it to Sky Frontier Foundation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 10% share of a defined pool (Step 1 Capital) is a verifiable number. The interim redirection trigger, 'until the Fortification Foundation is fully operational', is undefined, and no cadence or deadline is given.
metrics: Ten percent (10%) of Step 1 Capital allocated to the Fortification Foundation
Interim redirection to Sky Frontier Foundation until the Fortification Foundation is fully operational
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule governs Sky Core's own treasury allocation, so no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism reaches a deviation. The cited grants doc (ec2ebbba) is a cross-reference, not an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Core Council Buffer Multisig Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Core Council Buffer Multisig has a 5/6 signing requirement.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Buffer Multisig to use a 5-of-6 signing threshold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific actor (Core Council Buffer Multisig) and an exact numeric threshold (5 of 6 signers), which a third party can verify from the multisig configuration. It states no cadence, but a static signer threshold does not need one.
metrics: 5/6 signing requirement (5 of 6 signers must sign)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The multisig contract itself enforces the threshold on-chain, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph ties this rule to a consequence, so it cannot be rated mid or strong.

assessments.title: Core Council Buffer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote: The signers must use the Core Council Buffer Multisig to disburse funds on behalf of the Core Council.
assessments.description: Requires the signers to disburse Core Council funds only through the Core Council Buffer Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (signers) and a controlled system (the Buffer Multisig), so compliance can be checked against disbursement records. It gives no threshold, cadence, or definition of what counts as a disbursement, leaving the scope of the obligation open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells allow pre-authorized freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach unauthorized disbursements outside the multisig. The paragraph does not state a consequence, and the spell would need to be triggered by a party who identifies the violation.

assessments.title: Core Council Buffer Multisig Modification
assessments.quote:
The signers can change the signers of the Core Council Buffer Multisig so long as:

- there are exactly six (6) signers;
- exactly five (5) signers are required to execute transactions; and
- two (2) signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator, three (3) signers are controlled by Core GovOps, and one (1) signer is controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.
assessments.description: Constrains changes to Core Council Buffer Multisig signers: six total, five required to execute, split 2 Facilitator, 3 Core GovOps, 1 Soter Labs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Every operative parameter is a stated number: total signers (6), execution threshold (5), and a per-controller split (2/3/1). A third party could check compliance against the multisig's signer set directly from the text. No change cadence or notice period is given, which does not prevent verification of the constraint.
metrics: exactly six (6) signers
exactly five (5) signers required to execute transactions
two (2) signers controlled by the Core Facilitator
three (3) signers controlled by Core GovOps
one (1) signer controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention such as freezing when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a non-compliant signer configuration. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and depends on someone triggering the spell, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Expense Recognition For Legacy Account Consolidation
assessments.quote: The consolidation of funds from Legacy Accounts into the Core Council Buffer or the Demand Side Buffer (see [A.2.2.4.3 - Demand Side Buffer](862b6d83-f464-4125-8259-233b7de75ec4)) is recognized as a one-time expense for purposes of [A.2.3.1.2.1 - Step 0: Net Revenue](c09435ff-d876-442a-899c-ad494175500b). This achieves the same result as if the funds in Legacy Accounts had been returned to the Sky Surplus Buffer and subsequently transferred to the relevant downstream account.
assessments.description: Classifies consolidating Legacy Account funds into the Core Council or Demand Side Buffer as a one-time expense for Net Revenue.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the accounts, the buffers, and the Step 0 Net Revenue calculation, and gives a clear classification (one-time expense). It states no amount basis, measurement period, or timing, so how much is expensed and when is left open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or review mechanism watches how a consolidation is classified in Net Revenue; the only backstop is the generic misalignment and adjudication process.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Required Number Of Signers
assessments.quote: The Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig has a 3/4 signing requirement.
assessments.description: Sets the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig's signing requirement at 3 of 4 signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact signer threshold (3 of 4) for a named controlled system, so a third party could verify compliance from the text alone. It has no cadence or conditions, but none are needed for a static signing parameter.
metrics: Signing requirement: 3 of 4 signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The multisig's signing threshold would be technically self-enforcing on-chain, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph covers it, so no citable mechanism reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps must use the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig to disburse funds to Aligned Delegates.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps to disburse funds to Aligned Delegates only through the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names defined actors and a specific controlled system, and compliance is checkable as a binary question of whether disbursements used the multisig. It gives no amounts, cadence, signer thresholds, or definition of a disbursement, so it is procedural rather than quantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could plausibly reach an unauthorized disbursement path. The paragraph attaches no specific consequence, and no penalty or artifact review targets Core Facilitator or Core GovOps for this duty.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig Modification
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps can change the signers of the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig so long as:

- there are at least four (4) signers;
- a majority of signers are required to execute transactions; and
- an equal number of signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps.
assessments.description: Sets minimum signer count, majority execution threshold, and equal Core Facilitator/Core GovOps signer split for changes to the Aligned Delegates Buffer Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Concrete numeric thresholds are stated: at least four signers, a majority to execute, and an equal split between two defined actors. Gaps include no measurement cadence, no deadline for changes, and 'controlled by' is not defined, so the equal-split test is not fully objective.
metrics: at least four (4) signers
a majority of signers required to execute transactions
equal number of signers controlled by the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach an unauthorized change to multisig composition. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the signer-split condition itself.

assessments.title: Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.quote:
Step 1 Capital that remains after the Step 1 allocation becomes Step 2 Capital.

The allocation of Step 2 Capital depends on the level of Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) relative to the Turbo-Fill Floor (see [A.3.5.3.2.2 - Turbo-Fill Floor](db2aaf07-4ebb-4e5d-ae5e-575717d8fbcd)) and the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below the Turbo-Fill Floor, fifty percent (50%) of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and below the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, the portion of Step 2 Capital retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital is calculated as fifty percent (50%) multiplied by the fill factor, where the fill factor is one (1) minus the ratio of current Aggregate Backstop Capital to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and at or above the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, none of Step 2 Capital is retained; all of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).
assessments.description: Allocates residual Step 2 Capital between retention for Aggregate Backstop Capital and Step 3, based on backstop level versus thresholds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The retention percentage (50%) and the fill-factor formula (1 minus current over target backstop capital) are fully stated, and the three regimes are exhaustively covered. The Turbo-Fill Floor and Target Aggregate Backstop Capital values are delegated to other documents and not stated here.
metrics: Retention share of Step 2 Capital when Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Turbo-Fill Floor: 50%
Retention when between Turbo-Fill Floor and Target: 50% × fill factor
Fill factor = 1 − (current Aggregate Backstop Capital ÷ Target Aggregate Backstop Capital)
Retention when at or above Target: 0% (all Step 2 Capital passes to Step 3)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. This is a protocol allocation formula with no actor obligation whose violation carries a consequence; the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is a loss-absorption backstop, not an enforcement path for this allocation rule.

assessments.title: Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) consists of a portion of the excess capital of the Sky Protocol that is reinvested in providing Senior Risk Capital to Prime Agents. ISRC is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) in two components: one hundred percent (100%) of any Aggregate Backstop Capital in excess of the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)), plus one third (1/3) of Aggregate Backstop Capital up to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital.
assessments.description: Defines how Internal Senior Risk Capital is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital relative to its target.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The sourcing formula is fully specified (100% of excess over target, plus one-third of ABC up to target), but the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital value is only cross-referenced and not stated here. Nothing in the text dictates how or when the amounts are measured.
metrics: ISRC sourced at 100% of Aggregate Backstop Capital in excess of Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
ISRC sourced at one-third (1/3) of Aggregate Backstop Capital up to Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines a sourcing formula with no actor who could violate it and no consequence attached. Protocol-level backstop mechanics are not cited here and would not directly police this allocation rule.

assessments.title: Allocation Modification
assessments.quote:
In the short term, the Core Council may reduce the allocations of Step 1 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.2 - Step 1: Security And Maintenance](324e9d22-70fe-4e44-82ab-118815f5c42e)) and Step 2 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88)) below their specified levels and restore them up to those levels, and modify the allocation of Step 3 Capital among its specified uses (see [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121)). A reduction to the Step 1 allocation may be apportioned among its components as the Core Council determines. For Step 2 Capital, the specified level is the retention its allocation formula specifies for the current state. The Core Council exercises this authority through a public post by the Core Facilitator on the Sky Forum, confirmed by Core GovOps and the Core Council Risk Advisor.

The implementation of such modifications is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without requiring a prior Governance Poll.
assessments.description: Lets the Core Council reduce and restore Step 1 and Step 2 capital and modify Step 3 uses via a public Forum post and direct Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actors (Core Council, Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Risk Advisor) and a process (Sky Forum post, confirmation, Executive Vote without Governance Poll). Magnitudes are delegated: "short term" is undefined, reductions are at the Council's discretion with no cap, and Step 3 modifications have no criteria.
metrics: "Short term" (undefined duration)
Step 2 specified level = retention per its allocation formula for the current state
Step 1 reduction apportioned as the Core Council determines (no cap)
Public post by Core Facilitator on Sky Forum
Confirmation by Core GovOps and Core Council Risk Advisor
Executive Vote proceeds without prior Governance Poll
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Core Council is the actor exercising the authority, and the GovOps and Risk Advisor confirmation is a procedural gate with no defined escalation or penalty. Penalty Mechanisms and Agent Artifact Review target Primes and Agents, not the Council, and the Adjudication and Misalignment catch-alls are insufficient alone.

assessments.title: Operational Processes
assessments.quote:
The Monthly Settlement Cycle (MSC) synchronizes several key operational processes across the ecosystem, including:

1. Sky Protocol’s net revenue for the month covered by the cycle is calculated and allocated through the steps of the Treasury Management Function. See [A.2.3 - Treasury Management](6c0af059-5d33-4e2b-90f1-1606957b8f85).
2. The monthly Senior Risk Capital (SRC) origination process is settled: the clearing price is established, costs are deducted from winning Prime Agents’ accounts, and their accounts are credited with Originated SRC (OSRC) for the upcoming month. See [A.3.2.2.4.3.5 - Settlement Of Origination](fff0112a-58dd-4041-97f9-7baf113b4e70).
3. Queued conversions between USDS and srUSDS within the SRC system are processed. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.2 - Deposit And Redemption Queues](38a99586-4a13-4ce3-8b2f-cee025e0c390).
4. Pioneer Incentive Pools are funded with an amount equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS. See [A.2.2.9.3 - Pioneer Chain Primitive](4c7be4c6-44b5-407a-94ae-3d7ca7e8039c).
5. Smart Burn Engine parameters are updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle based on the prior month's state, and between Monthly Settlement Cycles as necessary as specified in [A.2.3.1.4.1 - Staking Rewards Rate Adjustment](de233df4-34cc-4e88-a065-9a9dde9add3c). See [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121) and [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a).
6. Critical Core GovOps functions related to the operationalization of Sky Primitives are executed, including payment/reimbursement processing, compliance monitoring, and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties.
assessments.description: Lists processes the Monthly Settlement Cycle synchronizes: net revenue allocation, SRC origination settlement, queue processing, Pioneer pool funding, Smart Burn updates, and Core GovOps functions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Item 4 gives a concrete formula (Sky Savings Rate times Unrewarded USDS) and the cycle is monthly, but most items delegate operative detail to cross-referenced sections. Item 5 allows between-cycle updates 'as necessary' and item 6 lists functions with no criteria.
metrics: Pioneer Incentive Pools funded with Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS
Monthly Settlement Cycle occurs monthly
Smart Burn Engine parameters updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle and between cycles as necessary
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a synchronization schedule with no stated consequence for missing a settlement step. The penalty machinery (b8ee2d12) applies to Prime and agent violations of other rules, not to this coordination duty, so it does not clearly reach it.

assessments.title: Payment Of Amounts Due To Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Amounts due to Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see [A.2.4.1.2.1.3.3 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents](07c5cfd2-d68a-40d6-873d-b82cea9a92be)), are transferred from the Sky Surplus Buffer to the Prime SubProxy Account through an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires amounts due to Prime Agents, excluding Operational Executor reimbursements, be transferred from Surplus Buffer to SubProxy by Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the source (Sky Surplus Buffer), destination (Prime SubProxy Account), and approval path (Executive Vote), plus a carve-out cross-reference. However, the amounts due are defined elsewhere with no magnitude, formula, or payment deadline stated here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) is protocol-level loss absorption rather than an actor-level penalty for mis-settlement, and no penalty, conservatorship, or artifact review is tied to this payment transfer. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Collection Of Amounts Due From Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Amounts due from Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see [A.2.4.1.2.1.3.3 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents](07c5cfd2-d68a-40d6-873d-b82cea9a92be)) are settled in a way that is equivalent to a transfer from the Prime to the Sky Surplus Buffer through actions included in an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Requires amounts due from Prime Agents, excluding OXA reimbursements, to be settled as transfers to the Surplus Buffer via Executive Vote actions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete destination (Sky Surplus Buffer) and a governing process (Executive Vote), but gives no amounts, deadlines, or cadence. Whether it binds before a specific vote sets the actions is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism is tied to non-payment of amounts due. The Surplus Buffer is the settlement destination, not an enforcer of payment, and the rule relies on Sky Core's own Executive Vote, which is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Revenue Share
assessments.quote: Grove and Spark agree to a bilateral revenue share, up to 40% maximum with JRC rental, see [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Caps the bilateral revenue share between Grove and Spark agents at 40% when paired with JRC rental.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A numeric ceiling (40% maximum) is stated, but the revenue base, calculation method, and payment cadence are undefined. The JRC rental condition is delegated to a cross-referenced primitive rather than specified here.
metrics: Bilateral revenue share up to 40% maximum
Revenue share applies with JRC rental
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Risk Capital penalty, conservatorship, and PSM mechanisms do not reach a commercial revenue-share cap between agents, and the cited Risk Capital Rental Primitive is a rule definition rather than an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: ASC Provision
assessments.quote: Grove retains the right to deploy into repo lending protocols to meet ASC requirements. Deposits must be capped at the lower of either 10% of protocol USDC deposits or the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral, as defined in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8). The Spark Agent retains the right to use the PSM for ASC, provided it covers the cost to Grove.
assessments.description: Lets Grove deploy into repo lending for ASC, capped at the lower of 10% of USDC deposits or Minimum ASC; Spark may use the PSM if it covers Grove's cost.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core cap is quantified at 10% of protocol USDC deposits and tied to a Minimum ASC threshold defined elsewhere, but that threshold's value is not stated here. The PSM condition ('covers the cost to Grove') has no measurable standard, and no measurement cadence is given.
metrics: Repo lending deposits capped at the lower of 10% of protocol USDC deposits or Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (A.3.3.2.2)
PSM use for ASC permitted only if it covers the cost to Grove (unquantified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) could reach a Grove deposit-cap breach, with Core GovOps as an enforcer distinct from the agent. However, no penalty amount is quantified for this specific cap, and escalation requires a review to be triggered.

assessments.title: Risk Capital Share
assessments.quote: Grove agrees to rent to Spark 50% of the Required Risk Capital associated with Spark’s investments in USDe and sUSDe as a Junior Risk Capital Rental. See [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Requires Grove to rent Spark 50% of the Required Risk Capital on Spark's USDe and sUSDe investments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified (50%), with named actors and defined asset scope (USDe, sUSDe). The base 'Required Risk Capital' is defined elsewhere, and no measurement cadence or settlement timing is stated.
metrics: 50% of the Required Risk Capital associated with Spark's investments in USDe and sUSDe
assessments.enforcementReasoning: As a Risk Capital rental term between Primes, a shortfall plausibly falls under the Penalty Mechanisms that incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules. The paragraph itself sets no consequence, so the penalty amount and escalation for this rental are unquantified.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote:
Spark and Grove expressly intend that Grove shares in 50% of the risks of Spark’s investment in USDe and sUSDe and not in the risk of any other investments by Spark.

To the extent that USDe or sUSDe investments experience losses and Spark is allocated a greater than 50% share of those losses relative to Grove under the TIP JRC mechanism (see [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2.1 - Initial Loss Absorption By "Tip JRC"](6c33bcf5-c29d-48ca-9ee5-e37dcdeb0630)), Grove will transfer funds to Spark so that Grove and Spark each bear 50% of the losses that occur.

To the extent that Spark experiences losses on investments other than USDe or sUSDe and a portion of those losses is allocated to the Junior Risk Capital rented from Grove, Spark shall reimburse Grove for those losses.
assessments.description: Sets a 50/50 loss-sharing split between Spark and Grove on USDe/sUSDe and requires Spark to reimburse Grove for other rented-JRC losses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 50% share is an explicit, verifiable number and the trigger (Spark allocated more than 50% of losses) is clear. Gaps: no settlement deadline or cadence for transfers, and the reimbursement for non-USDe/sUSDe losses is stated without a quantified amount or timing.
metrics: Grove bears 50% of the risk of Spark's USDe and sUSDe investments
Grove transfers funds to Spark when Spark's allocated share of USDe/sUSDe losses exceeds 50% relative to Grove under the TIP JRC mechanism
Spark reimburses Grove for losses on non-USDe/sUSDe investments allocated to the rented Junior Risk Capital (no cadence stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The transfer and reimbursement duties concern Risk Capital allocation between Primes, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship for capital-requirement breaches (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach a failure to transfer or reimburse. Escalation is not specified for this accord, and the TIP JRC reference is a loss-allocation mechanism rather than an enforcer, so the rating stops at mid.

assessments.title: Recourse
assessments.quote: Sky’s recourse for bad debt consists of (1) minting Prime Agent tokens; (2) terminating a Prime’s right to further borrowing; and (3) activation of the Resolution Mechanism which includes, without limitation, the authority to suspend all protocol operations, seize or reallocate all of the Prime assets, override or disable smart contract functions, initiate managed restructuring, or execute full and permanent liquidation of the affected sub-protocol and all of its assets, in order to contain risk and preserve the stability and solvency of the broader ecosystem.
assessments.description: Defines Sky's recourse for Prime bad debt: minting Prime Agent tokens, terminating borrowing rights, and activating a broad Resolution Mechanism.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The remedies are enumerated, but 'bad debt' has no quantified trigger, the Resolution Mechanism's activation criteria and actor are unstated, and 'without limitation' leaves its powers open-ended. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is itself a remedy that Sky applies to a Prime after bad debt, and it names concrete powers (asset seizure, liquidation, borrowing termination). Risk-Capital Incident Response and Conservatorship (named enforcer, escalation path) plausibly reach this scenario, but the activation path and trigger are not defined here, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: Each genesis capital allocation is subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)).
assessments.description: Makes each genesis capital allocation subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop, cross-referenced to A.3.7.1.6.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes a real obligation that every genesis allocation is subject to the backstop, but states no threshold, formula, or deadline. Its magnitude and mechanics are delegated entirely to the cross-referenced A.3.7.1.6, so a defender could argue it binds nothing concrete here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Genesis Capital Backstop (cited verbatim by UUID in the paragraph) is an economic loss-absorption mechanism that plausibly reaches genesis allocation losses. Its consequence for this rule is unquantified in the text, so it rates mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Current Control (Until 2026)
assessments.quote: The Peg Stability Module (PSM) remains directly managed and controlled by Sky until the full deployment and operationalization of the Actively Stabilizing Collateral (ASC) system. Sky retains responsibility for setting debt ceilings, determining liquidity levels, and overseeing asset management activities within the PSM during this period.
assessments.description: Keeps Sky in direct control of the PSM, including debt ceilings, liquidity and asset management, until ASC is fully operational.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Sky) and concrete parameters (debt ceilings, liquidity levels, asset management), but gives no magnitudes or cadence. The end condition, full ASC deployment and operationalization, is undefined, so compliance is arguable either way.
metrics: Control period ends at "full deployment and operationalization" of ASC (no date or measurable criteria given)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM's fixed-rate swaps (0082c12d) enforce the peg, not Sky's management decisions. Oversight would fall to Sky's own executive and spells, which is self-enforcement, so only the catch-all backstops remain.

assessments.title: Transition to Grove (2025)
assessments.quote: Beginning in 2025, Grove shall assume operational and accounting ownership of the PSM, incorporating the PSM’s assets into its total value locked (TVL). Sky maintains active oversight and retains final control over strategic and operational decision-making within the PSM until full ASC implementation occurs.
assessments.description: Transfers PSM operational and accounting ownership to Grove from 2025, with Sky retaining final control until full ASC implementation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The start date (2025) and the transfer of operational and accounting ownership and TVL inclusion are concrete. However, the end of Sky's final-control period depends on "full ASC implementation," which is undefined and has no verifiable criteria.
metrics: Beginning in 2025
until full ASC implementation occurs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Peg Stability Module's fixed-rate swaps enforce peg behaviour, not the ownership assignment, and no cited mechanism (Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship, Emergency Spells, Artifact Review) is linked to this transfer rule in the text.

assessments.title: Base Rate Obligation
assessments.quote: Grove will be required to pay the Base Rate on all assets within the PSM. The Base Rate is dynamic and will align with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate), expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates. See [A.2.8.2.2.2.2.3 - Base Rate](fd39df25-6093-49ae-be12-36df34754612).
assessments.description: Requires Grove to pay a dynamic Base Rate, tied to the SSR, on all PSM assets.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation names a defined actor (Grove), a controlled system (PSM), and a parameter (Base Rate tied to SSR), but the rate itself is delegated to a cross-referenced doc. 'Expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates' gives no numeric bounds, cadence, or formula.
metrics: Base Rate paid on all assets within the PSM
Base Rate aligns with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate)
Base Rate expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could check whether Grove is paying the Base Rate, and Penalty Mechanisms could price non-payment. Neither mechanism is quantified for this specific payment obligation, and no on-chain automatic enforcement is stated for the fee.

assessments.title: Yield on USDC
assessments.quote: Grove shall earn yield through Coinbase Custody on USDC holdings within the PSM, enabling potential positive carry depending upon the spread between custody yield and the Base Rate.
assessments.description: Requires Grove to earn yield through Coinbase Custody on USDC held within the PSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states an obligation ('shall earn yield') with a named actor, venue, and asset, but gives no minimum yield, allocation share, or cadence. The carry outcome is expressly contingent ('potential... depending upon the spread'), so a defender could argue both compliance and non-binding effect on the same facts.
metrics: Spread between custody yield and the Base Rate (referenced, no threshold or value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM's on-chain swap mechanism (0082c12d) enforces the peg, not Grove's yield-earning duty, and no penalty, review, or emergency path is tied to this obligation. Only the catch-all misalignment reporting applies.

assessments.title: Economic Rationale
assessments.quote: Grove will pay the Base Rate on the PSM for the purpose of meeting ASC requirements, if there are no better alternatives available. Unlike other alternatives, USDC in the PSM will have no capital requirement. If other, better options for ASC are available, Grove should empty the PSM and allocate the assets to those options. It is anticipated that other protocols will also be willing to rent ASC "points", potentially allowing for the management of ASC needs across several Prime Agents for a profit.
assessments.description: Explains Grove's economic rationale for using USDC in the PSM to meet ASC needs, with reallocation if better options exist.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Obligations are expressed in judgment terms such as 'if there are no better alternatives' and 'should empty the PSM', with no threshold or cadence. 'Base Rate' is referenced but not valued here, and the profit expectation is only 'anticipated'.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The PSM's fixed-rate swaps (0082c12d) enforce the peg, not Grove's allocation choice between PSM and other ASC options, and no mechanism watches this economic-rationale duty beyond the catch-all misalignment process.

assessments.title: Short Term (2025-2026)
assessments.quote: The PSM will remain a central liquidity hub for stablecoin deployment. Grove will manage the PSM, paying the Base Rate while earning USDC yield, under Sky oversight until full ASC implementation. PSM assets will count toward Grove's TVL, enhancing its economic standing and collateral efficiency.
assessments.description: Short-term plan: Grove manages the PSM under Sky oversight, paying Base Rate and counting PSM assets toward its TVL.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the Base Rate parameter and the Sky oversight role, but gives no Base Rate value, no oversight criteria, and no end date for 'full ASC implementation'. The text is largely descriptive ('will remain a central liquidity hub', 'enhancing economic standing'), so a defender could argue it imposes no measurable obligation.
metrics: Base Rate paid to Sky on PSM assets (value not stated)
Period 'until full ASC implementation' (milestone with no date or criteria)
Short Term (2025-2026) (from paragraph heading, not restated in text)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Grove is a Prime agent subject to Core GovOps artifact review, a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could reach its PSM management and Base Rate payments. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the PSM peg-arbitrage mechanism does not reach these economic-management duties.

assessments.title: Long Term (Post-2026)
assessments.quote: The PSM's role will diminish as the ASC system becomes the primary liquidity management tool. Grove can wind down the PSM entirely if ASC requirements are fulfilled through other mechanisms (e.g., Uniswap positions, Curve pools). If ASC obligations rise significantly, PSM usage will increase, but as the system matures, its relevance will gradually decline.
assessments.description: Anticipates the PSM's role declining as ASC becomes primary liquidity tool, with Grove permitted to wind down the PSM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is forward-looking posture language ('will diminish', 'will gradually decline') with no numeric threshold, metric, or deadline. 'Significantly' and 'gradually' are undefined, so it is a non-binding expectation rather than an operative rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism watches or penalizes a failure to follow this expected trajectory; the PSM's peg mechanism is not tied to this long-term statement, and only the generic misalignment backstop could apply.

assessments.title: Risk Management
assessments.quote: The PSM serves as a capital buffer, enabling Grove to scale liquidity massively without additional credit enhancement. As ASC obligations fluctuate, the PSM will act as a dynamic backstop, ensuring resilience during periods of high demand.
assessments.description: States that the PSM serves as a capital buffer and dynamic backstop for Grove's ASC obligations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a posture statement with no thresholds, formulas, metrics, cadence, or defined obligations; phrases like 'massively' and 'dynamic backstop' are aspirational. Nothing concrete exists to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism is tied to the claim that the PSM will backstop ASC obligations; the PSM's on-chain swap mechanism (0082c12d) enforces the peg, not this capital-buffer posture, and only the catch-all backstops apply.

assessments.title: Transfer Of Capital Funds
assessments.quote: The transfer of the Genesis Capital Allocation to each Prime SubProxy (i.e. the Spark SubProxy and Grove SubProxy) shall occur once funding from the Surplus Buffer is approved. This condition ensures that capital deployment is aligned with the successful launch of the Prime's token and the commencement of its independent operations.
assessments.description: Conditions transfer of the Genesis Capital Allocation to the Spark and Grove SubProxies on approval of Surplus Buffer funding.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actors (Spark and Grove SubProxies) and a trigger (Surplus Buffer funding approval), but gives no amount, deadline, or approving party. The launch-alignment rationale is qualitative, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no penalty or escalation for an early or unapproved transfer, and no listed mechanism reaches this funding gate. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Prime Revenue Credit
assessments.quote: Grove is owed 2,528,000 USDS based on the true-up of prior Monthly Settlement Cycles. Until this amount is paid to Grove through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle, this credit counts toward Grove's Total Risk Capital (TRC), as defined in [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).
assessments.description: Records a 2,528,000 USDS amount owed to Grove and counts it toward Grove's Total Risk Capital until paid.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The owed amount (2,528,000 USDS) and the TRC-counting condition are exact and checkable. The payment deadline is tied to the 'next Monthly Settlement Cycle', which is defined elsewhere and given no date or cadence in this paragraph.
metrics: Amount owed to Grove: 2,528,000 USDS
Credit counts toward Grove's TRC until paid
Payment deadline: through the next Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Counting toward TRC makes this a Risk Capital rule for a Prime (Grove), which the Penalty Mechanisms (A.3.2.2.7.2) reach. The penalty amount is not quantified for this specific credit, and no escalation is stated for failing to pay the amount.

assessments.title: Resilience Fund Aggregate Cap
assessments.quote: Claims will be subject to an aggregate cap for all claims in relation to a Claim Event determined by the risk models elaborated by the Resilience Technical Committee.
assessments.description: Caps aggregate Resilience Fund claims per Claim Event at a level set by Resilience Technical Committee risk models.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Resilience Technical Committee) and a metric (aggregate cap per Claim Event), but gives no cap value, formula, or cadence; the magnitude is delegated to unpublished models. A defender could argue no binding cap exists until those models are issued, so the score is capped at 2.
metrics: Aggregate cap for all claims in relation to a Claim Event, determined by Resilience Technical Committee risk models
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, capital-at-risk, penalty, or review mechanism in the catalog is tied to enforcing a claims cap; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication paths would apply.

assessments.title: Bug Bounty Program For Critical Infrastructure
assessments.quote: As one of the most important DeFi protocols with a high TVL, the Sky Protocol is a honeypot for hackers and other nefarious actors. The Sky Protocol must always be protected by an active Bug Bounty Program. This document regulates the budget and processes of the Bug Bounty Program, which serves to protect the Sky Protocol and its users from hacks and exploits. The Bug Bounty Program is conducted on the Immunefi platform.
assessments.description: Requires the Sky Protocol to always maintain an active Bug Bounty Program on Immunefi, with budget and processes set in a separate document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to 'always be protected by an active Bug Bounty Program' is identifiable, but 'active' is undefined and no budget, coverage, or payout threshold appears here. The paragraph is largely posture and defers operative detail to another document.
metrics: Sky Protocol must always be protected by an active Bug Bounty Program
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No listed mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, emergency spells, insurance pricing) is tied to maintaining the bounty program; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Introduction
assessments.quote:
The Bug Bounty Program aims to create incentives for hackers to contribute to the resilience of the Sky Protocol as opposed to exploiting vulnerabilities for personal gain. Immunefi is the party responsible for conducting the Bug Bounty Program; its setup and operations are based on standards set by Immunefi.

The Sky Ecosystem must continue to maintain a Bug Bounty Program for SparkLend until the launch of the Spark Agent.
assessments.description: Requires the Sky Ecosystem to keep a bug bounty program for SparkLend until the Spark Agent launches, run by Immunefi.
