assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to maintain a SparkLend bug bounty program has a named actor and an end event (Spark Agent launch), but no bounty amounts, scope, coverage metric, or maintenance standard. Immunefi's standards are referenced without values, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Bug Bounty Program maintained for SparkLend until the launch of the Spark Agent
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism is tied to failing to maintain the SparkLend bounty; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Assets In Scope
assessments.quote:
The Assets In Scope of the Sky Core Bug Bounty Program will be those identified as critical infrastructure for the Sky Ecosystem.

For Sky Core, the Assets In Scope accepted for this Bug Bounty Program are specified on Sky’s listing on the Immunefi platform, which can be found at ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/)). Assets in Scope include smart contracts, frontend applications, data infrastructure and oracles.

For SparkLend, the Assets In Scope for the Bug Bounty Program is specified on SparkLend’s listing on the Immunefi platform, which can be found at ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/)). For SparkLend, the Assets In Scope only include smart contracts.

The Protocol Security Workstream Lead is responsible for maintaining these lists of Assets In Scope, in consultation with the relevant stakeholders.
assessments.description: Defines the Assets In Scope for the Sky Core and SparkLend bug bounty programs by reference to Immunefi listings.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Scope is delegated to external Immunefi listings, and the inclusion test ('critical infrastructure for the Sky Ecosystem') has no defined criteria. Asset categories (smart contracts, frontends, data infrastructure, oracles) are enumerated, but no measurable threshold or verifiable inclusion rule is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sets bug bounty scope, not a compliance obligation, and no penalty, emergency, or pricing mechanism in the catalog reaches a violation of it. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication paths apply.

assessments.title: Severity Classification
assessments.quote: The Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System ([https://immunefi.com/severity-updated/](https://immunefi.com/severity-updated/)) is applicable to both Sky Core and SparkLend. The Protocol Security Workstream Lead is authorized to adopt a new severity system for the Bug Bounty Programs in consultation with relevant technical stakeholders.
assessments.description: Applies Immunefi severity classification to Sky Core and SparkLend bug bounties; the Workstream Lead may adopt an alternative system.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an external Immunefi severity standard by URL, but states no thresholds, metrics, or cadence for classifying severity. The Workstream Lead's authority to replace the system with a new one, after unspecified consultation, leaves compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph sets a classification scheme for bug bounty severity but attaches no penalty, escalation, or on-chain consequence to misclassification or non-application, and no catalogued mechanism reaches it.

assessments.title: Out Of Scope Vulnerabilities And Other Limitations
assessments.quote:
A selection of vulnerabilities is deemed out of scope for the Bug Bounty Program. An overview of these out of scope vulnerabilities can be found on Sky’s listing on the Immunefi platform ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sky/scope/)). Feasibility limitations also apply, which can be found in the aforementioned listing on the Immunefi website.

Specific rules applying to the Bug Bounty Program can be found at the website above, listed under the following categories:

- Repeatable attack limitations
- Restrictions on security researcher eligibility
- Public disclosure of known issues
- Proof of Concept (PoC) requirements
- Other terms and information
- Prohibited activities

For SparkLend, the rules, terms, and exceptions can be found on SparkLend’s listing on the Immunefi platform ([https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/](https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/sparklend/scope/)).
assessments.description: Defines out-of-scope bug bounty vulnerabilities and points to external Immunefi listings for the detailed rules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no thresholds, criteria, or defined scope items; it delegates all operative content to external Immunefi pages. Nothing verifiable can be checked from the text itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism reaches bug bounty scope exclusions; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Rewards Payout Process
assessments.quote:
All bounty payouts are handled by Sky Governance. Upon confirmation, bug bounty payouts should be included in the next possible Executive Vote. This would involve sending USDS directly from the protocol’s buffer to the whitehat hacker.

Immunefi will publicly contact the Core Facilitator with the request, including a specification of the respective vulnerability report, the requested amount and the Ethereum mainnet addresses of the beneficiaries. This should also include the payment details of the Immunefi fee, if it applies. Immunefi and the Core Facilitator should make sure the payout is made within one full calendar month after the report was approved.

For Bug Bounty rewards over USD 1,000,000: after the first million is paid out, the remaining amount is paid out over time with up to USD 1,000,000 per consecutive month until the determined amount for payout is reached.
assessments.description: Sets how and when bug bounty rewards are paid from the protocol buffer, including a $1M-per-month cap above $1M.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph quantifies the $1,000,000 first tranche, the $1,000,000-per-month cap on later installments, and a one-full-calendar-month payout deadline. Gaps remain: "should" softens the obligations, "next possible Executive Vote" has no timing bound, and the confirmation trigger is undefined.
metrics: Bounty payouts over USD 1,000,000: first USD 1,000,000 paid out, remainder paid up to USD 1,000,000 per consecutive month
Payout made within one full calendar month after the report was approved
Payout included in the next possible Executive Vote upon confirmation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Surplus Buffer is named only as the funding source, not as a consequence for a late or missed payout. Sky Governance and the Core Facilitator police their own payout obligations, which is self-enforcement, and no penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Rewards Budget
assessments.quote:
The Bug Bounty Programs incur fixed and variable costs.

- Variable costs: Bug bounty payouts including related fees to Immunefi are considered variable costs and are covered by the process described in [A.2.11.1.1.3.3 - Rewards Payment Terms](cf4e6968-18a3-48d8-b38e-15ae8009d03d).
- Fixed costs: Fixed costs comprise service fees for the Immunefi Premium Triaging Service, and compensation of a part-time Bug Bounty program steward. These costs will be funded by Sky.
assessments.description: Classifies Bug Bounty Program costs as variable or fixed, with Sky funding fixed service fees and steward compensation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the cost categories and the funder (Sky), but gives no amounts, budget caps, or payment deadlines. The 'will be funded by Sky' obligation is identifiable, yet how much and when remain undefined, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The cross-referenced Rewards Payment Terms (cf4e6968) is not in the rubric's enforcement catalog, and no penalty, escalation, or on-chain mechanism reaches a failure to fund these costs. Sky funding its own costs is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Safe Harbor
assessments.quote: Sky Ecosystem is adopting the Security Alliance Safe Harbor Agreement ("Safe Harbor") by executing the procedures specified in [A.2.11.1.2.2 - Execution](25015208-5234-4818-8479-c46f927c272c). Safe Harbor is a public agreement that protocols may adopt to waive the right to pursue legal claims against a whitehat hacker, provided that the hacker acts competently, lawfully, and in good faith. Under Safe Harbor, any whitehat hacker who identifies a time-critical active exploit that could result in the loss of funds is authorized to act immediately to rescue those funds. Immediate intervention prevents delays that might otherwise cause irrevocable financial harm. Once the funds have been secured, the whitehat hacker returns them within 72 hours to an Asset Recovery Address (see [A.2.11.1.2.2.3.3.2 - Asset Recovery Addresses](3f125522-dff7-48a3-948f-e99c71fc3929)) designated by the protocol that has adopted the Safe Harbor Agreement.
assessments.description: Adopts the Security Alliance Safe Harbor, letting whitehat hackers rescue funds from active exploits and requiring return within 72 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 72-hour return deadline and the named Asset Recovery Address are concrete and checkable. Qualifiers such as 'time-critical active exploit', 'competently, lawfully, and in good faith' and 'could result in the loss of funds' are undefined, so whether a given rescue qualifies is left to judgment.
metrics: Funds returned within 72 hours after being secured
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The safe harbor is a legal waiver conditioned on good faith, but no catalog mechanism or on-chain control reaches the whitehat's 72-hour return duty or the scope limits. Only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication paths apply.

assessments.title: Accounts
assessments.quote:
The `accounts` parameter for each chain is a list of contracts to be included in Safe Harbor. Each contract listed must include the sub-elements of (1) the `accountAddress` of the contract and (2) the `childContractScope`, which specifies whether child contracts of the specified contract are covered. The possible values for the `childContractScope` parameter are: (1) `None` (no child contracts are in scope), (2) `ExistingOnly` (only child contracts created prior to calling `adoptSafeHarbor` are in scope), or (3) `All` (all child contracts are in scope).

The value of the `scope` parameter is all contracts specified in the Bug Bounty Program.

The `childContractScope` parameter for each contract is specified in the Bug Bounty Program.
assessments.description: Defines the Safe Harbor accounts parameter: listed contract addresses and their child contract scope options per chain.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives exact field names and an enumerated set for childContractScope (None, ExistingOnly, All), which is verifiable. However, the per-contract childContractScope values and the full scope list are delegated to the Bug Bounty Program, so the operative content is not stated here.
metrics: childContractScope must be one of: None, ExistingOnly (contracts created prior to calling adoptSafeHarbor), or All
scope is all contracts specified in the Bug Bounty Program
each listed contract requires an accountAddress and a childContractScope
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism (penalty, liquidation, emergency spell, artifact review) is shown to reach misconfigured Safe Harbor account or scope entries, and the paragraph cites no UUID.

assessments.title: Maintenance
assessments.quote: The list of contracts covered by the Safe Harbor agreement for Sky must be updated when new contracts are added. Whenever a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program, it should also be added to Safe Harbor. The Spell Teams are primarily responsible for updating the Safe Harbor registry each time a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program. The Core Facilitator is responsible for reviewing the work of the Spell Teams to ensure that this requirement is met.
assessments.description: Requires Spell Teams to add each new Bug Bounty contract to the Safe Harbor registry, with Core Facilitator review.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (a contract added to the Bug Bounty Program) and the actors (Spell Teams, Core Facilitator) are concrete. However, the operative verb is 'should' in one place and 'primarily responsible' elsewhere, and no deadline, cadence, or verification method is stated, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Trigger: each time a contract is added to the Bug Bounty Program, it should also be added to Safe Harbor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core Facilitator review of Spell Team work plausibly maps to Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps, which uses a named enforcer distinct from the actor with published outcomes. The text does not define consequences or escalation for a missed registry update, and no penalty is quantified, so it stays mid.

assessments.title: Multisig Administrator
assessments.quote: A Multisig Administrator is the entity or individual responsible for the setup, configuration, ongoing management, and compliance of a Multisig. Each Multisig must have a designated Multisig Administrator, communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps prior to the Multisig's activation or operational use.
assessments.description: Requires each Multisig to have a designated Multisig Administrator, communicated to Protocol Security and Core GovOps before activation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor and a concrete timing condition (communicated before activation or operational use) that a third party could check. The administrator's ongoing management and compliance duties are described only in general terms, with no metrics, cadence, or standards.
metrics: Each Multisig must have a designated Multisig Administrator
Administrator communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps prior to the Multisig's activation or operational use
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when security rules are violated, and a Multisig operating without a communicated administrator plausibly falls under that trigger. The consequence is not quantified for this designation rule, and firing depends on someone invoking the spell.

assessments.title: Impact Assessment
assessments.quote:
Impact Assessment defines the assessment process in which the potential impact of a Multisig compromise or failure is evaluated. The result of this evaluation is the assignment of an Impact Classification level as defined below. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for determining this classification and must provide it to Core GovOps as part of the Multisig registration process in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 - Multisig Registration](110614e9-6375-464a-90b3-3b350d3cf79c).

| **Impact Classification Level** | **Financial Exposure** | **Decision Context** | **Reputational Impact** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | <$100k direct exposure | Minimal disruption, alternative paths exist | Limited scope impact |
| Medium | $100k – $1M exposure | Significant operational delays, workarounds available | Moderate reputational concern |
| High | $1M – $10M exposure | Major protocol disruption, difficult recovery | Serious reputational damage |
| Critical | >$10M exposure | Protocol-wide failure, catastrophic impact | Severe reputational damage |

When a Multisig falls between two classification levels, the higher security classification must be selected.
assessments.description: Defines how a Multisig's compromise impact is classified into four levels by dollar exposure, assigned by the Multisig Administrator and submitted at registration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Financial exposure bands are numeric ($100k, $1M, $10M), but "direct exposure" is undefined and the Decision Context and Reputational Impact columns are qualitative. No measurement cadence or method for exposure is given, and the Administrator's determination is self-assessed.
metrics: Low: <$100k direct exposure
Medium: $100k – $1M exposure
High: $1M – $10M exposure
Critical: >$10M exposure
When between two levels, the higher classification must be selected
Classification must be provided to Core GovOps as part of Multisig registration
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) plausibly reaches a submitted classification through scheduled review with penalty assessment, but no consequence is quantified for misclassifying a Multisig. No on-chain or priced mechanism is tied to the level.

assessments.title: Operational Assessment
assessments.quote:
Operational Assessment defines the assessment process in which the operational response requirements of a Multisig are evaluated. The result of this evaluation is the assignment of an Operational Classification type as defined below. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for determining this classification and must provide it to Core GovOps as part of the Multisig registration process in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.8 - Multisig Registration](110614e9-6375-464a-90b3-3b350d3cf79c).

| **Operational Classification Type** | **Response Time** | **Decision Context** | **Verification Process** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine | 24 - 48 hours | Standard procedures, predictable operations | Full verification protocols |
| Time-Sensitive | 2 - 12 hours | Market conditions, protocol needs | Streamlined but thorough |
| Emergency | <2 hours | Crisis response, preventing immediate damage | Minimal delays, risk-appropriate |

When a Multisig falls between two classification levels, the higher security classification must be selected.
assessments.description: Defines Multisig operational classifications with response-time ranges and verification levels, assigned by the Multisig Administrator and submitted to Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Response-time windows (24-48h, 2-12h, <2h) are numeric, but the criteria for assigning a classification are qualitative ('standard procedures', 'market conditions', 'crisis response'). Verification processes are described only as 'streamlined but thorough' or 'risk-appropriate', so compliance on a given classification is arguable.
metrics: Routine response time: 24 - 48 hours
Time-Sensitive response time: 2 - 12 hours
Emergency response time: <2 hours
Multisig falling between two levels must be assigned the higher security classification
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Multisig Administrator self-determines the classification and submits it to Core GovOps during registration; no penalty, review, or escalation tied to a misclassification appears in the text, and the cited registration doc is a procedural link rather than an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Threshold Requirements
assessments.quote:
The baseline minimum threshold standards applicable to all Multisigs are:

- Multisigs must have a minimum of three (3) signers.
- Multisigs must maintain a signing threshold of at least fifty percent (50%) of total signers.

These requirements apply unless explicitly exempted in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.2 - Threshold Exceptions](130a44af-0715-4aa6-b248-f4a267ebe1a4).

Additional threshold requirements or considerations may apply depending on the specific operational use case of the Multisig. Such requirements are defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.3 - Additional Use-Case Specific Threshold Requirements And Considerations](5af1115e-5155-449a-829d-6e641af49b0f).
assessments.description: Sets minimum baseline Multisig standards: at least three signers and a signing threshold of at least 50% of total signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Both core obligations carry explicit numeric thresholds (three signers, 50% of total signers) that a third party can check. The exemption carve-out is delegated to another section without its criteria appearing here, and no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Minimum of three (3) signers per Multisig
Signing threshold of at least fifty percent (50%) of total signers
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches a Multisig below these thresholds. Nothing quantifies a consequence specific to this rule, and triggering the spell depends on someone escalating the violation.

assessments.title: Threshold Exceptions
assessments.quote:
Threshold Exceptions define the limited circumstances under which Multisigs may operate below the baseline threshold requirements defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98).

Exceptions may be permitted by Core GovOps, in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. Examples include rate-setting or parameter adjustment operations where parameters are tightly bounded and set by governance, and where a defined recovery or replacement mechanism exists in the event of Multisig failure or compromise.

Certain Threshold Exceptions instead apply as standing exemptions to a defined category of Multisig, without requiring a case-by-case grant. These are specified in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Defines when Multisigs may operate below baseline signing thresholds, via Core GovOps-granted or standing exemptions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names actors (Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and a consultation step, but gives no numeric threshold, bound, or cadence. Eligibility rests on undefined judgment terms like 'tightly bounded' and 'defined recovery mechanism', and standing exemptions are delegated to documents elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism watches exception grants or misuse of exceptions; only the Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication catch-alls apply, which are always weak.

assessments.title: Emergency-Response Multisig Threshold Exception
assessments.quote: As a transitionary measure, pending the development of specific threshold requirements for emergency-response Multisigs, a Multisig whose sole capability is an emergency-response function — such as an emergency freeze, pause, or the removal of a compromised Relayer — that cannot move, custody, or allocate assets, is not subject to the minimum signer or signing-threshold requirements specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98). Such a Multisig is configured to optimize for rapid emergency response.
assessments.description: Exempts emergency-response-only Multisigs that cannot move or allocate assets from minimum signer and threshold requirements, pending future specific rules.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Eligibility is partly concrete (sole emergency-response capability, no ability to move, custody, or allocate assets), but no replacement signer count, threshold, or deadline is stated. The exemption is explicitly 'pending' undefined future requirements, so a defender could argue it does not yet bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism watches whether a Multisig qualifies for the exemption or stays within its non-asset scope. Artifact review and Emergency Spells target agents and security breaches, not this configuration exemption.

assessments.title: Additional Use-Case Specific Threshold Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: Additional threshold requirements and considerations may apply depending on the specific operational use case of the Multisig. These requirements supplement the baseline threshold requirements defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.2.1 - Threshold Requirements](89b7bcf9-8268-4e46-bdfb-dae3a5985a98).
assessments.description: States that additional multisig threshold requirements may apply by use case, supplementing the baseline threshold requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no operative requirement: 'may apply' and 'depending on' leave the obligation undefined, and the supplementary requirements are not specified anywhere in the text. It only points to the baseline threshold rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism is tied to this paragraph, and it creates no concrete obligation for any mechanism to enforce; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Control Multisig Threshold Consideration
assessments.quote: Higher signing thresholds should be used for operations involving contract upgrades or significant protocol changes. As a general guideline, thresholds equivalent to at least seven of nine (7/9) signers, or an equivalent supermajority, should be used where feasible. Lower thresholds may be acceptable for highly constrained operations where execution scope is limited by on-chain parameter bounds.
assessments.description: Sets a guideline that contract-upgrade multisig operations should use roughly 7-of-9 signing thresholds, with lower thresholds allowed for tightly constrained operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A concrete figure (7 of 9 signers) is given, but it is framed as a general guideline applied 'where feasible', with 'equivalent supermajority' and 'may be acceptable' left undefined. A defender could argue both that the threshold was met and that the rule does not bind, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: at least seven of nine (7/9) signers, or an equivalent supermajority, for contract upgrades or significant protocol changes (as a general guideline, where feasible)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No cited mechanism watches multisig signing thresholds; only the catch-all Reports Of Misalignment and Adjudication Process could reach a violation, which is weak by itself.

assessments.title: High-Value Asset Multisig Threshold Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisigs managing assets with a value equal to or greater than one million USD ($1,000,000) equivalent must have no fewer than seven (7) signers. This requirement applies to custodial control of assets, not emergency freeze functions.
assessments.description: Requires multisigs holding at least $1,000,000 in custodied assets to have seven or more signers, excluding emergency freeze functions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a $1,000,000 value threshold and a minimum of seven signers, with a scope carve-out for emergency freeze functions. Gaps remain: the valuation source for "equivalent" value, the measurement cadence, and which party must verify compliance are not stated.
metrics: Asset value managed by multisig >= $1,000,000 USD equivalent
Number of signers >= 7
Applies to custodial control of assets; excludes emergency freeze functions
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no enforcer or consequence, and the penalty and conservatorship mechanisms target Primes and Operational Agents rather than multisig signer configurations. Artifact review could reach it only if the multisig operator is an agent, which the text does not establish.

assessments.title: Module Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisigs must not utilize any modules or guards, except those explicitly permitted for the applicable use case in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2 - Use-Case Specific Configuration Requirements And Considerations](f8d0e4df-acca-4f20-a030-584efb4a8695).
assessments.description: Prohibits multisigs from using modules or guards unless permitted for their specific use case.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The prohibition on modules and guards is clear and checkable against a Safe's configuration, but the permitted exceptions are delegated to a linked use-case configuration section, so the operative list is not stated in this text. No numeric thresholds or deadlines are given.
metrics: Multisigs must not use any modules or guards
Exceptions limited to those explicitly permitted for the applicable use case in A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.3.2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches an unpermitted module or guard on a multisig. Risk-Based Pricing of insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry gives a priced incentive for poor multisig security, but neither mechanism quantifies a consequence specific to this rule.

assessments.title: Treasury Multisig Configuration Requirements
assessments.quote: Treasury Multisigs must use an allowance module that grants the Sky Pause Proxy allowance equal to the maximum amount of each token held by the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires Treasury Multisigs to grant the Sky Pause Proxy an allowance equal to the maximum amount of each token they hold.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The allowance is defined by an explicit formula (equal to the maximum amount of each token held), with a named actor and controlled system. It lacks a measurement window for "maximum", a verification cadence, and a stated check on whether the allowance is updated as balances change.
metrics: Allowance granted to the Sky Pause Proxy equals the maximum amount of each token held by the Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a non-compliant multisig configuration. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and depends on someone triggering a spell, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Capital Allocation Multisig Configuration Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: Capital Allocation Multisigs should implement on-chain constraints wherever feasible, including, but not limited to, smart contract limits or parameter bounds.
assessments.description: Recommends that Capital Allocation Multisigs implement on-chain constraints, such as contract limits or parameter bounds, where feasible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Capital Allocation Multisigs) and a control type (on-chain limits or parameter bounds), but uses 'should' and 'wherever feasible' with no threshold, scope, or verification standard. A defender could plausibly argue that feasibility was never established, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a non-binding 'should' guideline, and no listed mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, PSM, liquidation, emergency spell, or artifact review) reaches a failure to implement on-chain constraints.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Control Multisig Configuration Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote:
For Multisigs responsible for smart contract control, the following requirements apply:

- Major contract changes, including, but not limited to, upgrades or significant parameter changes, must be subject to timelock contracts or equivalent delay mechanisms where feasible.
- Protocol parameters controlled by Multisigs must be bounded through smart contract enforcement where feasible.
assessments.description: Requires timelocks or equivalent delays for major contract changes and smart-contract bounds on Multisig-controlled parameters, where feasible.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations name a concrete control (timelocks, contract-enforced bounds) and an actor (Multisigs controlling smart contracts), but 'major' and 'significant' changes are undefined and 'where feasible' makes compliance arguable. No delay durations or parameter bounds are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize executive freezes or pauses when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach a Multisig that bypasses timelocks or parameter bounds. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and depends on escalation, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Standard Threshold Recommendations
assessments.quote:
Standard Thresholds refer to recommended Multisig threshold configurations based on use case, Impact Classification level (as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.1 - Impact Assessment](3c0847fe-e117-40f8-86a3-9de56c9a3bba)), and Operational Classification type (as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a)). These standards serve as guidance to the Multisig Administrator during Multisig setup.

| **Use Case** | **Impact Classification Level** | **Operational Classification Type** | **Standard Threshold** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treasury - Large | High | Routine | 4/7 |
| Treasury - Small | Medium | Routine | 3/5 |
| Emergency Freeze | Critical | Emergency | 2/4 |
| Capital Allocation | High | Time-Sensitive | 3/5 |
| Protocol Parameters | High | Routine | 4/7 |
| Constrained DeFi | Medium | Time-Sensitive | 2/3 |
assessments.description: Provides recommended multisig signing thresholds by use case, impact level, and operational type as setup guidance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The table gives exact m/n threshold values for six combinations of use case, impact level, and operational type, so the magnitudes are concrete. However, the text says these standards 'serve as guidance,' the table covers only six combinations with no stated fallback, and there is no compliance cadence or verification requirement.
metrics: Treasury - Large (High, Routine): 4/7
Treasury - Small (Medium, Routine): 3/5
Emergency Freeze (Critical, Emergency): 2/4
Capital Allocation (High, Time-Sensitive): 3/5
Protocol Parameters (High, Routine): 4/7
Constrained DeFi (Medium, Time-Sensitive): 2/3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The thresholds are advisory guidance to the Multisig Administrator during setup, and no cited mechanism (penalty, artifact review, emergency spell, or insurance pricing) is shown to reach a deviation from them.

assessments.title: Backup Interface Setup Recommendations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator should ensure that alternative Multisig user interfaces are available to signers in the event that the primary interface becomes unavailable. These interfaces should ideally be accessible through independent infrastructure and may include self-hosted or locally runnable alternatives where available.
assessments.description: Recommends that the Multisig Administrator make alternative multisig interfaces available to signers if the primary interface fails.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Multisig Administrator) and a concrete purpose, but its operative language is judgment-based ('should ensure', 'ideally', 'where available') with no availability standard, test cadence, or deadline. A defender could reasonably argue the recommendation does not bind them.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The text is a non-binding recommendation with no stated consequence, and no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, Emergency Spells, Artifact Review) is tied to interface availability. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: RPC Redundancy Recommendations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator should maintain access to multiple RPC providers for each supported network to help preserve operational continuity if a primary provider becomes unavailable. Where possible, RPC providers should be selected to minimize shared infrastructure dependencies.
assessments.description: Recommends Multisig Administrators maintain multiple RPC providers per network and minimize shared infrastructure dependencies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names an actor (Multisig Administrator) and a control (multiple RPC providers per network), but gives no provider count, uptime target, failover timing, or measurement cadence. Phrases like 'should', 'to help preserve', and 'where possible' leave compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism (penalties, liquidation, emergency spells, artifact review, insurance pricing) reaches RPC provider redundancy; the only applicable backstop is the misalignment and adjudication catch-all, and the duty is self-policed by the administrator.

assessments.title: Communication Setup
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator is responsible for establishing and maintaining communication channels and communication readiness in accordance with the requirements defined in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Makes the Multisig Administrator responsible for establishing and maintaining communication channels and readiness per subdocument requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no thresholds, metrics, or deadlines; it delegates all operative requirements to subdocuments not included in the text. It names an actor but nothing verifiable in itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or artifact-review mechanism is tied to this paragraph's communication duty; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Primary Communication Channel Requirement
assessments.quote: A dedicated communication channel must be established for Multisig operations. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that the channel is restricted to Multisig signers and authorized participants and supports reliable and timely operational communication and coordination between participants.
assessments.description: Requires a dedicated, signer-restricted communication channel for Multisig operations, administered by the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Multisig Administrator) and a controlled system (the channel), but 'reliable and timely' communication and 'authorized participants' are undefined with no latency, uptime, or membership criteria. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to channel restriction or timeliness; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply, and self-policing by the Administrator is not an enforcer distinct from the actor.

assessments.title: Backup Communication Channel Requirement
assessments.quote: A backup communication channel, established on a different platform from the primary communication channel, must be established to maintain communication continuity in the event the primary channel becomes unavailable. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that the backup channel follows the same access and participation constraints as the primary channel.
assessments.description: Requires a backup communication channel on a different platform, with the Multisig Administrator ensuring equivalent access constraints.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 'different platform from the primary channel' criterion is concrete and checkable, and the Multisig Administrator is a named actor. However, 'unavailable' is undefined, there is no testing or verification cadence, and 'same access and participation constraints' is delegated to whatever the primary channel's constraints are, defined elsewhere.
metrics: Backup channel established on a different platform from the primary communication channel
Backup channel follows the same access and participation constraints as the primary channel
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain mechanism, capital at risk, or priced incentive attaches to the backup channel. The only applicable path is the generic misalignment backstop, and the Agent Artifact Review and Emergency Spells mechanisms are not shown to reach this communication-continuity duty.

assessments.title: Emergency Communication Readiness Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisig Administrators are responsible for ensuring that Multisigs classified with an Emergency or Time-Sensitive Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), maintain communication and alerting mechanisms capable of reliably and rapidly reaching signers, enabling timely execution of required actions in accordance with the operational response expectations of the Multisig. Multisig Administrators must also include Signers in the approved Emergency Response contact mechanisms as specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5).
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to keep alerting mechanisms for emergency-classified Multisigs and to enroll Signers in approved emergency contact mechanisms.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations to ensure 'reliable and rapid' reach and 'timely' execution are judgment language with no threshold, response time, or test cadence. The rule does name a concrete actor and a concrete requirement, to include Signers in the approved contact mechanisms, but the mechanisms themselves are defined only in a referenced document.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could review Multisig Administrator compliance and assess penalties, and the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) provides an escalation path for emergencies. Neither quantifies a consequence for this specific communication duty, and both require someone to trigger them.

assessments.title: Communication Access Removal Requirement
assessments.quote: Any signer removed from a Multisig must be promptly removed from all Multisig communication channels and communication systems associated with that Multisig, including primary and backup communication channels. The Multisig Administrator is responsible for ensuring that access is limited to current authorized participants.
assessments.description: Requires removing removed Multisig signers from all associated communication channels promptly, with the Multisig Administrator keeping access limited to current participants.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Multisig Administrator) and the scope (all channels, including primary and backup) are concrete and checkable. The operative timing, "promptly", is undefined, with no deadline or measurable window, so the magnitude is qualitative.
metrics: Removal of a removed signer from all Multisig communication channels and systems: "promptly" (no deadline stated)
Scope includes primary and backup communication channels
Access limited to current authorized participants (ongoing condition)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could reach lingering signer access to Multisig channels. No quantified penalty or defined path specific to this rule was found, so the consequence is unquantified.

assessments.title: Signer Security Check
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that all Multisig signers comply with the applicable signer security requirements as outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.2 - Signer Security Requirements](3f441562-4c03-429c-8934-f0f87fa0eee7), prior to operational use of the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure all signers meet referenced signer security requirements before the multisig is used operationally.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is actor-defined and has a timing condition ('prior to operational use'), but the actual security criteria are delegated to another document and no thresholds, checks, or verification method appear in this text. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
metrics: Compliance with applicable signer security requirements (delegated to A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.2)
Timing: prior to operational use of the Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches a non-compliant signer. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and firing requires escalation, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Multisig Registration
assessments.quote:
All Multisigs currently in use or intended for use within Treasury Management, Emergency Operations (including Freezer or equivalent emergency control Multisigs), Capital Allocation, or Smart Contract Control (including protocol parameter management and constrained DeFi operations) must be registered prior to their inclusion in any Spell or governance execution process.

The Multisig Administrator is responsible for communicating all necessary details about the Multisig to Core GovOps for registration in accordance with the information requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.4 - Multisig Registry](4d80cae1-b28a-4907-8d59-2ebcbba6003d). Core GovOps must coordinate with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to obtain approval prior to completing the registration.
assessments.description: Requires Multisigs in listed control domains to be registered with Core GovOps, with Protocol Security approval, before use in any Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Scope is enumerated and actors are named (Multisig Administrator, Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead), and the registration-before-Spell sequencing is checkable. However, the required registration details are delegated to another section, and the approval criteria and timing are unstated.
metrics: Registration must be completed prior to a Multisig's inclusion in any Spell or governance execution process
Core GovOps must obtain Protocol Security Workstream Lead approval prior to completing registration
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can check whether Multisig Administrators registered Multisigs before Spell use and assess penalties, though the rule does not state a specific consequence for non-registration. Unregistered Multisigs have no direct on-chain or priced consequence cited.

assessments.title: Signer Verification Process
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify their addresses prior to being added to a Multisig. The documents herein define the processes and requirements related to the Signer Verification Process.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig signers to verify their addresses before being added to a Multisig, with details deferred to other documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and has a sequencing condition (verify before being added), but 'verify' is undefined and the paragraph defers the process and requirements to other documents. No verification method, threshold, or cadence is stated, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
metrics: Address verification must occur prior to a signer being added to a Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain control reaches multisig signer address verification. Emergency Spells and Artifact Review cover security or agent conduct more generally but are not tied to this rule, and the catch-all misalignment backstop alone is weak.

assessments.title: Verification Signature
assessments.description: Requires a multisig signer to prove control of their address via a signed message stating intent, multisig address, signer address, and identity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The signed-message format and four required content elements are concrete and checkable, and the signer is a defined actor. However, 'sufficient to establish accountability' is a judgment standard with no defined criteria, and no deadline or verification procedure is stated.
metrics: Signed message proving control of the signer address
Statement of intent to join the specified Multisig
Multisig address included
Signer address intended for participation included
Handle, entity name, or identifying affiliation sufficient to establish accountability
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize freezes when security rules are violated, which plausibly reaches an unverified multisig signer, and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess missing signer disclosures with penalty assessment. Neither consequence is quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Verification Submission
assessments.quote: The verification signature must be shared with the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.description: Requires that a verification signature be shared with the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Multisig Administrator) and a single concrete action (sharing the signature), but gives no deadline, channel, or format, and 'verification signature' is undefined in the text. A regulated party could argue both that it complied and that the obligation is too unspecified to bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pre-authorize executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which plausibly reaches a failure to share a multisig verification signature. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and an intervention would depend on someone identifying and escalating the breach.

assessments.title: Signer Security Requirements
assessments.quote:
Multisig signers must comply with the following security requirements:

- All Multisig signers must use hardware wallets for signing operations. The associated seed phrase must be securely backed up using physical, offline storage methods only. Seed phrases must never be stored digitally, including in photographs, files, password managers, cloud storage, email, or messaging applications. Seed phrase backups must be stored on durable offline media and kept in secure physical locations with appropriate access controls to prevent unauthorized access or single-point compromise.
- Signers must use a unique signing address per Multisig and must not reuse the same signing address across Multisigs.
- Signers participating in Multisigs responsible for critical protocol configuration or security-sensitive operations should not use their signing addresses for personal transactions or other unrelated activities and should instead use a dedicated address created specifically for Multisig participation.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig signers to use hardware wallets, offline seed backups, unique per-Multisig addresses, and dedicated addresses for critical operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The per-Multisig address uniqueness rule is objectively checkable, but the seed-phrase rule relies on qualitative terms like "appropriate access controls" and "secure physical locations". The dedicated-address rule uses "should" and "critical" without defining which Multisigs qualify.
metrics: Each Multisig signer uses a unique signing address per Multisig; no address reused across Multisigs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk-Based Pricing of Insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) can raise a Prime's fees for poor security practice, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) can pause operations when security rules are threatened. Neither is quantified for signer hygiene specifically, and escalation depends on someone detecting the violation.

assessments.title: Signer Rotation Requirement
assessments.quote: Multisig signers may be rotated as operational or security requirements evolve. All signer rotations must be communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead by the Multisig Administrator, accompanied by clear documentation describing the reason for the change, the outgoing signer, and the incoming signer.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to notify the Protocol Security Workstream Lead of every signer rotation with documentation of the reason and the outgoing and incoming signers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Multisig Administrator), the recipient (Protocol Security Workstream Lead), and the required documentation contents, which are concrete and checkable. It gives no deadline or notice period for communicating a rotation, and the trigger for rotation is qualitative ('as operational or security requirements evolve').
metrics: Every signer rotation must be communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
Communication must be accompanied by documentation of the reason for the change, the outgoing signer, and the incoming signer
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to this paragraph, and the Multisig Administrator is not clearly an agent covered by the penalty or artifact-review mechanisms. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Signer Composition Documentation Requirement
assessments.quote: Any change to Multisig signer composition must be promptly communicated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead by the Multisig Administrator, including all updated signer addresses.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to promptly notify the Protocol Security Workstream Lead of any signer composition change, with updated addresses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actors (Multisig Administrator, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and the required content (all updated signer addresses) are concrete and checkable. The operative timing is delegated to the undefined term "promptly" with no deadline or cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review By Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) is a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment that could plausibly catch a missing or late signer-change notice. The consequence is unquantified for this rule, and no trigger ties it specifically to this duty.

assessments.title: Threshold Preservation Requirement
assessments.quote: Signer rotations must not reduce the total number of signers or decrease the signing threshold unless the Multisig Administrator provides a clear operational or security justification that is submitted to and approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.description: Requires signer rotations not to reduce signer count or signing threshold without a Workstream Lead-approved justification from the Multisig Administrator.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core prohibition is objectively checkable: signer count and threshold must not decrease. The exception is weaker, since 'clear operational or security justification' and the approval standard are undefined and judgment-based.
metrics: Total number of signers must not decrease in a signer rotation (absent approved exception)
Signing threshold must not decrease in a signer rotation (absent approved exception)
Exception requires a justification submitted to and approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could plausibly reach an unapproved threshold or signer reduction. The consequence is not quantified for this rule and depends on someone escalating, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Signer Offboarding Requirements
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that signers are offboarded in accordance with the procedures outlined in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure signers are offboarded per procedures in referenced documents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real actor and obligation are named, but the operative standard is only a cross-reference to undefined 'documents herein', with no thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable offboarding steps. A defender could argue the obligation is not yet bound to any specific procedure.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no consequence, and no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, liquidation, artifact review) is shown to reach signer offboarding failures. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Signer Removal
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must coordinate with the remaining signers to execute a signer removal transaction in accordance with the Multisig's standard signer rotation procedures. After execution, the Multisig Administrator must verify that the departing signer's address has been removed from the Multisig and that the change is appropriately communicated and documented as outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.1.2 - Signer Composition Documentation Requirement](2d434d95-a892-404f-9e59-216dce97ce89).
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to coordinate removal of a departing signer and verify and document the change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names a defined actor and a verifiable post-execution check (the departing signer's address is removed), but sets no deadline, cadence, or numeric threshold. The standard rotation procedure is referenced externally, and 'appropriately communicated' is judgment language, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can freeze or pause a multisig when security rules are violated or threatened, and Core GovOps artifact review with penalty assessment could plausibly reach a failed signer removal. Neither consequence is quantified for this rule, and escalation depends on someone raising it.

assessments.title: Access Revocation And Handover
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the departing signer relinquishes access to all Multisig-related communication channels, shared resources, and sensitive operational systems. Any locally stored sensitive Multisig information must be securely deleted. Departing signers should provide relevant operational context, including any pending actions or responsibilities, to the remaining signers to support a smooth transition.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to revoke a departing signer's access, securely delete local Multisig data, and hand over operational context.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligations are real and the actor is named, but the operative terms are judgment language: "all" channels, "securely" deleted, "relevant" context, and a "smooth" transition. No deadline, deletion method, or verification step is stated, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No cited mechanism watches access revocation for departing signers. Emergency Spells (b8266c11) could freeze a compromised multisig, but it does not reach a failure to revoke access, and Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) does not clearly cover Multisig Administrators.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Multisig Signer Composition Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote:
The signer requirements and considerations applicable to Multisigs classified with a Time-Sensitive or Emergency Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), are as follows:

- Emergency Response Multisigs must maintain 24/7 availability of a number of signers equal to or greater than the Multisig signing threshold.
- Geographic distribution of signers is encouraged for Emergency Response Multisigs where appropriate to support 24/7 operational coverage.
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Multisigs to keep at least signing-threshold-many signers available 24/7, and encourages geographic signer distribution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: signer availability must be at least the multisig signing threshold, on a 24/7 basis. Gaps remain: no method or cadence for verifying availability is stated, and the geographic-distribution bullet is only encouraged 'where appropriate'.
metrics: Available signers >= Multisig signing threshold
24/7 availability
Geographic distribution of signers encouraged where appropriate (not required)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System and Emergency Spells respond to incidents rather than verify signer staffing, and no penalty, artifact review, or on-chain mechanism is shown to police signer availability, so compliance rests on the multisig operators themselves.

assessments.title: Capital Allocation Multisig Signer Composition Requirements And Considerations
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that all signers participating in Capital Allocation Multisigs (Multisigs responsible for allocating or reallocating capital) possess sufficient protocol expertise.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure Capital Allocation Multisig signers have sufficient protocol expertise.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A defined actor and a real obligation exist, but 'sufficient protocol expertise' has no criteria, test, or minimum qualification. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with published findings and penalty assessment, with an enforcer distinct from the actor, so it plausibly reaches a Multisig Administrator's signer-vetting duty. The consequence is not quantified for this rule, and the paragraph does not state that expertise is a reviewable artifact.

assessments.title: Incident Reporting
assessments.quote: Incident Reporting defines the procedures governing the reporting of security incidents, operational issues, and security-relevant events relating to Multisig operations.
assessments.description: Defines procedures for reporting security incidents and operational issues relating to Multisig operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a posture statement that says procedures exist but states none of them. It has no metrics, deadlines, reporting thresholds, or defined actors beyond 'Multisig operations', so there is nothing to comply with yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism in the catalog or the paragraph text reaches a failure to report incidents; only the generic Reports of Misalignment catch-all could apply, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Security Incidents
assessments.quote:
Security incidents must be reported immediately upon discovery, in accordance with the process outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.2 - Emergency Incident Reporting Process](56e44cdc-1ba5-4254-9308-c4cfe189394a). Security incidents include, but are not limited to:

- Signing key compromise or suspected compromise
- Account takeover of email or communication platforms used for Multisig operations
- Device theft or loss involving signing or operational access
- Suspicious or unauthorized activity on Multisig accounts
- Phishing attempts targeting Multisig operations
- Compromise or suspected infiltration of communication channels used for Multisig coordination
assessments.description: Requires immediate reporting of listed Multisig security incidents, such as key compromise, account takeover, device loss, and phishing, via the Emergency Incident Reporting Process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The reporting trigger (upon discovery) and the enumerated incident types, such as signing key compromise and device loss, are concrete and checkable. However, 'immediately' has no measurable deadline, 'not limited to' leaves the scope open, and 'suspicious or unauthorized activity' requires judgment, with the procedure delegated to a linked process.
metrics: Report security incidents immediately upon discovery
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can pause or freeze when security rules are violated or threatened, and the Emergency Response System provides an escalation path outside normal governance, so both plausibly reach unreported incidents. Firing depends on someone reporting or escalating, and no penalty is quantified for failing to report.

assessments.title: Operational Issues
assessments.quote:
Operational issues must be reported within 24 hours of discovery, in accordance with the process outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.3 - Standard Incident Reporting Process](ec4cd423-74ba-4e74-82d9-46ba5f6cf526). Operational issues include, but are not limited to:

- Loss of access to signing keys or signing devices
- Hardware wallet or backup device failure
- Communication channel failures affecting Multisig coordination
- Verification tool malfunctions
- Operational difficulties preventing adherence to security procedures
assessments.description: Requires operational issues affecting Multisig security to be reported within 24 hours of discovery, listing example issue types.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified with a 24-hour reporting deadline, but "discovery" is undefined as a start trigger and the category list is open-ended ("not limited to"). Reporting mechanics are delegated to a linked process.
metrics: Operational issues must be reported within 24 hours of discovery
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled, distinct-enforcer review with penalty assessment that could catch late or missed reports, and the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) provides an escalation path for security-relevant operational failures such as lost signing keys. Neither sets a quantified consequence for late reporting specifically, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Emergency Incident Reporting Process
assessments.quote:
When an emergency incident occurs, the following steps must be completed:

- The reporting signer must take immediate actions to secure the situation and prevent further risk, including isolating affected devices or systems where appropriate.
- The reporting signer must notify the Multisig Administrator and other participants through the primary communication channel.
- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer immediately reports the incident to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, following the documentation requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.2.1 - Emergency Incident Documentation Requirements](6d6e7b53-8fcb-4ecb-8428-e07f682d13d4).
- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer follows up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgement is received within 24 hours.
assessments.description: Sets steps the reporting signer and Multisig Administrator must take after an emergency incident, including a 24-hour acknowledgement follow-up.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24-hour follow-up deadline and named actors are concrete, but 'immediate' actions, 'where appropriate' isolation, and the undefined 'primary communication channel' leave the operative timing and scope qualitative. The documentation requirements are delegated to a referenced sub-paragraph.
metrics: Follow up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgement is received within 24 hours
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) provides an escalation path, but it only fires once an incident is reported, so a signer or administrator who fails to report is not reached. Enforcement of the reporting duty depends on the same administrator chain that the rule obliges to act, which is self-policing.

assessments.title: Emergency Incident Documentation Requirements
assessments.quote:
All emergency incident reports must include sufficient documentation to allow review, follow-up, and operational learning. At minimum, security incident documentation must include:

- Multisig details and classification
- Incident type
- Time of incident occurrence and discovery
- Reporting signer
- Description of the incident
- Immediate actions taken
- Next steps required
- Current Multisig status
- Impact
assessments.description: Requires emergency incident reports to include nine specified documentation fields for review and follow-up.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates nine concrete fields that must appear, so presence is checkable. However, the governing standard is 'sufficient documentation to allow review, follow-up, and operational learning,' which is judgment language, and no deadline, cadence, or detail threshold is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System (1d940c6d) governs incident escalation but nothing in the text ties incomplete documentation to a penalty or remedy. Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) could in principle review incident records, but it is not tied to this rule, and only the catch-all misalignment backstop otherwise applies.

assessments.title: Standard Incident Reporting Process
assessments.quote:
When a standard incident occurs, the following steps must be completed:

- The Multisig Administrator must ensure that the reporting signer immediately reports the incident to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, following the documentation requirements outlined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.2.1.2.3.1 - Standard Incident Documentation Requirements](0aec011a-18d2-4945-90b5-8089fa01cefb).
- Follow-up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgement is received within 48 hours.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to ensure signers immediately report standard incidents and that unacknowledged reports are followed up after 48 hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 48-hour follow-up trigger is a concrete, checkable threshold with defined actors. However, the core reporting duty is "immediately" with no time bound, and the incident definition and documentation content are delegated to a linked document.
metrics: Report incident "immediately" to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead
Follow up with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead if no acknowledgement is received within 48 hours
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, review, emergency, or on-chain mechanism is tied to missed incident reporting, and the only general backstop is the catch-all misalignment reporting process. The linked documentation UUID is a requirements document, not an enforcement mechanism.

assessments.title: Standard Incident Documentation Requirements
assessments.quote:
All standard incident reports must include, at minimum, the following information:

- Multisig details and classification
- Incident type
- Time of incident occurrence and discovery
- Reporting signer
- Description of the incident
- Immediate actions taken
- Current Multisig status
- Impact
assessments.description: Requires every standard incident report to include eight specified information fields, such as incident type, timing, and impact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names eight concrete required fields, so a third party could check whether each appears in a report. However, it sets no deadline, cadence, or detail threshold for any field, and 'standard incident reports' is not defined in the paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, review, or emergency mechanism reaches a missing or incomplete incident report. Only the Reports of Misalignment catch-all plausibly applies, which is weak on its own.

assessments.title: Training And Operational Readiness
assessments.quote: Multisig Administrators must ensure that signers maintain sufficient operational expertise through ongoing training and familiarity with the Multisig's procedures. This includes, but is not limited to, training and periodic review of transaction verification practices, operational procedures, and incident response processes applicable to the Multisig's function.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to keep signers trained on transaction verification, operational procedures, and incident response.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation names an actor and enumerated training areas, but 'sufficient expertise' and 'periodic review' have no defined standard, cadence, or measurable outcome. Compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, review, or emergency mechanism is tied to signer training, and the paragraph cites no enforcer. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Backup Infrastructure Readiness Requirements
assessments.quote: The Multisig Administrator must ensure that signers are prepared to operate using backup infrastructure. This includes providing signers with access to offline or alternative Multisig interfaces, verifying that signers have practiced using backup interfaces, testing backup RPC providers during non-emergency periods, and maintaining documented procedures describing how to switch to backup infrastructure when required.
assessments.description: Requires the Multisig Administrator to prepare signers for backup infrastructure, including alternative interfaces, practice, RPC testing, and documented switchover procedures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete actions (provide offline interfaces, verify practice, test backup RPC providers, maintain documented procedures) and a defined actor. However, it sets no test frequency, verification cadence, or completion deadline, and terms like 'prepared' and 'when required' leave compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can plausibly reach the documented switchover procedures and readiness evidence, with a distinct enforcer and penalty assessment. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on a scheduled review occurring.

assessments.title: Emergency Operations Training And Readiness Requirement
assessments.quote:
Multisig Administrators are responsible for ensuring that Multisigs classified with a Time-Sensitive or Emergency Operational Classification level, as defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.1.1.2 - Operational Assessment](35224359-76a6-41fe-adc2-6f70a29f3f4a), maintain operational readiness appropriate to their function.

To satisfy this requirement, Multisig Administrators must ensure that the following activities are conducted:

- Periodic operational drills
- Quarterly testing of emergency communication and alerting systems to ensure continued reliability
- Semi-annual paging system tests to verify alert functionality
- An annual full emergency simulation involving all signers

The Multisig Administrator must document the completion and outcome of all required readiness activities and provide testing reports and confirmation of completion to Core GovOps.
assessments.description: Requires Multisig Administrators to run readiness drills and periodic tests for time-sensitive or emergency multisigs and report results to Core GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Quarterly, semi-annual, and annual cadences are stated for three activities, and reporting goes to Core GovOps. However, 'periodic operational drills' has no cadence, and the core standard of readiness 'appropriate to their function' is qualitative.
metrics: Quarterly testing of emergency communication and alerting systems
Semi-annual paging system tests
Annual full emergency simulation involving all signers
Document completion and outcome of all required readiness activities
Provide testing reports and confirmation of completion to Core GovOps
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Multisig Administrators' documented testing reports and completion confirmations to Core GovOps feed the Agent Artifact Review, a scheduled review with staged findings and penalty assessment by an enforcer distinct from the actor. The consequence is not quantified for this specific rule, and escalation depends on the review occurring.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process
assessments.quote: Any update to a Multisig signer address must be performed in accordance with the process defined in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Requires any Multisig signer address update to follow the process defined in its subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph imposes a real obligation (all signer updates must follow a defined process) but states no threshold, deadline, or verifiable criterion itself. Its operative content is delegated to subdocuments not included here, so a defender could argue it does not yet bind in a checkable way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: An unauthorized or improperly processed signer change is a security-rule violation that Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) can pre-authorize executive freezes or pauses to address. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and firing depends on the violation being identified and escalated.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process If Original Key Is Accessible
assessments.quote:
If the original key of the signer address that needs to be changed remains accessible, the following steps must be completed by the signer:

- The signer authorizes the address change by signing a message with the existing signer address. The signed message must clearly state the intent to replace the existing signer address with the new address.
- The signer must follow the steps defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Signer Verification Process](002821ab-c67c-4eb1-987c-69e759ab7b3c) prior to the new address being added to the Multisig.
assessments.description: Requires a signer with an accessible key to sign an intent message with the existing address and complete verification before a new address joins the Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The steps are enumerated and the sequencing is concrete: a signed message from the existing address, then verification before the new address is added. The message requirement ('clearly state the intent') is qualitative and the verification criteria are delegated to another process, so compliance is partly a judgment call.
metrics: Signed message from the existing signer address stating intent to replace it with the new address
Verification per A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1 completed before the new address is added to the Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalogued mechanism (penalty, liquidation, conservatorship, insurance repricing, artifact review) is tied to multisig signer changes. Emergency Spells would only respond generically to a threatened security rule, and the paragraph does not invoke them.

assessments.title: Signer Address Update Process If Original Key Is Lost Or Inaccessible
assessments.quote:
If the original key of the signer address that needs to be changed is inaccessible, the signer must verify their identity to the remaining signers through alternative verification methods such as:

- Authentication through a verified social media or publicly associated account
- Live verification via video call with existing signers
- Other comparable verification methods

Upon successful identity verification, the signer must follow the steps defined in [A.2.11.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Signer Verification Process](002821ab-c67c-4eb1-987c-69e759ab7b3c) and notify the Multisig Administrator once completed.
assessments.description: Requires a signer who lost access to their key to verify identity via alternative methods, then follow the signer verification process and notify the Multisig Administrator.
