Whether a given check satisfies the rule is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no penalty, escalation, or remedy for a failed or skipped verification, and no catalogued mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, liquidation, PSM, emergency spells) is tied to signer key-recovery procedures. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Transaction Verification And Signing Requirements
assessments.quote: Multisig signers must verify all transaction data prior to signing in order to reduce the risk of malicious or unintended transactions being executed. The procedures defined in the documents herein establish the relevant transaction verification processes for supported execution environments.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to multisig signer verification in this text; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply, and self-verification by signers is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: EVM Transaction Verification Requirements

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and names a defined actor (multisig signers) and a timing (before signing), but the verification method, depth, and standard of 'matches the intended operation' are undefined. A signer could argue any review satisfies the rule, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph contains no consequence and no catalog mechanism reaches signer verification failures: Risk Capital penalties and Risk-Based Pricing apply to Primes, and Emergency Spells are not tied to this signing duty. Only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Transaction Hash Verification
assessments.quote: Signers must verify that the transaction hash displayed on the signing device matches the expected transaction hash derived from the transaction parameters. When signing transactions involving nested Multisigs, the hash displayed on the signing device may correspond to an approval hash rather than the underlying transaction. In such cases, signers must verify both the nested transaction and the parent Multisig approval.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives an enumerated verification step (compare the displayed hash to the expected hash derived from transaction parameters) and a nested-Multisig case requiring verification of both transaction and parent approval. It states no metric, cadence, or method for deriving the expected hash, so compliance is checkable in principle but not quantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A signer approving a mismatched hash is a security-rule violation that Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) can freeze or pause when violated or threatened, and Risk-Based Pricing via the Prime Spell Security Registry raises insurance fees for poor security practice. Neither ties a penalty specifically to this verification duty, and the paragraph does not state any consequence.

assessments.title: SVM Transaction Verification Requirements

metrics: Verification must occur prior to signing (timing condition only; no cadence or quantified threshold)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could plausibly reach a signer approving a malicious or incorrect SVM multisig transaction. assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalog mechanism, such as Emergency Spells or Agent Artifact Review, is cited or reaches this advisory guidance; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Operational Guides
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead must maintain and make available operational guides to support Multisig Administrators in complying with the requirements specified in [A.2.11.1.3.2 - Multisig Security Guidelines](6033699f-1d55-45ba-8eb1-bd8982571cc0). assessments.title: Periodic Review Requirement
assessments.quote:
Core GovOps must engage the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and third party providers to conduct periodic reviews of registered Multisigs to verify that Multisig documentation, configuration, and operational classification remain accurate and aligned with current usage. At minimum:

assessments.title: Review Scope

Periodic reviews may include, but are not limited to:

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism in the catalog or the paragraph text watches whether periodic Multisig reviews occur or what they cover; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach it.

assessments.title: Monitoring Outcome
assessments.quote: Where monitoring or review activities identify inconsistencies, outdated documentation, or potential noncompliance, Core GovOps must proceed in accordance with [A.2.11.1.3.5 - Determination And Enforcement Of Multisig Security Noncompliance](2a36aafa-cfe3-4ba5-b549-f341fbb4c666).

assessments.title: Determination And Enforcement Of Multisig Security Noncompliance

assessments.title: Sky Savings Rate Current Value
assessments.quote:
The current value of the Sky Savings Rate can be obtained by calling the `ssr()` function on the sUSDS contract located on the Ethereum Mainnet at `0xa3931d71877C0E7a3148CB7Eb4463524FEc27fbD`. The value returned is the per-second compounding factor; the Sky Savings Rate is the annual percentage rate, as specified in [A.3.1.2.7 - Rate Conventions](154c3b5d-7a87-4dae-85f3-7d26deab9a31), whose accrual over one (1) year is equivalent to compounding that factor every second.

The `ssr()` function returns a per-second compounding rate in RAY precision (10^27). The Sky Savings Rate expressed as an annual percentage rate is given by the formula:

`annual percentage rate = 12 * ((ssr() / 1E27)^2628000 - 1)`

where 2,628,000 is the number of seconds in one (1) month of a 365-day year. The result is a decimal rate (e.g., 0.0346 represents 3.46% per year); the annual percentage yield equivalent is obtained by the conversion specified in [A.3.1.2.7 - Rate Conventions](154c3b5d-7a87-4dae-85f3-7d26deab9a31).
assessments.description: Specifies how to read the Sky Savings Rate from the sUSDS ssr() function and convert the per-second factor to an annual percentage rate.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The contract address, function, RAY precision (10^27), and APR formula with the 2,628,000-second month and factor of 12 are all stated exactly. The APY conversion is delegated to A.3.1.2.7 without its formula appearing in this paragraph, which leaves a small gap.

assessments.title: Limitations For Prime Agents Receiving Subsidized Rate

assessments.title: Rate Conventions
assessments.quote:
Unless otherwise specified, all rates defined in the Atlas are expressed as annual percentage rates with a monthly compounding frequency. The annual percentage yield equivalent of a rate is given by the formula:

`annual percentage yield = (1 + annual percentage rate / 12)^12 - 1`

A spread between two rates defined in the Atlas is the arithmetic difference between their annual percentage rates. Where the Atlas specifies one rate as another rate plus or minus a spread, that spread is added to or subtracted from the annual percentage rate directly. A rate specified as an annual percentage yield is first converted to its equivalent annual percentage rate before any such arithmetic is performed.

Rates may be displayed as their annual percentage yield equivalents in user-facing interfaces and communications. Where a rate is implemented by a smart contract that compounds at a different frequency, the technical parameter is set such that the accrual produced by the smart contract over one (1) year equals the accrual of the stated rate. Basis-point rate parameters, and the bounds on them, set through Bounded External Access Modules are expressed as annual percentage yields, matching the conversion enforced by the module contracts. A rate applied through periodic payments that are not added to an accruing balance is applied at the annual percentage rate divided by the number of payment periods in each year.
assessments.description: Defines how Atlas interest rates are expressed, compounded, converted, and implemented across display, spreads, and smart contracts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Gives an explicit APY formula with monthly compounding (12), a precise spread rule (direct arithmetic difference of APRs), and a specified conversion for periodic payments (APR divided by payment periods). Verifiable from the text alone.
metrics: Default compounding frequency: monthly (12 periods per year)
annual percentage yield = (1 + annual percentage rate / 12)^12 - 1
Spread = arithmetic difference between annual percentage rates
Periodic-payment rate = annual percentage rate divided by number of payment periods per year
Smart contract parameter set so one-year accrual equals the stated rate's accrual
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a unit-convention definition with no penalty, liquidation, or escalation path tied to its violation; the only generic backstop would be the misalignment catch-all, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Prime Agents who invest capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio using the Allocation System Primitive must hold Risk Capital to protect Sky from potential losses on these investments. This Article sets forth the framework governing Risk Capital.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents who invest Collateral Portfolio capital via the Allocation System to hold Risk Capital protecting Sky from losses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Prime Agents), the controlled activity (Allocation System investments), and a real holding obligation. It gives no threshold, sizing formula, or deadline, and defers the framework to the rest of the Article, so a defender could argue it does not yet bind them.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements reach a failure to hold Risk Capital, and Risk Capital itself is capital at risk. The paragraph does not quantify any consequence for this rule, and firing depends on the Article's broader framework rather than this text.

assessments.title: Capital Ratio Requirement
assessments.quote:
The Capital Ratio Requirement (CRR) with respect to one or more Instances is the Required Risk Capital with respect to such Instances divided by the amount of capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in such Instances.

Risk Capital requirements in the Risk Framework may be specified either as an amount of RRC or as a CRR. If a CRR is specified, then the RRC is equal to the amount of capital from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the relevant Instances times the CRR.

For example, if a certain Instance has a CRR of 5% and 100,000,000 USDS is invested in the Instance, then the RRC is 5,000,000 USDS.

CRR may be specified in aggregate (Aggregate CRR), for a particular Instance (Instance CRR), or for a particular type of risk with respect to an Instance (Instance Financial CRR, Instance Smart Contract CRR, or Instance Administrative CRR).
assessments.description: Defines the Capital Ratio Requirement as Required Risk Capital divided by invested Collateral Portfolio capital, and how CRR converts to RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives exact formulas (CRR = RRC / invested capital; RRC = capital × CRR) and a worked numeric example. The actual CRR values are defined in the Risk Framework rather than here, so the operative magnitudes are missing from this text.
metrics: CRR = Required Risk Capital / amount of Collateral Portfolio capital invested in the Instances
RRC = invested Collateral Portfolio capital × CRR when CRR is specified
Example: CRR of 5% on 100,000,000 USDS invested gives RRC of 5,000,000 USDS
CRR may be set as Aggregate CRR, Instance CRR, or per-risk-type Instance CRR (Financial, Smart Contract, Administrative)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is a computational definition, not a standalone requirement. The Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship escalation would reach breaches of CRR-based Risk Capital requirements that it measures, but no consequence is quantified for this definition itself.

assessments.title: Aggregate RRC

metrics: Aggregate RRC = sum of Instance Total RRC for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive deployed by the Prime Agent

Conservatorship for breach of capital requirements (5c3dd35a) gives Core GovOps an escalation path with direct control of the Prime, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) add quantified penalties for Risk Capital rule violations.

assessments.description: Defines Instance Total RRC as the sum of Financial, Smart Contract, and Administrative RRC for an Instance.

metrics: Instance Total RRC = Instance Financial RRC + Instance Smart Contract RRC + Instance Administrative RRC

assessments.title: Inability To Calculate Types Of RRC

metrics: Instance Total RRC = 100% if Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract RRC, or Instance Administrative RRC cannot be calculated
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The 100% fallback is a built-in capital cost on the Prime, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a Prime that fails to produce a calculable RRC. The penalty is not quantified for this specific rule, so it stays at mid.

Implementation is delegated to A.3.2.2.1.1.1.6, so the criteria cannot be checked from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Misclassifying a stablecoin as Cash changes the Required Risk Capital a Prime must hold, so a breach would fall under the Penalty Mechanisms that incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules. The penalty is not quantified for this classification rule, and this paragraph is a model description rather than a direct requirement.

assessments.title: Risk Rating
assessments.quote: The determination of Smart Contract Risk should initially be based on an evaluation of the risk that the investment could experience losses due to a bug or technical exploit. This determination should take into account factors such as (1) the technical complexity of the code base (e.g. cyclomatic complexity, decision points, number of external calls, lines of code), (2) the number, quality, and recency of audits, and (3) the "Lindiness" of the relevant smart contracts.
assessments.description: Directs that smart contract risk be initially assessed for bug and exploit losses, considering code complexity, audits, and lindiness.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph uses judgment language ('should initially be based on an evaluation', 'should take into account factors such as') and lists factors without thresholds, weights, or a required output. Metrics like cyclomatic complexity and lines of code are named but never given values, so a defender could argue either compliance or non-binding guidance.
metrics: cyclomatic complexity
decision points
number of external calls
lines of code
number, quality, and recency of audits
lindiness of the relevant smart contracts
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Smart contract risk feeds the Instance RRC, so a mis-determination can under-capitalize a Prime and trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), and Core GovOps artifact review (d4bf73e7) could assess the determination. No consequence is quantified for this specific evaluation duty, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Required Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The risk of a technical exploit in one protocol is unlikely to be correlated with the risk of a technical exploit in an unrelated protocol. Therefore, the risks from small exposures to even relatively risky protocols are likely to be diversified away. In contrast, very large exposures to even relatively safe protocols can create a risk to a Prime Agent and potentially to Sky itself if there is a technical exploit, especially if multiple Prime Agents have the same exposure. To account for this, the calculation of Instance Smart Contract RRC should take into account the risk rating, the level of exposure of the Prime, and the level of exposure of the Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: States that Instance Smart Contract RRC should account for protocol risk rating and Prime and Sky Ecosystem exposure levels.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names three calculation inputs (risk rating, Prime exposure level, Sky Ecosystem exposure level) but gives no formula, weights, thresholds, or definitions. 'Should take into account' is judgment language, so a defender could argue it does not yet bind any calculation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The RRC feeds Required Risk Capital, so breaches of capital requirements plausibly reach the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship. The consequence is not quantified for this calculation and the paragraph itself states no enforcement path.

assessments.title: Risk Rating
assessments.quote: The determination of Administrative Risk should initially be based on an evaluation of the risk that an investment could experience losses due to an abuse of privileged access. This determination should take into account factors such as (1) the level of privileged access that exists, (2) the security delay that such access is subject to, and (3) the "Lindiness" of the system.
assessments.description: Directs how Administrative Risk should be initially determined, based on privileged-access abuse loss exposure and listed factors.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names three factors (privileged access level, security delay, 'Lindiness') but gives no scale, formula, thresholds, or weighting; 'should initially be based on' and 'should take into account' are judgment language, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found: the paragraph sets no consequence for a misjudged Administrative Risk, and no catalog mechanism directly reaches a risk-determination method; only the catch-all misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Required Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The risk of an abuse of privileged access in one protocol is unlikely to be correlated with the risk of an abuse of privileged access in an unrelated protocol. Therefore, the risks from small exposures to even relatively risky protocols are likely to be diversified away. In contrast, very large exposures to even relatively safe protocols can create a risk to a Prime Agent and potentially to Sky itself if there is an abuse of privileged access, especially if multiple Prime Agents have the same exposure. To account for this, the calculation of Instance Administrative RRC should take into account the risk rating, the level of exposure of the Prime, and the level of exposure of the Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.description: Directs that Instance Administrative RRC calculations account for risk rating, Prime exposure level, and Sky Ecosystem exposure level.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names three calculation inputs (risk rating, Prime exposure, Sky Ecosystem exposure) but gives no formula, weights, thresholds, or measurement cadence. 'Should take into account' is judgment language, so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Risk Capital calculation and requirement breaches plausibly reach the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and escalate to conservatorship (5c3dd35a) by Core GovOps. However, no consequence is quantified for this calculation-method rule itself, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote: The implementation of the calculation of Instance Administrative RRC is specified in [A.3.2.2.1.3 - Instance Administrative RRC Calculation](277d6712-25ff-4566-a42b-38d7e860ae76).
assessments.description: Points to the section that specifies how Instance Administrative RRC is calculated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a cross-reference with no thresholds, formulas, or operative obligations; the calculation details live in the linked section A.3.2.2.1.3. A regulated party could argue this text binds it to nothing.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph states no violation mode, and the linked calculation section is not itself an enforcement mechanism. Penalty machinery would reach a breach of the calculation rules, not this pointer.

assessments.title: Total Risk Capital
assessments.quote: The documents herein define the conceptual framework for types of capital that contribute to a Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital (TRC). Prime Agents must maintain at all times a level of TRC that exceeds their Aggregate RRC or be subject to penalties.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep Total Risk Capital above Aggregate RRC at all times, or face penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative obligation is a clear inequality (TRC must exceed Aggregate RRC) with a continuous cadence ('at all times'). The components of TRC and RRC are defined elsewhere without values here, and the penalty magnitude is unstated.
metrics: TRC must exceed Aggregate RRC
maintained at all times
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph expressly makes breach subject to penalties, which reaches the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). Capital-requirement breaches also escalate to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), where Sky Core takes direct control of the Prime, giving a named enforcer and concrete remedy.

assessments.title: Total Risk Capital Definition
assessments.quote: Total Risk Capital is capital that is currently eligible, available, and verifiably under the Prime’s control. For capital to be included in a Prime Agent's TRC, it must be currently deployable towards covering its Required Risk Capital obligations. Consequently, in-flight capital (e.g., assets being bridged) does not contribute towards a Prime’s TRC. Similarly, commitments for future capital, such as Ecosystem Accords for renting Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) or Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) that have been agreed upon by counterparties but are not yet formally codified within the Atlas, cannot contribute towards a Prime’s TRC until such formalization is complete.
assessments.description: Defines Total Risk Capital as currently eligible, deployable, verifiably controlled capital, excluding in-flight assets and uncodified future commitments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are concrete: in-flight bridged capital is excluded, and uncodified Ecosystem Accord commitments are excluded until formalization. Core qualifiers such as 'currently eligible', 'deployable' and 'verifiably under control' are undefined and judgment-based, and no thresholds or measurement cadence are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is a definition, so no penalty attaches to it directly. A Prime that overstates TRC by counting in-flight or uncodified capital would breach the Risk Capital requirements, which reach the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship; those consequences are not quantified for this definition itself, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Junior Risk Capital
assessments.quote: Junior Risk Capital (JRC) is the first capital to absorb losses on investments under the Allocation System. Junior Risk Capital must experience 100% losses before any losses are absorbed by Senior Risk Capital.
assessments.description: Establishes Junior Risk Capital as the first loss-absorbing layer, requiring it to be fully consumed before Senior Risk Capital absorbs losses.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss-ordering obligation is quantified as 100% junior exhaustion before any senior absorption, which is objectively checkable. It lacks a measurement basis for 'losses', a valuation cadence, and any rule for partial or simultaneous allocations.
metrics: Junior Risk Capital must experience 100% losses before any losses are absorbed by Senior Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms and Risk-Capital Incident Response can reach a Prime that breaches the first-loss ordering, including escalation to conservatorship to make losses whole. The consequence is not quantified specifically for this waterfall rule, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
assessments.quote:
Internal Junior Risk Capital is capital owned by the Prime Agent itself. It serves as the foundation for the Prime’s risk capacity: the amount of IJRC directly dictates the maximum External JRC the Prime can source (governed by the External Per Internal ratio) and provides the primary capacity for enabling Senior Risk Capital (via the Senior Per Junior ratio), while also bearing the initial impact of any losses (the Tip JRC mechanism). IJRC must be eligible assets held in the Prime Agent’s designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), controlled by the Prime’s root governance.

See [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.1 - External Per Internal Ratio](ff374833-920c-40f6-ae6c-a71d33d99b82), [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2 - Senior Per Junior Ratio](fbc9a273-d217-4d52-8b3e-b496580f27a2), and [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.2 - JRC Loss Allocation Rules](c201122a-75d2-44fa-b221-4e7c09bf42f2).
assessments.description: Defines Internal Junior Risk Capital as Prime-owned eligible assets held in a designated treasury account under root governance control.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete parameters: Prime ownership, a designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), and root governance control. However, "eligible assets" is undefined here, and the operative ratios that set IJRC's capacity are delegated to other documents without values.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: IJRC is capital the Prime itself bears first losses on, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plus conservatorship for capital-requirement breaches (5c3dd35a) could reach a failure to hold eligible assets in the designated account. The consequence is not quantified for this specific eligibility rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Types Of Eligible Assets For IJRC
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define the types of assets that qualify as Internal Junior Risk Capital.

These types will be specified in a future iteration of the Risk Framework.
assessments.description: States that eligible asset types for Internal Junior Risk Capital will be specified in a future Risk Framework iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is an explicit stub deferring the eligible asset types to a future iteration, so no metrics, thresholds, or operative criteria exist to comply with. The deterministic 'future iteration' flag confirms this.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No mechanism watches this stub; with no defined asset types there is nothing for the Penalty Mechanisms or Conservatorship to attach to, leaving only the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Initial Loss Absorption By "Tip JRC"
assessments.quote:
The Tip JRC mechanism dictates that losses from a distinct risk event are first absorbed entirely by the Prime Agent's Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), up to a specific threshold amount. This threshold amount is calculated as a percentage of Total JRC and is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.1 - JRC Loss Allocation Parameters](b718459e-57e0-414f-9c99-fbc82685cc0f).

Only losses exceeding this threshold amount trigger absorption by other Junior Risk Capital components - specifically, the remaining IJRC and External Junior Risk Capital. This initial absorption solely by IJRC ensures that Prime Agents are highly incentivized to prevent losses and avoids the need to resolve disputes regarding the allocation of small losses to EJRC providers.
assessments.description: Requires IJRC to absorb losses up to a threshold, a percentage of Total JRC, before other Junior Risk Capital is drawn.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss-ordering mechanism and the IJRC-first sequence are concrete, but the operative threshold is a percentage of Total JRC whose value is delegated to A.3.2.2.2.1 and not stated here. No measurement cadence or deadline is given.
metrics: Losses from a distinct risk event are absorbed first by IJRC up to a threshold amount
Threshold amount is a percentage of Total JRC, specified in A.3.2.2.2.1 (value not stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The loss-ordering itself is capital at risk, since the Prime's own IJRC absorbs first losses. Risk-Capital Incident Response and Penalty Mechanisms can reach misallocation of losses, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Post-Tip JRC Loss Allocation
assessments.quote: If a loss event exceeds the Tip JRC amount, the remaining loss is allocated pro-rata across the rest of the JRC capital. This includes the remaining Internal Junior Risk Capital (Total IJRC minus the Tip amount) and all External Junior Risk Capital (Prime External Junior Risk Capital plus Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital).
assessments.description: Allocates losses exceeding the Tip JRC amount pro-rata across remaining internal and all external junior risk capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (loss exceeding Tip JRC amount) and the allocation pool (remaining IJRC plus all external JRC) are concrete and named. The pro-rata basis or weighting is never stated, so the share each pool bears cannot be computed from the text.
metrics: Trigger: loss event exceeds the Tip JRC amount
Pool: remaining IJRC (Total IJRC minus Tip amount) plus Prime External JRC plus Tokenized External JRC
Method: pro-rata allocation across pool (weighting basis unspecified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule defines how losses are distributed rather than imposing a duty with a consequence for non-compliance; the loss-bearing itself is capital at risk, but no cited mechanism polices correct allocation.

assessments.title: Per-Event Basis
assessments.quote:
The JRC loss allocation rules are applied independently based on the total losses attributed to each distinct risk event. The concept of "per-event basis" is crucial; the classification of a distinct risk event (classifying losses as one large event versus multiple smaller ones) can dictate whether the Tip JRC threshold is breached.

Breaching the threshold activates the pro-rata sharing mechanism for any losses exceeding the Tip JRC amount, distributing such excess losses between both the remaining Internal JRC (IJRC) and all External JRC (EJRC). Conversely, if the threshold is not breached for an event, the loss is contained entirely within the Tip layer and absorbed solely by IJRC.

The operational process for the determination of distinct risk events will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.description: Specifies per-event JRC loss allocation: losses above the Tip JRC threshold are shared pro-rata between IJRC and EJRC, while event classification is deferred.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The threshold-and-pro-rata split is described procedurally, but the Tip JRC amount has no value here and the criteria for classifying a distinct risk event are explicitly deferred to a future iteration. A defender could argue both that the stated split was followed and that the binding classification rule does not yet exist.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Misclassifying events to avoid the Tip JRC threshold would breach Risk Capital rules, which the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and conservatorship escalation (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach. The consequence is unquantified for this rule, and the stubbed event-classification process leaves the trigger undefined.

assessments.title: Senior Risk Capital
assessments.quote:
Senior Risk Capital (SRC) is protected from losses relative to Junior Risk Capital. Senior Risk Capital only begins to absorb losses after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses and absorbs 100% of losses thereafter.

Senior Risk Capital can be originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle; Prime Agents can also rent Senior Risk Capital from each other via the [A.2.2.10.2 - Risk Capital Rental Primitive](d8086dc0-7e77-4c6b-98c7-5fc41337a1ce).
assessments.description: Defines Senior Risk Capital as loss-protected behind Junior Risk Capital, originated monthly by Sky Core and rentable between Primes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The loss waterfall is quantified: SRC absorbs losses only after JRC has taken 100% losses, then 100% of losses thereafter, and origination has a monthly cadence. It gives no amount or sizing for SRC origination or rental, and the rental terms are delegated to the linked primitive.
metrics: SRC absorbs losses only after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses
SRC absorbs 100% of losses thereafter
SRC originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) quantify penalties for Primes who do not follow Risk Capital rules, which would reach misuse of SRC rental or origination. Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) can escalate to penalties or conservatorship if losses are misallocated, but neither consequence is quantified for this specific loss-ordering rule.

assessments.title: External Per Internal Ratio
assessments.quote: The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio determines the maximum amount of External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC and TEJRC combined) that a Prime Agent can source directly based on its held Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC). This acts as the primary constraint ensuring a baseline level of the Prime’s own capital backs its external JRC sourcing. The required External Per Internal ratio is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.2.1 - External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value](3ed32706-c072-42b5-b1e5-187bddf8dc37).
assessments.description: Defines the External Per Internal ratio capping how much external junior risk capital a Prime can source relative to its internal junior risk capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ratio, the actor (Prime Agent), and the capped quantity (PEJRC plus TEJRC against held IJRC) are named, but the operative value is delegated to A.3.2.2.2.2.1 and no magnitude appears in this paragraph.
metrics: Maximum External JRC (PEJRC + TEJRC combined) sourceable relative to held IJRC, set by the EPI ratio
Required EPI ratio value: specified in A.3.2.2.2.2.1 (not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship for breach of capital requirements plausibly reach a Prime that exceeds the EPI cap, but this definitional paragraph names no consequence and the escalation is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Senior Per Junior Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Senior Per Junior (SPJ) ratio defines the effectiveness of each type of Junior Risk Capital (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC) in supporting Senior Risk Capital (SRC). Specifically, it quantifies how many units of SRC (whether Originated or Rented) can be activated or "enabled" per unit of a given JRC type.

A Prime Agent's overall "SPJ capacity" is calculated by summing the potential enablement contributed by each type of JRC it holds (IJRC, PEJRC or TEJRC), where each contribution equals the amount of that JRC type multiplied by its specific SPJ ratio.

Since SRC only absorbs losses after JRC is depleted, the SPJ enablement mechanism validates that sufficient JRC backing exists, allowing enabled SRC to be counted as part of the Prime Agent's total eligible Risk Capital. Therefore, a Prime Agent might hold a certain amount of OSRC or rented SRC, but only the portion that is successfully "enabled" by its JRC according to the SPJ ratios is accounted by the system as eligible capital contributing towards the Prime’s satisfaction of its Required Risk Capital. The required ratio of Senior Per Junior is specified in [A.3.2.2.2.2.2 - Senior Per Junior (SPJ) Ratio Values](8578e240-3fe8-41c0-8b2c-15ec9a7181ab).
assessments.description: Defines the Senior Per Junior ratio and how JRC enables SRC to count toward a Prime's Required Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The capacity formula (sum of each JRC amount times its SPJ ratio) is explicit, but the operative ratio values are delegated to another section, and no measurement cadence or threshold for meeting Required Risk Capital is stated here.
metrics: SPJ capacity = sum over JRC types (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC) of JRC amount x that type's SPJ ratio
Only SRC successfully enabled under SPJ ratios counts toward Required Risk Capital
Required SPJ ratio values are specified in A.3.2.2.2.2.2 (Senior Per Junior (SPJ) Ratio Values)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule only excludes un-enabled SRC from eligible capital, so its consequence runs through Required Risk Capital breaches, which reach Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship; however, nothing here quantifies a penalty specific to SPJ non-compliance.

assessments.title: Alternative Use Of SPJ Capacity To Source External Junior Risk Capital
assessments.quote:
A Prime Agent may optionally choose to deploy all or some portion of its calculated SPJ capacity not to enable Senior Risk Capital, but instead to source additional External Junior Risk Capital. This provides a secondary mechanism to increase the total JRC potentially beyond the amount initially constrained by the EPI ratio applied solely to IJRC.

Crucially, the EJRC tranche acquired through utilizing SPJ capacity is permanently accounted for as having an SPJ ratio of zero (0). It contributes to the JRC buffer but provides no capacity itself for enabling SRC in any subsequent calculations. This contrasts with EJRC sourced normally via the EPI ratio, which retains its standard SPJ capacity.
assessments.description: Lets Primes use SPJ capacity to source External Junior Risk Capital, which is then permanently assigned an SPJ ratio of zero.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The zero SPJ ratio for EJRC sourced via SPJ capacity is a concrete parameter, but the portion of SPJ capacity deployed is left as 'all or some portion' with no threshold or formula. The 'calculated SPJ capacity' input is defined elsewhere and not restated here.
metrics: EJRC tranche acquired via SPJ capacity has an SPJ ratio of 0, permanently
Deployment of 'all or some portion' of calculated SPJ capacity (no bound given)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements could reach a Prime that miscounts the zero SPJ ratio, since this is a Risk Capital accounting rule. The paragraph sets no quantified consequence for this specific rule, and escalation depends on treating the miscount as a capital-requirement breach.

assessments.title: Interaction Between Ratios And SPJ Capacity
assessments.quote:
The sourcing of External Junior Risk Capital and enablement of Senior Risk Capital involves a sequential application of the Risk Capital sourcing ratios in conjunction with the Prime Agent’s deployment of its SPJ capacity.

First, the EPI ratio sets the initial limit for sourcing standard, SPJ-bearing EJRC based solely on the Prime Agent’s IJRC.
Second, the total SPJ capacity is calculated from the Prime Agent’s resulting JRC pool (IJRC + any EPI-sourced EJRC).

Finally, this total calculated SPJ capacity can be allocated by the Prime Agent to enable SRC (standard use), and/or to source additional, non-SPJ-bearing EJRC using the mechanism described under [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2.1 - Alternative Use Of SPJ Capacity To Source External Junior Risk Capital](03029174-91b4-4974-af1e-52438556a70b). Any specific portion of the total SPJ capacity allocated towards sourcing EJRC cannot simultaneously be allocated towards enabling SRC.
assessments.description: Sets the sequence for applying EPI sourcing ratios and SPJ capacity to EJRC and SRC, and bars double-allocating SPJ capacity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The order of steps (EPI ratio, then SPJ capacity, then allocation) and the no-double-counting constraint are clear and checkable. The EPI ratio value and the SPJ capacity formula are not stated here and are delegated to other paragraphs, so the operative magnitudes are missing.
metrics: SPJ capacity is calculated from the Prime Agent's resulting JRC pool (IJRC plus any EPI-sourced EJRC)
Any portion of total SPJ capacity allocated to sourcing EJRC cannot simultaneously be allocated to enabling SRC
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule governs Risk Capital sourcing, so a double-allocation breach is a breach of capital requirements. That reaches Conservatorship (Core GovOps escalation, Facilitator takes control of the Prime) and the Penalty Mechanisms that incentivize Primes to follow Risk Capital rules, though no penalty is quantified for this specific paragraph.

assessments.title: Calculate Probability Of Default
assessments.quote:
The first step is calculating the Probability Of Default $PD$. $PD$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\text{PD} = N(-d_1) + N(-d_2) \left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right)^{-2a}
$$

Here $N$ is the normal cumulative probability distribution function.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Specifies the formula for calculating Probability of Default as the first step of Risk Capital calculation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The PD formula is fully written out with explicit operators and exponent, so the core calculation is quantified. Inputs d1, d2, a, LT_i, V_0^i and D_0^j are not valued here and are deferred to subdocuments, leaving gaps in the operative magnitudes.
metrics: N is the normal cumulative probability distribution function
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms apply to Primes and Operational Agents who fail to follow Risk Capital rules, which plausibly reaches a miscalculated PD. The paragraph sets no specific consequence for this calculation step, so the penalty is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio $a$ is calculated as follows:

$$
a = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2}{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the Leverage Adjusted Drift To Risk Ratio as a closed-form formula over upside and downside weights, returns, and volatilities.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ratio is fully specified as an explicit formula with sums, indices, and a denominator, so it is mechanically computable. The inputs (w_U, w_D, r_c, r_s, r_d, σ, ρ) are not defined or bounded in this paragraph, and no cadence or valid range is stated.
metrics: a = (Σ_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) − Σ_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + ρ_UD σ_U σ_D − σ_U²) / (σ_U² + σ_D² − 2 ρ_UD σ_U σ_D)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a calculation input to Risk Capital requirements, so Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a Prime that miscalculates or misreports the ratio. No quantified consequence is attached to this formula itself, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Distance To Default
assessments.quote:
The Distance To Default $d_1$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
d_1 = \frac{\ln\left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right) + \left( \sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j) + \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2 \right) T}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D} \sqrt{T}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the Distance To Default formula used to calculate Instance Financial required risk capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with exact operators and terms, so the calculation is objectively reproducible. Inputs such as LT_i, V_0, D_0, weights, rates, volatilities, correlation, and T have no values or sourcing in this paragraph, leaving supporting elements undefined here.
metrics: d_1 = [ln(sum LT_i V_0^i / sum D_0^j) + (sum w_U^i(r_c^i + r_s^i) - sum w_D^j(r_d^j + r_s^j) + rho_UD sigma_U sigma_D - sigma_U^2) T] / [sqrt(sigma_U^2 + sigma_D^2 - 2 rho_UD sigma_U sigma_D) sqrt(T)]
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship for capital-requirement breaches plausibly reach a miscalculated d_1 that understates required risk capital. The consequence is not quantified for this formula, and it depends on the breach being detected and escalated.

assessments.title: Downward Adjusted Distance To Default
assessments.quote:
The Downward Adjusted Distance To Default $d_2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
d_2 = \frac{\ln\left( \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{j=1}^m D_0^j} \right) - \left( \sum_{i=1}^n w_U^i (r_c^i + r_s^i) - \sum_{j=1}^m w_D^j (r_d^j + r_s^j)+ \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D - \sigma_U^2 \right) T}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 + \sigma_D^2 - 2 \rho_{UD} \sigma_U \sigma_D} \sqrt{T}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the closed-form calculation of the Downward Adjusted Distance To Default d_2 used in Instance Financial Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact closed-form formula for d_2, so the calculation is fully specified. However, its inputs (asset and liability values, weights, rates, volatilities, correlation, horizon T) are defined elsewhere with no values here, so the output cannot be checked from this text alone.

assessments.title: Total Variance Of Underlying Asset Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Total Variance Of Underlying Asset Portfolio $\sigma_U^2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\sigma_U^2 = \sum_{i,k=1}^n w_U^i w_U^k \sigma_V^i \sigma_V^k \rho_{V,ik}
$$

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified in closed form, but the inputs (asset weights w_U, volatilities σ_V, and correlations ρ_V) are defined elsewhere and given no values or measurement cadence in this paragraph.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The variance feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculated figure could cause a capital breach that reaches the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and potentially Conservatorship (5c3dd35a). The paragraph itself names no consequence, and the link is inferred rather than stated.

assessments.title: Total Variance Of Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Total Variance Of Debt Portfolio $\sigma_D^2$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\sigma_D^2 = \sum_{j,l=1}^m w_D^j w_D^l \sigma_D^j \sigma_D^l \rho_{D,jl}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the total variance of the debt portfolio as a weighted, correlated sum over asset-level variances and correlations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with explicit summation indices and symbols, so it is objectively computable. The weights, volatilities and correlation inputs are defined elsewhere with no values, cadence, or update rule stated in this paragraph.

Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship for capital breaches could reach that outcome, but no consequence is quantified for this calculation rule itself.

assessments.title: Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio $\rho_{UD}$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
\rho_{UD} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^m w_U^i w_D^j \sigma_V^i \sigma_D^j \rho_{VD,ij}}{\sqrt{\sigma_U^2 \sigma_D^2}}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the formula for the correlation between asset and debt portfolios used in the Required Risk Capital calculation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with explicit summation bounds and operators, so the calculation is verifiable from the text. However, the weights, volatilities, and pairwise correlations (w_U, w_D, σ_V, σ_D, ρ_VD,ij, σ_U, σ_D) are not defined or valued here, and no measurement cadence or input source is stated.
metrics: ρ_UD = [Σ_i Σ_j w_U^i · w_D^j · σ_V^i · σ_D^j · ρ_VD,ij] / sqrt(σ_U² · σ_D²), with i = 1..n and j = 1..m
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This formula feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a misstated ρ_UD would understate required capital and fall under Risk Capital breach machinery: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and escalation to conservatorship (5c3dd35a). The paragraph sets no consequence of its own, so the reach is indirect and unquantified for this formula.

assessments.title: Weight Of Asset In Underlying Asset Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The weight of asset $i$ in the underlying asset portfolio $w_U^i$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
w_U^i = \frac{\text{LT}_i V_0^i}{\sum_{k=1}^n \text{LT}_k V_0^k}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the weight of each asset in the underlying portfolio as its liquidation-threshold-weighted initial value share.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact formula with a summation over n assets, so the calculation is fully specified. The inputs LT_i and V_0^i are not defined or valued in this paragraph and must be found elsewhere.
metrics: w_U^i = (LT_i * V_0^i) / sum_{k=1}^{n} (LT_k * V_0^k)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This formula feeds the Required Risk Capital calculation, so a misapplied weight would be a capital requirement breach that the Penalty Mechanisms and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements can reach. The paragraph itself sets no consequence for this formula, so the escalation is not quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Weight Of Debt Instrument In Debt Portfolio
assessments.quote:
The weight of debt instrument $j$ in the debt portfolio $w_D^j$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
w_D^j = \frac{D_0^j}{\sum_{l=1}^m D_0^l}
$$
assessments.description: Defines the weight of each debt instrument in the debt portfolio as its share of total debt, via a formula.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The weight is given by an exact formula, w_D^j = D_0^j / sum over l=1..m of D_0^l, so it is objectively computable. The inputs D_0 are defined elsewhere in the document and no value or source is stated here, which is a minor gap.

assessments.title: Correlation Coefficient
assessments.quote: The correlation coefficient $\rho$ between two instruments is the correlation of block-weighted log returns of those assets over the last 365 days. For example, $\rho_{UD}$ is the correlation between the underlying asset portfolio $U$ and the debt portfolio $D$ as specified in [A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.1.6 - Correlation Between Asset Portfolio And Debt Portfolio](ae1dbcb9-828d-40c0-8ad8-96b3072dad4e). The subscript may begin with $V$ or $D$ to indicate whether the relevant instruments are part of the asset portfolio or debt portfolio. For example, $\rho_{VD,ij}$ is the correlation coefficient between the asset $i$ and the debt instrument $j$.
assessments.description: Defines the correlation coefficient between two instruments as correlation of block-weighted 365-day log returns and explains subscript notation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is concrete: correlation of block-weighted log returns over the last 365 days, with explicit notation examples. assessments.title: Calculate Loss Given Default
assessments.quote:
The second step is calculating the Loss Given Default $LGD$. $LGD$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$
LGD = min(1 - \frac{(1 - LP) * (1 - S)}{LT}, 0)
$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lower of the two specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein. All of these parameters should be specified as decimal numbers. For example, 3% should be specified as `0.03`.
assessments.description: Defines the formula for calculating Loss Given Default (LGD) as a capped function of three subdocument parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully explicit and the min(…, 0) cap is defined, with a decimal-input convention. However, the inputs LP, S, and LT are deferred to subdocuments and carry no values here, and no calculation cadence is stated.

All parameters expressed as decimal numbers (e.g., 3% = 0.03)

That breach triggers the Penalty Mechanisms and can escalate to Conservatorship under Sky Core, a named enforcer distinct from the Prime. The paragraph itself does not state these consequences.

assessments.title: Calculate Asset Correlation Coefficient
assessments.quote:
The third step is to calculate the Asset Correlation Coefficient $R$. $R$ is calculated as follows:

$$
R = a \times \left(1 - e^{-K \times PD}\right) + b \times \left(1 - \left(1 - e^{-K \times PD}\right)\right)
$$

Here $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Asset Correlation Coefficient R formula as the third step of Risk Capital calculation, with its parameters deferred to subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified and computable, but its inputs a, b, K and PD have no values in this paragraph and are delegated to subdocuments. No cadence or bounds are stated.

The paragraph sets no consequence of its own, and nothing ties a calculation error to these remedies specifically.

assessments.title: Calculate Capital Requirement Without Buffers
assessments.quote:
The fourth step is to calculate the Capital Requirement Without Buffers $K$. $K$ is calculated as follows:

$$
K = \left[ LGD \times N\left( \frac{N^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{R} \cdot N^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1-R}} \right) - PD \times LGD \right]
$$

Here $N$ is the cumulative normal probability distribution function and $N^{-1}$ is the inverse cumulative normal probability distribution function.
assessments.description: Defines the formula for the Capital Requirement Without Buffers K from LGD, PD, and correlation R.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with an exact 0.999 confidence level, normal CDF and inverse CDF, and explicit operators. The inputs LGD, PD, and R have no values or derivation in this paragraph, and no cadence or deadline is stated.
metrics: confidence level 0.999 in N^-1(0.999)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: K feeds the Risk Capital requirement, which is subject to Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) that could reach a Prime that miscalculates or underfunds it. No consequence is quantified for this formula specifically, and escalation to conservatorship is not stated here.

assessments.title: Calculate Required Risk Capital
assessments.quote:
The final step is to calculate the Instance Financial RRC $RRC$. $RRC$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{RRC} = K \times \frac{1}{CR} \times \text{EAD} \times \text{ECR}
$$

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the formula for calculating a Prime's Instance Financial Risk Capital, with its parameters delegated to subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula RRC = K × (1/CR) × EAD × ECR is exact, but none of its four parameters (K, CR, EAD, ECR) has a value or metric in this paragraph; they are delegated to subdocuments. The paragraph is therefore quantified in structure but not in operative magnitude.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: This calculation sets the Risk Capital requirement, and breaches of Risk Capital rules trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and escalation to conservatorship (5c3dd35a), with Core GovOps as a distinct enforcer. assessments.title: Reference Implementation
assessments.quote:
A reference implementation of the calculation of Instance Financial RRC for lending markets is included herein.

```python
import math

from scipy.stats import norm

# Constants
RISK_FREE_RATE = 0.04  # SOFR
TIME_HORIZON = 1  # 1 year


class FinancialRRCModel:
    def __init__(self):
        # For demo purposes, we hardcode a dummy correlation map
        self.token_correlation_map = {
            "TOKENA": {"TOKENB": 0.5},
            "TOKENB": {"TOKENA": 0.5},
        }

    def _calculate_effective_volatility(self, list_1, list_2):
        """
        Calculate the effective variance between two sets of positions.
        """
        effective_variance = 0.0
        for sym1, pos1 in list_1.items():
            for sym2, pos2 in list_2.items():
                if sym1 == sym2:
                    corr = 1.0
                else:
                    corr = self.token_correlation_map.get(sym1, {}).get(
                        sym2, self.token_correlation_map.get(sym2, {}).get(sym1, 0.0)
                    )
                effective_variance += (
                    pos1["share"]
                    * pos2["share"]
                    * pos1["volatility_30d"]
                    * pos2["volatility_30d"]
                    * corr
                )
        return effective_variance

    def _estimate_rrc_for_position(self, wallet_data):
        """
        Estimate the required-risk capital (RRC) for a given wallet_data dict.
        """
        # 1) compute effective volatilities
        var_coll = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
        )
        var_debt = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
        )
        vol_coll = math.sqrt(var_coll)
        vol_debt = math.sqrt(var_debt)

        # 2) correlation collateral↔debt
        cov_cd = self._calculate_effective_volatility(
            wallet_data["collateral_positions"],
            wallet_data["debt_positions"],
        )
        corr_cd = cov_cd / (vol_coll * vol_debt) if vol_coll * vol_debt > 0 else 0.0

        # 3) drift terms
        eff_coll_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["supply_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )
        eff_borrow_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["borrow_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["debt_positions"].values()
        )
        eff_stake_rate = sum(
            p["share"] * p["staking_apy_30d"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )

        drift_cd = (
            eff_coll_rate + eff_stake_rate - eff_borrow_rate + (var_debt - var_coll) / 2
        )

        vol_cd = math.sqrt(
            max(var_coll + var_debt - 2 * corr_cd * vol_coll * vol_debt, 0)
        )

        # 4) Black-Cox inputs
        a = (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) / (vol_cd**2) if vol_cd > 0 else 0.0
        L = wallet_data["collateral_usd_lt"]
        D = wallet_data["debt_usd"]
        log_term = math.log(L / D) if L > 0 and D > 0 else float("-inf")
        denom = vol_cd * math.sqrt(TIME_HORIZON) if vol_cd > 0 else 1e-10

        d1 = (log_term + (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) * TIME_HORIZON) / denom
        d2 = (log_term - (drift_cd - vol_cd**2 / 2) * TIME_HORIZON) / denom

        # 5) Probability of Default
        try:
            pd = norm.cdf(-d1) + norm.cdf(-d2) * (L / D) ** (-2 * a)
        except OverflowError:
            pd = 1.0
        pd = max(0.0, min(pd, 1.0))

        # 6) Loss Given Default
        recovery = sum(
            p["share"]
            * (1 - p["liquidation_penalty"])
            * (1 - p["slippage"])
            / p["liquidation_threshold"]
            for p in wallet_data["collateral_positions"].values()
        )
        lgd = max(0.0, min(1 - recovery, 1.0))

        # 7) Exposure at Default
        ead = sum(
            debt["debt_usd"]
            * math.exp((RISK_FREE_RATE + debt["borrow_apy_30d"]) * TIME_HORIZON)
            for debt in wallet_data["debt_positions"].values()
        )

        # 8) Asset Correlation Coefficient
        a_acc, b_acc, c_acc = 0.13, 10, 0.33
        exp_term = math.exp(-b_acc * pd)
        acc = a_acc * (1 - exp_term) / (1 - math.exp(-b_acc)) + c_acc * (
            1 - (1 - exp_term) / (1 - math.exp(-b_acc))
        )

        # 9) Credit risk weight
        default_threshold = (
            norm.ppf(max(pd, 1e-10)) + math.sqrt(acc) * norm.ppf(0.999)
        ) / math.sqrt(1 - acc)
        credit_risk = max(lgd * norm.cdf(default_threshold) - lgd * pd, 0)

        # 10) RRC
        rrc = credit_risk * ead
        return rrc


# -------- DEMO USAGE --------

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # 1) Build a dummy wallet_data structure
    wallet_data = {
        "collateral_positions": {
            "TOKENA": {
                "share": 0.6,
                "volatility_30d": 0.2,
                "supply_apy_30d": 0.05,
                "staking_apy_30d": 0.02,
                "liquidation_penalty": 0.1,
                "liquidation_threshold": 0.8,
                "slippage": 0.01,
            },
            "TOKENB": {
                "share": 0.4,
                "volatility_30d": 0.25,
                "supply_apy_30d": 0.04,
                "staking_apy_30d": 0.015,
                "liquidation_penalty": 0.12,
                "liquidation_threshold": 0.85,

        "debt_positions": {

                "borrow_apy_30d": 0.06,

        },

    }

    # 2) Instantiate and run

    rrc = model._estimate_rrc_for_position(wallet_data)
    print(f"Estimated Required Risk Capital (RRC): ${rrc:,.2f}")
```

assessments.title: Basis In Basel Framework

assessments.title: Citations To Basel Framework
assessments.quote:
Citations are made throughout the process for calculating Instance Financial RRC for Real World Assets to relevant provisions from the Basel Framework.

These citations follow the standard format of `[Prefix][Chapter Number].[Paragraph Number]`, where `Prefix` is a three letter prefix indicating the regulatory standard area or chapter family. For example, a citation to `CRE20.1` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapter 20 regarding "Standardised Approach: Individual Exposures", paragraph 1.

When reference is made to a range of documents, a hyphen may be used. For example, `CRE20.1-93` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapter 20 regarding "Standardised Approach: Individual Exposures", paragraphs 1 through 93.

Similarly, discrete sets of documents may be referenced using a comma. For example, `CRE40-41, 45` refers to Credit Risk Standards, Chapters 40 to 41 and 45.
assessments.description: Specifies the notation format for citing Basel Framework provisions in Real World Asset Instance Financial RRC calculations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The citation syntax (prefix, chapter, paragraph, hyphen ranges, comma sets) is exactly specified with worked examples, so compliance with format is objectively checkable. However, the operative requirement is delegated: it never says which provisions must be cited or at which calculation steps.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, emergency, or review mechanism reaches citation formatting; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Smart Contract Risk Rating Calculation
assessments.quote:
The second step in calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Smart Contract Risk Rating $SCRR$ for the covered smart contracts identified in [A.3.2.2.1.2.1 - Defining Relevant Smart Contracts](162cfc93-77bd-4878-a8be-370d8862d792). The $SCRR$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{SCRR} = min[\text{CAP}, (\text{SR} + \text{CCR}) \times \text{LAF} \times {AF}]
$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.
The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

assessments.title: Code Complexity Rating
assessments.quote:
The Code Complexity Rate $CCR$ is a measure of the complexity of the code of the smart contracts used by the protocol. The $CCR$ is calculated as follows:

$$
CCR = \text{CCRMax} \times min(1, \frac{\text{RawCCR} + 1}{\text{CCRUpperBound} + 1})
$$

Here the $min$ function is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Code Complexity Rate, a capped ratio of raw smart contract code complexity, as an input to Risk Capital calculation.

assessments.title: Raw Code Complexity Rating

The Raw Code Complexity Rating $\text{RawCCR}$ is an unnormalized measure of the complexity of the code of the smart contracts that implement the protocol. The $\text{RawCCR}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{RawCCR}=(\text{TCC} \times \text{CCweight}) + (\text{TDP} \times \text{DPweight}) + (\text{TEC} \times \text{ECweight}) + (\text{ID} \times \text{IDweight}) + (\frac{\text{CS}}{\text{CSfactor}} \times \text{CSweight})
$$

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with five named terms and explicit operators, so a checker can compute the structure. assessments.title: Lindy Adjustment Factor
assessments.quote:
The Lindy Adjustment Factor $\text{LAF}$ is a measure of the "Lindiness" of the smart contracts and is based on the idea that vulnerable smart contracts with large TVL for a significant period of time would have already been hacked. Therefore, protocols with a greater time integrated TVL are safer, all other things equal, than protocols with a lower time integrated TVL. The $\text{LAF}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
\text{LAF} = max(0, 1 - \frac{ln(1 + \lambda \times \text{AGEeff})}{ln(1 + \lambda \times \text{max})})
$$

Here $max$ is the mathematical maximum function that returns the greater of the specified parameters and $ln$ is the natural logarithm.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Defines the Lindy Adjustment Factor formula, which reduces risk capital requirements for smart contracts with longer, larger TVL history.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is fully specified with an exact expression and a max(0, ...) floor. However, the inputs λ, AGEeff, and max have no values here and are deferred to subdocuments, so the magnitudes are not stated in this paragraph.
metrics: LAF = max(0, 1 - ln(1 + λ × AGEeff) / ln(1 + λ × max))
λ, AGEeff, and max parameter values specified in subdocuments (not stated here)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: LAF is an input to the required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculated factor would under-capitalize a Prime; the Penalty Mechanisms plausibly reach this, but no consequence is quantified for the LAF formula itself.

assessments.title: Decay Factor
assessments.quote:
The Decay Factor $decayFactor$ is a parameter indicating how rapidly the effectiveness of audits in reducing risk decreases over time. The $decayFactor$ is calculated as follows:

$$

$$

The parameter of this formula is specified in the subdocument herein.
assessments.description: Defines a decay factor that reduces audit risk-reduction effectiveness as audit age rises, from 1 to 0 by age thresholds.

assessments.title: Calculate Blended Average Required Capital Percentage
assessments.quote:
The final Required Capital Percentage $x$ should be calculated as a weighted average of the F1 Required Capital Percentage and the F2 Required Capital Percentage as follows:

$$
x = b \times \alpha \times f_2 + (1 - \alpha) \times f_1
$$

The parameters of this formula are defined in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.description: Specifies a weighted-average formula combining F1 and F2 Required Capital Percentages to produce the final Required Capital Percentage x.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula x = b×α×f2 + (1−α)×f1 is explicit and fully specified as an operation. The inputs b, α, f1 and f2 are defined only in linked subdocuments and no values are given here, and the 'should' wording is soft.
metrics: x = b × α × f2 + (1 − α) × f1, where x is the final Required Capital Percentage, f1 and f2 are the F1 and F2 Required Capital Percentages, and b and α are weighting parameters defined in subdocuments
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The output x sets the Risk Capital requirement, so a Prime that under-holds against a miscalculated x is exposed to the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). The penalty is not quantified for this formula, and the paragraph does not state that the instance contract enforces it on-chain.

assessments.title: Alpha
assessments.quote:
Alpha $\alpha$ is a weighting factor indicating how close the Risk Rating is to the threshold for a High Risk Protocol versus the threshold for a Low Risk Protocol. It is calculated as:

$$
\alpha = \dfrac{r - 25}{50 - 25}
$$

Here $r$ is the Risk Rating of the protocol.
assessments.description: Defines the alpha weighting factor as a linear function of protocol Risk Rating between the High and Low Risk thresholds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula alpha = (r - 25)/(50 - 25) is fully specified with exact constants and no ambiguity in the calculation. The Risk Rating r is defined elsewhere and the paragraph does not state its scale or measurement cadence, so the input is not fully verifiable from this text alone.
metrics: alpha = (r - 25) / (50 - 25), where r is the protocol's Risk Rating
Denominator/threshold constants: 25 (High Risk Protocol threshold) and 50 (Low Risk Protocol threshold)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Alpha feeds the required Risk Capital calculation, so a miscalculated alpha would understate or overstate required capital, which is a capital-requirement breach reachable by the Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship escalation. The consequence is not quantified for this specific formula, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Piecewise Function
assessments.quote:
The Piecewise Function $CRR(x)$ calculates a percentage risk capital requirement based on an input $x$ and is defined as follows:

$$
\text{CRR}(x) =\begin{cases}a & \text{if } x \le x_{\text{start}}, \\[8pt]b \times \dfrac{x - x_{\text{start}}}{x_{\text{kink}} - x_{\text{start}}} & \text{if } x_{\text{start}} < x \le x_{\text{kink}}, \\[8pt]b \;+\; c \;\dfrac{x - x_{\text{kink}}}{x_{\text{max}} - x_{\text{kink}}}& \text{if } x_{\text{kink}} < x < x_{\text{max}}, \\[8pt]d& \text{if } x \ge x_{\text{max}}.\end{cases}
$$
assessments.description: Defines a piecewise function that maps an input x to a percentage risk capital requirement CRR(x).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The piecewise formula and its breakpoints (x_start, x_kink, x_max) are exactly specified, so the calculation is fully verifiable. The parameter values a, b, c, d and the breakpoints are not given in this paragraph and are defined elsewhere.
metrics: CRR(x) = a if x <= x_start
CRR(x) = b × (x − x_start)/(x_kink − x_start) if x_start < x <= x_kink
CRR(x) = b + c × (x − x_kink)/(x_max − x_kink) if x_kink < x < x_max
CRR(x) = d if x >= x_max
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is a calculation definition with no consequence of its own. The percentage it produces sets the Risk Capital a Prime must hold, so Penalty Mechanisms and conservatorship for breach of capital requirements plausibly reach a failure to hold the computed amount. No quantified consequence is attached to this formula specifically, so the rating is mid.

The Starting Threshold $x_{\text{start}}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
x_{\text{start}}(r) = i \times (r_i - r)
$$

The parameters of this formula are defined in [A.3.2.2.1.2.3.3.1.5.4 - Threshold Parameters](654528b9-d7c8-4cee-9261-d5a745ea231e).

assessments.title: Kink Threshold
assessments.quote:
The Kink Threshold $x_{\text{kink}}$ is calculated as follows:

$$
x_{\text{kink}}(r) = x_{\text{start}}(r) \;+\; i_{kink} \times\bigl[\;x_{\text{max}}(r)\;-\;x_{\text{start}}(r)\bigr]
$$

Here $r$ is the Risk Rating.

The parameters of this formula are defined in [A.3.2.2.1.2.3.3.1.5.4 - Threshold Parameters](654528b9-d7c8-4cee-9261-d5a745ea231e).
assessments.description: Defines the Kink Threshold as a per-Risk-Rating formula interpolating between start and max values using a kink input.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is exact and fully specified, but its inputs x_start(r), x_max(r), and i_kink are defined only by cross-reference to A.3.2.2.1.2.3.3.1.5.4, and no values appear in this paragraph. No measurement cadence or deadline is stated.
metrics: x_kink(r) = x_start(r) + i_kink × [x_max(r) − x_start(r)], where r is the Risk Rating
Parameters x_start, x_max, i_kink defined in A.3.2.2.1.2.3.3.1.5.4 (values not stated here)

assessments.title: Reference Implementation
assessments.quote:
The document herein contains a reference implementation of the calculation of Instance Smart Contract RRC based on the Smart Contract Risk Rating.

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Function Definition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def piecewise_coverage(x, x_start, x_kink, x_max):
    """
    Returns a coverage fraction in [0.0 ... 1.0] given x
    and piecewise linear thresholds:
      - 0% coverage if x < x_start
      - linear 0%→25% from x_start to x_kink
      - linear 25%→100% from x_kink to x_max
      - 100% if x > x_max
    """
    # Safely handle edge cases
    if x <= x_start:
        return 0.0
    if x >= x_max:
        return 1.0

    # If between x_start and x_kink -> map linearly from 0% to 25%
    if x_start < x <= x_kink:
        span = x_kink - x_start
        # fraction of the way through that segment
        frac = (x - x_start) / span
        # coverage goes 0 -> 0.25 (25%)
        return 0.25 * frac

    # If between x_kink and x_max -> map linearly from 25% to 100%
    else:  # x_kink < x < x_max
        span = x_max - x_kink
        frac = (x - x_kink) / span
        # coverage goes 0.25 -> 1.0
        return 0.25 + (0.75 * frac)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Thresholds
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating):
    """
    Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
    in % terms, e.g. 5%, 23.75%, 30%, etc.
    """
    x_start = (50 - rating) * 0.01  # e.g. rating=0 -> 0.5 (50%)
    x_max = x_start + 0.50  # always a 50% gap to max
    # kink is 75% of the way from start to max
    x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)
    return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)


def f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating):
    """
    Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
    in fraction form (0.50, 0.875, 1.00, etc).
    """
    # starting threshold = (75 - rating) * 2%:
    x_start = (75 - rating) * 0.02
    x_max = x_start + 0.50
    x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)  # 75% of the way
    return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# RRC Calculation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def calculate_rrc_coverage(
    rating,
    exposure_internal,
    exposure_total,
    liquid_surplus_internal,
    total_exposure_beyond_surplus,
    total_collateral,
):
    """
    Returns the coverage fraction (0 - 1) for a given rating & scenario.
    For the absolute coverage amount, multiply coverage_fraction
    by `exposure_internal`.
    """

    # 1) Compute the two driver ratios
    f1 = max(
        0.0, total_exposure_beyond_surplus / total_collateral
    )  # Ensuring it is non-negative when surplus > exposure
    f2 = (
        exposure_internal + 0.1 * (exposure_total - exposure_internal)
    ) / liquid_surplus_internal

    # 2) Determine which category the rating is in
    if rating <= 25:
        # TRR Category 1 (Low Risk)  => use only f1 piecewise
        x_start, x_kink, x_max = f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating)
        coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

    elif rating <= 50:
        # TRR Category 2 (Medium Risk) => blend coverage from f1-curve and f2-curve
        # First get coverage from the "f1 low-risk"
        x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1 = f1_thresholds_low_risk(25)
        cov_f1 = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1)

        # Then get coverage from the "f2 high-risk"
        x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2 = f2_thresholds_high_risk(50)
        cov_f2 = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2)

        # Blend factor alpha
        alpha = (rating - 25) / (50 - 25)
        coverage_fraction = (1 - alpha) * cov_f1 + 0.15 * alpha * cov_f2

    elif rating <= 75:
        # TRR Category 3 (High Risk) => use only f2
        x_start, x_kink, x_max = f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating)
        coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

    else:
        # TRR Category 4 (Extreme Risk) => special piecewise lumps.
        if rating > 75:
            return 1.0

    return coverage_fraction
```

It loses a point because inputs such as total_collateral and liquid_surplus_internal are not defined in the text, the docstrings conflict with the code (e.g., the f2 example values), and it is unclear whether a reference implementation is itself binding.

assessments.title: Delay Factor

The Delay Adjustment Factor $\text{DF}$ is a factor indicating the extent to which the risk associated with backdoor access is mitigated by a security delay between the time that a change using backdoor access is approved and the time that such a change becomes effective. This delay gives users time to raise issues or withdraw funds in the event of malicious or undesirable use of backdoor access.

The Delay Factor is `1` if there is no security delay and `0` if the security delay is 48 hours or greater. For security delays between 0 hours and 48 hours, the Delay Factor is linearly reduced for each hour of security delay. So a security delay of 24 hours would result in a Delay Factor of `0.5`.

assessments.title: Tip Junior Risk Capital Percentage
assessments.quote:
The Tip JRC amount is **10%** of the Prime Agent's Total Junior Risk Capital (IJRC + PEJRC + TEJRC).

For example, if a Prime Agent has $20 million of Internal Junior Risk Capital and $20 million of Prime External Junior Risk Capital, the Tip Junior Risk Capital would be $4 million.

assessments.title: External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value
assessments.quote:
The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio is **1.00**. For example, if a Prime Agent has $20 million of Internal Junior Risk Capital, the EPI ratio enables it to source $20 million of External Junior Risk Capital.

This EPI ratio governs the initial mechanism for sourcing EJRC (PEJRC + TEJRC) and is based purely on the Prime’s IJRC; Primes can source EJRC via this initial mechanism up to a maximum amount equal to their IJRC holdings. However, additional EJRC may potentially be acquired via the alternative use of SPJ capacity, as described in [A.3.2.1.2.3.1.2.1 - Alternative Use Of SPJ Capacity To Source External Junior Risk Capital](03029174-91b4-4974-af1e-52438556a70b).

It is incomplete because the extra EJRC route via SPJ capacity is delegated to another document, and no measurement cadence is given.
