assessments.title: Senior Per Junior (SPJ) Ratio Values
assessments.quote:
The SPJ ratio varies by the JRC type used for enablement:

- Internal Junior Risk Capital SPJ: **1.00**,
- EPI-acquired Prime External Junior Risk Capital SPJ: **0.75**,
- EPI-acquired Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital SPJ: **0.50**,
- SPJ-acquired External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC or TEJRC): **zero (0)**.

For example, if a Prime Agent has $20 million of Internal Junior Risk Capital, $10 million of Prime External Junior Risk Capital, and $10 million of Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital, then it would be able to count or "enable" $32.5 million of Senior Capital towards its required Risk Capital.

assessments.title: Deposit And Redemption Queues
assessments.quote:
The srUSDS contract utilizes distinct queues for managing conversions. Users can add USDS to the deposit queue for conversion into srUSDS; or add srUSDS to the redemption queue for conversion back into USDS at any point during the month.

Assets placed in either queue can be withdrawn by the user at any time before the Monthly Settlement Cycle begins.

At the Monthly Settlement Cycle, all assets remaining in the queues are processed: queued USDS is converted into srUSDS, and queued srUSDS is converted into USDS based on the prevailing Conversion Rate. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.3 - Conversion Rate](2220b1b5-f2f6-4325-9bb5-43cca84e184c).

assessments.title: Conversion Rate
assessments.quote:
The conversion rate represents the amount of USDS redeemable per unit of srUSDS. This rate increases or decreases over time, reflecting the net return earned by the ESRC pool. The rate is updated at the conclusion of each Monthly Settlement Cycle based on the performance of the ESRC pool during the preceding month, according to the following standard compounding formula:

`New srUSDS Conversion Rate = Previous Conversion Rate * (1 + Monthly srUSDS Yield)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein.
assessments.description: Defines how the srUSDS conversion rate is updated monthly by compounding the ESRC pool's monthly yield.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The update formula and monthly cadence are explicit, but the key input, Monthly srUSDS Yield, has no defined value or calculation method and is deferred to other documents. The paragraph does not state how the yield is measured.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a computational accounting rule with no actor who can violate it in a way that triggers penalties, liquidation, or emergency action. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Monthly srUSDS Yield
assessments.quote:
`Monthly srUSDS Yield` represents the net percentage return earned solely by the ESRC pool during the concluded monthly cycle, distributable to srUSDS holders via the conversion rate adjustment. It directly reflects the risk-adjusted performance of the capital deployed and is calculated as:

`[(Total Interest Paid by Stars on ESRC Portion - Losses Allocated to ESRC) / ESRC Principal at start of month - Sky Spread] * (1 - ESRC Earnings Fee)`

The Sky Spread and ESRC Earnings Fee are specified in [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.1 - Sky Spread](c160f99c-c3d8-41e9-a3d1-cde514b7a2da) and [A.3.2.2.4.2.3.3.2 - ESRC Earnings Fee](559f6fb6-daf6-41b2-9882-53a91aaf132f), respectively.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core formula is explicit and the cycle is monthly, but the Sky Spread and ESRC Earnings Fee values are delegated to other sections, and the parenthesization of the division and subtraction is ambiguous. No measurement deadline or rounding convention is stated.

assessments.quote: This document defines the operational details of the recurring monthly process allowing Prime Agents to originate Senior Risk Capital (Originated Senior Risk Capital or OSRC) from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool. assessments.title: Available Total Senior Risk Capital Pool Determination
assessments.quote: Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) is the amount of Senior Risk Capital that is available each Monthly Settlement Cycle for Primes to originate and thus turn into Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) through the monthly origination process. TSRC is the sum of designated Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) (see [A.2.3.1.3 - Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital](ac7a6636-acbc-40c9-abc1-4543c0beb300)) and available External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) from the srUSDS contract. Prior to each monthly bidding window, the TSRC is calculated and publicly announced. Additional operational details will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

assessments.title: Allocation & Clearing Price Determination
assessments.quote: Bids are ranked descending by price. TSRC is allocated sequentially to the highest bids until the pool is exhausted or all bids are filled. The price of the lowest successful bid that receives an allocation (even partial) sets the uniform clearing price for the month. All winning bidders pay this clearing price per unit of OSRC allocated, regardless of their original bid price. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

assessments.title: Ecosystem Accord Requirements
assessments.quote:
Rental of Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) requires a registered Ecosystem Accord specifying: Amount, Duration, and Price/Terms. As the system permits sub-renting (allowing a Prime to rent out OSRC it has previously rented), the Accord must explicitly state if the borrower is granted this permission. In regards to Duration, the Ecosystem Accord must specify the rental period, which cannot extend beyond the end of the current Monthly Settlement Cycle. Primes may agree on any Duration within this limit.

Standardized Ecosystem Accord templates will be provided in a future iteration of the Atlas.

assessments.quote: A registered OSRC-rental Ecosystem Accord effectively transfers the claim on the specified amount of the lender’s OSRC to the borrower for the duration of the agreement. assessments.title: Length Of Breaches
assessments.quote:
The length of a breach refers to the duration measured between its defined start and end points, which depend on the specific aspect of the breach being considered.

If a breach is initially a Low Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a High Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until it became a High Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until that high-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).

Likewise, if a breach is initially a High Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a Low Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until it became a Low Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until that low-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).
assessments.description: Defines how breach duration is measured, including how time is split when a breach changes severity level.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The severity-transition segmentation is stated as explicit logic, but the start and end points are delegated to the breach aspect and the conclusion is given only as "e.g., upon final resolution". No units, cadence, or magnitudes are stated.

assessments.title: Alternative Enforcement Mechanisms
assessments.quote:
In the event that the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital is less than its Required Risk Capital at the time of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, or the collection of the penalty would cause the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital to fall below its Required Risk Capital, then Sky may exercise the alternative enforcement mechanism described below.

In this instance Sky, at its discretion, may issue additional tokens of the Prime Agent and sell them on the open market until it has collected proceeds equal to the calculated penalty. Any proceeds above the calculated penalty shall be refunded to the Prime Agent SubProxy account.

Alternatively, Sky may convert the penalty into a debt owed by the Prime Agent to Sky Core at terms mutually agreed between Sky Core and the Prime Agent.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is concrete: Total Risk Capital below Required Risk Capital at the Monthly Settlement Cycle, or penalty collection breaching that minimum. The remedy magnitudes are delegated, though: the penalty is 'calculated' elsewhere, sale proceeds are open-market, and debt terms are 'mutually agreed'.

assessments.title: Short-Term Exemption
assessments.quote: While the Risk Framework undergoes refinement, penalties for any Prime Agent breaches of Required Risk Capital will be calculated by Core GovOps once the infrastructure is in place to do so. This calculation serves the purposes of system monitoring, data gathering, and framework calibration. However, throughout this interim phase, such calculated penalties will not be formally assessed against Prime Agents, and consequently, Prime Agents will not be required to make payment for these penalties. Notwithstanding this temporary exemption from penalty payment, Prime Agents are expected to maintain a Encumbrance Ratio of less than or equal to 90%. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9).
assessments.description: Suspends payment of calculated Required Risk Capital penalties during the Risk Framework refinement, while expecting Primes to keep Encumbrance Ratio at or below 90%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 90% Encumbrance Ratio ceiling is a concrete, checkable threshold, but it is framed as an 'expected' maintenance level with no measurement cadence. Penalty calculation is tied to undefined infrastructure ('once the infrastructure is in place') with no deadline, and the exemption leaves it arguable whether the ratio is binding.
metrics: Encumbrance Ratio less than or equal to 90%
Core GovOps calculates Required Risk Capital breach penalties once infrastructure is in place (no deadline stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found: the penalty machinery that would normally reach a Risk Capital or encumbrance breach (Penalty Mechanisms b8ee2d12) is expressly suspended for payment during this interim, and calculated penalties are for monitoring only. No conservatorship, emergency spell, or artifact review is stated to reach the 90% ratio.

assessments.title: Additional Token Issuance For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.quote: In the event that financial penalties are not sufficient to address the shortfall because payment of the penalties would exacerbate an existing capital shortfall, Core GovOps may require the Prime Agent to issue additional tokens and sell them to the extent it deems necessary. Operational GovOps will assist Core GovOps in executing any such transaction. Future iterations of the Risk Capital framework will specify a more detailed methodology for required token issuance.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps require a Prime Agent to issue and sell tokens when penalties cannot cover a capital shortfall.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actors (Core GovOps, Prime Agent, Operational GovOps) and the trigger (penalties insufficient because payment would exacerbate a shortfall) are named, but the quantity of tokens and the sale scope are left to Core GovOps 'to the extent it deems necessary'. The paragraph also defers the methodology to future iterations, so compliance is largely arguable.
metrics: Trigger: financial penalties are not sufficient to address the shortfall
Trigger: penalty payment would exacerbate an existing capital shortfall
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is a remedy within the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) that Core GovOps, a distinct enforcer, can invoke against a Prime after penalties fail. The issuance amount is unquantified and the power is discretionary ('may'), so escalation depends on Core GovOps acting.

assessments.title: Restrictions On Investments For Breach Of Capital Requirement
assessments.quote: Core GovOps may impose whatever restrictions it deems necessary on the usage of the Allocation System Primitive by the Prime Agent, including limiting the Prime Agent’s exposure to certain Instances (conduits) or prohibiting the Prime Agent from using certain Instances. These restrictions may extend for a period of time that Core GovOps deems fit.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps restrict a Prime Agent's use of the Allocation System Primitive, including exposure to or use of specific Instances, for a period it sets, after a capital requirement breach.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is real and the actor (Core GovOps) and restriction types are named, but the trigger, scope, and duration are left to the body's discretion ("whatever restrictions it deems necessary", "a period of time that Core GovOps deems fit"). No thresholds, criteria, or deadlines are stated, so compliance is judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is itself a remedy within the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), and the sibling Conservatorship path (5c3dd35a) provides escalation for breaches of capital requirements. Core GovOps is a distinct enforcer with concrete restrictions, but the magnitude and duration are unquantified and imposition depends on Core GovOps choosing to act.

assessments.title: Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.quote: In the event that less extreme measures are not adequate to address the capital shortfall, Core GovOps may seek to put the Prime Agent into conservatorship, in which case the Sky Core Facilitator takes direct control of the Prime Agent to maximize value for Sky and other Prime Agent stakeholders. Seeking to put a Prime Agent into conservatorship requires immediate escalation to Sky Core Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48).
assessments.description: Allows Core GovOps to seek conservatorship of a Prime Agent after less extreme measures fail to address a capital shortfall.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names actors (Core GovOps, Sky Core Facilitator, Sky Core Governance) and enumerated steps (immediate escalation, expedited Executive Vote, direct control). The trigger, 'not adequate' to address the shortfall, and the timing, 'immediate', have no numeric threshold or deadline.
metrics: Escalation to Sky Core Governance is 'immediate'
Conservatorship requires an expedited Executive Vote per A.1.9.1.5.4.1
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph is itself the conservatorship escalation: Core GovOps and the Facilitator are enforcers distinct from the Prime, with a concrete remedy of direct control. It is mid rather than strong because Core GovOps 'may seek' conservatorship, so firing depends on someone volunteering the escalation, and the penalty machinery (b8ee2d12) is not quantified for this step.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Operational Executor Agents
assessments.quote: In the near term there are no penalties for Operational Executor Agents for failure of the Prime Agents they supervise to maintain appropriate levels of capital. In future iterations of the Risk Framework, Operational Executor Agents will be required to put up collateral and act as "insurers" of all activities by the Prime Agents they supervise with regard to the Sky Primitives. At that point Core GovOps will be able to seize this collateral in the event of failure to obtain compensation for breaches of the Risk Capital requirement by the Prime Agent.
assessments.description: States Operational Executor Agents face no near-term penalties for Prime capital failures, with future collateral requirements deferred.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a posture statement that defers the operative obligation to future iterations, with no collateral amount, coverage ratio, or trigger defined. Nothing currently binds the Operational Executor Agents to a checkable standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph explicitly states there are no penalties for Operational Executor Agents in the near term, and the future collateral seizure mechanism is not yet specified. The general Penalty Mechanisms doc (b8ee2d12) covers Primes and Operational Agents but is not applied here by the paragraph's own terms.

assessments.title: Termination Of Executor Accord
assessments.quote: In the event that Core GovOps determines that the Operational Executor Agent is not appropriately supervising the activities of the Prime Agent, Core GovOps may terminate the respective Executor Accord. This requires an immediate escalation to Sky Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48). Core GovOps must arrange for another Operational Executor Agent to stand in until the Prime Agent can Invoke the Executor Accord Primitive to enter into a new Executor Accord. The Prime Agent must suspend all operations until a new Executor Accord is voted on and formally integrated into the Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.description: Lets Core GovOps terminate an Executor Accord for inadequate supervision, requiring escalation, a stand-in executor, and suspension of Prime operations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Named actors (Core GovOps, Operational Executor Agent, Prime Agent) and enumerated steps (escalation, stand-in, suspension) are concrete. The trigger, 'not appropriately supervising', and the timing ('immediate', 'expedited') are qualitative with no thresholds or deadlines.
metrics: Immediate escalation to Sky Governance
Expedited Executive Vote
Another Operational Executor Agent must stand in until a new Executor Accord is entered
Prime Agent must suspend all operations until a new Executor Accord is voted on and formally integrated into the Artifact
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps, distinct from the supervised executor, can terminate the accord and suspend the Prime, with a defined escalation to an expedited Executive Vote under the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and the cited remedies path (3f5f79fa). The trigger is discretionary ('may'), which keeps it from being fully automatic.

assessments.title: Triggers For Escalation
assessments.quote: In the event of a disagreement regarding the penalties for a violation of Risk Capital requirements, either party may escalate the matter to Sky Governance. In addition, the extraordinary remedies of Prime Agent Conservatorship and Executor Accord Termination must always be escalated to a Sky Governance Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Lets either party escalate penalty disputes to Sky Governance and requires Executive Votes for conservatorship or executor termination.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The mandatory route (conservatorship and Executor Accord Termination must go to an Executive Vote) is a named, enumerated step. However, the escalation trigger 'disagreement' is undefined, 'may escalate' is permissive, and no deadline, threshold, or penalty magnitude is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) are the remedies this escalation routes to, with Sky Governance as a distinct enforcer. Escalation only fires if a party volunteers a dispute, and the penalty amounts are unquantified here, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Sky Governance Process
assessments.quote: Once a matter has been escalated to Sky Governance, the Sky Core Facilitator may request any information they deem necessary from Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, and the Prime Agent. Sky Governance then acts through a Governance Poll to determine its resolution of the matter.
assessments.description: Governs how escalated matters reach Sky Governance, including the Facilitator's information requests and resolution by Governance Poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors (Sky Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, Prime Agent) and a decision mechanism (Governance Poll) are named, but the information scope is 'any information they deem necessary' and there are no thresholds, deadlines, or criteria for resolution.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This paragraph is the escalation step that routes Risk-Capital matters to Sky Governance, where the Risk-Capital Incident Response framework (12b7d480) and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can impose penalties up to conservatorship. The consequence is not quantified here and depends on the matter being escalated and a Governance Poll being run.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management framework establishes universal rules for Prime Agents deploying Sky’s Collateral Portfolio to maintain the stability of the USDS peg through highly liquid assets. The Asset Liability Management framework governs collateral allocation across all Agents, via the Allocation System Primitive, and replaces Sky Core’s historical Asset Liability Management mechanisms which will be offboarded entirely or transitioned to Prime Agents.
assessments.description: Introduces the Asset Liability Management framework governing Prime Agents' deployment of Sky's Collateral Portfolio to support the USDS peg.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a framing statement that says universal rules exist and that the framework governs allocation, but it sets no thresholds, formulas, or deadlines. The operative rules are not stated in this text, so there is nothing a third party could check against it.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph names no enforcement path, and the Allocation System Primitive it references is not one of the catalogued mechanisms. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: The "Sky Collateral Portfolio" consists of all assets backing USDS, whether deployed by Prime Agents or Sky Core. The Asset Liability Management framework is based on ensuring that a certain percentage of Sky Collateral Portfolio is invested in Actively Stabilizing Collateral, highly liquid market making non-USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS. In this way, if there is ever downward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to buy USDS to maintain the peg.
assessments.description: Defines the Sky Collateral Portfolio and states a framework to hold an unspecified share of it as Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the metric (share of Sky Collateral Portfolio held as Actively Stabilizing Collateral) but states no percentage, threshold, measurement cadence, or enforcing actor, only 'a certain percentage'. A defender could reasonably argue no binding obligation exists yet.
metrics: Share of Sky Collateral Portfolio invested in Actively Stabilizing Collateral: 'a certain percentage' (no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a conceptual framework with no operative threshold, and no catalog mechanism reaches it; the Penalty Mechanisms and artifact review that could apply belong to the later operative minimum (A.3.3.2.2), not this text.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management also ensures that a certain percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio is invested in a Demand Absorption Buffer, highly liquid market making USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS. In this way, if there is ever upward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to sell USDS to maintain the peg.
assessments.description: Requires a percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio to be held in liquid USDS market-making assets to defend the peg against upward pressure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a parameter (a Demand Absorption Buffer share of the Collateral Portfolio) but never states its magnitude, saying only 'a certain percentage'. 'Highly liquid' and 'close to 1 USD' are qualitative with no tolerance, cadence, or verification method, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Percentage of Sky Collateral Portfolio invested in Demand Absorption Buffer (value unspecified: 'a certain percentage')
USDS trading price of buffer assets 'close to 1 USD per USDS' (tolerance unspecified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism attaches to the obligation to maintain the buffer; the Peg Stability Module enforces the peg itself, not the buffer's size, and the Surplus Buffer is a loss-absorption backstop rather than an actor-level consequence.

assessments.title: Application To Prime Agents
assessments.quote: Each Prime Agent investing a portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio must maintain, with respect to its portion of same, the percentage of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8). By ensuring that every Prime Agent maintains these levels, Sky as a whole remains compliant with the required thresholds of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain ASC and Demand Absorption Buffer percentages on their Collateral Portfolio portion, per the cross-referenced minimum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Prime Agents), the portion (their Sky Collateral Portfolio share), and the metrics (ASC and Demand Absorption Buffer). The operative percentages are delegated by cross-reference to A.3.3.2.2 and are not stated in this text.
metrics: Percentage of Actively Stabilizing Collateral specified in A.3.3.2.2 (Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral), applied to the Prime's portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio
Percentage of Demand Absorption Buffer specified in A.3.3.2.2, applied to the Prime's portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review Prime compliance with the referenced minimums, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can quantify consequences for breaches. Neither is quantified for this specific rule, and escalation depends on review being triggered.

assessments.title: Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Actively Stabilizing Collateral is collateral that actively supports the peg of USDS by market-making and providing buy support at a price close to 1 USD per USDS. The implementation of the Asset Liability Management framework specifies the downside spread that is allowed for collateral to qualify as Actively Stabilizing Collateral. See [A.3.3.2 - Implementation](bf1a1991-1c2b-457c-b1ca-6147049e93c5).
assessments.description: Defines Actively Stabilizing Collateral as collateral that market-makes and buys USDS near 1 USD, with the spread deferred to implementation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a conceptual definition using judgment language ("close to 1 USD") and delegates the allowed downside spread to A.3.3.2 with no value stated here. A defender could reasonably argue it imposes no binding threshold on its own.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is definitional and imposes no operative duty. Its qualification consequences sit in the separate A.3.3.2 minimum-ASC rule, which is not cited here, and no mechanism in this text reaches the definition itself.

assessments.title: Application To Sky Core
assessments.quote: While its legacy ALM infrastructure is being transferred to Prime Agents, Sky Core manages the portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio not deployed by Prime Agents ("Sky Core Collateral Portfolio"). During this transitional period, Sky Core allocates the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral as specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf).
assessments.description: During the ALM transition, Sky Core allocates its non-Prime collateral portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral per a cross-referenced rule.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation to allocate to Actively Stabilizing Collateral is real, but this paragraph gives no threshold, share, or cadence and defers all operative parameters to A.3.3.2.6. A defender could argue the rule has no concrete content in this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism in the catalog reaches Sky Core's own allocation decision: penalties and conservatorship target Primes and Operational Agents, and the Surplus Buffer and SKY Backstop respond only to realized losses rather than the allocation breach itself. The duty is effectively self-enforced by Sky Core.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event
assessments.quote: In addition to the requirement for Prime Agents to hold a certain percentage of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral and the Demand Absorption Buffer, Prime Agents have special responsibilities in extraordinary situations where the stability of the peg is threatened. The definition of these events and the obligations for Prime Agents are specified in the implementation of the framework. See [A.3.3.2 - Implementation](bf1a1991-1c2b-457c-b1ca-6147049e93c5).
assessments.description: Defers Prime Agents' extraordinary peg-defense responsibilities and the definition of peg-threat events to a cross-referenced implementation section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines no events, thresholds, or obligations; it states that both 'are specified in the implementation of the framework' and points to A.3.3.2. Nothing in the text itself can be checked for compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph creates no operative duty, and the cited implementation UUID is a cross-reference rather than an enforcement mechanism. Peg Stability Module applies to peg deviation generally, not to this paragraph's undefined Prime obligations.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management Rental
assessments.quote: To allow the Asset Liability Management obligation of Prime Agents to be satisfied in the most efficient way possible, Prime Agents may enter into Asset Liability Management Rentals between each other, as specified in the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive. This allows one Prime Agent to hold a greater amount of Actively Stabilizing Collateral to offset another Prime Agent holding a lesser amount. Thus, the overall level of Actively Stabilizing Collateral is unaffected but the Actively Stabilizing Collateral can be held by a Prime Agent that is able to more efficiently hold it.
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agents to rent Actively Stabilizing Collateral obligations between each other to reallocate holdings efficiently.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is permissive and defers the operative mechanics to the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive, which is not included. The only verifiable condition is that total Actively Stabilizing Collateral is unchanged, with no thresholds, caps, or cadence.
metrics: Total Actively Stabilizing Collateral across Prime Agents is unaffected by rentals
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a permission, and no penalty, liquidation, or emergency mechanism reaches a rental violation. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls would apply.

assessments.title: All Asset Liability Management Obligations Are Rented Together
assessments.quote: When Asset Liability Management obligations are rented, the associated obligations with regard to Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Demand Absorption Buffer, and Peg Defense Events are all transferred together.
assessments.description: Requires that rented Asset Liability Management obligations transfer together, covering Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Demand Absorption Buffer, and Peg Defense Events.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names three concrete obligation categories and a binary all-or-nothing transfer, but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or mechanics for how or when the transfer occurs or who is bound. A defender could argue it is definitional and imposes no separately verifiable duty.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, on-chain, or emergency mechanism watches whether obligations transfer together during a rental, so the only backstop is the catch-all Reports of Misalignment process, which is weak on its own.

assessments.title: Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Prime Agents must maintain at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to keep at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Prime Agents), a numeric floor (5%), and a verifiable portfolio share against the Collateral Portfolio. A third party could check compliance from the text alone, though no measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: at least 5% of Collateral Portfolio held in Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess Prime compliance with a published outcome and penalty assessment, and the Penalty Mechanisms can attach to a shortfall. No consequence is quantified for this specific 5% floor, and firing depends on the review being triggered, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the sum of (1) Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Defines Actively Stabilizing Collateral as the sum of Resting and Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives an exact additive formula for a defined term, but it is a definition rather than an obligation. It states no threshold, valuation method, or actor duty, and the two components are not quantified here, so a defender could argue it does not bind anyone.
metrics: Actively Stabilizing Collateral = Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral + Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional statement with no operative duty. No penalty, liquidation, peg-arbitrage, or review mechanism attaches to the definition itself; enforcement would only attach to the downstream minimum-ASC rule that uses it.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements.
assessments.description: Requires Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral to provide USDS buy support at or above 0.999 USD.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core price floor (0.999 USD per USDS, a 10bps downside spread) is quantified and checkable. Eligibility depends on undefined 'redemption price and transparency requirements' that are not specified here, and the required buy-support quantity is not stated.
metrics: buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS
10 bps downside spread
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a Prime's failure to maintain resting buy support, since it is a Minimum ASC component. No consequence is quantified for this specific price-floor obligation, and the PSM (0082c12d) only arbitrages peg deviation rather than enforcing resting bids.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines how Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is calculated, as a sum of six named USDC and Cash Stablecoin balances across PSMs, Curve, GUNI and Uniswap.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The calculation is an explicit sum of six enumerated components, which makes the metric verifiable. Gaps remain: "Cash Stablecoins" is an input defined elsewhere with no value here, and there is no measurement cadence or stated threshold.
metrics: Resting ASC = sum of: USDC in LitePSM; USDC in PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; USDC in GUNI 0.05%; Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap (paired with USDS)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can check whether the reported ASC calculation is correct, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can follow from a miscalculation that breaches the Minimum ASC. The penalty magnitude is not quantified for this calculation rule.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote:
Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins.

Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral:

1. The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles;
2. The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and
3. The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels.
assessments.description: Defines Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral as convertible Cash Stablecoins meeting verifiability, 15-minute conversion, and automated-trigger requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 15-minute conversion window is a concrete numeric threshold, but the automation trigger depends on undefined "specified levels", "normal market conditions" and "reputable APIs or oracles" are not defined, so key operative criteria are delegated.
metrics: Conversion into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions
Conversion triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels (levels not stated)
Assets verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles (no source criteria stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Latent ASC is part of Minimum ASC, so Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a failure to meet the conversion or verifiability requirements. No consequence is quantified for this specific rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the 15-minute conversion.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral as a sum of cash stablecoin exposures across listed protocols, with discretionary exposure limits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The calculation names six concrete components and is additive, but it gives no numeric values for the limits, which are left to Core Executor Agents' discretion. The 'cash stablecoins' input and the 'limitations' magnitude are undefined.
metrics: Latent ASC = sum of Cash Stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS), Uniswap (not paired with USDS), SparkLend, Aave, Morpho, and Prime ALM Proxy
Exposure limits on Latent ASC protocols or pools may be imposed by Core Executor Agents with Core Council Risk Advisor consultation, with no stated size or timing
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph defines a measurement and a discretionary power to cap exposures, but no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain constraint attaches to misreporting the sum or ignoring a limit.

assessments.title: Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Caps Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral at 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 25% ceiling and the ratio base (ASC) are explicit and checkable. The regulated actor is not named, and no measurement cadence or verification method is stated; Latent ASC is defined only in the parent context.
metrics: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral ≤ 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (A.1.14.2.10) and the Penalty Mechanisms (A.3.2.2.7.2) could plausibly reach a Prime that exceeds the latent-ASC cap, as they do for the sibling Minimum ASC rule. No consequence is quantified for this specific ceiling, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.quote: In the near term there will be no penalties for Prime Agents for failing to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Instead, failures to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral will be detected and reported as specified in [A.3.3.2.2.2.1 - Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement](b74ba49a-de9e-4c4c-866c-b04d9dd208f7).
assessments.description: States that Prime Agents face no penalties near-term for missing the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral, with failures detected and reported under a referenced doc.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a concrete outcome (no penalties) but gives no duration for 'near term' and delegates the detection and reporting process entirely to another document. No threshold, cadence, or deadline appears here.
metrics: 'In the near term' (no defined duration or end date)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The paragraph expressly disclaims penalties, and the referenced reporting doc (b74ba49a) provides detection and reporting only, not a consequence. The catch-all Reports of Misalignment would be the only backstop.

assessments.title: Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to build a tool detecting Prime Agent ASC shortfalls and report each violation within 24 hours to named parties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24-hour reporting deadline and the five named recipients are concrete and checkable. However, the tool's build deadline is only "in the near term," and the violation trigger depends on the Minimum ASC threshold defined elsewhere, not stated here.
metrics: Each violation by a Prime Agent reported within 24 hours
Reported to the Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, the Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for the Prime Agent, and the Prime Agent
Tool to automatically detect failures to maintain Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (developed "in the near term")
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The reports go to Core GovOps and the Core Facilitator, who can invoke the Penalty Mechanisms and escalate to conservatorship for capital-requirement breaches, so the detection plausibly feeds consequences. The paragraph does not quantify any penalty for failing to report, and the escalation requires a human to act on the report.

assessments.title: Near Term Exemption For Keel
assessments.quote: In the near term, due to limitations in the infrastructure on Solana, Keel is exempt from the requirement to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. This exemption will be removed in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management Framework.
assessments.description: Exempts Keel from the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement in the near term due to Solana infrastructure limits.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Keel) and the requirement it is exempt from are named, but the duration is judgment language ("near term", "future iteration") with no date, milestone, or removal criterion. No threshold or metric is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is an exemption that removes Keel from the Minimum ASC requirement, so no penalty, liquidation, or other mechanism reaches a violation; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Near Term Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive
assessments.quote: In the near term, Prime Agents are eligible for an Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive for fulfilling Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirements.
assessments.description: Makes Prime Agents eligible for an Actively Stabilizing Collateral incentive in the near term for meeting ASC requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states a real eligibility condition (fulfilling ASC requirements) but gives no incentive amount, no ASC threshold, and no defined meaning for 'near term'. Because 'eligible' is permissive and the requirements are not restated here, a defender could argue it does not yet bind anyone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The incentive is tied to meeting ASC requirements, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach ASC shortfalls that would forfeit eligibility. No consequence is quantified for this paragraph itself, so the rating stays at mid.

assessments.title: Calculation
assessments.quote:
The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is calculated on a per block basis as follows:

`Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.1 - Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral](e0b95f42-2021-44ab-a979-491a113ccbc1), and SOFR is specified in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.3 - Secured Overnight Financing Rate](2edd1333-6ca6-4c10-9d71-80b85d4a4265).
assessments.description: Defines a per-block incentive payment for holding Actively Stabilizing Collateral, calculated as eligible collateral times the spread between a base rate and SOFR.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula and per-block cadence are exact, but the Base Rate is never defined in the paragraph or linked. Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral and SOFR are delegated to other documents, and no value is given for either in this text.
metrics: Calculated on a per block basis
Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a payment incentive, not a compliance constraint, and no penalty, liquidation, or escalation attaches to misstating or failing to pay it. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops could reach it.

assessments.title: Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.quote: The Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the lesser of (1) the Prime Agent’s Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) the Prime Agent’s Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8).
assessments.description: Defines Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral as the lesser of a Prime Agent's actual ASC and its Minimum ASC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is exact, a lesser-of minimum of two named quantities, with a defined actor. The Minimum ASC magnitude is delegated to the referenced section A.3.3.2.2 and is not stated here, so the threshold is not verifiable from this text alone.
metrics: Eligible ASC = min(Prime Agent's Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Prime Agent's Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. This is a definitional calculation with no consequence attached to its own output. Any consequence would flow through the parent Minimum ASC rule and its enforcement, which this paragraph does not itself invoke.

assessments.title: Payment
assessments.quote: The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is paid on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.description: Specifies that the Actively Stabilizing Collateral incentive is paid monthly as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Gives a concrete cadence (monthly) and a named process (Monthly Settlement Cycle), but the incentive amount, eligibility, and payment deadline are not stated here and must be defined elsewhere.
metrics: Payment cadence: monthly
Payment occurs within the Monthly Settlement Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a payment-timing statement with no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain mechanism tied to failing to pay or to the underlying collateral rule; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: Every Prime Agent must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of their required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.description: Requires each Prime Agent to hold a Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of its required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a 25% ratio applied to a defined base (required Actively Stabilizing Collateral) for a defined actor (every Prime Agent). The paragraph gives no measurement cadence, no definition of what counts toward the buffer, and no test date.
metrics: Demand Absorption Buffer ≥ 25% of required Actively Stabilizing Collateral, per Prime Agent
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a Prime that under-funds this buffer, as they do for the parallel Minimum ASC rule. No consequence is quantified for this specific buffer, and no on-chain mechanism enforces it, so the rating stops at mid.

assessments.title: Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.quote: To further stabilize USDS during periods of excess supply, Prime Agents must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer (DAB), a subset of ASC consisting of USDS that is for sale for at most 1.001 USD per USDS. The Demand Absorption Buffer includes USDS or DAI in PSMs. The Demand Absorption Buffer can also be fulfilled by autonomous systems that generate USDS dynamically through the allocation as needed.
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer of USDS offered for sale at no more than 1.001 USD.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 1.001 USD price ceiling is a concrete numeric threshold, but no minimum buffer size or funding amount is stated, so the core magnitude of the obligation is missing. Eligible sources ('USDS or DAI in PSMs', autonomous systems 'as needed') are also loosely defined, with no measurement cadence.
metrics: DAB offered for sale at most 1.001 USD per USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps could reach a missing or non-compliant buffer, and the Penalty Mechanisms could apply quantified penalties to the Prime. Neither is quantified for this specific buffer rule, and no on-chain mechanism enforces the Prime's obligation to hold the buffer.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Demand Absorption Buffer Requirement
assessments.quote: Penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer will be specified in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management framework.
assessments.description: States that penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer are deferred to a future framework iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is an explicit stub: it names no penalty, threshold, amount, or deadline and defers all content to a future iteration. Nothing is verifiable or complying-with today.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No penalty is defined in this text. The paragraph refers only to a future specification, and none of the catalogued mechanisms (Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship, Liquidation Penalty) is cited here or reached by the stated rule. Only the catch-all backstop would apply, so the rating is weak.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event Definition
assessments.quote: A Peg Defense Event is a situation where the average price of USDS on DEXes that are connected via LayerZero falls below 0.999 USD per USDS.
assessments.description: Defines a Peg Defense Event as average USDS price on LayerZero-connected DEXes falling below 0.999 USD.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is a numeric threshold (0.999 USD) on a named metric (average DEX price). The averaging window, sampling cadence, and the set of 'LayerZero-connected' DEXes are left undefined, so the core test is quantified but its supporting inputs are not.
metrics: Average price of USDS on LayerZero-connected DEXes
Threshold: below 0.999 USD per USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph imposes no obligation or consequence itself. The Peg Stability Module makes peg deviation arbitrageable on-chain, which plausibly reaches the below-peg condition this event describes, but no consequence is tied specifically to the event being declared.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event Alert Tool
assessments.quote: The Core Council Risk Advisor, in consultation with Core GovOps, will develop a tool that calculates the average price of USDS on DEXes that are connected via LayerZero in real time. This tool must be made available to all Prime Agents and functionality must be developed that notifies Sky and Prime Agents in real time when a Peg Defense Event has been triggered.
assessments.description: Requires Core Council Risk Advisor and Core GovOps to build a real-time LayerZero DEX USDS average-price tool and peg-defense alerts.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actors, the metric (average USDS price across LayerZero-connected DEXes), and the real-time requirement are named, but there is no averaging method, DEX list, deviation threshold, or delivery deadline. The Peg Defense Event trigger is defined elsewhere and not given here.
metrics: average price of USDS on DEXes connected via LayerZero, calculated in real time
tool made available to all Prime Agents
real-time notification to Sky and Prime Agents when a Peg Defense Event is triggered
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a development deliverable with no stated consequence for late or missing delivery, and no listed mechanism (penalties, Emergency Response System, artifact review) is tied to this obligation. The misalignment and adjudication catch-alls alone make it weak.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: In a Peg Defense Event, all Prime Agents must immediately begin to buy USDS at a rate of at least 6.25% of their Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement every six (6) hours. The six (6) hour periods run consecutively from the onset of the Peg Defense Event, and the Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement is measured as of the start of each period. Each Prime Agent is responsible for monitoring its Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement and maintaining sufficient capacity to satisfy this obligation for the duration of the Peg Defense Event.
assessments.description: Requires all Prime Agents in a Peg Defense Event to buy USDS at 6.25% of their ASC requirement every six hours.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a 6.25% rate per six-hour consecutive period, measured against the ASC requirement at each period's start. The trigger (Peg Defense Event) is defined elsewhere, and the text does not say what happens if a Prime lacks capacity to meet the obligation.
metrics: Buy USDS at a rate of at least 6.25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement
Every six (6) hours
Six-hour periods run consecutively from onset of Peg Defense Event
ASC requirement measured as of the start of each period
Obligation begins immediately upon Peg Defense Event
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Risk-Capital Incident Response (12b7d480) plausibly reach a Prime that fails the ASC-linked purchase obligation during a peg event. The paragraph does not quantify a consequence for this specific rule, so it is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Alternatives For Satisfying Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: Peg Defense can be performed through a combination of (1) selling other types of collateral for USDS, or (2) by using USDS, or generating new USDS via the Allocation System, that is then used as collateral to borrow other types of assets (e.g. USDC or USDT on Aave) and buy USDS with it.
assessments.description: Permits Peg Defense to combine selling other collateral for USDS with borrowing against USDS to buy USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names two concrete peg-defense methods but gives no thresholds, amounts, timing, or criteria for choosing or combining them. Its permissive wording ('can be performed') also leaves it unclear whether it imposes any obligation at all.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is permissive and specifies no violation mode, and no cited mechanism (such as the Peg Stability Module) directly reaches how peg defense methods are combined.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failure To Satisfy Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.quote: Penalties for failing to fulfill the Peg Defense Obligations will be specified in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management framework.
assessments.description: States that penalties for failing Peg Defense Obligations are deferred to a future framework iteration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is an explicit stub with no thresholds, penalty amounts, or operative criteria; it defers all content to a future iteration. Nothing is verifiable today.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph itself specifies no penalty; the only general backstops (Reports of Misalignment, Adjudication) are catch-alls and cannot establish enforcement for this rule. Peg Stability Module self-enforcement covers peg deviation generally but not penalties for failing Peg Defense Obligations.

assessments.title: Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules
assessments.quote: Pursuant to [A.3.3.1.4 - Application To Sky Core](6e050b66-0bc8-43f1-b32d-2220c9df466b), Sky Core manages the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio by allocating capital to the Lite PSM (see [A.3.3.2.7.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module](39473e1a-63f8-433b-a850-08f53b2dcf02)).
assessments.description: Requires Sky Core to allocate capital from its Collateral Portfolio to the Lite Peg Stability Module.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (Sky Core), a controlled system (the Collateral Portfolio), and a target (Lite PSM), so the obligation is identifiable. It gives no amount, percentage, cadence, or criteria for the allocation, so compliance could be argued either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Peg Stability Module (0082c12d) self-enforces peg deviation, not Sky Core's allocation decision, and no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain check reaches a failure to allocate. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module
assessments.quote: Control of the Lite PSM is being transitioned to Grove. Until this transition is complete, the Lite PSM continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage the Lite PSM as an ASC asset pursuant to the rules defined in this Article.
assessments.description: Transfers control of the Lite PSM from Sky Core to Grove and sets interim Sky Core control under A.3.3.2.6.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names actors and a cross-referenced rule set (A.3.3.2.6), but gives no threshold, deadline, or criterion for when the transition is complete. Whether Grove's post-transition obligations are met depends on undefined terms and the external Article rules.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) allow pre-authorized executive intervention when security rules are violated or threatened, which could plausibly reach unauthorized control of the Lite PSM. The consequence is not quantified for this transfer rule, and the PSM's on-chain swap mechanism does not enforce who holds control.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Buffer Definition
assessments.quote: `buf` is a fixed-sized amount of pre-minted Dai which LitePSM is designed to maintain in most situations. Note, however, that when a user calls `buyGem`, the amount of Dai available can be temporarily larger than `buf`.
assessments.description: Defines the LitePSM buf as a fixed-size pool of pre-minted Dai that the module aims to maintain.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Names the buf parameter and calls it fixed-sized, but gives no amount, unit, or formula. "Maintain in most situations" and "temporarily larger" are judgment language with no threshold or duration, so compliance is arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The LitePSM is an on-chain fixed-rate swap module, so buffer depletion limits swap capacity and the peg is arbitraged by the contract itself. No quantified consequence attaches to buf deviating from its definition, so this is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Values
assessments.quote:
The current values of the Lite Peg Stability Module parameters are:

- `tin`: 0%
- `tout`: 0%
- DC-IAM `line`: 10,000,000,000 DAI
- DC-IAM `gap`: 800,000,000 DAI
- DC-IAM `ttl`: 43,200 seconds
- `buf`: 800,000,000 DAI
- Authorized Parties: None
assessments.description: Lists the current numeric parameter values (fees, DC-IAM line, gap, ttl, buffer) for the Lite Peg Stability Module.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Every parameter has an exact value, so compliance can be checked against the live settings. It is a descriptive snapshot with no stated update cadence, no owner for changing the values, and no operative obligation beyond reporting them.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Modification
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, may recommend changes to any of the parameters specified in the subdocuments of [A.3.3.2.7.1.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Definitions](9196786a-18b6-4dea-b4e2-852090371dd7). These changes will be subject to an Executive Vote through the Operational Weekly Cycle.
assessments.description: Routes recommended changes to Lite PSM parameters through the Core Facilitator, Risk Advisor consultation, and a weekly Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and the approval path (Executive Vote via the Operational Weekly Cycle) are named, but no thresholds, criteria, or limits govern when a change may be recommended. "May recommend" is discretionary and the parameters are delegated to a subdocument.
metrics: Changes are approved through an Executive Vote in the Operational Weekly Cycle
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Executive Vote is a governance approval step, not an enforcer distinct from the actors, and no penalty, emergency, or on-chain mechanism reaches the violation of making unapproved parameter changes.

assessments.title: Andromeda
assessments.quote: Historically, Andromeda balanced Sky Core’s Cash Stablecoin liquidity by allocating excess into low-risk treasury strategies and replenishing shortages. Control of the Andromeda RWA Arranged Structure is currently being transitioned to Grove. Until the transition to Grove is complete, Andromeda continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements defined in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage Andromeda as a non-ASC asset within its Collateral Portfolio, subject to JRC requirements. Andromeda is not currently operational and its debt ceiling has been reduced to zero.
assessments.description: Describes legacy Andromeda RWA control transitioning from Sky Core to Grove, with Andromeda's debt ceiling set to zero.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives one concrete value (debt ceiling reduced to zero) but its operative obligations are delegated: pre-transition Andromeda is 'subject to' an external ALM rules section, and post-transition it is subject to unspecified 'JRC requirements'. No transition deadline, metric, or threshold is stated.
metrics: Andromeda debt ceiling reduced to zero
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is largely descriptive and its binding obligations are delegated to referenced rules. The zero debt ceiling is an on-chain constraint, but no catalogued mechanism governs it, and the JRC and ALM requirements it cites are not enforced by any mechanism tied to this text.

assessments.title: Other RWA Offboarding
assessments.quote: Other than Andromeda, all old RWA exposure that was added before Endgame must stay for as long as necessary, and optimized for yield if possible. When it is possible, the Core Facilitator should take action to wind down and offboard all such Legacy RWA. Governance actions related to optimizations, wind down and offboardings can be done directly in Executive Votes with no prior Governance Poll needed.
assessments.description: Directs Core Facilitator to hold, optimize, and wind down legacy RWA exposure (except Andromeda) and permits executive-vote approval without a poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative duties rely on undefined judgment terms such as "as long as necessary," "if possible," and "when it is possible," with no thresholds, deadlines, or metrics. The actor (Core Facilitator) and procedural route (Executive Votes) are named, so the obligation is identifiable but not objectively verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found: no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, liquidation, emergency spells, artifact review) reaches the Core Facilitator's wind-down duty, and the only backstop is the generic misalignment/adjudication process.

assessments.title: Agent Owner For Arranged Structures
assessments.quote: Arranged Structures must have an Agent owner. The Agent owner assigns instructions to the Arranged Structure on behalf of Sky, and determines if and how other Agents can access the Conduit of the Arranged Structure.
assessments.description: Requires every Arranged Structure to have an Agent owner who instructs it on Sky's behalf and controls other Agents' access to its Conduit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The existence requirement is objectively checkable: each Arranged Structure must name an Agent owner. The owner's access-control role is stated only as discretion ("determines if and how"), with no criteria, thresholds, or cadence.
metrics: Each Arranged Structure must have an Agent owner
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess whether an Agent-owned structure and its access decisions comply, with penalty machinery available if findings are adverse. Consequences are not quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Arrangers
assessments.quote: This Section defines procedures related to Arrangers, Ecosystem Actors that assist in the design and operation of Arranged Structures. Every Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger responsible for conducting ongoing reporting. All aspects of this relationship, including the Arranger's duties, must be defined in this Section.
assessments.description: Requires every Arranged Structure to have a designated Arranger responsible for ongoing reporting, with duties deferred to this section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete: each Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger, which can be checked. However, 'ongoing reporting' has no cadence, content, or threshold, and the duties are deferred to 'this Section' without being stated, so a defender could argue the rule does not yet bind.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, liquidation, conservatorship, or other mechanism is tied to Arranger designation or reporting; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, which are weak on their own.

assessments.title: Introduction
assessments.quote:
Arrangers are Ecosystem Actors who specialize in sourcing, negotiating, structuring, and reporting on Real World Assets, as well as maintaining and monitoring the underlying Arranged Structures used by the Sky Protocol. The Arrangers manage a restricted function on the Arranged Structure Conduit that allows them to send assets onwards to the predetermined blockchain account of the Arranged Structure.

Arrangers are generally prohibited from occupying any position where they could cause damage or loss to the Sky Ecoystem, notwithstanding delays or inconveniences.

After the Arranged Structures are established and assets are allocated, Arrangers must not have the capability to operate or influence the legal and operational structure’s asset operations in any manner that could cause significant harm or losses to the stability of USDS.

Arrangers are directly approved by SKY voters, and all LRA collateral exposure must be structured by an approved Arranger.
assessments.description: Defines Arrangers' role in sourcing and monitoring RWA structures, limits their control over asset operations, and requires LRA exposure to route through approved Arrangers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Arrangers), a restricted Conduit function, and a binary approval requirement for LRA exposure. Its operative limits ('generally prohibited', 'significant harm or losses', 'could cause damage') are judgment language with no thresholds, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Arrangers are approved and implicitly overseen by SKY voters, but no penalty, conservatorship, insurance repricing, or emergency mechanism is tied to these prohibitions. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, so none found.

assessments.title: Onboarding And Offboarding of Arrangers
assessments.quote: When they deem it necessary, the Core Facilitator may initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Arrangers. The list of current active Arrangers is maintained in [A.3.4.3.2.1 - List Of Active Arrangers](b8791aaa-84b7-4012-8a4f-053595ec232a).
assessments.description: Lets the Core Facilitator initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Arrangers at its discretion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: A real process exists (Core Facilitator initiates a Governance Poll, with the active list maintained in A.3.4.3.2.1), but the trigger is purely discretionary ("when they deem it necessary") with no criteria, cadence, or thresholds. A defender could plausibly argue the rule imposes no binding obligation at all.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule only authorizes a governance poll; no penalty, conservatorship, on-chain control, or emergency mechanism attaches to a failure to onboard or offboard Arrangers appropriately.

assessments.title: Reporting And Stress Test Requirements
assessments.quote:
Arrangers must publish monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure they have arranged.

Every six (6) months, Arrangers are also required to publish a stress test analysis that demonstrates how the structures would perform under historical financial crisis scenarios and other hypothetical scenarios.

The Core Facilitator must periodically fund independent Ecosystem Actors to review and verify the quality and the results of the stress tests. Should an independent review produce an unfavorable result, the Core Facilitator must propose a Governance Poll for warning, temporarily deactivating, or permanently offboarding the Arranger and/or the Asset Managers connected to the discovered issue.

To be considered compliant, Arrangers’ monthly reports must satisfy the requirements of one of the following documents:

- [A.3.4.3.3.1 - Monthly Arranger Report Requirements](7b902bb1-68b4-477d-a575-29aaa02e9e7b)
- [A.3.4.3.3.2 - Access To Accounts](47eedd39-5bb9-492f-a4aa-9405bb5d196f)
assessments.description: Requires Arrangers to publish monthly structure reports and six-monthly stress tests, subject to independent review and possible governance action.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The monthly reporting and six-month stress test cadences are concrete, but report content is delegated to two cross-referenced documents. Independent review is funded only 'periodically', and 'unfavorable result' is undefined, so compliance is not fully checkable from the text.
metrics: Arrangers must publish monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure
Stress test analysis published every six (6) months
Reports must satisfy one of A.3.4.3.3.1 or A.3.4.3.3.2
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph's Governance Poll path (warning, deactivation, offboarding) is not a catalog mechanism and fires only if the Core Facilitator funds a review that finds an unfavorable result, which depends on 'periodically' being met. Monthly reporting lapses have no citable trigger, and the cross-referenced UUIDs define compliance standards rather than enforcement.

assessments.title: Monthly Arranger Report Requirements
assessments.quote:
The following information must be included in the monthly Arranger report. Each item must be reported for at least the start and end date of the reporting period. If these dates fall on days when markets are closed, the first business day after the start date and the last business day before the end date may be used instead.

- Cash balance.
- Cash income over the reporting period. Any income over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Cash expenses over the reporting period. Any expense over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Market value of publicly traded equities, ETFs, and mutual funds.
- Market value (the closing price) of publicly traded debt securities. Debt securities that are investment grade and less than 12 months from maturity may alternatively be reported at cost basis + linearly recognizing scheduled interest income.
- A valuation for illiquid or privately traded assets. This should utilize a valuation from a reputable third party with relevant expertise or follow a well-defined methodology that is explained in detail in the report.
- CUSIPs, date of purchase, date of maturity, coupon, cost basis, and face value of all publicly traded debt securities in the portfolio for the last day of the reporting period.
- USDS inflows from the Sky Protocol during the reporting period.
- Total repayments on-chain to the Sky Protocol either to a vault or for surplus. If repayments are derived from multiple sources, they should be broken out into line items for each source.
- Vault debt to the Sky Protocol.
- Copies of original statements for all bank, brokerage, exchange, custodial, or other accounts. The Arranger may redact the names for non-Arranger service providers if and only if that is a requirement of confidentiality agreements with the non-Arranger service providers.

The Core Facilitator must publicly confirm on the Sky Forum that they have reviewed the original account documentation and verified that it supports the Arranger’s summary.

assessments.title: Current Value

The current value of the Surplus Buffer can be calculated using the Vat contract, Sky’s central accounting contract, located on the Ethereum Mainnet at `0x35D1b3F3D7966A1DFe207aa4514C12a259A0492B`. The current value of the Surplus Buffer is the difference between:

1. The assets of the Vow contract obtained by calling the `dai` function on the Vat contract with the address of the Vow contract, and
2. The liabilities of the Vow contract obtained by calling the `sin` function on the Vat contract with the address of the Vow contract.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can modify the `kbump`, `hop`, and `burn` parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. LSEV2-SKY-A-USDS rewardsDuration should always match the value of the `hop` parameter without requiring prior governance authorization.

The Core Facilitator must modify all parameters of the Smart Burn Engine as necessary to implement the allocation specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121). Such a modification can be enacted either by proposing it for inclusion in an Executive Vote pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, or by executing it directly through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds.

Except as provided in the preceding paragraphs, modifications to the parameters of the Smart Burn Engine require a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.
