assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) enables a designated, Governance-whitelisted Operator to adjust the Kicker Lot Size (`kbump`), the SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`), and the Splitter Interval (`hop`) parameters of the Smart Burn Engine, as specified in [A.3.5.2.2.1.2 - Kicker Lot Size Parameter](fc9cece1-84bf-4133-a2ef-ef2182a23a35), [A.3.5.2.1.1.2 - SKY Accumulation Percentage Parameter](e16d6215-c2f1-4140-affd-30e52a17fd43), and [A.3.5.2.1.1.1 - Splitter Interval Parameter](39a67e65-33f0-4f2c-917d-efff544cf5ab). Adjustments are governed by the SBE-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance.

The SBE-BEAM Operator can raise or lower these parameters within the bounds set by Sky Governance. Those bounds are one-sided guardrails on the rate of accumulation: the Kicker Lot Size cannot be set above `maxKbump`, the Splitter Interval cannot be set below `minHop`, and the combined throughput, expressed as the Kicker Lot Size divided by the Splitter Interval, cannot exceed `maxRate`. The rate of accumulation therefore cannot be raised beyond the maximum that Sky Governance has sanctioned, while no corresponding bound limits reductions to it. The SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`) is not subject to these bounds, which limit only the rate of accumulation, and the only technical constraint on it is the maximum specified in [A.3.5.2.4.4 - Technical Limitations](42ea8a7b-fb28-455e-8038-5fcf25250f17). The `tau` parameter separately requires a minimum interval between operations, applying to any operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the parameters. The SBE-BEAM holds the following bounding parameters: (i) `maxKbump`, (ii) `minHop`, (iii) `maxRate`, and (iv) `tau`. The bases on which these parameters may be modified are specified in [A.3.5.2.3 - Modification](499570de-9fae-4009-be34-c3330266030a).
assessments.description: Lets a whitelisted Operator adjust Smart Burn Engine kbump, burn and hop parameters within Governance-set bounds on accumulation rate.

The burn parameter is bounded only by a maximum set elsewhere.

assessments.quote: The `maxKbump` parameter defines the maximum permitted value of the `kbump` parameter when set using the SBE-BEAM. The SBE-BEAM can set `kbump` to any value at or below `maxKbump`, whether that raises or lowers the current value, but cannot set `kbump` above `maxKbump`.

No numeric value for maxKbump or kbump is stated here, and the cadence of changes is not specified, so the parameter magnitudes sit elsewhere.

The cap is a self-limiting bound on the SBE-BEAM's own parameter setting, so it is self-enforcement with no named enforcer, penalty, or on-chain check described in the text. The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is only an economic loss backstop and does not reach a violation of this ceiling at the actor level.

assessments.title: Min Hop Definition
assessments.quote: The `minHop` parameter defines the minimum permitted value of the `hop` parameter when set using the SBE-BEAM. The SBE-BEAM can set `hop` to any value at or above `minHop`, whether that raises or lowers the current value, but cannot set `hop` below `minHop`.

assessments.title: Tau Definition
assessments.quote:
The `tau` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the SBE-BEAM.

A SBE-BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once a SBE-BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent SBE-BEAM operation can be performed. This interval applies to every operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the affected parameters.

The tau value itself is defined elsewhere and not stated, so the magnitude cannot be checked from this text alone.

The paragraph does not state that the delay is contract-enforced and the consequence is unquantified for this rule, so the rating is mid.

The bounding parameters set by Sky Governance for the SBE-BEAM are as follows:

- The value of the `maxKbump` parameter is 12,000 USDS.
- The value of the `minHop` parameter is 550 seconds.
- The value of the `maxRate` parameter is 350,000,000 USDS per year.
- The value of the `tau` parameter is 1,800 seconds.

Such changes are proposed by the Core Facilitator, on behalf of the Core Council and in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor.

assessments.title: Technical Limitations
assessments.quote:
The SBE-BEAM enforces technical limitations, including the following, that apply independently of the bounding parameters set by Sky Governance. An attempt to use the SBE-BEAM in a manner that exceeds these limitations will revert.

The `hop` parameter cannot be set higher than five (5) years. This limitation prevents the Smart Burn Engine from being placed in a state in which its reward stream — the staking rewards funded by the non-burned portion of surplus and streamed out over the Splitter Interval — can no longer be revived through the SBE-BEAM.

The `burn` parameter cannot be set higher than 100%, the point at which the entire surplus is directed to SKY accumulation. A higher value would cause the Smart Burn Engine to halt.

The `kbump` parameter must be set to a whole multiple of `RAY` (10²⁷). A value that is not an exact multiple of `RAY` will revert, ensuring the Kicker Lot Size is always expressed in the protocol's standard fixed-point precision.
assessments.description: Sets technical caps on SBE-BEAM parameters: hop at most five years, burn at most 100%, and kbump a whole multiple of RAY.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Each limit is a concrete, checkable value: hop is capped at five years, burn at 100%, and kbump must be an exact multiple of 10^27. The text also states that violating attempts revert, so a third party could verify compliance from the text alone.

assessments.title: Operators

Changes to the `kbump` and `hop` parameters, and to their combined throughput, are limited by the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, and `maxRate` parameters, and every change is subject to the `tau` cadence. The `burn` parameter is not subject to the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, or `maxRate` bounds, which limit only the rate of accumulation, and the only technical constraint on it is the maximum specified in [A.3.5.2.4.4 - Technical Limitations](42ea8a7b-fb28-455e-8038-5fcf25250f17). The Operator can be changed by an Executive Vote.

metrics: Signing requirement of 4 of 6 signers for the Operator Multisig
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The multisig threshold is contract-enforced in principle, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph reaches this rule, so it is rated weak.

assessments.title: Operator Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.quote: The signers of the Operator Multisig must use the multisig to operate the SBE-BEAM in accordance with the instructions specified in [A.3.5.2.4.6 - Update Process](859e8e2f-61da-453f-91bb-f50f701149c8).
assessments.description: Requires Operator Multisig signers to use the multisig to operate the SBE-BEAM per the referenced Update Process instructions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Operator Multisig signers) and controlled system (SBE-BEAM) are defined, but the operative standard is delegated to an external 'Update Process' document, and no threshold, cadence, or metric appears in this text. Compliance depends on what the cross-referenced instructions say, which is not stated here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled review with penalty assessment that could reach Operators who misuse the multisig, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) allow pre-authorized freezes if operating security rules are violated. Neither is quantified for this specific rule, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Operator Multisig Modification
assessments.quote:
The signers can change the signers of the Operator Multisig so long as:

- there are exactly six (6) signers;
- exactly four (4) signers are required to execute transactions; and
- two (2) signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator, two (2) signers are controlled by Core GovOps, and two (2) signers are controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.
assessments.description: Constrains Operator Multisig signer changes to six signers, four required approvals, and a 2/2/2 split across Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, and Soter Labs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Signer count (6), approval threshold (4), and per-controller allocation (2/2/2) are all exact and checkable from the multisig's configuration. The only soft point is the undefined meaning of 'controlled by', but the numbers carry the obligation.

exactly four (4) signers required to execute transactions
two (2) signers controlled by the Core Facilitator
two (2) signers controlled by Core GovOps
two (2) signers controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells can freeze or pause the Smart Burn Engine if the multisig composition is changed in violation of security rules, and Core GovOps artifact review can assess the Operational GovOps signer allocation. Neither sets a quantified penalty for this specific rule, so the rating is mid.

assessments.title: Update Process
assessments.quote: The Smart Burn Engine parameters are managed by the SBE-BEAM Operator through the SBE-BEAM, as specified in the documents herein. The SBE-BEAM Operator's use of this authority must adhere to the requirements specified in [A.3.5.2.3 - Modification](499570de-9fae-4009-be34-c3330266030a).
assessments.description: Assigns management of Smart Burn Engine parameters to the SBE-BEAM Operator, subject to the Modification requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a defined actor (SBE-BEAM Operator) and system (SBE-BEAM) but gives no thresholds, bounds, or cadence. Compliance depends entirely on the referenced Modification section (A.3.5.2.3), so the operative criteria are delegated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The only UUID cited (499570de, A.3.5.2.3 Modification) is a requirements document, not an enforcement mechanism. The parent Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is a protocol-level loss absorber that does not police operator conduct, and no penalty, emergency spell, or artifact review is tied to this rule.

assessments.title: Recommendation By Core Council Risk Advisor
assessments.quote: A recommendation to modify the Smart Burn Engine parameters through the SBE-BEAM must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Core Council Risk Advisor. See [A.3.5.2.3 - Modification](499570de-9fae-4009-be34-c3330266030a).
assessments.description: Requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to post recommendations to modify Smart Burn Engine parameters via the SBE-BEAM on the Sky Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a defined actor (Core Council Risk Advisor), a concrete required step (posting to the Sky Forum), and a specific channel (SBE-BEAM), so compliance is verifiable. It sets no deadline, cadence, or content criteria for the recommendation, and the cross-referenced Modification section is not reproduced here.
metrics: Recommendation to modify SBE parameters must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Core Council Risk Advisor
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, artifact review, or on-chain mechanism is tied to a missed or improper forum posting; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops would apply.

assessments.title: Agreement By Core Facilitator
assessments.quote: Before a recommended change is executed, the Core Facilitator must post to the Sky Forum to indicate its agreement with the recommendation.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to post agreement on the Sky Forum before executing a recommended Smart Burn Engine change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Core Facilitator), the action (post agreement on the Sky Forum), and the sequencing (before execution) are concrete and checkable from a forum record. However, the text sets no content requirements for the agreement, no deadline before execution, and no defined forum thread or channel.
metrics: Agreement must be posted to the Sky Forum before the recommended change is executed
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, emergency, or review mechanism in the catalog watches this forum-posting duty; Emergency Spells and the Emergency Response System target security violations, not a missing pre-execution forum post, so only the catch-all backstop applies.

assessments.title: Execution By Operator
assessments.quote: Once the Core Facilitator has agreed to a recommended change, the Operator prepares and executes the change through the SBE-BEAM. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs.
assessments.description: Requires the Operator to prepare and execute agreed Smart Burn Engine changes through the SBE-BEAM, optionally simulating inputs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors (Operator, Core Facilitator) and a controlled system (SBE-BEAM) with ordered steps, but gives no thresholds, deadlines, or verification requirements. Simulation is optional ('can include'), so compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph cites no penalty, conservatorship, or on-chain constraint, and no catalog mechanism clearly reaches an Operator's execution of a change. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Public Communication
assessments.quote: Once a change has been executed through the SBE-BEAM, the Operator must publicly communicate the execution to the Sky Ecosystem. This communication may take the form of either (1) a post to the Sky Forum or (2) the inclusion of the execution in an informational dashboard that allows community members to see each change executed through the SBE-BEAM.
assessments.description: Requires the SBE-BEAM Operator to publicly communicate each executed change via a Sky Forum post or a dashboard.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation, the actor (Operator), and two enumerated communication channels are named, so compliance is checkable. However, there is no deadline or cadence for communicating after execution, and no content requirements, so the timing and scope of compliance are left open.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain or penalty mechanism reaches a failure to publicly communicate a change; only the catch-all Reports of Misalignment (c6c6f595) and Adjudication Process (560e1024) plausibly apply, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.quote: The Target Aggregate Backstop Capital is one and one half percent (1.5%) of the total supply of USDS.
assessments.description: Sets the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital at 1.5% of total USDS supply.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The target is an exact formula (1.5% of total USDS supply) with an observable input, so a third party could compute it. It gives no measurement cadence, deadline, or tolerance band, and it states a target rather than a binding minimum.
metrics: Target Aggregate Backstop Capital = 1.5% of the total supply of USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is the protocol-level capital that this target sizes, and its burn behaviour responds to buffer level, which plausibly reaches a shortfall. The paragraph attaches no quantified consequence to missing the target itself, so the rating caps at mid.

assessments.title: Turbo-Fill Floor
assessments.quote: The current Turbo-Fill Floor for the Aggregate Backstop Capital is 150 million USDS. The Turbo-Fill Floor is the level below which an accelerated retention rate applies, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.description: Sets the current Turbo-Fill Floor for Aggregate Backstop Capital at 150 million USDS and defers the accelerated retention rate to another section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The floor is a concrete value (150 million USDS), so the core parameter is quantified. The accelerated retention rate that applies below the floor is delegated to the cross-referenced section A.2.3.1.2.3 with no value here, and the text gives no update cadence for the 'current' figure.
metrics: Turbo-Fill Floor for Aggregate Backstop Capital: 150 million USDS (current)
Accelerated retention rate applies when Aggregate Backstop Capital is below the floor (rate not stated in this paragraph)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a capital-level parameter with no actor obligation or violation mode. The referenced UUID 2b28d464 is a cross-reference, not an enforcement mechanism, and the Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) is protocol-level loss absorption that does not directly reach compliance with this floor value.

assessments.title: Capital Retention To Achieve Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.quote: When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, a portion of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.description: Requires retaining a portion of Step 2 Capital to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital when it is below target.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger (Aggregate Backstop Capital below Target) and the named capital flow (Step 2 Capital retention) are concrete, but the retained portion is not quantified here and is delegated to the cross-referenced Step 2 paragraph. No deadline or measurement cadence is stated.
metrics: Trigger: Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
Retained amount: 'a portion of Step 2 Capital' (magnitude unspecified; defined in A.2.3.1.2.3)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The obligation is a Sky Core treasury allocation rule with no distinct enforcer or penalty for non-retention. The Surplus Buffer (3eb6f099) is loss absorption rather than compliance enforcement, and SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) only disciplines governance indirectly, so neither reaches this rule's violation modes; the rule is effectively self-enforced.

assessments.title: SKY Backstop
assessments.quote: This Article governs the SKY Backstop. If the USDS Stablecoin becomes undercollateralized, the Sky Protocol will automatically generate and sell SKY to recapitalize the system. The period when the recapitalization mechanism is actively minting and selling SKY to close the shortfall is termed a "SKY Backstop Event."
assessments.description: Defines the SKY Backstop as automatic SKY minting and sale to recapitalize USDS when it becomes undercollateralized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The mechanism is described as automatic and its steps (mint and sell SKY) are enumerated, but the trigger 'undercollateralized' has no threshold, measurement method, or cadence. Whether the backstop is active is open to argument on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SKY Backstop itself is the consequence: dilutive last-resort recapitalization that disciplines governance economically and triggers on undercollateralization. It is protocol-level rather than an actor-level rule, and the trigger is unquantified, so it caps at mid.

assessments.title: Emission Rate
assessments.quote: An emissions rate for the SKY backstop function that prevents risk of sudden failure must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst case scenarios.
assessments.description: Requires a defined SKY backstop emission rate that prevents sudden failure, continuously assessed and improved for worst-case stability.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires that an emission rate be defined and continuously assessed, but gives no value, formula, or threshold for the rate. Terms like 'prevents risk of sudden failure' and 'maximize stability' are judgment language, and a defender could argue the obligation does not yet bind.
metrics: emission rate must be defined
continuously assessed and improved
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) dilution could economically discipline governance, but it does not reach a failure to define or assess the emission rate, and the paragraph names no enforcer, penalty, or escalation path.

assessments.title: Limitless
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop is temporarily limitless.
assessments.description: States that the SKY Backstop's emission rate is temporarily unlimited, with no cap or duration specified.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a single posture-style statement. It gives no emission cap, rate, duration, or end condition, and 'temporarily' is undefined, so nothing is measurable or checkable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. The text describes the backstop's own emission state rather than an obligation on an actor. The SKY Backstop mechanism (4d8b0d82) is the subject of the rule, not a consequence that enforces compliance with it.

assessments.title: Maximum Level Of Emission
assessments.quote: A maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst-case scenarios.
assessments.description: Requires a maximum SKY emission level per undercollateralization event to be defined and continuously improved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete parameter (maximum SKY emission per undercollateralization event) but gives no value, formula, or deadline. Its operative obligations, "must be defined" and "continuously assessed and improved", are judgment language, so a defender could argue nothing binding exists yet.
metrics: Maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event (must be defined; no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is the mechanism whose dilution the cap would limit, but nothing in the paragraph or the catalog penalizes failing to define or exceeding the cap, so only the catch-all misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Override Mechanism
assessments.quote: The Protocol must include an override mechanism that allows Sky Governance to continue emitting SKY beyond the maximum level. This Section must specify research processes and principles to guide when and how the override mechanism can be safely used.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol to include an override allowing Sky Governance to emit SKY beyond the maximum level, with research guidance deferred to this Section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph contains no thresholds, metrics, or defined procedures. It obligates the Protocol to contain an override and says this Section must specify research processes and principles, which are not stated here, so there is nothing yet to measure compliance against.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph only mandates that an override exist and restricts nothing, so no citable mechanism reaches a violation. The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is dilutive, but it disciplines actor-level behavior and does not police this design obligation.

assessments.title: Halt Mechanism
assessments.quote: The Protocol must contain a SKY backstop halt mechanism that immediately halts the backstop event in case of severe risk of total failure.
assessments.description: Requires the Protocol to include a SKY backstop halt mechanism that immediately stops the backstop event on severe total-failure risk.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is concrete: a mechanism must exist and act immediately. But the trigger, 'severe risk of total failure', has no threshold or metric, and no verification method or actor is defined, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Halt must occur 'immediately' once triggered
Trigger: 'severe risk of total failure' (unquantified)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5) provide pre-authorized executive halts for threatened security failures, and the Emergency Response System offers an escalation path outside normal governance, so both plausibly reach a missing or failed halt. Neither quantifies a consequence specific to this rule, and firing depends on someone escalating.

assessments.title: Mitigate Worst Case Scenario
assessments.quote: In case the backstop limit is reached and not overridden, or in case the backstop is halted during the event, the USDS target price receives a haircut to settle the remaining bad debt of the system. This Section must define elements and infrastructure to address this worst-case scenario, including research concerning ways to mitigate damage.
assessments.description: Specifies that a USDS target price haircut settles remaining bad debt when the SKY backstop limit is reached without override or is halted.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger conditions (backstop limit reached and not overridden, or backstop halted during an event) are named, but the limit value, the haircut magnitude, and the settlement method are absent. The second sentence defers the operative elements to a future Section, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Backstop limit reached and not overridden (limit value not stated)
Backstop halted during the event (no duration or criteria stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SKY Backstop (A.3.6) sets the trigger, and the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (A.3.5) is the loss-absorption layer the haircut would backstop. Neither quantifies this haircut, and it binds no actor, so the rating is mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Relation To Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop may not be invoked unless the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)) has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized.
assessments.description: Bars invoking the SKY Backstop unless the Genesis Capital Backstop has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two gating conditions are named and binary, giving a clear sequencing rule. However, 'undercollateralized' has no numeric threshold or measurement method here, and the trigger for applying the Genesis Capital Backstop is not defined in this paragraph.
metrics: Genesis Capital Backstop has been applied before SKY Backstop invocation
USDS remains undercollateralized at the time of invocation
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The SKY Backstop's dilution discourages use but is the consequence of invoking it, not a penalty for breaching this gate. No penalty, escalation, or automatic mechanism is tied to premature invocation, leaving only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops.

assessments.title: Native Vault Engine

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The cited Stability Fee (0257a420) is a user-facing incentive to migrate, not a consequence for Core GovOps failing to implement the limits. No catalog mechanism, such as Emergency Spells or Artifact Review, is tied to this implementation duty.

assessments.title: Liquidation Ratio
assessments.quote:
The Liquidation Ratio parameter limits the maximum amount of Dai debt that a vault user can draw from their vault given the value of their collateral locked in that vault. In practice, it expresses the minimum collateral in percentage terms that can support a given Dai debt. If the ratio of a Vault user's collateral to their debt drops below this value, their vault can be liquidated. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Ratio. The Liquidation Ratio for each vault type is expressed as a percentage value of the collateral that must be present in the vault to support its debt.

Changes to the Liquidation Ratio are subject to the Operational Weekly Cycle, requiring a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.
assessments.description: Sets a per-vault-type minimum collateral percentage for Dai debt, with changes made through the weekly governance poll and executive vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The liquidation trigger is a defined ratio of collateral to debt compared against a per-vault-type Liquidation Ratio, and the change process is specified. However, no numeric Liquidation Ratio values are stated; magnitudes are delegated to each vault type's parameter.
metrics: Collateral-to-debt ratio below the vault type's Liquidation Ratio triggers liquidation eligibility
Liquidation Ratio expressed as a percentage of collateral that must be present to support debt
Changes subject to the Operational Weekly Cycle, requiring a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A vault whose collateral-to-debt ratio falls below its Liquidation Ratio can be liquidated, and the Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b) is an on-chain, contract-enforced automatic cost that reaches this violation mode without human intervention.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling Limit
assessments.quote:
The Debt Ceiling Limit is numerically provided and acts as an upper limit. Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can propose changes within this limit.

Debt Ceiling Limit = Unlimited is defined as large enough to avoid being reached in the near future.

The DC-IAM methodology contained in [A.3.7.1.1.2.4 - Debt Ceiling Instant Access Module (DC-IAM)](93c9f662-4e0d-477e-8fc9-e3726877e842) acts as a risk mitigation tool. It limits the rate at which exposure can increase in a short period of time in the event of an unexpected emergency.
assessments.description: Sets a numerical debt ceiling as an upper limit on exposure, with changes proposed by Core GovOps and DC-IAM limiting its rate of increase.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph says the ceiling is 'numerically provided' but states no value here, and 'Unlimited' is defined only as 'large enough to avoid being reached in the near future'. The actor and change process are named, but the magnitude and DC-IAM parameters are delegated to other documents.
metrics: Debt Ceiling Limit is a numerically provided upper limit (value not stated in this paragraph)
Debt Ceiling Limit = Unlimited is defined as large enough to avoid being reached in the near future (qualitative)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The debt ceiling functions as a chain-enforced cap on minting, and the DC-IAM cited in the text automatically limits how fast exposure can rise during an emergency. The mechanism is automatic, though the paragraph does not describe any penalty for proposing changes outside the limit.

assessments.title: Stability Fee
assessments.quote:
The Stability Fee parameter is an annual percentage fee charged on the Dai generated on Vaults. It is expressed as an annual percentage yield but it is charged on a per-block basis in Dai. The Dai from this fee is minted, added to the Dai debt for the vault, and then transferred into the Surplus Buffer which is under the control of Sky Governance. Each vault type has its own Stability Fee that can be adjusted independently.

The Stability Fees can be modified through either Executive Votes or the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).

The Stability Fees must be gradually increased over time to incentivize users to migrate to SparkLend and other borrowing platforms offered by Prime Agents.
assessments.description: Defines the Stability Fee on Vault Dai, its per-block charging and Surplus Buffer routing, modification routes, and a directive to raise it gradually.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The fee is defined as an annual percentage charged per block, but the operative directive that fees 'must be gradually increased over time' has no magnitude, step size, or deadline. Compliance could be argued either way, since any upward drift would arguably satisfy 'gradually'.
metrics: Stability Fee expressed as an annual percentage yield, charged on a per-block basis in Dai
Each vault type has its own Stability Fee adjustable independently
Stability Fees must be gradually increased over time
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The bounded external access module (47b8b035) constrains who may change fees but nothing enforces the directive that fees rise gradually; the Surplus Buffer receives fee revenue but does not penalize non-compliance.

assessments.title: Maximum Debt Ceiling (line)
assessments.quote:
The `line` parameter refers to the maximum value for the Debt Ceiling that the DC-IAM will allow in the given vault type. When using the DC-IAM to manage the Debt Ceiling of a vault type, the `line` parameter essentially replaces the Debt Ceiling parameter for that vault type. Rather than Sky Governance setting the Debt Ceiling directly, they will need to set the Maximum Debt Ceiling `line` in the DC-IAM. The `line` parameter is defined in Dai.

The Maximum Debt Ceiling is defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.2 - Debt Ceiling Limit](b490d4d0-8eb8-4dc6-9ef3-c85d357f1f4b) and is currently unlimited.
assessments.description: Defines the DC-IAM maximum Debt Ceiling (line) parameter for a vault type, set by Sky Governance and currently unlimited.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the line parameter and its role in replacing direct Debt Ceiling setting, but states no numeric bound, cadence, or formula. Its only value, 'currently unlimited', imposes no constraint, and the operative definition is delegated to another section.
metrics: line: maximum Debt Ceiling the DC-IAM allows per vault type (currently unlimited)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog enforcement mechanism is cited or reaches this rule. The DC-IAM would technically cap debt once a line is set, but the referenced limit is currently unlimited, so no enforcement attaches to any stated magnitude.

assessments.title: Target Available Debt (gap)
assessments.quote: The `gap` parameter controls how much of a gap the DC-IAM aims to maintain between the current debt usage and the Debt Ceiling of the vault type. The higher this value, the more risk there is from large collateral drops in very short amounts of time. The smaller this value, the more vault use is negatively affected. The `gap` parameter is defined in Dai.
assessments.description: Defines the gap parameter, the Dai-denominated buffer the DC-IAM keeps between vault debt usage and the Debt Ceiling.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the gap parameter, its unit (Dai), and its reference points (current debt usage and the vault type's Debt Ceiling), but gives no value, formula, or bound. It only states directional effects, so compliance cannot be checked from the text.
metrics: gap: Dai-denominated spacing between current debt usage and the vault type's Debt Ceiling (no numeric value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no operative obligation or cited consequence, and no catalog mechanism (liquidation, PSM, penalties) reaches the gap target. Only the misalignment and adjudication catch-alls apply.

assessments.title: Ceiling Increase Cooldown (ttl)
assessments.quote: The Ceiling Increase Cooldown (`ttl`) parameter controls how frequently the Debt Ceiling can be increased by the DC-IAM. If a user attempts to use the DC-IAM to increase the Debt Ceiling of a vault type before this time expires, the transaction will fail to execute and the Debt Ceiling will remain unchanged. The `ttl` parameter in combination with the `gap` parameter enforces a maximum rate at which debt usage can increase over time using a given vault type. These parameters should be set such that the maximum increase over time can accommodate all reasonable usage of the vault type in question. The `ttl` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.description: Sets a seconds-based cooldown between DC-IAM Debt Ceiling increases for a vault type, reverting any earlier increase attempt.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The ttl parameter is named, measured in seconds, and its enforcement effect is concrete: increases before expiry revert. However, no ttl value is given, and calibration is delegated to a qualitative standard ('should be set such that... all reasonable usage').

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The cooldown is contract-enforced in the text (transactions revert before expiry), but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph reaches this ceiling-increase rule, so nothing citable supports a mid or strong rating; none found.

assessments.title: Auction Parameters
assessments.quote: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the parameters specified in this document. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, has the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. The parameters contained herein must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.
assessments.description: Requires justification and analysis for parameter changes, Governance Poll approval before Executive Votes, an emergency bypass, and regular monitoring.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Actors and process steps are named (Core GovOps, Core Council Risk Advisor, Governance Poll, Executive Vote), but there is no numeric threshold, cadence for "regularly monitored," or criteria defining "emergency." Compliance on the same facts is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Governance Poll gate is self-policed by Core GovOps, and no catalog mechanism (penalties, conservatorship, liquidation, PSM, emergency spells) reaches unauthorized parameter changes or misuse of the emergency bypass.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (calc)
assessments.quote:
The Auction Price Function is the mathematical function that determines how the collateral price changes over time during a collateral auction. Collateral auctions use a falling price auction, where the price starts high and decreases according to the function defined in this parameter.

The Exponential Stair Step function contains two key parameters, `cut` and `step`, defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.1 - Auction Price Function (cut)](1ff3ceac-abd0-4195-9a60-a4aaf48c3d31) and [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.2 - Auction Price Function (step)](4b46633c-4d6c-4a9c-9be0-93d242ce9db9), respectively.
assessments.description: Defines the falling-price function, an Exponential Stair Step, that sets how collateral auction prices decline over time.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the function type and its two parameters (cut and step) but gives no values, formulas, or cadence. Magnitudes are delegated to child parameter documents, so compliance cannot be checked from this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The function is executed on-chain in the auction contract, but the paragraph imposes no obligation whose violation would be penalized. Setting cut and step is ordinary governance, and no citable mechanism reaches this definition.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (cut)
assessments.quote: The `cut` parameter controls the ‘depth’ of each step in the function. A smaller `cut` means a smoother line; a large one means more pronounced steps. The `cut` parameter is defined as a multiplicative factor. For example, 0.99 equated to a 1% price drop.
assessments.description: Defines the cut parameter as a multiplicative per-step price factor controlling step depth in the auction price function.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a formula-like meaning (multiplicative factor, 0.99 equals a 1% drop) but states no operative value, range, or bound for cut, and it imposes no obligation on a defined actor. It is a descriptive definition, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: cut is a multiplicative factor
example: cut of 0.99 equates to a 1% price drop per step
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no actor or obligation, and no cited mechanism enforces a cut value or its step depth; the auction contract's behavior is not stated to be bound by this text.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (step)
assessments.quote: The `step` parameter controls the length of time between price drops. A smaller step means a smoother line; a large one means more pronounced steps. The `step` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.description: Defines the step parameter of the auction price function as seconds between price drops, controlling curve smoothness.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the parameter, its unit (seconds), and its effect on the price curve, but gives no value, range, or default. Whether any actor is bound to a particular setting is left unstated, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with no obligated actor or violation mode, and no cited mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, PSM, emergency spell, or review) reaches a breach of it.

assessments.title: Auction Price Multiplier (buf)
assessments.quote: The `buf` parameter is a multiplier that is applied to the starting price of a collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Auction Price Multiplier that can be adjusted by Sky Governance separately. This multiplier is intended to be greater than 1.0x because Liquidations 2.0 uses falling price auctions. This means that it is generally preferable for the auction price to begin above the market price and then fall to the correct value over some amount of time. The `buf` parameter is defined as a multiplicative factor.
assessments.description: Defines the buf multiplier on collateral auction starting price per vault type, intended to exceed 1.0x.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter, its role, and per-vault-type governance adjustment are named, but the only numeric bound (greater than 1.0x) is framed as 'intended' rather than binding, and no value or range is set. A defender could argue the rule does not yet bind any specific magnitude.
metrics: buf intended to be greater than 1.0x
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph is a parameter definition with a non-binding intent, and no cited mechanism (Liquidation Penalty, Emergency Spells, Penalty Mechanisms) is shown to police the choice of buf value; the on-chain auction applies buf but does not enforce the >1.0x intent.

assessments.title: Max Auction Drawdown (cusp)
assessments.quote:
The Max Auction Drawdown is the maximum percentage drop in collateral price during a collateral auction before the auction is reset. 'Collateral price' in this context refers to the collateral auction price rather than the collateral market price.

The Max Auction Drawdown parameter overlaps with the Max Auction Duration parameter in that an auction will need to be reset once either maximum is exceeded.
assessments.description: Defines the Max Auction Drawdown parameter, which resets a collateral auction once the auction price drops past a maximum percentage.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph gives a formula-like trigger (percentage drop in collateral auction price) and a concrete action (reset), but no numeric value or measurement cadence appears in the text. The magnitude is left to the parameter's value elsewhere, so the operative threshold is not stated here.
metrics: Maximum percentage drop in collateral auction price during a collateral auction, before the auction is reset
Auction is reset once either Max Auction Drawdown or Max Auction Duration is exceeded
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The reset is a contract-level liquidation-auction behavior, so the Liquidation Penalty (on-chain, contract-enforced) plausibly reaches it. However, the consequence here is an auction reset rather than a quantified cost to an actor, so it is rated mid rather than strong.

assessments.title: Max Auction Duration (tail)
assessments.quote:
The Max Auction Duration parameter sets the maximum time that can elapse before an auction needs to reset for a particular vault type. Expressed in seconds, this parameter determines when an auction can no longer settle and must be reset.

The Max Auction Duration parameter overlaps with the Max Auction Drawdown parameter in that an auction will need to be reset once either maximum is exceeded.
assessments.description: Defines the Max Auction Duration parameter, in seconds, after which a vault-type auction must reset, and its overlap with Max Auction Drawdown.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter is named and its unit (seconds) and reset trigger are stated, but no numeric value or per-vault-type figure is given. A defender could argue the text binds no specific limit yet, so compliance is arguable.
metrics: Max Auction Duration, expressed in seconds, per vault type
Auction must reset once the maximum duration or the Max Auction Drawdown is exceeded
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph gives no enforcer or consequence, and no catalogued mechanism (Liquidation Penalty concerns position collateral, not auction timing) is cited as reaching this parameter. Only the catch-all backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Proportional Kick Incentive (chip)
assessments.quote: The Proportional Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Proportional Kick Incentive is set as a percentage and represents a portion of Dai based on the debt of the vault that is being liquidated. The Dai is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Proportional Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Proportional Kick Incentive, a percentage of vault debt paid in Dai to keepers who trigger collateral liquidation auctions, set per vault type.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The base (vault debt), payout timing (when the auction is triggered), and per-vault-type scope are concrete, but the percentage itself is not stated and is left to Sky Governance. No cadence or bounds are given.
metrics: Reward is a percentage of the debt of the vault being liquidated
Reward is paid in Dai at the point each liquidation auction is triggered
Each vault type has its own Proportional Kick Incentive percentage, adjustable separately by Sky Governance
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The chip is a keeper reward parameter with no violation mode for a regulated party. Collateral enforcement comes from the Liquidation Penalty (bce9331b), which this paragraph does not invoke, so the chip itself has no consequence attached.

assessments.title: Flat Kick Incentive (tip)
assessments.quote: The Flat Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Flat Kick Incentive is a fixed amount of Dai that is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Flat Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Flat Kick Incentive as a fixed Dai reward paid to keepers per triggered liquidation auction, set per vault type by governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the parameter, the payee (keepers), the trigger (auction initiation), and per-vault-type governance adjustment, but gives no fixed Dai amount or range. The operative magnitude is delegated to Sky Governance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The kick is paid by on-chain liquidation contract logic when an auction is triggered, so the payout is contract-executed, which implicitly ties to the Liquidation Penalty machinery (bce9331b). No quantified consequence or named enforcer attaches to misconfiguring or misapplying this specific parameter, so it stops short of strong.

assessments.title: Liquidation Penalty (chop)
assessments.quote: The Liquidation Penalty parameter controls the fee vault owners must pay when their position is liquidated due to insufficient collateral. For a vault holder to receive any collateral back from the liquidations process, the debt and Liquidation Penalty must be covered by the collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Penalty that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Defines the Liquidation Penalty fee that liquidated vault owners pay, which must be covered by collateral auction before any residual collateral is returned.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The parameter is named and its role in liquidation is clear, but no penalty magnitude or formula is stated, and per-vault-type values are left to Sky Governance adjustment. The only verifiable condition is that debt plus penalty must be covered by the collateral auction before any collateral is returned.
metrics: Debt and Liquidation Penalty must be covered by the collateral auction before the vault holder receives any collateral back
Each vault type has its own Liquidation Penalty, adjustable by Sky Governance (no value stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Liquidation Penalty is charged automatically by the on-chain liquidation machinery when a position is undercollateralised, so the cost of breaching collateral requirements is contract-enforced with no human in the loop.

assessments.title: Local Liquidation Limit (hole)
assessments.quote: The Local Liquidation Limit sets the maximum amount of Dai debt for which collateral auctions can be active at any one time within a particular vault type. When the total Dai value of auctions exceeds this maximum for a particular vault type, no more collateral can be auctioned using that vault type until others are completed. Each vault type has a separate Local Liquidation Limit.
assessments.description: Caps total Dai debt in active collateral auctions per vault type, halting new auctions when the cap is exceeded.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific parameter and an operative test (total Dai value of auctions versus the maximum, per vault type), but the limit's magnitude is not stated and is left to parameter settings. No measurement cadence or update process is given.
metrics: Total Dai value of active collateral auctions per vault type must not exceed the vault type's Local Liquidation Limit
No new collateral auctioned for a vault type while its total auction Dai value exceeds the limit, until other auctions complete
Each vault type has a separate Local Liquidation Limit
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The cap is a contract-level throttle on the liquidation engine: when auction exposure exceeds the limit, the protocol automatically blocks further collateral auctions for that vault type without human intervention. The cited Liquidation Penalty doc is the on-chain liquidation machinery this throttle governs, so the mechanism is self-executing.

assessments.title: Debt Floor (dust)
assessments.quote: The Debt Floor parameter controls the minimum amount of Dai that can be minted using a specific vault type for an individual vault. If a user tries to mint Dai and the amount of Dai minted would not put the vault's amount of Dai minted above its Debt Floor, the transaction will fail and no DAi will be minted. Likewise, if a user attempts to pay back debt such that their debt will equal less than the Debt Floor and greater than zero, the transaction will fail and no Dai will be paid back. Each vault type has its own Debt Floor that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.description: Sets a per-vault-type minimum Dai debt, rejecting mints and repayments that leave a vault's debt between zero and the floor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The operative mechanics are concrete: mints or repayments that leave debt below the floor (but above zero) fail and no Dai moves. The floor magnitude is not stated and is left to Sky Governance per vault type.
metrics: Debt Floor is the minimum Dai debt per individual vault, set separately for each vault type
Minting must leave the vault's debt above its Debt Floor, otherwise the transaction fails
Repayment must not leave debt greater than zero and less than the Debt Floor, otherwise the transaction fails
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The transaction revert is on-chain, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the text reaches this debt-floor rule; Liquidation Penalty covers collateral violations, not floor violations.

assessments.title: Offboarding Low Usage Collateral
assessments.quote: To protect the Protocol from unnecessary complexity, the Core Facilitator must offboard collateral types specified in [A.3.7.1.1.1 - Vault Types](64971463-0650-4462-b9c4-1eecb704fa1a) if they fall below a total debt of 20 million.
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to offboard collateral types whose total debt falls below 20 million.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The actor (Core Facilitator), the action (offboard), and a numeric threshold (total debt below 20 million) are all stated. Gaps remain: no unit or currency, no measurement cadence, and no clarity on whether 'total debt' is per collateral type or aggregate.
metrics: total debt below 20 million per collateral type (unit and scope unspecified)

assessments.title: Oracles
assessments.quote:
The Native Vault Engine collateral types of ETH, STETH, WBTC will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026. The Native Vault Engine collateral types must be migrated to the new version of the Chronicle v3 oracle when it is feasible to do so.

Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and only if there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles.

Use Chronicle v3 oracle until at least January 1st 2026
Other oracles considered only until January 1st 2026
Other oracles only if unresolvable security concerns with Chronicle v3 exist

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module
assessments.quote: The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the Stability Fees of supported vault types, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), and the Sky Savings Rate (SSR). Adjustments are governed by the SP-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. SP-BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each vault type or savings rate: (i) `min`, (ii) `max`, (iii) `step`, and (iv) `tau`.
assessments.description: Defines SP-BEAM, letting whitelisted operators adjust Stability Fees, DSR and SSR within min, max, step and tau bounds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names four concrete parameters (min, max, step, tau) and the rates they govern, but gives no values, formulas, or update cadence. Magnitudes are delegated to Sky Governance and the contract logic, which is not specified here.

tau: per vault type/savings rate, value set by Sky Governance (not stated)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The smart contract logic arguably bounds adjustments on-chain, but no catalog mechanism or UUID in the paragraph text reaches this rule, so none citable were found and the rating defaults to weak.

Attempts to use the SP-BEAM in this manner will revert. To avoid confusion, `max` should not be set to a value higher than 50% (5,000 basis points).

assessments.title: Tau Definition

The `tau` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.

An SP-BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once an SP-BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent SP-BEAM operation can be performed.

tau duration must expire before any subsequent SP-BEAM operation can be performed

assessments.title: Legacy Context
assessments.quote:
Periodically, collateral and vault types (ilks) are re-evaluated, which sometimes results in an offboarding of that collateral or vault type.

There have been several instances where users entered official Sky forums/chats to understand why they had been suddenly liquidated, despite historically comfortable collateralization ratios ([https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836)). This is, understandably, a poor user experience.

Even with liquidation penalties set to 0%, the forced unwinding of levered positions conceivably can result in user losses, as well as potentially taxable events.

This Section defines procedures concerning the dissemination of information about upcoming collateral offboarding on a best-effort basis. The objective is to minimize the number of users who are unaware of the offboarding prior to getting their positions liquidated.
assessments.description: Describes collateral and vault offboarding context and a best-effort goal of informing users before liquidation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is explanatory and states a best-effort posture with no threshold, deadline, metric, or named actor. The text says the procedures are defined elsewhere in the section, so it contains no operative obligation to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No on-chain, capital-at-risk, or named institutional mechanism reaches a best-effort information-dissemination duty, and the paragraph cites no enforcement path.

assessments.title: Legacy Context Specific Goals
assessments.quote:
Specific Goals:

1. Codify a series of good-faith communication efforts.
2. Provide an easy-to-follow process for Sky contributors to follow without significant burden.
3. Minimize the number of users unaware of a collateral offboarding.
4. Provide a method to bypass these requirements in the event a collateral is being offboarded due to serious security or solvency concerns.
assessments.description: Sets goals for communicating legacy collateral offboardings, simplifying contributor process, and bypassing requirements in security emergencies.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states real goals (codify communication, a bypass method for security or solvency cases) but uses judgment language such as 'series of good-faith communication efforts', 'significant burden', and 'minimize the number of users unaware', with no counts, thresholds, or deadlines. A defender could argue these are non-binding aspirations.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, or emergency mechanism is tied to these offboarding communication goals, and the only available routes are the catch-all misalignment and adjudication processes.

assessments.title: Immediate Actions
assessments.quote:
Upon approval by Sky Governance to offboard a permissionless collateral type or vault type, the following actions are taken as soon as is practicable:

- Set debt ceiling to zero (0) Dai or USDS.
- Make an initial public announcement on all communication channels listed in [A.3.7.1.5.3.0.6.1 - Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing](9ac8a70b-8b6a-4825-a5e0-5e9019e50bc4).
- Make a second public announcement on all communication channels in the above cited document no later than 14 calendar days after the initial public announcement.
- Once the second public announcements have been made, set the liquidation penalty to 0%.
assessments.description: Specifies the steps taken after Sky Governance approves offboarding a collateral or vault type, including zeroing debt ceilings and liquidation penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The debt ceiling is set to exactly zero, the second announcement is due within 14 calendar days, and the liquidation penalty is set to 0% after the second announcement. However, the first action is only "as soon as is practicable", and the announcement channels are delegated to another document.

Second public announcement no later than 14 calendar days after the initial announcement
Liquidation penalty set to 0% after the second announcement
Initial announcement made "as soon as is practicable" after governance approval
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The rule regulates Sky Core's own offboarding steps, and no cited mechanism (Penalty Mechanisms, Conservatorship, Emergency Spells, or Agent Artifact Review) reaches a missed announcement deadline or a failure to zero the debt ceiling. The only remaining backstops are the catch-all misalignment and adjudication processes.

assessments.title: Following Actions
assessments.quote: Parameter changes designed to offboard users, such as changes to the liquidation ratio or stability fee, can only be implemented once 14 calendar days have passed following a second public announcement.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The core obligation is quantified: a 14-calendar-day delay after a second public announcement. Gaps remain: "designed to offboard users" is not defined by criteria, and the announcement's required form and channel are unspecified.
metrics: 14 calendar days must pass following a second public announcement before offboarding parameter changes are implemented
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog mechanism or in-paragraph UUID reaches this delay rule; Emergency Spells cover security violations, not offboarding timing. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply, so enforcement is weak.

assessments.title: Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing
assessments.quote:
The following channels should be used for initial and second public announcements of collateral offboarding. The order of announcement publication is as follows:

1. The author of the collateral offboarding notice shall post to the Sky Forum detailing the recommended offboarding. This forum thread is used to inform downstream announcements on other channels.
2. Core GovOps publishes the associated notices to:
    - All public Sky Calendars
    - The Sky Official Discord’s Announcement channel.
    - The official Sky subreddit.
3. Partner Relationship Leads from relevant Ecosystem Actors reach out to:
    - Affected collateral partners (e.g., Aave)
    - Affected frontend service providers (e.g., Oasis, DeFi Saver)

Additionally, outreach may be done to cover more channels not listed here. These may include other Ecosystem Actor or Facilitator owned Twitter accounts, communication channels, and platforms.

Unless otherwise noted in [A.3.7.1.5 - Offboarding Process](3da8a0fd-952c-4f80-b674-f60c9a293cb9) and its subdocuments, Core GovOps will take the lead in coordinating channels announcements.
assessments.description: Specifies the order and channels for publicly announcing collateral offboarding, with Core GovOps coordinating announcements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The publication sequence and named channels (Sky Forum, Core GovOps notices to calendars, Discord, subreddit, partner and frontend outreach) are concrete. However, the operative language is 'should' and 'may', with no deadlines, cadence, or timing between steps, so compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No penalty, conservatorship, emergency, or on-chain mechanism reaches a failure to publish or sequence offboarding announcements; Penalty Mechanisms and Artifact Review target Prime and agent risk-capital and artifact conduct, not communications.

assessments.title: Requirements
assessments.quote:
When a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol, an expedited offboarding is in order. Expedited offboardings override the timeline specified in [A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process](305e2bd6-a594-4aec-8713-adbe7bc87120) and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters.

Expedited offboardings must proceed pursuant to the following requirements:

- The Offboarding Proposal must state that the offboarding should be expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern, as defined in [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)**.**
- The Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference this Atlas document.
assessments.description: Requires expedited collateral offboarding proposals to state an emergency or urgent concern and explicitly reference the Atlas document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The two proposal-content requirements are objectively checkable, but the trigger ('threatens the security or solvency') is qualitative and no expedited timeline is stated, only that the A.3.7.1.5.2 timeline is overridden. Whether a threat exists is open to judgment.
metrics: Offboarding Proposal must state the offboarding is expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern (per A.1.9.1.1)
Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference the Atlas document (A.3.7.1.5.4.1)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) is the defined escalation protocol that expedited offboardings invoke, so the proposal-content gate sits on that path. No quantified penalty applies to a non-compliant proposal, and enforcement requires someone to challenge the proposal.

assessments.title: Announcements
assessments.quote: The public announcements defined in [A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process](305e2bd6-a594-4aec-8713-adbe7bc87120) must still be carried out. However, the timing of these announcements no longer constrains the modification of parameters. These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons for this accelerated process.
assessments.description: Requires offboarding announcements to state that offboarding is expedited and explain why, with no timing constraint on parameter changes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names concrete required content (a statement that offboarding is expedited and an explanation of reasons) and an operative effect (timing no longer constrains parameter changes). However, it sets no deadlines or thresholds and defers the announcement mechanics to the referenced section A.3.7.1.5.2.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: none found. No citable mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, artifact review, or on-chain enforcement) is tied to the announcement duty; only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops apply.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.quote: If losses exceed a Prime Agent’s capital and cannot be absorbed by the Sky Surplus Buffer, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized to cover the portion of the loss that exceeds what the Prime Agent’s capital and the Sky Surplus Buffer can absorb, up to a maximum of the Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)).
assessments.description: Requires a pro-rata haircut on Genesis Agents' Genesis Capital, transferred to the Surplus Buffer, when Prime losses exceed capital and buffer.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger, pro-rata allocation, and sizing formula (excess loss beyond Prime capital and Surplus Buffer) are stated. The cap refers to Aggregate Backstop Capital without a value here, and "eligible assets" is not defined in this paragraph.
metrics: Trigger: losses exceed a Prime Agent's capital and cannot be absorbed by the Sky Surplus Buffer
Haircut sized to the portion of loss exceeding Prime capital plus Surplus Buffer absorption
Haircut allocated pro-rata across each Genesis Agent's Genesis Capital
Maximum haircut equals Aggregate Backstop Capital (6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is the loss-absorption layer that this haircut feeds into, giving an economic backstop. Genesis Agents bear the haircut as capital at risk, but the rule is a loss-allocation mechanism triggered by losses, not an actor-level compliance duty, and no quantified penalty attaches to any violation.

assessments.title: Implementation
assessments.quote:
In the near term, transfers are made through Executive Votes and may be made through Emergency Spells (see [A.1.10.5 - Emergency Spells](b8266c11-3a84-4bbe-abe2-de9474f74ffd)) as part of the Emergency Response System (see [A.1.9.1 - Emergency Response](20dcf582-8862-48b3-9ca9-c3703871bd14)).

A solution must be developed to allow these transfers to be accomplished on an automated basis without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay (see [A.1.10.3 - Governance Security Delay Requirements](c5f0e955-0441-42e0-a6fc-eab875bba568)).
assessments.description: Governs how Genesis Capital Backstop transfers are executed near-term via Executive Votes or Emergency Spells, and calls for an automated solution bypassing the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The near-term path is named, but 'may be made' is permissive and the automated solution is only required to be 'developed' with no specification, thresholds, or deadline. The operative content is a future stub with nothing verifiable to comply with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. Emergency Spells and the Emergency Response System are cited as transfer channels, not as penalties for improper transfers, and no consequence attaches to a violation of this procedural rule.

assessments.title: Post Backstop Settlement
assessments.quote: If, after the haircut, losses still exceed the combined capacity of the Prime Agent’s capital and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)), the SKY Backstop (see [A.3.6 - SKY Backstop](4d8b0d82-97da-4041-b185-4b98c2779cbe)) is activated. The SKY mint must be sized to cover the remaining loss. If losses still exceed what the SKY Backstop can absorb, Sky will adjust the USDS target price below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit; Sky will then distribute 24 billion SKY to USDS holders via an airdrop.
assessments.description: Sets the loss-settlement cascade after a haircut: SKY Backstop minting, then USDS target price reduction and a 24 billion SKY airdrop.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The 24 billion SKY airdrop is a fixed quantity and the trigger conditions are defined by reference to capital layers. However, the SKY mint size ('sized to cover the remaining loss') and the target price cut ('to the extent necessary') are delegated to outcomes rather than stated as formulas or values.
metrics: Losses exceed combined capacity of Prime Agent capital and Aggregate Backstop Capital, triggering SKY Backstop activation
SKY mint sized to cover the remaining loss
USDS target price adjusted below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit
Airdrop of 24 billion SKY to USDS holders
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SKY Backstop (4d8b0d82) is a dilutive last-resort recapitalization that economically disciplines governance, and Aggregate Backstop Capital (6dbead44) is capital at risk that absorbs losses first. Neither reaches Sky Core's own conduct in settling losses directly, and the escalation is not separately quantified for this rule, so mid is the ceiling.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital
assessments.quote: The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the Eligible Genesis Capital of the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. The Eligible Genesis Capital of an Agent is the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.1 - Amount Of Capital Contributed By Sky To Agents](0331556e-e7ae-48a2-a693-75468c416321)) minus the Phased-Out Genesis Capital of the Agent (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3.0.6.1 - Current Phased-Out Genesis Capital](41bf89b5-dae5-47f3-bd6b-73b5598d9a0d)).

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The Genesis Capital formula is explicit (min of Eligible Genesis Capital and total capital, with Eligible equal to Sky-contributed capital minus Phased-Out Genesis Capital). The two input amounts are delegated to other paragraphs by UUID and no values, measurement cadence, or update timing appear here.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Phase-Out
assessments.quote:
As the ecosystem matures and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) reaches a sufficient level, Genesis Capital will phase out. The documents herein define the eligibility conditions and phase-out amounts.

Phase-out is effected by increasing an Agent's Phased-Out Genesis Capital (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3 - Phased-Out Genesis Capital](8f813186-1317-41b1-86d1-47fce7f42af5)), which reduces the Agent's Eligible Genesis Capital and therefore its Genesis Capital, progressively reducing the Genesis Capital subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)). Phase-out does not involve any repayment or transfer of capital from the Genesis Agents to Sky.
assessments.description: Describes Genesis Capital being phased out as Aggregate Backstop Capital matures, reducing Agents' eligible Genesis Capital without any repayment to Sky.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger is a 'sufficient level' of Aggregate Backstop Capital with no value stated, and the eligibility conditions and phase-out amounts are delegated to documents not in this paragraph. Named parameters (Phased-Out Genesis Capital, Eligible Genesis Capital) exist, but a defender could argue no binding threshold yet exists.
metrics: Phase-out begins when Aggregate Backstop Capital reaches a 'sufficient level' (no value stated)

assessments.title: Usage Standards
assessments.quote:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer in the event that Spark is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Operational GovOps Soter Labs before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Spark. Operational GovOps Soter Labs may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Operational GovOps Soter Labs and, if necessary, other Ecosystem Actors, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The Emergency Response System and Emergency Spells govern responses to Spark's violations, not the signers' own freeze and reporting duties. Reporting to the Sky Forum is self-disclosure, and the only general backstop is misalignment reporting.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.

assessments.title: Allocator Role

Actors submit allocation operations through the AdministeredAgent. The Arbitrum Diamond PAU actors are:

- ALM Relayer Multisig: `0x8a25A24EDE9482C4Fc0738F99611BE58F1c839AB`.
- Spark hot wallet: `0x062cE42caE04c51D04E77e3D64cc8953a2296FfE`.

assessments.title: Calculate Swap Limit
assessments.quote:
The operator must calculate the `swap` `limit` per transaction. The maximum amount of USDC that can be swapped to DAI in one transaction is calculated based on the DAI balance held by the PSM. `psmTo18ConversionFactor` converts DAI’s 18 token decimals to USDC’s 6 token decimals.

`uint256 limit = dai.balanceOf(address(psm)) / psmTo18ConversionFactor;`
assessments.description: Requires Spark operators to compute the per-transaction USDC swap limit from the PSM's DAI balance using a decimal conversion factor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The formula is explicit and checkable: limit equals the PSM's DAI balance divided by psmTo18ConversionFactor. The conversion factor's numeric value (10^12 implied by 18-to-6 decimals) is not stated in the paragraph, so it is defined by reference rather than given.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps can assess whether the operator's swap-limit calculation matches the specified formula, with penalty assessment available. The penalty is not quantified for this rule, and the on-chain PSM does not itself enforce the operator's computed limit.

assessments.title: Split Into Multiple Swaps If Limit Exceeded
assessments.quote:
If the `usdcAmount` exceeds the limit, the operator must split the swap into multiple smaller swaps as follows.

1. The operator must refill the PSM with DAI by calling `psm.fill()`.
2. The operator must recalculate the limit to see how much USDC can be swapped after the refill.
3. The operator must swap the maximum possible USDC amount that doesn't exceed the limit.
4. The operator must update `remainingUsdcToSwap` by subtracting the amount just swapped.
5. The operator must repeat the process until the full `usdcAmount` is swapped.
assessments.description: Requires operators to split USDC-to-DAI PSM swaps exceeding the limit into refilled, limit-capped tranches until fully swapped.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates concrete steps and names specific parameters (psm.fill(), remainingUsdcToSwap), but the operative limit is never given a value or formula in this text. The 'maximum possible' amount and the loop's end condition are defined only by reference to the undefined 'limit'.

Each swap is the maximum USDC amount that does not exceed the limit after refill
remainingUsdcToSwap reduced by the amount just swapped
Repeat until the full usdcAmount is swapped
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The PSM contract enforces the swap limit on-chain, so exceeding it is impossible, but the required splitting and refill sequence is not contract-enforced. Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps and the Penalty Mechanisms could reach procedural non-compliance, though no penalty is quantified for this specific rule.
